author: mfagerstrom
body:
## Summary
- New `src/services/ClientObservability.ts` registers listeners for `shardError`,
  `shardDisconnect`, `shardReconnecting`, `shardResume`, `warn`, `invalidated`, and the REST
  `rateLimited` event, each writing a structured log line through `LogUtils`.
- When the gateway session cannot recover, the bot destroys the client and exits with code 1
  so the process manager restarts it with a fresh session.
- `rateLimited` logs method, sanitized route, limit, retry-after (ms), global, and scope.
- Unit tests in `src/tests/client-observability.test.ts` emit each event on a real, unconnected
  discord.js `Client` and check the log output and the shutdown callback.

## Judgment calls
- Shutdown also triggers on `shardDisconnect`, not only `invalidated`. The issue asked for a
  shutdown on `invalidated`, but discord.js 14.27 still declares that event and no longer emits
  it anywhere since its move to `@discordjs/ws`. In `WebSocketManager.js`, a session that cannot
  come back surfaces as `shardDisconnect`, which only fires for unrecoverable close codes. Keying
  the shutdown on `invalidated` alone would leave a dead bot running. The `invalidated` listener
  stays in case a later version emits it again, and a guard makes the shutdown run once.
- The rate limit log leaves out `url`: interaction follow-up and `editReply` URLs embed the
  interaction token. `route` is discord.js's sanitized bucket route
  (`/webhooks/:id/:token/...`) and still identifies the endpoint.
- The disconnect log records the close code and its `GatewayCloseCodes` name instead of
  `CloseEvent.reason`, which is deprecated and always holds a fixed placeholder string.
- Severity per event: `shardError` and `shardDisconnect` log as errors, `shardReconnecting`,
  `warn`, and `rateLimited` as warnings, and `shardResume` as info, because a resume means the
  connection recovered. The issue only named `logWarn`/`logError`. Logging a successful resume
  as a warning would add noise without adding signal.
- The listeners live in their own service module instead of inline in `RPGClub_GameDB.ts`. The
  issue pointed at the main file, but a module with an injected shutdown callback can be unit
  tested without exiting the test process.
- Shutdown calls `bot.destroy()` before `process.exit(1)` so the gateway socket closes cleanly.
  The nonzero exit code matches the existing `uncaughtException` crash-and-restart path.
- No Testing section: these events come from the gateway and REST layers and cannot be
  triggered by a Discord command.

## Self review
Two passes.
- Pass 1, four findings, all fixed in 41ffeb4:
  - `invalidated` is never emitted by discord.js 14.27, so the shutdown never ran. It now also
    runs on an unrecoverable `shardDisconnect`.
  - The `rateLimited` log included `url`, which leaks interaction tokens. It was removed.
  - The disconnect log read the deprecated `CloseEvent.reason`. It now logs the close code name
    instead.
  - No test covered the shutdown on disconnect. One was added, including the run-once guard.
- Pass 2: clean.

## Checklist
- [x] Type-check passes (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [x] Lint passes (`npm run lint`)
- [x] Tests pass (`npm test`)

Closes #1222

author: emooreatx
body:
Closes #740

## What was wrong
`DirectoryStateAdapter` bridged the sync `StateProvider` / `StateApplier` traits to persist with `block_in_place` + `Handle::block_on`. Each bridged read held one blocking-pool slot (the replacement worker) while it waited for a second slot (persist's SQL). A kick runs every `(peer, kind)` at once, so 3 peers × 14 kinds = 42 reads against a 32-slot pool took every slot before any read could start, and the node stopped. With 2 peers the kick is 28 reads, which fit, and that is why every two-node witness passed.

## The fix (two parts)
1. **No sync-over-async on the read path.** `StateProvider` (`local_refs`, `local_holdings`, `fetch_envelope`, `subject_refs`, `accord_evidence_since`) and `StateApplier::apply_envelope` are now `#[async_trait]`. The adapters await persist directly, and `Session` and the coordinator await the adapters. The sync methods that remain are in-memory probes by contract. No `block_in_place` or `block_on` is left anywhere on a round's path.
2. **A kick is bounded.** A single `RoundGate` semaphore sits in the scheduler. It covers `round_now_all`, `sync_and_await`, `Propagate` and the start-up tick, and limits in-flight rounds to `SchedulerConfig::max_concurrent_rounds`. The default is `max(1, max_blocking_threads / 2)`, which is 16 for the 32-slot pool, and a compile-time assert keeps at least 9 slots free for persist's 8 readers and 1 writer. You set it on `ReplicationRuntimeConfig.scheduler`, and `edge_node` derives it from its `RuntimeBudget`. Rounds over the limit wait for a permit: none are dropped, and there are no sleeps or retry counts. `ReplicationRuntime::round_bound()` reports `bound`, `in_flight`, `peak_in_flight` and `waited`.

## Rust API break
- Every `StateProvider` / `StateApplier` implementor must become `async` with `#[async_trait::async_trait]`.
- `Session::start_round` and `Session::on_message` are now `async`.
- `SchedulerConfig` has a new field, `max_concurrent_rounds`. Struct literals need `..SchedulerConfig::default()`.
- CIRISServer does not implement either trait. Its `tests/trace_round_e2e.rs` calls `DirectoryStateAdapter::local_refs` and drives `Session` synchronously, so it needs `.await` when it adopts this.

## Witness
`tests/kick_three_peers_740.rs` sets up D1 with three rooted peers over 14 kinds. Each node has a real persist directory and hybrid-signed routes, the nodes talk Reticulum over loopback, and the self room is installed. The test runs on a `max_blocking_threads(32)` runtime, and the test thread enforces a hard wall-clock timeout.
- **v34.3.0 (852f43d):** wedges during the start-up fan-out. After 240 s only 3 of 42 rounds had finished and the counter was frozen. The same file with `PEERS = 2` passes on v34.3.0 in 3.5 s.
- **This branch:** 42 start-up rounds and 42 kicked rounds finish in about 5 s, and all 42 `(peer, kind)` rounds of the kick reach their peer on the wire.
- Unit test `scheduler::tests::a_kick_of_n_plus_one_rounds_runs_at_most_n_at_once`: with N+1 rounds kicked, N are in flight, one waits and is counted, all N+1 finish, and the peak is N.

FSD `CIRIS_EDGE_TRANSPORT.md` gains §4.5 and invariant 10, both with the arithmetic.

## Gates
`cargo fmt`, `cargo check --all-targets` and `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on `transport-http,transport-reticulum,pyo3,lxmf,mesh-harness,test-anchor`. `--lib replication::` passes 431 tests. Run on their own: `kick_three_peers_740`, `first_contact_ladder_659`, `owned_devices_route_682`, `link_plane_728`, `route_table_e2e`, `reticulum_loopback`, `blob_federation_e2e`, `observability_metrics`, plus the lib `inbound_ingest_tests` and `runtime_budget`. All pass.

author: sultanalrashidi
body:
Fixes for the problems we hit while screen-recording the site for the launch promo, plus the promo video itself under `marketing/promo-video/`.

## Site fixes

- **Send queue opened the wrong guest's chat.** Tapping «أرسل عبر واتساب» marked the current guest as sent but opened WhatsApp for the *next* guest (their number and personal link), because the card advanced before the browser followed the link. The local note is still written on tap; the card now advances a task later. A second tap within a second anywhere on the card is ignored, so a double tap can't act on the next guest.
- **«بانتظار الرد» counted unsent guests.** Pending now means sent, not blocked and not answered, so the replies card adds up to «X دعوة مرسلة». The «ما ردّن» chip and row badges follow the same rule. A guest who answered without a recorded send (forwarded link, or admitted at the door by name) is no longer counted as both sent and unsent.
- **RSVP submit button cut off on iPhones.** On phones ≤430px, choosing «سأحضر» pushed «إرسال التأكيد» into a hidden inner scroller. For guests the RSVP box now grows from its authored top edge (upward only once it reaches the stage bottom), so the button stays visible from 360 to 1280px wide. The editor is unchanged.
- **Link preview was English-first.** The WhatsApp description and image now use the Arabic names in the host's couple format and the Hijri/Gregorian date the invitation prints. If the font can't load, the image falls back to a bare frame instead of failing.
- **Names:** «فيصل و نورة» → «فيصل ونورة» for new events. Names starting with «أم / أبو» no longer break across lines («أم / عبدالله»); they're bound with a no-break space at render time only.
- **Copy:** Updated text that no longer matched the product:
  - wedding-only;
  - each guest gets their own link;
  - the door scanner admits a whole party with one scan;
  - the PIN is 4–8 digits;
  - gender-neutral reply badges;
  - «عدد الحضور» column.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - Arabic-Indic digits on the event page and events list.
  - The page background keeps one element across the envelope opening, so the art isn't lost for a frame.
  - A pass with its own full-stage card shows on the theme's plain colour instead of over the page art.
  - The door scanner holds its last frame with a «جارٍ التحقق…» overlay while a code is checked, and restarts after a failed entry.

No schema changes and no migrations. Existing events keep their stored name until their form is saved again.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` on every changed file, and `tsx --test scripts/*.test.ts` (200 pass, 1 skipped). `next build` succeeds.
- Checked in Chromium against a local copy with demo data:
  - The send queue opens the tapped guest's chat on consecutive taps, undo and double taps.
  - Dashboard sums checked with sent, unsent, blocked and door-admitted guests.
  - RSVP form checked at 8 viewport sizes.
  - OG image checked with and without the font.
  - Full smoke pass in `/ar` and `/en`.
- An independent review pass found one blocking issue (the OG font fallback); it is fixed in the last commit.

Not verified in this environment: the door scanner's new overlay (no camera was available in the final headless run) and behaviour on real iOS devices.

## Not in this PR (theme data, change in the builder)

The jasmine design's welcome line touching the roses, and the small seat count on its pass, come from the theme's layout data, not code.

author: emscape
body:
## Summary
Chunk 1 of 3 for the shopping cart: server-side changes that multi-item checkouts need. Functions only; no site changes.

- **Webhook records every line item.** `listLineItems` was called without a limit, so Stripe returned only its default 10 per page and any further items never reached the Firestore order or the confirmation email. It now requests 100, the maximum a Checkout Session can hold.
- **Per-category quantity limits** in `lib/pricing.js`: plant up to 20; pottery and "other" up to 1 (one-of-a-kind pieces). A missing or unknown category counts as pottery, matching the shop pages.
- **`validateItemList`** rejects more than 50 distinct products and a sku listed twice (which would let each copy pass the per-product limit). `createCheckoutSession` runs it before reading any product from Firestore.

The existing shop-card quick order always sends a single item with qty 1, which every category allows, so it's unaffected.

## Testing
- `firebase/functions` vitest: 239/239 pass, 99% statement coverage.
- New tests: 12-item order fully recorded; per-category limits (plant 20, pottery/other/uncategorised 1); duplicate sku rejected, both in pricing and at the function boundary without any Firestore read.

## Next chunks
2. `feature/cart`: client-side cart, working Add to Cart on product pages and shop cards, header count.
3. `feature/cart-page`: `/cart` page and multi-item checkout.
4. Calculated shipping at checkout (separate follow-up).

**Trello:** https://trello.com/c/w3rR0BF7


## Updates since review
- **8812e16**: a non-string category (e.g. `['plant']`) now counts as pottery (limit 1). `Object.hasOwn` coerced it before (Copilot finding).
- **6774fb7**: **Stripe Checkout collects the shopper's details.** `createCheckoutSession` reads only `items`, turns on Stripe's phone number collection (required) and an optional "Special requests" text field, and no longer sets `customer_email`/`metadata`. `sessionToOrderData` takes name, phone and notes from what Stripe collected, still preferring metadata for sessions created before this change. The Astro `/api/checkout` validation no longer requires a customer. Today's quick-order pop-up keeps working after this merges (its typed details are ignored and Stripe asks for them); #57 removes the pop-up.
- **5be5d94**: the Special requests field's `maximum_length` is 255, Stripe's maximum. 500 was rejected with `parameter_invalid_integer`.
- **Verified** with a local Stripe test-mode checkout against the Firestore and Functions emulators: the session is created and returns a `checkout.stripe.com` url.

**Merge before #57**, which is stacked on this branch.

author: bunsdev
body:
## Context

- Summary: Follow-up to #1163's recorded nit. `legacy.import.v1` inserted each definition through `insert_definition`, which stamps `created_at` and `updated_at` with the wall clock (`now_iso()`), and the `definition.imported` event copied that stamp. The adoption's `adopted_at` never reached the row or the event, unlike every other adopted definition command.
- Files changed: `automations/import_legacy.rs`, `automations/store.rs`, `automations/command_adoption.rs`, `docs/architecture/coven-automations-v1.md`
- Closes #: none. This is part of #1054.

## Implementation

- Approach: `import_codex_as_draft` now takes `adopted_at`. For each definition it runs `monotonic_definition_timestamp` against that id, as the other adopted commands do, and inserts through a new `store::insert_definition_at(conn, definition, at)`. `insert_definition` is now a thin wrapper that passes `now_iso()`, so its many test and legacy callers are unchanged.
- User-visible behavior: an imported draft's `createdAt`/`updatedAt` and its `definition.imported` event's `recordedAt`/`observedAt` equal the adoption's `adoptedAt` rather than the wall clock at import time.
- Compatibility notes: the unversioned `coven.automations.import` path (`import_legacy_codex_automations`) still stamps the wall clock; it has no adoption timestamp. Replay behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --locked` (3596 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored)
- [x] `python3 scripts/check-secrets.py`
- [x] `python3 scripts/check-coven-privacy.py --staged`
- [x] Additional manual checks:
  - `v1_import_lands_in_draft_and_dry_run_writes_nothing` now asserts the row's `created_at`/`updated_at` and the event's `recorded_at`/`observed_at` (columns and JSON body) equal the adopted timestamp.
  - Mutation check: with the wall-clock insert restored, that test fails at the new `created_at` assertion (`2026-09-30T02:07:35.817Z` vs `2026-09-28T09:00:00.000Z`); it passes with the fix.
  - Local Policy guard: every step passes except `conformance/automations/runner/audit.test.mjs`, which fails identically on a pristine `origin/main` (`6add05a2`) checkout in the same environment: the test helper sets `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=""` and local Homebrew Cargo 1.98.1 rejects it with `error: target was empty`. CI's stable toolchain passed Policy guard on that base commit. Not related to this diff.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk level: Low. Only the timestamp written by the v1 import changes; the rows, events, and report shape are the same.
- Rollback plan: Revert.

## Agent Handoff

- Current state: The fix is in place on top of `6add05a2`.
- Follow-ups: Within one import run, a duplicate source id is still reported as `already exists` even though that id isn't in the store (also noted in #1163). The audit test's empty `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` may need a look against newer Cargo.
- Known gaps: No caller authority check, the same as every definition mutation (#857).

author: pullely
body:
RB3: opt-in rate benchmarks. The one cross-tenant surface in Rateboard, built to epic design §6 as a security design.

**What lands**
- Migration `220_bench_core`: `bench_contributions` (per-org consent, revocable; re-opting in is a new consent), `bench_runs` (operator totals, never served), `bench_cells` (**exactly the §6.5 fields**: key, `flat`/`cpm` p25/p50/p75, contributor band, snapshot) and `bench_cell_contributors` (private, read by no route; members are SHA-256 pseudonyms, never org ids).
- `packages/db/src/bench`: `readContributedBookings` — **the only function in the codebase that reads `deal_bookings` without an `orgId`**; one statement, joined to `bench_contributions WHERE revoked_at IS NULL`, reading only format, niche, audience, price, currency (USD, not `other`, audience > 0). Plus the consent writes, the snapshot writes (≤ 99 bound params per statement for D1) and `readOrgAdmins` (owners/admins from the membership tables).
- `apps/bench-worker` (dependsOn db-migrate, membership-worker, policy-worker; `workers_dev: false`):
  - `GET|PUT|DELETE …/benchmark-contribution` — `bench.contribute` (owner, admin); builder/viewer/non-member 404.
  - `GET …/benchmarks/cells`, `GET …/benchmarks?niche=&band=&format=` — `bench.read` AND a live contribution (else 404); all three exact keys or 422; `{ "published": false }` byte-identical for 0 and k − 1.
  - `scheduled()`: per org eligibility (opted in ≥ 30 days, ≥ 3 qualifying bookings) → orgs sharing an owner or admin merged (usr_/UUID normalised, trap 39) → per contributor one median per metric → 525 disjoint cells → publish only with **k = 5** → p25/p50/p75 by linear interpolation, **rounded to 2 s.f.**, band `5–9`/`10–24`/`25+` → **withheld if the member set differs from ANY published version of the cell by exactly one org**. Writes the snapshot, then marks the run done; a failed run leaves the previous snapshot serving.
- Policy: `bench.contribute` (owner, admin), `bench.read` (owner, admin, builder, viewer). api-edge: `bench` facade, `BENCH_WORKER` binding, `bench` rate-limit family. Contracts `bench.ts`, SDK `client.bench`. Console: Benchmarks page (consent switch with the exact shared-field list, published cells, exact-key lookup) + nav.
- **Stage-only override (departure):** stage vars `BENCH_MIN_OPTIN_DAYS=0` and cron `*/5 * * * *`, so stage can reach k = 5 eligible contributors today and show a publish then a withhold. **Prod: vars `ENVIRONMENT` only, cron `0 4 * * 1`, and the code ignores the override whenever `ENVIRONMENT` is `prod`** (test-pinned against the wrangler template).
- Docs: RB2 marked ✅ (README, plan, status) with its deploy and stage evidence; RB3 departures recorded (history of published member sets instead of last-only — the §6.7 property test requires it; pseudonyms kept on revocation — deleting them would reopen the differencing attack; ISO-week snapshot labels with `.n` for extra runs; consent on the Benchmarks page).
- Trap 17: policy-engine, db and contracts change → redeploy markers on all 14 other workers.
- Also: the inventory slot order was `created_at, id` (random within one millisecond — an RB1 test flaked on it); now `created_at, rowid`.

**The eight §6.7 tests (tests/bench-worker, real node:sqlite) — all green**
1. Threshold: k pinned at 5; 4 contributors → `{"published":false}`, byte-identical to an empty cell; 5 → published, band `5–9`.
2. No rows: `PRAGMA table_info(bench_cells)` is exactly the §6.5 columns; a published response has exactly the §6.5 keys and no org id, count, min, max or mean.
3. Dominance: one org with 50 bookings at $10,000 + four at ~$500 → p75 within 5% of $500 (median $510).
4. Query differencing: every booking of a random 2,000 maps to exactly one of the 525 keys; published cells of a 3,000-booking dataset are pairwise disjoint; 9 malformed queries (missing key, `*`, `all`, `other`, duplicate key, extra `rollup`) → 422.
5. Snapshot differencing + revocation: 6 publish; one revokes via the route; `readContributedBookings` returns none of its rows; the next run's input excludes it and withholds (`change_by_one`); a second org's change republishes. Property test: 25 random trials × 40 join/revoke steps — no two published versions of the cell differ by exactly one org.

author: loosep
body:
## 背景：把翻译从「圈记之后」挪到「划词那一刻」

第一版把翻译入口挂在「圈记 → 句尾小标号 → 相关词汇面板」之后。实测反馈是**这里根本到不了** —— 用户的 `l3_contexts` 当时只有 1 行圈记，「圈记 → 复习」那条链路他根本不用。把功能建在一条不走的通路上，是判断失误，不是用法问题。

于是拆成两条路径，各管各的：

| | 落库路径 | 无状态路径（本 PR 重点） |
|---|---|---|
| 端点 | `POST /l3/contexts/:id/translate` | `POST /l3/translate-text` |
| 前提 | 语境必须存在 | **给什么翻什么** |
| 存储 | `l3_contexts.translation` | 浏览器 localStorage |
| 适合 | 「这句我要留着」 | 「扫一眼，读完就走」 |

无状态路径刻意**不落库**：划词选中的句子多半不是任何一篇文章里的固定语境，落库会造出一批没有 `occurrence` 的 `l3_contexts` 行，污染按语境做的读模型。缓存放 localStorage —— 免费端点随时可能消失，完全不缓存又会让「重读同一段」反复打它。

## 交互

监听器挂在 `App` 根（`BrowserSessionGate` 之内、Routes 之外），一次覆盖全部页面。挂在任何单页都会在另外几页「划了没反应」。

划词后 350ms 去抖自动翻译，不等按钮 —— 用户要的是「一扫一读」，多一次点击这条路径就断了。重复文本命中缓存不打网络。

**扩句是质量关键**：单词丢给翻译端点多半译不出人话（`abandon` 的义项取决于句子），所以选区会先扩到所在句子再翻。浮层同时显示「你选中的」和「扩出来的」两段，避免困惑。

## 翻译源

免费非官方端点，链式降级：Google 网页翻译端点（Chrome 同款，无 key）→ MyMemory（匿名 5000 字符/天）。

**它们无 SLA、随时可能消失，上云会因 IP 被拒** —— 我早先说过「免费无限」，那是夸大，已收回。整套设计的前提就是「端点会死」，所以：缓存即价值、降级不报错、降级不毁缓存。provider 可插拔（`src/translation/`），将来换有 key 的只改组合根。

真机实测里 Google 端点失败过若干次、由 MyMemory 顶上 —— 降级链不是理论兜底。

## 过程中修掉的 4 个真 bug

都靠真机截图 / 实测暴露，不是单测能覆盖的：

1. **RLS 身份丢失** — `translateContext` 走 `txRunner` 而非 `withActorRepository`，`auth.uid()` 拿不到，owner-RLS 把用户自己的行也过滤掉。表现为「刚 quick-context 建的 context 立刻 translate 却报 NotFound」。纯 mock 测不出（mock 不带 RLS），已加回归锁断言事务带上 `actorId`。
2. **半句选区不扩句** — 规则是「选区 < 12 字才扩句」，用户选整句后半截（34 字）于是不扩，译文成了「但异常水平是一个问题」，「但」悬空。正确判据不是长度而是**有没有对齐句子边界**。
3. **缓存淘汰删错条目** — 注释写「localStorage 保序插入 → 最早的就是最久没写的」，紧接着 `keys.sort()`；键是哈希，排序等于随机顺序。改为在值里存自增序号，不依赖任何存储实现的迭代顺序保证。
4. **浮层跑到屏幕外** — 「优先下方 / 否则翻上方」在选区位于视口外时算出的两个位置都在屏幕外，浮层渲染了但用户看不见。已加无条件视口夹取 + 12 条定位测试。

另外**撤掉页脚裸露的 provider id**（`google-web` / `mymemory`）：有用户看到裸 `mymemory` 以为「请求发到别处去了」—— provider 是上游翻译源，跟请求打到哪个端点无关，裸 id 长得就像个地址。诊断信息归日志。

## 验证

- tsc（node + frontend）：**0 错误**。顺带首次全绿 —— 被删的 `tmp-seed-2025.ts`（缺 `actor`）是长期红灯的唯一来源。
- 全量：**4703 passed / 4 failed**。4 个失败全是 `not a git repository`（本地容器无 git 二进制），与本 PR 前的基线同源，CI 有 git。
- `db:schema:drift`：OK
- 契约门禁：`openapi-contract` / `authorization-registry` / `l3-response-contract` / `generate-openapi-client` 全过（新增两个 operation 都要求显式登记 auth/CSRF 与 owner 写面清单，门禁正确地拦了两次）
- 真机：划词→扩句→译文→缓存命中→关闭全通；输入框内划词正确不触发；浮层始终在视口内

**验证口径**：以上都是在**提交后的树**（`git archive HEAD`）上跑的，不是工作区。

## 已知限制

- 目标语言固定中文。API 支持 `targetLang`，UI 没有选择器。
- `jsdom` 下 `Range.getBoundingClientRect` 不存在，已降级而非抛错；位置相关断言留给真机。
- 无状态路径**不记 `userId` 到任何地方** —— 它无状态，这是有意的（`userId` 只用于鉴权与日志）。

## 顺带

`chore(git)` 那个提交补了 `.gitignore`（`scripts/tmp-*` / `coverage_bak*`）。清理掉的 7 个文件里 `tmp-local-db-setup.ps1` 含 7 个明文数据库密码，且从未被忽略 —— 一次 `git add .` 就会泄露。2025 考研的 6 篇文章（177,224 字正文）从未进库，已备份到 `%TEMP%\opencode\exam2025-data-20260930\` 再从工作区移除；**那批数据要正式纳管的话值得单独做一件事**。

author: scbrown
body:
## Scope

Two hardware-backed **verdict signature schemes** beside the existing raw ed25519, so a human can sign a quipu verdict with a passkey or a FIDO security key whose private key never leaves the device. All of them sign the unchanged v1 canonical message `v1|predicate|target|outcome|evidenceHash|tier|verifier`.

| scheme tag | device | algorithm |
|---|---|---|
| `ed25519` (default) | host key | unchanged v1 path |
| `webauthn-es256` | passkey / platform authenticator | ECDSA P-256 + SHA-256 (COSE -7) |
| `webauthn-eddsa` | security key | Ed25519 (COSE -8) |
| `sshsig-sk-ed25519` | `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n quipu-verdict` with a FIDO key | `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com` |

**Scheme binding.** A `VerifierRegistration` declares `aegis:signatureScheme` (absent means `ed25519`). `quipu_verdict_verify` takes an optional `scheme`. A hardware verdict verifies only against registrations that declare the same scheme, and it is `trusted` only when *that same registration* attests the predicate. The v1 key lookup now skips registrations that declare a non-ed25519 scheme, so a passkey registered under the same verifier name cannot shadow its ed25519 key. A store with no scheme facts gets byte-identical answers, and the existing ed25519 tests pass unchanged. A mutation test showed this filter is load-bearing: without it, the coexistence test fails.

## Verification rules

**WebAuthn** (every rule refuses on failure):
1. `clientDataJSON.type == "webauthn.get"`.
2. `challenge` (base64url) equals `SHA-256("quipu-verdict-webauthn-v1\0" || message)`. Quipu derives this value. A challenge supplied by the caller is never taken as truth.
3. `origin` is exactly the registration's `aegis:webauthnOrigin`, and `crossOrigin` is not true.
4. `authenticatorData` is at least 37 bytes, and `rpIdHash == SHA-256(aegis:webauthnRpId)`.
5. Both the UP and UV flags are set.
6. The signature verifies over `authenticatorData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON)` under the registered COSE key (base64url in `aegis:publicKey`). The key's `alg` is required and must match the scheme. A strict COSE parser refuses indefinite lengths, duplicate labels, trailing bytes and unsupported key types.
7. Counter check (below).

**SSHSIG sk-ed25519** (`PROTOCOL.sshsig` + `PROTOCOL.u2f`):
1. The armor and envelope parse exactly: magic, version 1, no trailing bytes.
2. `namespace == "quipu-verdict"`.
3. The hash is `sha256` or `sha512`.
4. The embedded public key blob is byte-identical to the registered OpenSSH key line.
5. The signature type matches the key type.
6. The ed25519 signature verifies over `SHA256(application) || flags || uint32 counter || SHA256(signed-data)`.
7. The user-presence flag (0x01) is set. UV is reported.
8. Counter check.

A plain `ssh-ed25519` SSHSIG parses and verifies at the envelope level, but it is refused as a hardware verdict.

**Counter policy (clone detection), per WebAuthn Level 3 §7.2:** once a nonzero `aegis:signCount` has been recorded (the maximum over the registration), a signature whose counter does not exceed it is refused, **including a presented 0**. Accepting 0 would tell the recorder to store 0, which would switch clone detection off for that credential. Only when both counters are 0 (an authenticator that does not count, such as a synced passkey from its first use) is the signature accepted without an advance. Verification stays **read-only**: `sign_count` is returned, and whatever records the verdict must persist it.

**Registration hygiene:** a hardware registration with more than one `publicKey`, `webauthnRpId` or `webauthnOrigin` is refused as ambiguous. Scanning continues past a registration that verifies but does not authorize, so the order in which keys were enrolled cannot decide the result. User verification is required for WebAuthn; for SSHSIG it is only reported, because it depends on the key having been created with `verify-required`.

## Safety gate: `[quipu.governance] hardware_verdict_schemes`, default `false`

`VerifierRegistration` is still graph-writable until S3 lands, which will restrict registry amendments to an enrolled human key. Enabling these schemes adds no forgery path beyond today's, because the same writer could register an ed25519 key. But a verdict labelled hardware-backed invites more trust than the registry can currently justify, so turning them on must be a deliberate operator act. While the gate is off:
- `quipu_verdict_verify` with a hardware `scheme` returns an error that names the config key.
- A write that asserts a non-ed25519 `aegis:signatureScheme` is refused at the write gate (refusal label `signature-scheme`).

Unknown scheme tags are always refused, whether the gate is on or off.

## Tests (all passing)

- **WebAuthn unit, 17:** the counter test now has one arm per case: 0/0 accept, 0/7 accept, 9/0 refuse, 9/7 refuse, 9/9 refuse, 9/10 accept. a software authenticator (ring P-256 and Ed25519) produces spec-shaped assertions. Accepted: ES256, EdDSA, and an advancing or zero counter. Refused: wrong challenge; a different verdict message; a raw caller-chosen challenge (re-signed so that only the challenge differs); wrong origin; crossOrigin; wrong rpIdHash; UP=0; UV=0; type `webauthn.create`; tampered clientDataJSON; tampered authenticatorData (counter byte) and truncation; signature by a different key (ES256 and EdDSA); counter equal to and below the recorded value; a scheme/COSE-alg mismatch; COSE trailing bytes, indefinite length, truncation, missing alg, duplicate label, and an RSA key.
- **SSHSIG unit, 14 (the counter arm now also refuses a presented 0 after a recorded 5):** (a) **real OpenSSH 10.2 output** (plain ed25519, `ssh-keygen -Y sign`, cross-checked with `ssh-keygen -Y verify`) is accepted at the envelope level. Refused: wrong namespace, tampered message, not a hardware key, armor/magic/trailing damage. (b) **sk-ed25519** built in-test over the exact u2f digest layout is accepted, and UV is reported. Refused: wrong namespace; no UP; flags forged after signing; tampered message; a different signer's key; an envelope that claims the registered key but was signed by another; counter regression; sha1; a key line whose type is inconsistent with its blob.
- **End-to-end through `quipu_verdict_verify` and the write gate, 12:** an ambiguous registration (two origins) is refused; an unauthorized enrolment of the same key does not mask an authorizing one (confirmed with a mutation test). the gate defaults to off; hardware registrations are refused while it is off and land when it is on; an unknown scheme is refused with the gate on; WebAuthn (both algorithms) is refused while off and trusted while on, and a tampered outcome is untrusted; SSHSIG sk is trusted, and a wrong namespace is untrusted; a verdict cannot pick a scheme its registration does not declare; a predicate grant cannot be borrowed from another registration; a recorded `signCount` refuses a stale counter; missing WebAuthn parts are an error; ed25519 verdicts are unaffected by a hardware registration under the same verifier, with the gate on or off.
- Existing: `test_signed_verdict_end_to_end_root_of_trust`, `signing::tests`, and all transition-signature tests are unchanged and passing. The full default suite passes (1773 lib tests), as does the quipu-server binary suite, including `every_pooled_tool_survives_a_read_only_connection` and the input-field schema audits.
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean. Clippy `-D warnings` is clean for `--features shacl`, `--no-default-features` and `--features full`. The wasm32 `cargo check` passes.

## Dependencies

- `base64 = "0.22"` is now a direct dependency. It was **already in Cargo.lock** transitively, so it adds no new supply chain. It handles base64url for WebAuthn and standard base64 for the SSHSIG armor.
- All cryptography uses `ring`, which was already a dependency: ECDSA P-256 ASN.1 verify, Ed25519, and SHA-256/512. No p256, CBOR or ssh-key crates were added. COSE_Key parsing is a small, strict, purpose-built read

author: agent-bureau-bot-3[bot]
body:
A fix run no longer loses finished edits by ending its turn while a test suite runs in the background. The Fix step now turns off Claude Code's background tasks. Its prompt tells the agent to push before any long check and never to run the whole suite locally. The engineer brief no longer promises a fix run a post-run delivery that nothing performs.

Card: https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-5271/bureau-pipeline-a-fix-agent-ends-its-run-while-a-test-suite-it-started

## The runs, and the rule each one broke

| Run | PR | Final words | Rule it broke |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 36637466321 | bureau-pipeline #564 | "Full serial suite still running (~17 min). I'll commit and push once it reports." | no full suite locally · push before long checks · never end a turn on a background task |
| 36654315141 | bureau-pipeline #571 | "Waiting for the full suite to finish before I update the PR body and push." (after `Command did not complete within its 600s timeout and was moved to the background`) | no full suite locally · push before long checks · never end a turn on a background task |
| 36648432869 | portico #790 | "The infra suite is still running in the background. I'll push once it reports." | push before long checks · never end a turn on a background task. A record-only document needed no suite at all |
| 36653891976 | portico #790 | "Tests are still running; I'll wait for the notification." | never end a turn on a background task |
| 36636092095 | bureau-pipeline #568 | "The full suite is still running. I'll finish the gate when it reports." | no full suite locally · never end a turn on a background task |
| 36629912273 | bureau-pipeline #566 | same ending | never end a turn on a background task |
| 36302880123, 36328431916, 36337385573 (bureau-pipeline), 36297449104 (agent-bureau) | Claude Code 2.1.282, 09-26 to 09-28 | same ending | never end a turn on a background task. This shows the problem predates the 2.1.284 bump |
| 36640595665 | bureau-pipeline #569 | waited about 40 minutes for two full suites, then got HTTP 401 on push and said "the workflow mints a fresh token and delivers a committed branch after the agent ends" | no full suite locally · push before long checks. It trusted a brief sentence that is only true for agent-task.yml |

The runs that pushed (36644875326 on #568 and 36626531084 on #558) either waited in the foreground or pushed first. The new rules require exactly that.

## What changed

- **Fix step setting.** `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS: "1"`. I checked it two ways. Anthropic documents it at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars ("disable all background task functionality, including the `run_in_background` parameter on Bash and subagent tools, auto-backgrounding, and the Ctrl+B shortcut"). The Claude Code 2.1.284 binary the install step proves also reads it: its Bash tool sets `canAutoBackground` false whenever the variable is set. The comment beside the step records both sources.
- **Per-command limit left alone, on purpose.** `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` exists on the same page. A longer foreground wait only brings the agent closer to the 60-minute token expiry, which a fix run cannot yet survive (DRE-4911). The comment says so.
- **Fix prompt, step 4.** The unbounded "run the local checks until green" now says: do not run the whole suite locally, because CI runs it on the push. Run only the test files the change touches, each under a timeout. Commit and push before any check that runs longer than a few minutes. Never end your turn while a background task is still running. A finished edit with no push is the one outcome that loses the work. The body-before-push order from DRE-3011 is unchanged: step 4b still comes before the push.
- **Engineer brief.** The delivery sentence now names agent-task.yml. It also says plainly that agent-fix.yml has no delivery step yet (DRE-4911), so a fixing agent must push itself.

## Proof

- `tests/test_fix_run_no_background_wait.py`: 16 tests. They run against the parsed workflow prompt and the brief's sentences:
  - Each of the three rules is pinned, along with its reason, and must sit inside step 4.
  - The env setting and its cited comment are pinned.
  - The brief check finds every workflow a delivery sentence names and fails when one has no `push_rescue.py` step. It also fails when a delivery sentence names no workflow at all.
- RED first: 12 of 16 failed on `main` (commit 8fe410e). All 16 pass now.
- Mutation checks run this session: making the brief promise delivery for agent-fix.yml fails `test_no_delivery_sentence_names_a_workflow_without_a_delivery_step`, and renaming the env key fails `test_the_fix_step_disables_background_tasks`.
- The 109 test files that read agent-fix.yml or the briefs: 3,416 passed, 1,012 subtests passed, in 4 minutes, foreground. Following this card's own rule, I did not run the full 12,918-test suite locally. CI runs it on this push.
- Every other check `tests.yml` runs (YAML parse, pipeline_ref, action pins, WIP cap, reconcile env, watchers, death receipts, workflow prompts, act registry and receipts) exits 0. `check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD` exits 0.

## Rollout and do-not-touch

There is nothing for the operator to deploy. This takes effect for agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline, which ride `@main`, when it merges. The rest of the fleet gets it at the next `vN` cut.

Do not touch: this PR does not change any token mint, the Report step, or the push path. **DRE-4911 shares agent-fix.yml** and will add the post-Fix delivery step. When it lands, the brief test lets the delivery sentence name agent-fix.yml, and the "has no delivery step" warning test skips itself.

body:
## Summary

F5 and F6 from the OpenID Federation 1.0 Final review.

**F6: `kid`.** §3.2 step 11: an Entity Statement's header `kid` "MUST be a non-zero length string and MUST exactly match the kid value for a key" of its issuer. §3.1.1: "Every JWK in the JWK Set MUST have a unique kid". Before this change, a statement without a `kid` was verified against **every** key of the right algorithm, and missing or duplicate key IDs in `jwks` were accepted.

**F5: `crit`.** §3.1.1 and §3.2 step 13: each claim a statement's `crit` claim names "MUST be understood and be able to be processed". We handled the JOSE *header* `crit` but ignored this *claim*, so a statement demanding an extension we don't implement was accepted.

**Now** (`internal/federation`):
- `Parse` rejects: no header `kid` (`ErrMissingKeyID`); a `jwks` key with no `kid`, or two sharing one (`ErrMalformedJWKS`); any `crit` claim, or a malformed one (`ErrUnsupportedCriticalClaim`), since this package implements no extension claims. An extension claim nobody marked critical is still ignored.
- The resolver selects the verification key by exact `kid`.
- `Create` refuses to issue what `Parse` would reject: an empty `KeyID`, or `jwks` with missing or duplicate key IDs. Our issuers already set both.

**BREAKING** (`fix!`; UPGRADING.md v0.41.0 section): federation members publishing such statements no longer resolve. The OIDF suite signs its statements with `kid` (`AbstractSignJWT`: `builder.keyID(signingJwk.getKeyID())`). I've dispatched a conformance run on this branch to confirm.

## Test plan

- [x] `Parse`: no header `kid` rejected, `kid` accepted; a `jwks` key without a `kid` and duplicate key IDs rejected; `crit` naming a claim, non-array or empty rejected; a non-critical extension claim still accepted
- [x] `Create`: an empty `KeyID` and duplicate `jwks` key IDs are refused
- [x] `Resolve` end to end: an Entity Configuration without `kid` is rejected
- [x] Mutation-checked: removing each check (header `kid`, `jwks` `kid`, duplicates, `crit`, and both `Create` guards) fails a test
- [x] `go test -race ./...` (internal test fixtures updated to sign with a `kid`), demo, `golangci-lint`
- [ ] Conformance workflow on this branch

body:
Terraform/OpenTofu provider for AT Protocol records, built on the Terraform Plugin Framework.
It is the source the Crossplane (Upjet) and Pulumi providers will be generated from.

## Resources

- Record-only: `atproto_tangled_follow`, `atproto_tangled_knot`, `atproto_tangled_profile`, `atproto_tangled_public_key`. Updates merge into the stored record, so fields the provider doesn't manage (such as the profile avatar) survive.
- `atproto_tangled_repository` creates the repo on the knot with `sh.tangled.repo.create` (which mints the repo DID), then writes the `sh.tangled.repo` record. Destroying it deletes the repo from the knot.
- `atproto_tangled_knot_member` and `atproto_tangled_repository_collaborator` call the knot's ACL methods and write no record, matching the appview on knots with the `knot-acl` capability. Other knots are refused.
- `atproto_record` manages a record in any collection, with its body as a JSON string.
- Data sources `atproto_identity` and `atproto_account`.

Knot calls use a service-auth token from `com.atproto.server.getServiceAuth`, scoped to the knot's `did:web` and the method.

## Testing

Ginkgo specs run `terraform-plugin-testing` steps through OpenTofu 1.12.6 against a fake PDS and knot (`internal/provider/fake_test.go`): create, update, drift, import and destroy.
All 15 pass locally with Go 1.27.1, including under `-race`.
Nothing has run against a real PDS or knot yet.

`nix build`, `nix flake check` and golangci-lint were not run locally (no nix in the environment); this PR's CI is their first run.
`flake.lock` is copied from terraform-provider-netgear, whose nixpkgs pin has `go_1_27`.

## Not in this PR

- Registry release signing: needs the `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` and `PASSPHRASE` secrets, as in terraform-provider-netgear.
- Acceptance tests against a real account.

author: jsantoru
body:
This change makes scored tricks visible and extends skating into ROC City's streetscape.

All nine grinds use their correct truck/deck support, and all eight grabs use distinct body poses with board-relative palm contact and finger curl. Regular/switch, rotations, interrupted grabs, landing recovery and rail exits retain the existing scoring state. Switch now mirrors travel-relative truck support, front/rear limb roles, grabs, pushing and flips. Manuals load the correct wheels in both stances and smoothly change axles during a revert. Feeble uses down-left; Smith uses down-right.

Cars, fence tops, bench seat/back edges, curbs and river-wall coping now provide 51 additional grind segments. Cars have solid bodywork built from the same geometry as the visible meshes; connected car panels and fence corners sustain one grind. New street targets require Grind input within 65 cm, so nearby fences do not steal established park approaches. Ollie dismounts cannot be undone by automatically catching the same object; a fresh Grind press permits a deliberate regrind. Car-only body posing keeps the rider upright over steep window segments while board contact follows the surface.

Validation:
- Street physics: 18/18 checks, 32 real input routes, both directions/stances and both scales, plus 612 rendered-edge samples (maximum discrepancy 2.28 mm).
- Grind poses: 9 checks / 18,309 frames / 35,290 foot contacts, including both characters and every grind on all five car panels.
- Grab contact, 28 actual-input animation transition checks / 146 trajectories, footplant, scoring, touch, ROC geometry/progress, scale, fixtures and environment lifecycle checks pass.
- Production browser: car/fence/bench/curb approach → hold → exit → bank; final car pose, native touch and paced playback pass with zero browser errors.
- Switch regression: 224 actual input sequences and 9,136 immutable render frames; 23 production-browser checks including native touch, nose contacts, swapped diagonal inputs, grabs, pushing and paced manual reverts. Before/after images and a normal-speed clip accompany the reports.
- Existing warehouse, control timing and saved progress remain intact.

See TRICK-ANIMATION.md, STREET-GRINDS.md and SWITCH-STANCE.md for the pose/reference matrix, implementation details, reviewed screenshots and clips. Screenshots are also posted in this PR's conversation. Mobile checks are browser emulation, not physical-device performance measurements. The rig remains procedural; cars are parked props, and only useful upper edges are grind targets.

The branch includes an ancestry-only reconciliation of already deployed source after the previous squash merge; that merge changes no files.

author: haz4rdovisk
body:
Fixes #772

One of a series of timeline improvements.

## Merge order

Stacked on #774, which is rebased on current `main` (#773, #775 and #779 are in). This branch carries #774's two commits and adds two of its own (d285f95, and 0d4b48b for the review). Please merge #774 first; GitHub then shows only this PR's commits.

## Why

ChatGPT closes each round of work with a short recap in the past tense ("Inspected downloads and updated the test plan"), and titles the collapsed block with it. In the app, a group of calls was named after its latest call instead ("Ran 2 commands: Start-Sleep -Seconds 12; …"), with the recap repeated inside it under a globe, the same icon as a web search. In three recorded sessions the recap was the last item of its block in most rounds; when a block held several rounds, each had its own recap and the last one described the whole block.

## What changed

- A group that ends in ChatGPT's recap is titled with it, and the recap heads the group instead of repeating inside it. A group without one keeps its current name (its latest real action). When an observed phase precedes the group, that phase still names it, as before.
- The recap is picked by position, never by wording, so it holds in any language of the page: it is the native step that ends a finished round, that is, the last member of its group once prose follows it or the turn is over. A step that ends a round still in progress is a note, whatever it says, and leaves the group named after its latest call. No English pattern is read anymore (`NATIVE_SEARCH` is gone, and nothing here uses `NATIVE_STEP_NOW`).
- The icon follows position too. A native step written after this app's calls in its round is about that work and is marked done with `check-circle` (added to the icon vocabulary and the font's codepoint table), unless it ends a round still in progress. A step before any call, such as a web search between two paragraphs, keeps the globe.
- The live row is left exactly as #774 has it.

This reverses the rule "name the group after its latest real action, not after a thinking note", which was right for loose notes but not for the recap that closes a round. The test that encoded it is rewritten for the new rule, and its original case (a round that ends in a call is named after that call) is kept as its own test.

Known edge: a web search that happens to be the last step of a finished round, after this app's calls, is taken as that round's recap. Position cannot tell it from a recap, and nothing else language-independent is recorded.

## Test

`test/renderer-timeline.test.ts`:
- "titles a finished round with the native step that ends it, by position and in any language" (Spanish labels: the recap titles the group with a check and is not repeated inside; a step before the calls keeps the globe).
- "names a round still in progress after its latest real action, until prose ends it" (the same step is a note while the turn works, and the recap once prose follows).
- "names a finished round that ends in a call after that call, and keeps the globe on a step before its calls" (today's naming, kept).

The first two fail on #774's code; the third passes there too, as it pins the behavior that must not change. All renderer suites (25 files): 551 passed.

## Screenshots

Before (on #774) — the group is named after its last call, and the recap sits inside with a globe:

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Haz4rdovisk/chat-on-steroids-mainstream/c2bf4deca6014c4ca4bffa47ece13119bc169a11/recap-turn-before.png)

![before, open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Haz4rdovisk/chat-on-steroids-mainstream/c2bf4deca6014c4ca4bffa47ece13119bc169a11/recap-open-before.png)

After — the recap titles the group, with a check; the globe stays on the web search:

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Haz4rdovisk/chat-on-steroids-mainstream/c2bf4deca6014c4ca4bffa47ece13119bc169a11/recap-turn-after.png)

![after, open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Haz4rdovisk/chat-on-steroids-mainstream/c2bf4deca6014c4ca4bffa47ece13119bc169a11/recap-open-after.png)

## Checklist

- [ ] `npm run verify` passes on my machine (OS: Windows 11). Not run in full locally; CI runs `verify:ci` on Windows, macOS and Linux. The affected suites pass locally and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] For interface changes: `npm run verify:ui` was 33 of 37 on the first version of this branch (the other 4 fail the same way on `main` on this machine); not re-run after the review change, which only touches how the group is named.
- [x] The PR contains nothing unrelated beyond #774's commit, which it is stacked on (see Merge order).
- [x] Screenshots, logs and examples contain no real names, paths, chat text, IDs or credentials (fixture data only).

author: fidelodok
body:
> Stacked on #937 (FORGE-346). Retarget to `main` once that merges.

D4 is "CAD authoring through the Design IR (validated, named parts); **STEP /
URDF reference-design import**".

The first half was there: the IR lowers to CadQuery and FreeCAD, and STEP
import preserves the file's own part labels (MET-534/535/616). **URDF had
export only** — you could write one out of an assembly, and there was no way
to bring an existing arm in to design against.

`twin.import_urdf` reads one and records it through the *same* recorder as
`twin.commit_system_architecture`: links become components, joints become
interfaces. A URDF is a rigid-body graph, which is the shape the twin already
holds — no new representation that nothing else reads.

## Geometry does not come in, and says so

A URDF references meshes by path, usually `package://` URIs that resolve only
inside a ROS workspace this server does not have.

```json
{
  "robot_name": "two_link_arm", "component_count": 3, "interface_count": 2,
  "not_imported": [
    {"kind": "mesh", "name": "base_link/visual",
     "detail": "package://arm/meshes/base.stl -- geometry is referenced by path and was not resolved; the structure was imported without it"}
  ]
}
```

Importing the structure and naming what was left behind beats failing
outright, and beats a robot with no shape that reports success — the failure
mode this codebase keeps turning up.

## Reported rather than guessed

- **A joint type outside the URDF spec's own set.** Inventing a mapping would
  make it move wrongly in every downstream simulation.
- **A joint naming a link the file does not contain.**

## Refused rather than partly read

Malformed XML, a root that is not `<robot>`, and a file with no links. An
empty import reporting success is worse than an error.

## Verification

- `tests/unit/test_urdf_import.py` (15), including the tool driving the real
  architecture recorder rather than the parser in isolation
- `pytest tests/unit` — 8095 passed, 26 skipped
- The annotation coverage ratchet caught the new tool, which is what it is for
- `ruff`, `mypy` (227 files) clean
- `cd docs-site && npm run build && npm test` — 13/13

author: kroisse
body:
Implements #1177 and uses it to cut the CodSpeed job time.

In simulation mode, CodSpeed runs each benchmark's setup 7 times and the routine 6 times (`WARMUP_RUNS` is fixed at 5). Every setup recompiled its input from source, so a single measurement of `after_boundary_exit` compiled the program to the boundary exit about 7 times. The job took about 18.5 minutes after #1172: 3.7 to build and 14.7 to run.

These two commits were pushed to #1172 after it had been merged, so they are reopened here on top of current `main`.

## Changes

### `feat(trunk-ir): implement Clone for IrContext`

- Derive `Clone` on the arena data types (`OperationData`, `ValueData`, `BlockData`, `RegionData`) and on the intern tables. Cloning copies each table's hasher, so the copied index stays valid.
- Implement `Clone` for `IrContext` by hand so that **every clone gets a fresh identity**. Analyses are cached by `(identity, revision)`, and a clone diverges from its original at the same revision. `revision` is copied.
- Derive `Clone` on `FrontendCompilation`.
- Add a unit test. Changing a clone's use-chains and interning a new type in it leaves the original's printed IR and use-chains unchanged, and the two contexts have distinct identities.

### `perf(bench): clone prepared stage inputs` and `clone_with_headroom`

- Each program's shared middle-end output and boundary-exit IR are built once and cloned in every iteration's setup.
- The per-program skip checks now produce those prepared inputs, so the checks no longer compile the program a separate time.

### `ci(bench): run CodSpeed simulation and memory measurements in parallel`

- `simulation` and `memory` now run as separate matrix jobs (`fail-fast: false`) instead of back to back in one job. Each job builds on its own, and the run takes as long as the slower job.
- Only the simulation job saves the Rust cache on `main`, so the two jobs do not race on the same cache key.

### Timing (CodSpeed run step, 28 benchmarks, same pinned workflow)

| Setup | Simulation | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Recompile each input from source (`main` `8d94a1e9`) | 15.1 min | 39.3 min |
| `clone_with_headroom` (`0e6f1bdc`) | 11.2 min | 24.0 min |

Measured values are unchanged: on `0e6f1bdc`, CodSpeed left all 28 simulation benchmarks untouched against `main`.

### CodSpeed result on `9d643d2d` (vs `main` `8d94a1e`)

- Simulation: all 28 benchmarks unchanged.
- Memory: 8 regressions and 4 improvements, all artifacts of the cloned inputs rather than compiler changes:
  - The `after_boundary_exit` stages grew by +300–500 KB, most visible on the small programs (for example `wasm_dynamic_output/wasm`, 62 KB → 543 KB). The likely cause is `ListPool`: it cannot reserve capacity, so the value and type pools are cloned exactly, and the first list the routine allocates reallocates a whole pool of several hundred KB.
  - `to_boundary_exit` shrank by about 15%, not yet explained.
- The bias applies to every commit equally, so memory comparisons after this PR are consistent, but their absolute values differ from a from-source setup. The memory regressions are acknowledged as a change of measurement method.
- The two matrix jobs took 1.2 + 12.7 min (simulation) and 1.0 + 15.7 min (memory), so the whole workflow took about 17 minutes. CodSpeed merged both jobs into one report.

## Notes

- `Clone` gives each arena capacity equal to its length, so the measured routine's first insertions reallocated every arena. On an earlier revision of this PR, CodSpeed flagged this as a -10.95% regression on the smallest stage. The benchmark therefore uses `IrContext::clone_with_headroom`, which keeps the growth room that insertion would have left: primary maps get the next power of two of their length, and secondary maps keep the original capacity. `ListPool` has no way to reserve capacity, so the value and type pools are cloned as-is.

author: qigao
body:
Tracks #102 and #95.

This PR closes the typed composition gap between the now-reference-compatible
open-vocabulary relation runtime and the existing scene graph / temporal stack.

## Relation vocabulary version

`RelationFrame` now carries:

```cpp
std::uint64_t vocabulary_version;
```

Semantics:
- legacy baked `RelateAnything` emits version 1;
- `OpenVocabularyRelation` starts at 0 before any vocabulary is installed;
- every successful `set_vocabulary()` commits one new monotonically increasing
  positive version;
- failed vocabulary updates are transactional and keep the previous vocabulary,
  logits buffer and version unchanged.

The open-vocabulary version is exposed through
`OpenVocabularyRelation::vocabulary_version()`.

## Transactional vocabulary swap

`set_vocabulary()` now validates/allocates the entire candidate state before
committing it:
- normalized W;
- alpha contract;
- tensor byte limits;
- output byte limits;
- version exhaustion;
- predicate-logit buffer allocation.

This prevents a failed update from leaving text names/W/alpha out of sync with
the active runtime buffer.

## SceneGraphPipeline open-vocabulary support

`SceneGraphPipeline::create()` now has an overload for:

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<relation::OpenVocabularyRelation>
```

while preserving the legacy `RelateAnything` overload.

The implementation type-erases the two relation model variants behind an
internal runner so detector/tracker/region composition remains one code path.

Track IDs already flow:
```text
ByteTrack -> Region.track_id
          -> RelationEdge subject/object_track_id
          -> SceneGraphFrame
```

and the relation vocabulary version is preserved in the same frame.

## Temporal vocabulary semantics

`SceneBehaviorModel` can bind itself to a positive `vocabulary_version`.
Zero retains backward-compatible wildcard/legacy behavior.

When `SceneInteraction` receives a frame with a different positive version:
- all active pair states are cancelled with reason `VocabularyChanged`;
- pair state is cleared;
- that frame's predicate indices are NOT consumed;
- subsequent mismatched frames remain ignored;
- processing resumes only after the behavior model is configured for the new
  version.

This prevents old ESN input semantics from silently interpreting a reordered or
replaced predicate vocabulary.

## Tests

Scene graph:
- relation version preserved beside object table / track IDs.

Scene interaction:
- active behavior cancellation on vocabulary change;
- explicit `VocabularyChanged` event reason;
- mismatched frames ignored;
- pair state cleared;
- processing resumes after behavior model reconfiguration.

CI expected:
- Relation contract;
- Scene graph contract;
- Scene interaction contract.

This PR does not yet claim full #102 qualification: detector-box pair-recall
ceilings, ORT CPU pipeline evidence, performance breakdown, and GPU/TensorRT
end-to-end parity remain separate gates.

author: mwolson
body:
## What Changed

The executed WSL cache tests now mark a runtime busy, and hold an install lock, with helper processes that end when the test script ends. Each test waits until its holder is in place before it runs the install or prune script.

This is an alternative to #13907 (keep the fake WSL runtime visible), which fixes the same two failures by appending `:` to the fixture's `sh -c` command.

## Why

Two tests fail on hosts where `/bin/sh` is bash, such as Arch and Fedora: `removes an aged stale tree after replacing an active unready cache` and `prunes old and markerless caches without touching retained, active, locked, or unrelated roots`. The fixture ran `sh -c "sleep 30" <runtime>/t3`, and bash runs a lone `-c` command in place of the shell, so the process's command line becomes just `sleep 30`. The scripts detect a busy runtime by scanning `/proc/*/cmdline` for its path, so they treated the "active" cache as idle and removed it. Production is unaffected, since a real server keeps its path in its command line.

The holders now carry the runtime entry as their `argv[0]` and read a pipe the test script keeps open. The fixture no longer depends on how `sh` handles `-c`, nothing sleeps on a 30-second timer, and no holder outlives a test that fails partway. A bounded wait for each holder replaces the fixed `sleep 0.1`, so a slow runner cannot start the scripts before the holder exists. On Arch the file goes from 2 failed to 50 passed; with the in-use check deliberately broken four tests fail, and with the prune script ignoring install locks the prune test fails.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why
- [ ] I included before/after screenshots for any UI changes
- [ ] I included a video for animation/interaction changes

## identity: themeable sign-in pages and a shared fake-idp command (for identity/v0.4.0)

This is PR A of M5, Urth identity and login. It lets a second product brand the shared sign-in pages, and it gives any product the fake identity provider as a command.

### Theme tokens and product wording (`identity/pages`)
Until now the pages were Exp-Bench's in everything but the product name:
- **Colours.** The stylesheet hard-coded Exp-Bench's cyan, so `ThemeCSS` could only restyle by re-declaring selectors.
- **Wording.** The template carried Exp-Bench's copy: "Continuous experimentation", "Connect to your research.", "Configure projects. Inspect evidence…", "Join a research account", "agent tokens".

What changes:
- **Colours** become `@sre-norns/components` theme tokens, with the Exp-Bench theme's values as defaults. `ThemeCSS` is now simply a product theme's `:root` block.
  - Five colours with no kit token are named `--page-*`: glow, field outline, success, success container and error container.
  - The success mark gets its own token instead of borrowing `--secondary-fixed`, because the kit's Urth theme makes `secondary` critical red.
- **Wording** becomes `pages.Config.Copy`. Empty fields keep `pages.DefaultCopy`, which is the current wording. The device-approval result title follows the headline.
- **`httpapi.Config`** becomes an alias of `pages.Config`, so `Mount` carries every page setting. Existing keyed literals still compile.

### `identity/cmd/fake-idp`
The command moves here from `experibench/cmd/fake-idp`, so that Urth can `go run` it without depending on another product.
- It uses the standard `flag` package with `FAKE_IDP_*` environment fallbacks. The identity module has no kong dependency to take on for a development tool.
- It still refuses non-loopback addresses.
- Its Google issuer serves OpenID discovery, so it also works as the generic `oidc` issuer.

A follow-up can switch Exp-Bench to this command; nothing in its Makefile or docs refers to its own copy.

author: hwang2409
body:
Automations can now be triggered by inbound webhooks. Phase 1 is a loopback-only receiver owned by `zeta automation daemon`; public ingress (phase 2) and zeta registering its own webhook URLs (phase 3) come later.

- **Trigger schema:** `{"kind":"webhook","verify":"github"}` or `verify:"hmac-sha256"` with signature/prefix/optional timestamp headers. Unknown schemes/fields and model-authored paths/URLs are rejected. Drafts stay inert; the model can't read or set credentials.
- **Per-job credentials:** approval generates an independent random 32-byte secret and opaque route token per job (0600 store, 0700 dir); `zeta automation webhook url|show-secret|rotate-secret|rotate-url` (+ slash equivalents).
- **Receiver:** stdlib server on `127.0.0.1:8765` by default (non-loopback requires an explicit flag); routes only `/hooks/<token>` checked against current approved+enabled state per request; POST only (405 + Allow otherwise); strict framing; 1 MiB cap; constant-time HMAC before parsing; integer timestamps with 5-min tolerance; permanent delivery-id dedupe; per-job rate limit and pending count/byte caps; header/body read timeouts, bounded handler concurrency (503), and shutdown that waits for all handlers before closing the store.
- **Durability:** deliveries and runs share one SQLite state machine; each delivery is recorded before 202, runs the accepted revision exactly once, and is never replayed once started (with a migration separating webhook-run and scheduled-run uniqueness). Payloads are passed as delimited untrusted input and dropped after completion.
- Bash/zsh completions for the new surfaces.

- **Tipo do caso de teste** (seção 1.1 do documento de Casos de Teste): **funcional** quando o critério é uma regra verificada em um único ponto (uma tela ou uma requisição), com o estado montado como pré-condição; **End-to-End** quando o resultado esperado é a consequência de o incidente atravessar etapas do fluxo, e o caso percorre essas etapas.


A `main` recebeu o PR #26 (validação de requisitos e nova matriz) depois que a branch foi criada. Ela foi integrada por **merge** (sem reescrever o que já estava publicado), e as linhas da matriz foram refeitas no formato novo. Com o squash merge, o histórico final na `main` fica em um único commit.

## Summary

Both daemon platforms hardcoded the CloudSync HTTP `User-Agent` as `"FocusLock-Daemon/1.2.1"`, three major versions behind the current `1.5.0` in `ui/package.json`. 1. Both daemon literals now read `"FocusLock-Daemon/1.5.0"` and match each other.

author: washingtonmsdj
pannal
body:
Snoozing or dismissing a full-screen alert can make the ongoing phone notification disappear while the foreground service and sensor readings continue. On an Android 16 phone, system logs captured Android removing the ongoing notification when it dismantled an automatic notification group. The notification was posted again on the next reading, about 57 seconds later.

The phone builder assigns the status notification to `aa2` without posting a group summary. Android can fold that incomplete group into its automatic alerting group. This change leaves the phone notification ungrouped at the app level so Android can track it through its normal ungrouped-notification path. Wear keeps its existing group, and separate alert builders retain their existing behavior.

The captured cancellation sequence was:

- Alert `81432`: reason 8, `REASON_APP_CANCEL`.
- Automatic `Aggregate_AlertingSection` summary: reason 16, `REASON_UNAUTOBUNDLED`.
- Ongoing notification `81431`: cancellation requested by system UID 1000, reason 12, `REASON_GROUP_SUMMARY_CANCELED`.

[Android's removal-reason definitions](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/service/notification/NotificationListenerService#REASON_GROUP_SUMMARY_CANCELED) distinguish this from an app exit or notification timeout. The service dump still reported `isForeground=true`. The change does not alter snooze duration, alert acknowledgement, or activity closing.

Validation:

- Production-builder regression: one of three tests fails against the original code; all three pass with the fix. Covers phone grouping, retained Wear grouping, and separate alert builders.
- Local-build integration: all 3,504 mobile release tests pass, with zero failures, errors, or skips. ARM64 release assemble, lint and R8 completed.
- `git diff --check` passes.

The updated APK has not been tested on the phone yet. The system logs establish the removal mechanism; the builder regression does not reproduce Android's complete grouping implementation.

author: jaysheeldodia
body:
Fixes #752 

Models that use mean pooling have been returning `float64` embeddings, even though the ONNX model outputs `float32`. The values are correct, but the embeddings take twice the memory. `tobytes()` also writes the wrong byte size, and anything expecting `float32` rejects them.

**Why it happened**

`mean_pooling` multiplies the `float32` embeddings by the `int64` attention mask, and NumPy turns the result into `float64`. A final `.astype(np.float32)` used to hide this, but #492 removed it. Custom mean-pooling models from #479 had the same problem.

**The fix**

The result is now converted back to the model's output format in `PooledEmbedding`, `PooledNormalizedEmbedding` and `CustomTextEmbedding`. For custom models this only happens for float outputs, so integer outputs aren't cut off. The conversion comes after `normalize()`, because converting a `float16` result first can overflow the norm and turn the embedding into all zeros.

The values don't change. The new output is exactly the old output in `float32`, with no speed difference and half the memory.

**Tests**

- `test_embedding` and `test_mock_add_custom_models` now also check the output format.
- New `test_mean_pooling_keeps_model_dtype` checks the format and the values for both built-in mean-pooling classes, with `float32` and `float16` input.
- New `test_custom_mean_pooling_keeps_float16_without_overflow` checks that a `float16` custom model with large values still gets the right result.

body:
Follow-up split out of #5301 (owner ruling 09-29). The earlier attempt is saved on `wip/secure-prepay-rail-4ffd82e`. This one is rebuilt on the canonical coverage rule.

**Problem.** A customer who picks annual prepay on the /secure card page gets an unpaid `payment_pending` term and invoice. Nothing is stamped on `scheduled_services` until that invoice is paid, so the re-price guard could not see the pick. Staff could reprice a visit the unpaid invoice will cover at the old price.

**Fix.**
- New rail `securePendingPrepayCoverageReasons` inside `findBillingCoveredVisits` (liveInvoice only; the plan-trim and series-cancel fee rails are unchanged). For each of the customer's `payment_pending` terms with a live invoice, it asks `coverageRowsForTerm`, the same function payment activation uses, whether that term would cover this visit. It does not use a hand-built window.
- **Final state, not stored state.** The guard runs on the locked pre-save row. Every coverage column the save posts (date, start time, service, property on an address change, and so on) is overlaid as `_proposed`, and a single builder (`saveCoverageProposed`) feeds the single-visit guard and both 'following' guard calls. 'Following' siblings also get the propagated service fields. `coverageRowsForTerm` accepts `extraCandidateRows`: it removes each overridden row's stale DB version, re-applies the window and renewal-scope gates, and re-sorts in its own `scheduled_date, window_start, id` order with nulls last, so a moved visit competes for a sold slot at its new position.
- **Locking.** The guard try-locks the per-customer `ANNUAL_PREPAY_LOCK_NS` advisory lock. It already holds the visit and customer rows, so a blocking acquire could deadlock; a miss returns 409 `VISIT_BUSY_RETRY`. `selectSecurePlan` takes the same namespace first in its mint transaction, and now re-checks the visit's live `estimated_price` against the price it quoted (`plan_unavailable` on mismatch, and the customer re-quotes).

**Local pre-push audits.** Five rounds, each fixed here: slot order after a date override, a stale row surviving a move out of the window, the start time, the service identity, and the 'following' path. After the fourth, the one-column-at-a-time overlays were replaced with the single post-save row builder. The last audit was clean.

**Fable review (parallel to round 1): 2 P2s, both fixed in 46b8f707d7.**
- *Mid-activation gap.* The webhook commits `payment_pending` → `active` before visits are linked and stamped. The rail now also reads `active`/`renewal_pending` terms that have **no linked visit** (the same "never activated" test that `ensureCoverageRowsForTerm` uses). A term with any linked row stays with the direct `annual_prepay_term_id` rail.
- *Late-payment slide.* `coverageRowsForTerm` takes `projectFirstActivationOn`, and the rail judges each term on the window a payment **today** would give it, using activation's own anchors and `windowFixedAtCreation` exemption. **Known limit:** a payment later than today slides the window further, so a visit just past today's projected end can still be repriced and then covered later. The successor-term cap is not applied, which only makes the guard stricter.

**Tests.** New `annual-prepay-coverage-extra-candidates.test.js` (5) covers slot order, moving into and out of the window, and the start time kept from the DB row. `billing-covered-visits-open-balance.test.js` adds tests for moving into coverage by date, start time and service; moving out by service; lock contention; and liveInvoice-only. 211 related suites pass locally (5,670 tests).

**Scope ruling (owner, 2026-09-30).** The block is price-only, the same as #5253. A service-only change with an unchanged price is not refused, even when a pending prepay would then cover the visit (Codex r5 thread declined on this ruling).


**Follow-up (not in this PR).** A cadence-only edit (pattern or interval change, same per-visit price) leaves an already-minted pending /secure prepay invoice sized for the old visits-per-year. It needs a decision: retire and re-quote the pending selection, or refuse the edit. Codex r6 raised it; it is declined here under the price-only ruling.

author: zoonamoo
body:
## Why

The GraphQL endpoint has no login, and it accepts any `POST` body as a GraphQL request whatever its content type. So a web page open in the user's browser could run mutations on their daemon (cancel workflows, drop queue entries, install plugins) or read the subscription stream:

- **Another website**, through a cross-site `fetch` or WebSocket. Binding to `127.0.0.1` doesn't stop this, because the browser is on the same machine.
- **A DNS-rebinding page**, which reaches `127.0.0.1` under its own host name.

Separately, `transport/start` bound the port in a background task and replied `127.0.0.1:8081` before knowing whether the bind worked. If another process held 8081, the CLI was told the API lived there anyway. The dashboard is about to proxy to whatever address this reply names, so it has to be true.

## What changed

- **Local-only rule on every route** (`src/loopback.rs`), including `/graphql/ws`:
  - `Host` must be `localhost`, `127.x.x.x` or `[::1]`, any port.
  - `Origin`, when present, must be one of those too.
  - Anything else gets `403`. Requests without an `Origin` (curl, scripts, the web UI's server-side proxy) still work.
- **`allowed_hosts`** config key (`ANIMUS_TRANSPORT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` for standalone runs) adds host names for deliberate non-loopback binds.
- **`transport/start` binds before replying.** A taken port returns `AddressInUse`, and a denied one returns `PermissionDenied`. The reply carries the address actually bound, so port `0` works too.
- **Version 0.2.4** in `Cargo.toml` and `plugin.toml` (which said 0.1.0). Releases v0.2.0–v0.2.3 were cut from an older code line, so the next release has to sort above them.
- README section on the rule.

## Tested

- `cargo test`: 17 tests pass. That includes 7 new ones in `tests/loopback.rs`:
  - local requests served (with and without a local `Origin`);
  - cross-site `Origin` and `null` refused;
  - rebound `Host` refused;
  - WebSocket upgrade from another site refused;
  - `allowed_hosts` honored;
  - `start` reports the real port;
  - `start` fails on a taken port.
- With the middleware removed, the 4 refusal tests fail.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` are clean.

## After merge

Tag `v0.2.4`. The release workflow builds and signs it, and the Animus CLI then pins it for `animus web serve`.

## Follow-up

`animus-transport-http` restricts CORS to localhost but has no `Host` check, so it has the same DNS-rebinding gap. The risk is lower there, because it only accepts JSON bodies. It will be tracked separately.

body:
## What changed
- make outlined buttons and chips use the shared visible neutral control boundary
- remove the NavigationBar's duplicate face/elevation/shadow so the surrounding GlassPanel is the single visual surface
- keep the existing selected-icon motion, reduced-motion behavior and navigation indicator intact
- add source-level regression guards for control contrast and single-surface navigation chrome

## Why
The current navigation paints depth twice (GlassPanel + NavigationBar), which makes the bottom chrome visually heavier than the rest of the app and adds unnecessary paint work. Secondary controls also still used very low-alpha borders, so some actions could fade into white/glass surfaces.

This keeps the UI simple: no new wrappers, no new navigation model, no domain changes.
