author: pedroads002
body:
Resgate do commit `149493a` (25/09), da branch `ficha-do-atendimento`, que nunca virou PR.

## Metade da branch já estava na main

A branch fazia duas coisas: a **ficha** e o **scroll** (altura fixa do chat + abrir no fim da conversa). O scroll já havia chegado à main pelos ajustes de layout (#31 a #33), numa versão melhor — a partir de `lg` quem manda na altura é a linha das três colunas. Mantive a da main. O composer da branch também era a versão antiga, de textarea e botão só; a main já tem anexo, nota de voz e preview. Mantive a da main.

Sobrou a ficha, que continuava sem equivalente nenhum.

## A ficha

Na aba Agenda, acima do botão de agendar: **CLIENTE**, **CLÍNICA** (nome, endereço, cidade, horário) e **ESPECIALIDADES** daquela clínica, com a duração de cada uma.

**Sem preço.** O sistema não guarda nem exibe valor de nada nem de ninguém. A branch original mostrava o valor de cada especialidade; isso foi removido no commit `161d22a`. A tabela `clinica_especialidades` tem uma coluna `valor`, e a consulta não a lê.

As especialidades vêm de `clinica_especialidades`, não da lista geral de `especialidades`: é o que **esta** clínica atende. Só as **ativas** — a trava 3 proíbe oferecer procedimento desativado, e a tela não pode contradizer a conversa. A de interesse do lead vem primeiro e marcada em verde.

Se a clínica não estiver no cadastro, cai no nome que vem no lead e avisa "Endereço não cadastrado."

## O profissional continua de fora — por outro motivo

A branch dizia que era por não existir tabela de profissionais. Existe desde o #38. O motivo hoje é outro: um lead chega para a **clínica**, e uma clínica pode ter **várias unidades**; profissional está ligado à unidade por `profissional_unidades`. Listar todo mundo que atende em qualquer unidade dela faria o CRC oferecer um profissional que não está no endereço que o lead acabou de informar. Enquanto o agendamento não escolher a unidade, não há resposta certa. O comentário no código foi reescrito para dizer isso.

## O que esta tela vai mostrar hoje

**Vazio.** `clinica_especialidades` está zerada e **nada no painel escreve nela** — o cadastro de clientes liga especialidade a *pessoa* (`profissional_especialidades`), não a clínica. Então todo lead vai ler "Esta clínica não tem especialidade ativa cadastrada."

A ficha está certa; o vazio é o estado verdadeiro do banco. Falta a tela que preenche esse vínculo, que é outro trabalho.

## Teste

**No banco**, como `authenticated`, dentro de bloco com rollback: 3 vínculos inseridos, um deles desativado, um lead com interesse apontado. A consulta da ficha trouxe as duas ativas, excluiu a inativa e pôs a de interesse em primeiro. Select depois confirmou que nada ficou gravado.

**Na tela**, componentes reais em `next dev` com dados de mentira, três casos: com especialidades (interesse em primeiro e em verde), sem nenhuma (estado vazio) e sem clínica cadastrada (cai no nome do lead). Andaime removido, conferido com grep.

O teste de tela foi feito antes da remoção do preço; a versão sem preço passou por `tsc --noEmit` e `next build` limpos.

`tsc --noEmit` e `next build` limpos.

author: prajwolrg
body:
## Description

Publishes the SP1 guest ELFs and the account predicate as release artifacts, like asm does. The guests are built in SP1's Docker image so anyone can rebuild them and get the same bytes.

Unlike asm, our guests bake in `alpen-params.json`. So one ELF can't serve every network, and every network gets its own build. The setup follows strata-bridge's `publish-sp1-bridge-guests.yml`:

- `publish-guests.yml` builds one network. It takes its params from `params/<network>/alpen-params.json`, or from a `params_url` for networks that aren't in the repo yet. It publishes the ELFs, the predicate, the params used, a `.sha256` for each file and a manifest. The files always go to a 90-day workflow artifact. They go to S3 once the `ALPEN_GUESTS_S3_BUCKET` and `ALPEN_GUESTS_S3_ROLE_ARN` repo variables are set. They go to a GitHub Release when one is given.
- `release.yml` runs on a `v*` tag. It creates a draft release, builds every network in `params/` and attaches the files, then publishes. The release starts as a draft because releases in this repo are immutable once published.
- `ci-build.yml` now also builds with `docker-build`, so the ELFs in the image match the released ones.

Only `params/dev` exists for now. It is a symlink to the existing test fixture.

### Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature/Enhancement (non-breaking change which adds functionality or enhances an existing one)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] New or updated tests
- [ ] Dependency Update

## Notes to Reviewers

Start with `publish-guests.yml`. `release.yml` is a thin matrix around it.

Things this PR does not do:

- **Staging, testnet and mainnet params.** None exist in `AlpenParams` format yet. `deployments` still has the older `ee-params` shape (`account_id`, `genesis_*`) inline in the Helm values. Until they are added here, use dispatch with `params_url`.
- **S3.** This needs a bucket and an OIDC role from infra. Until then the S3 step is skipped with a warning.
- **Deployed ELFs vs network params.** The staging, testnet and mainnet clusters load ELFs from the `alpen-client` image (`ELF_BASE_PATH=/app/elfs/sp1`). `ci-build.yml` builds those with the dev params. If the guests need each network's params, those deployments may be running the wrong ELFs. This is worth checking separately.
- **Version-tagged image.** The image is still tagged by short SHA only.

Expect the ELF hashes in `ci-build` images to change once, because the guests are now built in Docker instead of on the host.

Testing:

- Built both guests locally with `--features docker-build` and the dev params. It succeeds, and the build also showed that the guest lockfiles were out of date. That fix is its own commit.
- Ran `guest_publish.py` `validate`, `params` and `stage` against that build. The error cases fail as expected, and `sha256sum -c` passes on the staged files.
- actionlint, zizmor, ruff and codespell pass.
- The workflows themselves have not run. They only trigger on a tag or a dispatch from `main`. The first real run will be the next tag, or a dispatch after merge.

Is this PR addressing any specification, design doc or external reference document?

- [ ]  Yes
- [x]  No

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code.
- [x] I have commented my code where necessary.
- [x] I have updated the documentation if needed.
- [x] My changes do not introduce new warnings.
- [ ] I have added (where necessary) tests that prove my changes are effective or that my feature works.
- [ ] New and existing tests pass with my changes.
- [x] I have [disclosed my use of AI](https://github.com/alpenlabs/alpen/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assistance-notice) in the body of this PR.

## Related Issues

None.

## What

`dogfood-graph.yaml` moves from `src/vise/assets/workflows/` (bundled, installed into every user's repo) to this repository's `.claude/workflows/` (project scope, ships to nobody).

## Why

`dogfood` is vise developing vise. Its triage step tags issues by vise's own areas (CLI, hooks, workflows, adapters), and `test_orchestration_skill_sync.py` already kept it off the routing table as "not user-facing". It was bundled anyway, so `graph_list_available` offered it in every repo that installs vise.

`.claude/workflows/` is the highest-precedence scope `graph_activate` reads, so it still resolves when working on vise itself. I checked that with `resolve_workflow_dirs(".")`.

## Follow-through

- README and CLAUDE.md: 12 → 11 bundled workflows. `test_asset_honesty` pins this count.
- `test_node_gate_coverage.py`: removed the four `dogfood` exemptions. They would otherwise be flagged as stale.
- `test_orchestration_skill_sync.py`: `_INTENTIONALLY_UNROUTED` is now `{"decouple"}`.
- CHANGELOG: new **Behaviour change** entry under `[Unreleased]`.

`.vise/quality.yaml` is untouched on purpose. It is not a workflow. It is the quality profile that `quality_check`, `tests_pass` and `lint_pass` read to run vise's own gate.

## Verified

- `ruff check . --exclude .claude`: clean
- full pytest suite: green
- coverage after `combine`: 85%, at the floor

author: protodotdesign
body:
The actual MagicBox checkpoint requires bidirectional attention, centered gated convolution, complete final-layer FFN rows, and 4 pointer projections. This adds an explicit `EncoderOps` extension, segmented CPU/WGPU implementations, a checked encoder loader/executor, asynchronous pointer tasks, and choice/ordinal/binary/extraction decoding.

Pointer decoding uses FP64 host values with fixed compensated sums matching the pinned training decoder's supported CPython 3.12/3.13 behavior. Review repaired padded attention dispatches and distinct block-normalization epsilon handling before publication. Causal inference and prefix semantics retain their existing path.

Validation: 15 portable encoder tests; 5 actual WGPU encoder tests, including a 65,536-logical-group dispatch boundary; all-source Naga shader validation; Clippy/format; clean-checkout `ci` and `quick`. Independent decoder execution matches 91 FP64 values and 44 decisions in Python 3.12/3.13 and Rust debug/release.

Actual encoder qualification on both GPU implementations preserves all 10 typed answers in each precision. FP16/INT8/NF4 pass the independent numeric guard; ternary retains a recorded strict NumPy numeric failure. A 111-token CPU trace supports propagated F32 rounding. Frozen backend-specific regression references and A/A admission follow with the host; this PR makes no performance claim.

Experiments: `docs/encoder-pointer-runtime.md` and `docs/research/runtime-pointer-host-summation-2026-09-29.md`.

Stack: base `feat/runtime-f16-int8-foundation` (PR20).

author: bthecoderr
body:
Ships Formation Clash into the hardened online multiplayer engine without mixing it into Classic competition.

- public Battle tables and private Battle challenge links
- server validates Battle Chess access and the creator's selected unlocked formation
- opponent must also have Battle Chess unlocked
- alternate Formation Clash FENs run through the existing server-authoritative move engine
- reconnect/resume, clocks, resignations, draw offers and rematches all work for Battle
- Battle rematches preserve the original formation
- separate Battle Elo, W-L-D, games played and per-formation usage stats
- Battle results do not change Classic Elo, Classic W-L-D or Season standings
- Battle leaderboard only includes players who have completed a Battle match
- Battle history is separated from Classic history
- Online table displays Formation Clash identity and Battle rating movement
- Universe Hub links unlocked players directly to Battle Online
- browser roles may read Battle competition stats but cannot write them or invoke Battle creation RPCs directly
- migration tracking, generated types and regression coverage

Production-safe rollback testing verified +16/-16 Battle Elo at equal ratings, formation stats, rematch formation preservation, and unchanged Classic rating/wins.

author: sana-sagegami
body:
## 背景 / 目的
Closes #144

#140 で捕獲の申告を鬼側に移したが、`catches` / `catchPhotos` は認証済みなら誰でも書ける暫定ルールのままだった。そのため、他人になりすまして任意の相手を鬼にできた。これをルールで塞ぐ。

ルールで拒否されるようになると、取り消しの失敗がこれまでと違って実際に起きうる。だが今は取り消し画面が先に閉じてしまい、エラーが出なかった。これもあわせて直す。

## 変更内容
### `database.rules.json`
- `catches/{catchId}`
  - **作成**: 書く本人が `demonUserId` であること。`fugitiveUserId` は自分以外で、同じルームの参加者であること。`caughtAt === now`。作成時に `catchPhotoId` を含めないこと。既存IDの上書きは禁止
  - **削除(取り消し)**: 捕まえた鬼か、捕まった逃走者本人だけ。10秒の期限はルールでは判定しない(時計ずれで正当な取り消しを弾かないため。クライアントの責務)
  - **更新(写真の紐づけ)**: 鬼本人だけ。`demonUserId` / `fugitiveUserId` / `caughtAt` は書き換えられない
  - 各フィールドの型を検証し、未知の子(`$other`)を禁止
- `catchPhotos/{photoId}`
  - **作成**: `demonUid === auth.uid`、`takenAt === now`。書く本人と `fugitiveUid`(本人以外)が同じルームの参加者であること。**更新は不可**
  - **削除**: 鬼か逃走者本人
- 親ノードに一括の `.read` / `.write` は置いていない(子のルールが無効になる事故の再発防止)

### ルールのテスト(`rules-test/`)
- Firebase Local Emulator Suite と `@firebase/rules-unit-testing` を使った `node:test` のテストを34件追加
- 実行方法: `cd rules-test && npm install && npm test`。`firebase-tools` を devDependency に入れているので、グローバルの firebase CLI は不要
- `rules-test/node_modules/` は `.gitignore` に追加

### 取り消し失敗のエラー表示
- 取り消しの実行を、オーバーレイから `GamePage` 側の `useUndoCatch` に移した
  - 楽観的なローカル削除で捕獲が消え、オーバーレイがサーバーの拒否より先に閉じる。このためオーバーレイの `context` では SnackBar が出せなかった
- 失敗したら、ゲーム画面の SnackBar に `undoCatchErrorMessage`(期限切れ等以外は `userFacingErrorMessage`)の文言を出す
- `CaughtByDemonOverlay` は `isUndoing` / `onUndo` を受け取るだけにした

### ドキュメント
- `docs/rtdb-schema.md` に `catches` / `catchPhotos` のルール表と判断の理由、テストの実行方法を追記。「暫定」の記述を削除

## 動作確認
- `flutter test`: 全件成功(909件)
- `flutter analyze`: error / warning なし(既存の info のみ)
- `rules-test`(エミュレータ): 34件すべて成功。次を確認している
  - 正しい鬼が正しい逃走者を捕まえられる
  - なりすましで捕獲を書き込めない
  - `caughtAt` を過去・未来にできない
  - 当事者以外は取り消せない
  - 写真の紐づけで `caughtAt` などを書き換えられない
  - `undoCatch` が行う3つの書き込み(捕獲の削除・写真の削除・自分の役割を戻す)が逃走者に許可される
  - 既存機能(位置共有・足元写真・イベントログ)の書き込みが通る
- ウィジェットテスト: 取り消し失敗時に、オーバーレイが閉じた後でも SnackBar が出る。成功時は出ない。実行中は二重送信しない
- **未実施**: 実機2台での確認(拒否時の表示、既存機能)
- **未実施**: `firebase deploy --only database`(本番。マージ後に go-live-checklist を通してから実施)

## スクリーンショット / 動画
なし(見た目の変更は、失敗時に SnackBar が出ることだけ)

## レビューで見てほしいところ
- 取り消しの期限をルールで判定していない点(Issueの方針どおり)
- `catchPhotos` の作成時に、対応する `catches` の存在を確認していない点。取り消しと写真送信が競合したときの孤立レコードは #145 で扱う
- `useUndoCatch` の戻り値に record(`UndoCatchAction`)を使っている点。値クラスではなく hook の戻り値なので、`useAsyncAction` と同じ扱いにした

## 影響範囲・注意点
- **ルールは本番にデプロイするまで効かない**
- 互換性は確認済み: `reportCatch` は `catchPhotoId` を含めずに作成し、写真の紐づけは `attachCatchPhoto` の別のトランザクションで行うので、新ルールに当たらない

body:
## What

[RFC-004](docs/proposals/004-design-direction.md), accepted as [ADR-011](docs/decisions/011-one-design-system.md) and planned as [Plan-004](docs/plans/004-one-design-system.md): one design system for Auracle's words, marks, picture, interaction, sound and explanation. It is written once in `www/brand/`, generated into every surface, built into shared components, and checked. It records the maintainer's seven decisions and narrows [Plan-003](docs/plans/003-one-instrument-contracts.md) (Wave 2) to the contracts that don't depend on the rebuild. Also a measurement note, [`docs/notes/text-2026-09/`](docs/notes/text-2026-09/README.md), with the script that made it. Documentation only; nothing changes in the app yet.

## Why

Watching the first round of view films (recorded and held; see `docs/runbooks/finish-the-view-films.md`) showed four gaps:

- **Pace:** the narration measured 195–203 words a minute.
- **Sound:** the films play the harsh, noisy and blaring sounds a seed deals.
- **Explanation:** the films show what the app does but rarely why.
- **UI quality:** the interaction review's quality findings are still open.

The maintainer then asked for a refresh of the components and the interaction design, with each view rethought around progressive disclosure and far less text. Measured on 2026-09-30:

- Every view shows five or six sentences of guidance at rest, each from a different surface.
- Each view holds 800–1,700 more words in tooltips.
- How to play the first note is said three ways.
- The **?** card is 799 words.

`ui-hierarchy.md` already set one teaching surface per view and no placeholder rows. Those rules came undone because nothing enforced them.

## How

Eight parts:

1. One token source.
2. A voice guide.
3. The marks fixed where surfaces break the spec.
4. A type scale, grid and motion.
5. **New:** components, interaction and disclosure.
   - A component set.
   - Three levels of disclosure.
   - A text budget, checked by a browser spec built from `measure.js`.
   - Learning by doing.
   - Each view's disclosure map and layout drafted as a specimen and approved before it is rebuilt.
6. Sound: a sonic floor for first deals and film casting, and no UI sounds.
7. Films: `af_heart` at speed 0.81, a speaking rate of about 176 words a minute and about 160 overall, explaining with a figure before showing the app.
8. One grammar for explanatory graphics.

**Decided (2026-09-30):**
- **Tagline:** "A synthesizer that searches for your sound".
- **Light mode:** the docs only.
- **UI sounds:** none.
- **Voice:** `af_heart` at 0.81, chosen by ear from six renders.
- **Design:** Claude drafts, the maintainer approves.
- **Sonic floor:** the first deals and the films only.

- **Wave 2 is split.** The word table and its check, undo, the keymap and bank stability go ahead in Plan-003. The colour looks, message channels, onboarding surface and printed key hints are built into the rebuild (Plan-004 task 6), so they aren't built twice. Wave 2's film task becomes Plan-004 task 8.

Plan-004's eight tasks:
1. Tokens.
2. The voice guide.
3. Marks.
4. Specimens for approval.
5. The component set and the text-budget spec.
6. The views rebuilt, one at a time.
7. One explanation figure.
8. The films' second pass.

The sonic floor goes to RFC-005. `apps/web/AGENTS.md` and `www/AGENTS.md` point to ADR-011.

## Checklist

- [x] `make check` passes: docs only; `make dev-check` passes (link and name checks, run by the pre-commit hook)
- [ ] New behavior is covered by a test: n/a, a proposal (`measure.js` was run once as committed)
- [x] Docs updated where relevant (`docs/README.md` index, a new note, ADR-011, Plan-004, Plan-003 narrowed, `AGENTS.md` pointers)
- [ ] If Rust used by the web app changed: n/a

author: ithealthtech
body:
Before: every ticket sync ended with "No tickets listed (no tickets (tickets by company: not found; ticket list: not found; service tickets: not found))", so the ticket dashboard stayed empty. Separately, RMM health counted every device as "online unknown".

After: the sync reads tickets from the ConnectWise platform's service ticketing API and online status from its heartbeat API. Both use the same calls CallBridge makes against this API. Open and recently closed tickets appear on the dashboard and on each client, each ticket links to its page in the ConnectWise web app, and devices show as online or offline.

**Why it was broken**

- **Tickets:** the three ticket addresses the sync tried were guesses, and none of them exist. It read "not found" from all three as "no tickets", so the failure never showed up as an error.
- **Online status:** the device records don't include whether the agent is online. That comes from a separate heartbeat API the sync never called.

**How: tickets**

- `GET /api/platform/v1/service/ticketing/statuses` gives the status list. A ticket is closed when its status is in the `Closed` category, whatever the status is called.
- `GET /api/platform/v2/service/ticketing/tickets?companyIds=…&pageSize&pageNum&sortBy=createdAt&sortDir=desc` is called twice:
  - once with `statusIds=[notIn],<closed ids>` for open tickets, the same filter CallBridge uses;
  - once with `statusIds=[in],<closed ids>` for closed tickets, read to the last page (at most 200 pages).
- The dashboard keeps tickets closed in the last 90 days.
- If ConnectWise refuses the closed-ticket query, the open tickets still sync, the closed tickets already synced for that company are kept, and the sync log notes it.
- Paging follows `totalCount`.
- A closed ticket with no closing date is counted as closed on its last update.
- Ticket links use the web app's route with the ticket number and the company's numeric external ID. They only work in North America, the one region whose web address is known.

**How: online status**

- After listing a company's devices, the sync calls `GET /api/platform/v2/device/endpoints/heartbeat?resourceType=companies&resources=<company>` once and takes each endpoint's `Availability`.
- If the heartbeat can't be read, devices still sync with the status they had.

Both syncs still only read.

**Tests**

- The fake platform serves the ticketing endpoints. Tests cover:
  - the status filters;
  - closed status by category;
  - the web links;
  - closed tickets kept when their list is refused;
  - a key without ticket access stopping after one sign-in.
- A new test in the health tests checks that the heartbeat sets online status.
- Lint, typecheck and all 284 tests pass locally.

body:
## Summary

- make the operational-safety workflow unconditional so protected checks cannot be skipped by a path filter
- remove the retired one-off workflow that retained repository write credentials and pushed a generated mutation
- update actions/attest to the current immutable v4.2.2 commit and add a semantic repository-wide workflow policy guard
- require a separate fine-grained Hugging Face dataset reader instead of reusing the Space publisher
- preflight every canonical lane pointer at one immutable private-dataset revision, then bind the live four-lane canary to those exact snapshots
- bind health, replacement login, build evidence, and the public frontier board to one per-run non-secret rotation generation so rolling processes cannot compose a false green result

## Scope

This signed successor is rooted at exact protected `main` `a6953dfb60c6daa2b32ef4e533dacdcd40484c8b`. It preserves the David v2 implementation, private dataset boundary, CodeQL, Dependabot, CODEOWNERS, Hub writer locks, PostgreSQL proof lanes, and generated evidence contracts.

The publisher token and runtime reader remain separate. The workflow can prove that the reader is fine-grained and can read the selected private repository, but it does not claim visibility into Hugging Face permission checkboxes that the identity API does not expose.

## Verification

- all selected dataset-reader, live-canary, operational-safety, workflow-policy, release-truth, and Hub-lock contracts passed
- all browser-state and evidence-constellation Node contracts passed
- every workflow YAML document and the embedded rotation Python parsed successfully
- the changed Python modules compiled and the new modules passed Ruff checks
- the preflight contract accepted all canonical pointers from private dataset revision `3e7cdabbec98b07bc5e9d2fffb040652e06fa9af`
- `git diff --check` passed
- the final commit is signed with the registered SSH signing key
- an independent security re-review found no remaining issue after the login-generation race was closed

## Activation boundary

Merge does not by itself claim that the federal lanes are operational. Activation still requires the owner to create the repository-scoped read-only fine-grained token and save it directly as the protected environment secret `DAVID_DATASET_READ_TOKEN`. The protected rotation workflow must then converge and prove exact source, generation, pointer, login, logout, and live-lane bindings.

## Result: closed unmerged — broader local search did not resolve D2 feasibility

The initial eight-direction implementation exceeded Hydrology Reset Geometry's 15-minute limit and was reduced from 32 to 12 oblique candidates per route point. The narrowed exact head passed CI #4956, Hydrology Reset Geometry #488, DR-40 #1137, DR-50 #1096, and Windows A/B determinism.

Key-287 still has zero curvature-admissible feasible samples/routes. Final maximum envelope gap is 27.4343 units versus 27.4330 baseline (slightly worse); integrated gap improves from 112.9395 to 112.6518. The local corridor diagnostic found only 8 curvature-admissible samples, with best admissible gap 27.2744; the minimum before curvature admission is 13.1263. Thus the experiment does not resolve the controlling curvature/terrain/cross-section conflict despite passing machine regression checks.

No authored semantics, thresholds/calibration, or Minecraft authority changed. Preserve the search and evidence as a negative experiment; do not merge or request human visual review.

## ⚠️ Approval PR（認可モデルの変更・自動マージ対象外）
ADR-0004（2026-09-30 ユーザー決定）を bim へ適用。認可モデルの変更のため **自動マージ対象外**。ユーザーの明示的な承認後にマージしてください。

## 🎯 目的
BIM モデル・点群は一覧で絞り込みなし、ID 指定の取得・更新・削除は組織照合なし、作成は本文の `organization_id` をそのまま保存していた。BIM 要素はモデル ID さえ分かれば他組織のモデル配下を閲覧でき、要素 ID 取得・検索は全組織を横断していた。

## 🔧 変更（services/bim のみ）
| エンドポイント | 変更後（一般ユーザー） | admin |
|---|---|---|
| 🏗️ `POST /models`・`POST /pointclouds` | 本文の他組織 → 403 `ORG_FORBIDDEN`（書き込みなし） | 本文の組織で作成 |
| 📋 `GET /models`・`GET /pointclouds` | 自組織に固定（count・ページ両方）。`organization_id` クエリを新設し、他組織指定 → 403 | 未指定で全組織、指定でその組織 |
| 🔎 `GET/PUT/DELETE /models/{id}`・`/pointclouds/{id}` | 組織条件付き検索、他組織 → 404（更新・削除は書き込みなし） | 条件なし |
| 🧱 `GET /{model_id}/elements`・`/elements/by-category`・`/elements/by-level` | 親モデルを組織条件付きで確認し、他組織 → 404（要素は取得しない） | 親モデルの存在のみ確認（不存在は 404） |
| 🧱 `GET /elements/{element_id}` | `bim_models` と JOIN し親モデルの組織で絞る。他組織 → 404 | 条件なし |
| 🔍 `GET /elements/search` | 親モデルの組織で JOIN 絞り込み（`model_id` 指定時も同様）。`organization_id` クエリ新設、他組織指定 → 403 | 未指定で全組織 |
| 💚 `GET /health` 等 | 変更なし（組織所有データなし） | — |

- 🔧 `src/middleware/tenant.py`：safety と同一（bim の `TokenData.roles` が `Optional` のため erp と同じく `user.roles or []` の 1 行のみ差異）
- 🧱 BIM 要素は独自の `organization_id` を持たないため、親モデル（`bim_models.organization_id`）経由で分離。点群は独自の `organization_id` 列で分離（モデルとの親子関係はスキーマ上なし）。
- 📁 ファイルのダウンロード／アップロード URL を発行するエンドポイントは bim に存在しない（`file_key` を保存・返却するのみ）ため、該当なし。

## 🧪 テスト（services/bim、CI と同一）
ruff ✅ / mypy ✅（16 files）/ pytest ✅ **112 passed**（新規 `tests/test_tenant_isolation.py` 73 件）
- ❌→403：全 14 ルート × org 無し `ORG_REQUIRED`／不正 `ORG_INVALID`（DB 未アクセス・書き込みなし）
- 一覧の他組織指定 403、ID 指定の他組織 404＋WHERE に組織条件＋`add/flush/delete/commit` 未実行、作成の他組織 403、要素の親モデル 404（要素クエリ未実行）、要素 ID 取得・検索の JOIN 組織条件、admin 横断
- 🧬 ミューテーション確認：点群の組織条件と要素の親モデル確認を外すと 17 件が失敗することを確認
- 既存テスト（`test_bim.py` 等）は無修正で通過（認証なし 401 のみを検証しているため）

## 📊 影響
- 一般ユーザーは自組織の BIM モデル・要素・点群のみ扱える。他組織指定は 403、他組織レコードは 404。
- admin の要素一覧（モデル配下）は、存在しないモデル ID に対し従来の空配列から 404 に変わる。
- ⚠️ デプロイ前確認：検証環境の `bim.bim_models` / `bim.point_clouds` の `organization_id` と利用者トークンの `org` が一致していること。

## 🔒 セキュリティ
- fail-closed（org 無し・不正 UUID は 403）。固定 UUID へのフォールバックなし。
- ID 指定は組織条件付き検索のため、他組織レコードの存在を明かさない（404）。
- secret・資格情報・PII の追加なし。

## 🔍 発見（本 PR では未修正）
- 🐛 `GET /api/v1/bim/elements/search` は、先に登録された `GET /elements/{element_id}` に一致して `element_id="search"` の UUID 検証で **常に 422** になり到達不能（ルート定義順の問題）。本 PR では検索にも組織条件を実装し、ハンドラを直接呼ぶテストで検証済み。ルート順の修正は別 Issue 推奨。
- ⚠️ 作成時の `project_id`（他サービスの案件）は組織一致を検証していない（bim から project を参照できないため）。

## 🗄️ Migration
なし

## 🚀 Deployment
bim サービスの再デプロイのみ（人が実施）

## ↩️ Rollback
本 PR の revert → bim 再デプロイ

## 📝 残課題
- `/elements/search` のルート順修正（上記）
- `project_id` の組織整合（案件サービス側との連携設計が必要）

author: shrirangmhalgi
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

In the PivotFirst fast path, `firstAgg` groups by `(groupByKeys, pivotColumn)`. When the table has many distinct pivot column values outside the explicit `IN` list, `firstAgg` creates one group per distinct non-matching value - all of which
`PivotFirst` ignores in `secondAgg`.

This PR wraps the pivot column group-by key in `IF(pivotColumn IN (pivotValues), pivotColumn, null)`, collapsing all non-matching values into a single null group. `PivotFirst` skips the null group as before, and the group-by keys are preserved in `secondAgg`, keeping query results identical to the un-optimized plan.

The optimization is skipped when:
- The pivot column contains an aggregate expression (SPARK-24722)
- A NULL pivot value is present (non-matching rows mapped to null would merge with legitimate null-key rows)

### Why are the changes needed?
For a table with 10,000 distinct course values pivoting on 2:
- Before: `firstAgg` creates 10,000 groups per group-by key (99.98% wasted)
- After: `firstAgg` creates 3 groups per group-by key (2 matching + 1 null)

This reduces memory (fewer HashAggregate entries), CPU (fewer hash/compare/aggregate operations), and spill risk.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

No. Query results are identical. This only affects the internal execution plan for the PivotFirst fast path.

### How was this patch tested?

Five new tests in `DataFramePivotSuite`:
- Plan-level assertion that `If(In(...), col, null)` appears in the analyzed plan
- NULL pivot value correctly skips the optimization
- Aggregate pivot column (SPARK-24722) correctly skips the optimization
- Multiple aggregates (sum + avg) with the optimization
- Group-by key with only non-pivot values is preserved as `Row(year, null, null)`

## Summary

What o3co/auth.provider#762, #768 and #769 did for the provider, done here: comments state what holds now, not history. This repository's comments were mostly that already; this pass shortens the longest blocks to the rule they keep, removes what told the story of an earlier implementation, and corrects the comments that disagreed with the code.

Only comments and the README change. The README's corrections are the streaming ones below; the rest of its history ("used to be resolved", "no longer logs", "a follow-up, not something this release does") goes too.

## Passes

- [x] Comment blocks of 10 lines or more keep the rule they state; the worked example and the remedies for a refused placeholder value point to the README, which carries them. History goes: what an interceptor used to authorize, what an earlier implementation read, which test is "the regression".
- [x] Comments agree with the code, including these corrections:
  - **Streams.** A server-streaming RPC's generated handler calls `RecvMsg` once, so on gRPC it is checked before the handler runs and at that read, and never again; sends are not re-checked. The comments and the README said a server-streaming handler never receives, and that the per-`RecvMsg` re-check stops delivery on any long-lived stream. Streams refuse `field_mappings` because the policy interceptor runs before any request message is read, not because a stream has none.
  - **`generateRequestID`**: the suffix is the Unix nanoseconds in hex, nothing random.
  - **`WithO3coRequireConfirmedRevision`** refuses an allow in which a rule with no policy source satisfied a group, not every allow whose groups contain one.
  - **Extracted fields** are forwarded on ConnectRPC unary only, and of package `endpoint` only the o3co endpoint reads them; `ResolveResource` also calls `ResolveResourceWithFields`.
  - **`ResourceValueError`** names all three refusals (empty, outside the segment token, structural); a nil `Decision` also means no backend was asked.

Comment lines (`//`, all tracked Go files but `*.pb.go`): 1,205 → 1,179 (most of what changed is wording, not length).

## How to check

A `go/scanner` comparison of every changed Go file's token stream at the base and at the head, comments left out: no token differs. `gofmt -l` is clean, and `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass in each module (CI green).

Reviewed before publishing by two reviewers, one of them adversarial (it tries to falsify each rewritten claim against the code), and the fix commits again; every finding was checked against the code and applied, Minor ones included.

## Found along the way, not changed here

- #12: a stream is not re-checked while it only sends, on either framework, so revoking a grant does not stop a server-stream.
- #13: generated request IDs are the wall clock, so two requests that read the same clock value share one — and `Decision.RequestID` is the key that joins to the verifier's log.

## Not in this PR

- Code, string literals and test names (Go test function names, e.g. `…_BehavesAsBefore`, are identifiers).

author: thanatostyrannos
body:
Module 4 (spec section 7), part 3 of 8: the continuity plan and the exercise record, review dates and test cadences from the framework, and module 4's own findings for the ones that are missed. This builds on Plan 10b (PR #27, merged as d81182d): the artifact-type plug-ins, the lifecycle to signing, the out-of-date rule and the framework plug-in. API (Application Programming Interface) only. The screens are Plan 06's.

## What it does
- **Continuity plan** (belongs to a process): how the business keeps working while systems are down. Each workaround says what to do, which role does it and how long it can hold (ISO 8601, above zero, at most a year). A process's cover is its longest hold time, checked against its MTD (Maximum Tolerable Downtime). The spec says "a process or group of processes" and module 3 has no group, so a plan belongs to one process and names the others it covers by id. Cover shorter than the MTD, no workaround, no MTD, or a process that cannot be found are warnings that never stop signing.
- **Exercise record** (belongs to a plan or a runbook): tabletop, functional or full failover, the date, who took part, the actual recovery time against the RTO (Recovery Time Objective) of what was exercised, what went wrong, and fixes, each with a reference, an owner and a due date. It names which signed version of the plan or runbook was used. A tabletop measures no time and must leave it blank. A plan or runbook has many records, each its own artifact with a series number. A record is a point in time: the map moving never makes it out of date.
- **Cadences.** ITIL ITSCM 1.2.0 says a continuity plan is reviewed yearly, and a runbook and a continuity plan are tested yearly (NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 says both are done annually, checked against the published text). A tenant may set a smaller whole number of months (at least one) and clear it again, never a larger one. New permission `continuity.cadences.set`.
- **Findings**, kept as modules 2 and 3 keep theirs (open or resolved, first seen, last seen, with the same meaning as in PR #25): `review-missed`, `test-overdue`, `exercise-missed-rto` (on the plan or runbook exercised) and `fix-overdue` (on the exercise record). `GET /api/continuity/findings`, and `ContinuityFindings` for other modules. They are worked out when a version is signed, when a fix is marked done, when a cadence changes, on request, and on a schedule through a platform-wide list of tenants.
- **A fix is marked done outside the signed record.** The signed record never changes, so a separate append-only record holds who, when and a note. Only the fix's owner or the owner of what was exercised may do it.
- Export (Plan 10e) works on both types with no change; two integration tests show it.

## Rulings (the owner can overturn any)
- A review date only moves earlier: the earlier of the date a version was signed with and the signing date plus the cadence now. A shortened cadence takes hold on versions already signed; a longer one from the framework does not excuse a date already set.
- A functional or full exercise counts as a test of a runbook or a plan; a tabletop counts as a test of a plan only. Only signed records count.
- An exercise that missed its RTO is resolved only by a later measured exercise that meets it, whichever version it used.
- All dates are UTC calendar dates. An exercise may be dated at most tomorrow in UTC. A fix's due date runs to the end of its day. A review is missed only after its instant, not at it.
- A covered process's change does not make a plan out of date; it shows as a warning.
- A tenant is worked out once for each interval: one guarded statement takes it, so replicas ticking together do not both work it out.

## Review (one adversary against the plan's Review Focus)
Two real problems, both fixed test first:
- **Two refreshes at once undid a finding.** One that read state before a change applied its answer over a finding another had just opened, resolving it and resetting its first seen. The refresh now locks the tenant's row before it reads. A test with eight refreshes at once fails without the lock.
- **A fix owner of 2000 characters would have made every refresh in the tenant fail**, since a finding's detail is kept in 1000 characters. The owner is shortened in the detail as the fix's text is.

Checked and sound: a review due at midnight; 29 February and month ends; an exercise dated tomorrow in another zone; the scheduler (once, no cross-tenant finding, module off in a tenant, and back on); an exercise against a runbook signed again since; signed versions (the fix record, cadences and findings never write a version; a test checks the revision and hash); nothing loosens an objective (a cadence can only be shortened, a tabletop cannot carry a time, a tabletop of a runbook does not count).

## Deferred minors
- A change to a process a plan also covers is a warning, not a new draft.
- A refresh reads every signed version of the tenant each time; fine for hundreds of artifacts.
- The first refresh ever in a tenant, run twice at the same moment, can fail for one of them; the event is delivered again or the next tick does it.
- `ContinuityFindings` has no in-process caller until module 5 exists; the HTTP API is tested.
- The runbook plug-in keeps its own copy of the duration rules.
- A signed version shows the review date it was signed with; a finding can use an earlier one after a cadence is shortened.
- CP-2(1), CP-4 and CP-4(1) are from memory of NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, not fetched. Sections 2.2.1, 3.4.6, 3.5 and 3.5.3 of SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and its yearly review and test were checked.
- The tests for the plan and exercise rules, the cadences and the findings were written before the classes they test (compile-red, then green on the first run); mutation checks below stand in for seeing each fail.

## For the owner: one schema decision
A release may only add to the schema, and the old unique key on artifacts (tenant, type, subject) would refuse a second exercise record. Migration 0003 adds a new key that includes a series number and **disables** the old one; the next release's drop script should remove it. Every artifact an older replica can write is series 1, so the new key is at least as strict for it. If you would rather not leave a disabled constraint, the alternative is a table of exercise records apart from artifacts.

## Mutation checks
Each rule was broken, the tests run, the code restored: 34 mutations, all caught in the end. Three survived the test first meant to catch them. Two were caught after a test was added (the first-signature baseline of a test never held; a tenant that switches the module off on the schedule, now `FindingsClockTest`), and the third, a tenant failing in any other way, survives the integration test but is caught by `FindingsClockTest`.

| Area | Mutations | Caught by |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | exactly-the-MTD warns; shortest not longest hold; uncovered process allowed; hold time unchecked | PlanTypeTest |
| Exercise | exactly the RTO missed; a tabletop with a time; a measured kind with none; a date after tomorrow; a version that does not exist; a fix due before the exercise; references case-sensitive; lenient dates | ExerciseTypeTest |
| Exercise (platform) | a point in time goes out of date; a type cannot have several per subject | ContinuityExerciseTest |
| Cadences | missed at the instant; due date past on its day; a longer tenant cadence wins; a cadence in days; months as 30 days | CadencesTest |
| Fixes | anyone may mark done; the exercised owner may not | ContinuityFollowUpsTest |
| Findings | stored date only; computed date only; a tabletop counts; exactly the RTO missed; oldest exercise decides; another record's fix counts; overdue on the day; baseline ignores the first signing | FindingRulesTest |
| Findings (platform) | refreshes not serialized | ContinuityFindingsTest (eight at once) |
| Schedule | taken for no interval | ContinuityFindingsScheduleTest |
| Schedule

body:
## Summary

The daemon's read views (`/status`, `/attention`, `/board` and `/tickets/ID`, with the supervisor and parked-ticket items they share) now live in `holophyte/serve/views.py`. The server module keeps the token checks, static files, `StatusHandler`, `StatusServer` and the serve loop. Every module in `holophyte/serve/` is also trimmed to comments that state a constraint the code cannot express. No route's behaviour or JSON shape changes.

## Why

The server module was 1166 lines, over the 1000-line ceiling and pinned there, so it could not grow. Its first 180 lines were a docstring restating the route contract, which `docs/reference/http.md` already holds. About 28% of the package was comments and docstrings, and 24 of those lines cited a ticket. Moving the views takes the server module off the size table. The trim brings the package to the 5% comment budget with no ticket ids.

## Changes

| Before | After |
| ------ | ----- |
| The read views and `FAILED_WINDOW_MS` sit inside the server module, which is over its ceiling and pinned. | They live in `views.py`. The server module imports every moved name it or an importer reads, so `status`, `supervisor_view`, `parked_item`, `attention`, `board` and `ticket_detail` are the same objects from either module. |
| The server module is on the `PINNED` size table. | It is off the table, and both it and `views.py` are under 900 lines. |
| The serve package carries module docstrings, history and ticket ids in its comments. | Short constraint comments and one-line docstrings remain. Where a docstring was the whole body of a class or function, it becomes `pass` or is dropped. |
| The comment-budget pins hold the old counts, and `docs/development.md` does not name the new module. | Pins are reset to the measured counts, `views.py` has an entry, and no serve module has a `CITED` entry. `docs/development.md` lists `views.py`. |

## Decisions and risks

- The moved block is unchanged. `StatusHandler` still calls the views through the server's globals, so a patch of the server's `status` still reaches it. Tests that read or patch moved names on the server module stay unedited.
- `views.py` imports nothing from the server module. Its dependencies (`paused_item()`, `SWEEPABLE_PHASES` and the working-time reads) do not import the server either, so the split adds no import cycle.
- The trim removes or shortens comments and docstrings only. String literals, including SQL and prompt text, are code and stay byte for byte. Every `# noqa` that ruff still needs is kept.
- Some comments were kept only as short constraint notes where the code cannot say why (for example the config write's lock and backup mode, the host ledger being a file rather than a store). Names that used to lean on a deleted comment are not renamed here; that is a follow-up.
- Someone who relied on the deleted module docstrings for route detail now goes to `docs/reference/http.md`.

## Verification

The pull request's checks finished successfully. The ticket's verify block covers:

- The guard modules `test_file_sizes.py`, `test_comment_budget.py`, `test_import_cycles.py`, `test_eager_import.py`, `test_store_surface.py`, `test_docs*.py` and `test_holophyte_package.py`.
- The focused modules `test_serve*.py`, `test_drawer*.py`, `test_console_fixture.py`, `test_note_delivery.py`, `test_toil.py`, `test_working_time_consumers.py` and `test_reconcile.py`.
- `wc -l` on `server.py` and `views.py`, each under 900.
- An import check that the six view names are identical objects from both modules, with `__module__` set to `holophyte.serve.views`.
- A split check against the merge base: each named top-level statement of the old server module is defined in exactly one of the two modules, unchanged.
- A code check on every other serve module against the merge base, with comments, docstrings and imports dropped: no top-level statement differs.
- The comment share over `holophyte/serve/`, at 5% or less with no ticket ids.
- `ruff check .`

_Requested by **Walter** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_019qVmjX2uTV3rJxFf4NtmmN?thread=cmsg_019qVmjX2uTV3rJxFf4NtmmNN1EZkTDCGbjawMvLS7bJfZ)_

Before: there was no common notion of a query source. Observed-read records and the repository file listing were handled separately, and nothing checked that what a source reports maps to a graph identity before it was used.

After: sources register in one registry and each is evaluated against a pipeline. A source is `connected` only when every asset it reports resolves to an existing graph identity; otherwise it stays `not_enabled` with total, matched and unmatched counts and sample unmatched references. A source that raises is reported as `error` without hiding the others.

What it does: adds a source interface, registry and the documented `sources[] {name, kind, state, matched}` payload.

How: new `src/kumosql/query_sources.py` defines `QuerySource` (name, kind, `assets()`), `SourceRegistry.evaluate/to_json(pipeline)`, and the first two entries. `ObservedReadsSource` wraps the records `graph.py` ingests (destinations and referenced tables). `GitHubRepoSource` wraps the `github_repo.connect` file listing, with each path matched as an asset identity against models loaded from the same path. Resolution uses `Pipeline.resolve_reference`. `matched` is a 0-1 fraction (null when a source reports nothing, which is never enabled). Minimal edits: the UI sources panel gets a "Not enabled" label and `docs/ui-roadmap.md` documents the states and extra count fields. Issue #8 is untouched.

Blocked/deferred: `/api/changes` keeps its preview data and banner because no runtime pipeline plus source records reach the server yet; the real builder is exposed with the documented shape. Repository files only match once a whole-project repository loader builds a pipeline with those paths (part of #8, not done here), so today such a source would report not enabled.

Part of #38

Tests: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -m "not slow" -q` gives 371 passed. New tests in `tests/test_query_sources.py` cover enabled, unmatched, empty, error isolation, repository paths and duplicate names.

author: hibiki5201
body:
## 必須チェック（未チェックのPRは提出しないでください）
- [x] コンパイルエラーが無いことを確認した（Unity 未起動のため、`KillChord.Editor.ProjectSetup` の2ファイルを UnityEngine/UnityEditor のモジュール参照の dotnet build で確認）
- [x] 変更が関係しうるシーンでPlayModeを最低1回通した（不要: エディタ起動時だけ動く処理と、Unity 外の CLI のみ）

## 概要
クローン後の初期セットアップを、ダブルクリックで実行できる CLI（`Setup.bat`）でほぼ自動化した。あわせて、セットアップが足りない状態で Unity を開くと警告ウィンドウが出るようにした。

## クローズするIssue
- #2334

## 原因
セットアップの手順が README と Notion「Unity導入方法」に分かれていて、手作業が多かった。
- サブモジュール（private の `Assets/AssetStoreTools` と `Docs/NotionSpecifications`）の取得
- pull でサブモジュールを追従させる `submodule.recurse` の設定
- Unity のバージョンと Android Build Support の確認

`Assets/AssetStoreTools` が無いと、NuGet パッケージが無くてコンパイルエラーになる。Unity は Safe Mode で開き、エディタのスクリプトが動かない。そのため、Unity の中だけでは案内できなかった。

## 対処
- **CLI**: `PowerShell/ProjectSetup/Setup-Project.ps1`（PowerShell 5.1 で動作）と、ルートの `Setup.bat`（ダブルクリック用）
  - クローン先のパスに日本語・空白があれば警告する。
  - クローン先のフォルダ名が `SymphonyKillChord` でなければ Error にする。Unity と IDE はフォルダ名からソリューション（`<フォルダ名>.slnx`）を作るため、名前が違うと別名のソリューションができて二重になる。期待するフォルダ名は `project-setup.json` の `RepositoryFolderName` に持たせた。
  - `git config --local` の `submodule.recurse` / `core.longpaths` を true にする。
  - 未取得のサブモジュールを `git submodule update --init` で取る。`ignore = all` のもの（仕様書）は `--remote --depth 1` で最新を取る。git の進捗はそのまま表示する。
  - `ProjectVersion.txt` のバージョンの Unity と、Android Build Support が入っているかを確かめる。場所は Hub の既定の場所と `secondaryInstallPath.json` から探す。無ければ `unityhub://<版>/<リビジョン>` を案内する。
  - .NET SDK 10 は、役職によって必要なものとして表示だけする。
  - 必須の項目がすべて通ったら、`UserSettings/KillChord/ProjectSetupState.json` に `SetupVersion` を記録する。`-Check` のときは確認だけで、何も変更しない。
- **Unity**: `Assets/Editor/ProjectSetup/`（asmdef `KillChord.Editor.ProjectSetup`。参照なし・Editor 専用）
  - 他のアセンブリのコンパイルエラーに巻き込まれないよう、何も参照しない専用アセンブリにした。
  - `ProjectSetupChecker`（`[InitializeOnLoad]`、エディタ起動ごとに1回、バッチモードでは動かない）が次を確かめる。
    - 記録の `SetupVersion` が `PowerShell/ProjectSetup/project-setup.json` の値以上か
    - `.gitmodules` の各サブモジュールに中身があるか
    - Android Build Support が入っているか
    - クローン先のフォルダ名が `RepositoryFolderName` と一致するか
  - 足りなければ `ProjectSetupWindow` を開く。ボタンは「セットアップを実行」（Setup.bat を起動）・「再確認」・「閉じる」。
- 手順を増やしたら `project-setup.json` の `SetupVersion` を上げる。既存メンバーも次の起動で再実行を促される。
- README のセットアップ節を、この手順に書き直した。
- 迷子の `SS.slnx` を削除した。フォルダ名が `SS` の環境で生成され、`*.slnx` が .gitignore の対象なのに 2026-05 にコミットされたまま残っていた（最終更新 2026-07）。
- `SymphonyKillChord.slnx` の追跡もやめた（`git rm --cached`）。pull すると各自の手元のファイルが消えるが、Unity を開けば IDE 連携パッケージが作り直す。消えたままなら Unity の Preferences → External Tools の「Regenerate project files」で作り直せる。

## 確認済みの内容
- `-Check` を手元のクローンで実行した。未設定の `submodule.recurse` だけが Error になり、他は OK になった（終了コード1）。
- GitHub から新しくクローンした作業ツリー（必要なファイルだけの sparse checkout）で、修正モードを実行した。
  - `submodule.recurse` / `core.longpaths` が設定された。
  - `Assets/AssetStoreTools` が取得された。
  - `Docs/NotionSpecifications` は、仕様書リポジトリに Windows で使えないファイル名があったため checkout に失敗し、Error として表示された（この不具合は #2331 で修正）。
- Unity 側の2ファイルは dotnet build でコンパイルできた（警告なし）。
- フォルダ名の確認: `SymphonyKillChord` のフォルダでは OK、`clonetest` のフォルダでは Error になることを `-Check` で確かめた。

## 未確認・残論点
- **Unity 上での動作は未確認**（Unity を起動していない）。ウィンドウの表示、Safe Mode にならないときに専用アセンブリが読み込まれること、`.meta` の取り込みを確かめていない。
- 必須項目がすべて通ったときの `ProjectSetupState.json` の書き出しは未確認。テスト用クローンでは仕様書サブモジュールが失敗したため、最後まで通っていない。
- **マージ後、既存のメンバー全員に一度だけ警告ウィンドウが出る**（まだ Setup.bat を実行していないため）。狙いどおりだが、周知したほうがよい。
- Notion「Unity導入方法」の手順（AssetStoreTools を Drive の unitypackage で入れる）は、もうサブモジュールになっていて古い。Setup.bat 前提に直す必要がある（Notion への書き込みはまだしていない）。
- 仕様書サブモジュールの不具合（#2331）が develop に入って CI が再実行されるまでは、Setup.bat で仕様書の取得に失敗する。

ご確認いただけますと幸いです。

author: joelbondoux
body:
## Summary
- **What changed?** Local CI (the trusted-branch runner and reviewed-PR local CI) now works for repositories owned by an organisation. For those, AtlasMind pins the one account allowed to start the job by its numeric GitHub id (`github.actor_id == '<id>'`) instead of writing `github.actor == github.repository_owner`.
- **Why?** An organisation owns no account. In an org-owned repository `github.repository_owner` is the organisation's name (e.g. `Hill-To-Die-On`), which no actor's login can equal. So GitHub skipped every job before asking a runner, and the start preflight (which compared the run's actor login with the slug owner) would have refused one anyway. Found while trying to run `Hill-To-Die-On/Director-Of-Realms` CI locally while its hosted Actions runners are unavailable. That repo had hand-patched its workflows to an `actor_id` pin (its 0.10.1195), which AtlasMind's policy then refused.

Details:
- New `src/core/localCiActorGuard.ts`:
  - reads a workflow's one actor condition, with comments set aside: the owner condition, or one pinned id. It refuses both at once, two different ids, or a condition that appears only in a comment.
  - `localCiActorBlocker` decides whether an account may start the job, matching a pinned account by id (a renamed login still matches; a reclaimed login does not).
  - `lookUpLocalCiDispatcher` asks GitHub who owns the repository.
- Patcher (`/localci patch`) and **Write it for me…** pin the account signed in to GitHub CLI when an organisation owns the repo. The reviewed-PR contract stores it as `authorizedAccount` in `.atlasmind/local-ci.json`. The workflow is generated from it, so the exact-bytes managed-file check covers the pin. A malformed pin is refused, never dropped back to the owner condition. If GitHub CLI can't be asked, the patcher keeps an existing pin, or writes the owner condition and says so in the dialog.
- `prepare()` holds the queued run's actor to the reviewed file's condition (id for a pin). A reviewed-PR dispatch checks the signed-in account first, so a dispatch GitHub would skip is refused with a reason instead of timing out in the queue.
- **Personal repositories are unchanged:** generated workflows, runner and config are byte-identical to 0.482.3. I checked this by diffing generator output before and after for several inputs.

## Linked Work
- None. Surfaced by Hill-To-Die-On/Director-Of-Realms local-CI setup (its `trusted-local-ci.yml` notes "Serving an organisation-owned repository needs a change in AtlasMind itself").

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated: new `tests/core/localCiActorGuard.test.ts`, plus cases in `localCiRunner`, `localCiRepositoryPatch`, `reviewedPrLocalCi` and `trustedLocalCiStarter` (the property test now also covers pinned accounts). Red before the change. Five break probes each failed the intended tests (comments counted, owner+id accepted, id ignored, pin not written, bad pin dropped).
- [x] `npm run compile` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run test` passes: 508 files, 9,803 tests (5 skipped)
- [x] Documentation updated: `docs/local-ci-and-safe-runners.md` (new "Organisation-owned repositories" section, template note, preflight wording), `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/development.md`, `README.md` (structure + banner + what's new), `wiki/Architecture.md`, `wiki/Security.md`, `wiki/Tool-Execution.md`, `wiki/Changelog.md`. `docs/agents-and-skills.md` checked: no local-CI content, unchanged.
- [x] Security impact assessed: the authorization condition gets stricter, not wider. Exactly one actor condition is accepted, commented conditions no longer count, and a pinned account is compared by id at both dispatch and start.
- [x] `package.json` version bumped: 0.482.3 → 0.483.0 (minor: new capability)
- [x] Matching `CHANGELOG.md` entry added

## Risk and Rollback
- Risk level: Low for personal repos (byte-identical output); Medium for the new org path (new authorization branch, covered by the tests above).
- Rollback plan: revert this commit. Org repos return to the previous state, where they could not use local CI at all.

## Screenshots or Logs (if applicable)
- n/a. The VS Code command paths (`reviewedPrLocalCiCommands.ts`, dashboard starter) are not unit-tested and were not exercised in a live VS Code host.

body: ## Why Top bars weigh. A gram spec batches without guesswork, guests ask how strong a drink is, and a low-ABV menu needs the real number, not a hand-typed guess. `items.abv` was typed by hand and nothing added it up from the spec; Batch put a flat 20% water in stirred drinks only. Gap 1 of the Ethyl study (the rest of it: #148 handled grams in specs and Batch). Stacked on #153 (ethyl/service-spec) with #148 merged in; retarget to main once those merge. ## What changed - **`lib/drinkMath.ts`** (pure, with `drinkMath.check.ts`): density from the ingredient's own figure, else the name (syrups, honey, juice), else the ABV (a 40% spirit is about 0.95, so 50 g of rum is 52.7 ml); ethanol per line; ABV before dilution; dilution by method (stirred 20, shaken 25, built 10) with the venue's own defaults, the drink's measured figure first, and 0 when water is already in the spec; serve size, serve ABV and UK units; g · ml · oz conversions. `gramsPerMl` from #148 now lives here. - **Migration `20261001130000_drink_math.sql` (draft, local stack only, needs your OK before prod):** `items.density_g_ml`, `dilution_pct`, `serve_ml`, `serve_abv`, `abv_source` and `bars.dilution_defaults`. `private.refresh_drink_strength()` runs the same rules in SQL and stores `abv` (only when it was calculated or empty; a typed ABV stays), `serve_ml` and `serve_abv`; triggers call it when a spec line, an ingredient's ABV or density, the method, the drink's dilution or the venue's defaults change, and a backfill runs once. House-made ingredients with a recipe get their own ABV, which then feeds the drinks that use them. `app_item_presentation` carries the new columns, so Floor and guests see the strength without the amounts. - **Drink page:** ABV ("from the spec" or "typed in"), Serve ("after 25% water") and Serve ABV ("in the glass") in the facts. Tapping any of them (with the amounts) opens the **strength sheet** (`StrengthSheet.tsx`): each line's ml and ethanol, before and in the glass, the dilution and where it came from, and, for editors, a measured dilution field. A **g · ml · oz switch** on the spec, remembered per person (`useSettingsStore.specUnit`), puts each line's conversion and ethanol under it (`SpecRow.detail`). - **Batch** takes the drink's dilution: the venue's figure or the measured one, and bottled, carbonated and draught drinks get water in the bottle too. A spec that already has water gets none. The note says the percent it used. - **Venue settings, Dilution** (`/settings/bar/[id]/dilution`): the house figure per method, Admin only; saving recalculates every drink at the venue on the server. Linked from the bar's settings next to Publishing. - `supabase/tests/drink-math.test.mjs` (7 tests: the daiquiri figures, employee sees strength but no amounts, venue and drink dilution, ingredient ABV ripple, typed ABV kept, water in the spec, house-made ABV). vercel.json rewrite for the new route. ## How it was verified Local Supabase with the demo seeds (ingredient ABVs set), signed in as the demo Admin at Little Rye, web at 390 px and 1280 px: | Facts, phone | Spec read in grams, phone | Strength sheet, desktop | |---|---|---| | | | | | Dilution settings, desktop | Batch with the venue's dilution, phone | |---|---| | | | - Saved a stirred dilution of 22% through the settings screen and read `bars.dilution_defaults` and the recalculated `serve_ml` of the venue's stirred drinks (75 ml became 91.5 ml) back from the local database. - The Penicillin in the seeds lands at 24% before dilution and 19.2% in the glass, the same figures the check script and the server test pin. - `test:security` on this checkout's migrations: 340/340 (drink-math 7/7). `test:unit` 52/52, `check:design`, lint (0 errors, no new warnings) and typecheck clean. - iOS: not driven, for the same reason as #153 (the simulator access prompt was not answered). The new pieces are ds components already on these screens plus a Modal built like the prep Make sheet. ## CI covers typecheck, lint, check:design, test:unit (drinkMath.check.ts, batch.check.ts, spec.check.ts), test:security (drink-math.test.mjs), build:web. ## How to check it yourself Vercel preview, then open a venue drink whose ingredients have an ABV: the facts show ABV, Serve and Serve ABV; tap one for the sheet; switch the spec to g. Open Batch on a stirred drink to see the dilution line. As an Admin, the bar's settings page links to Dilution. The migration is not applied to production, so on the preview the facts stay as they were until it is; against the local stack, `supabase db reset` and load the demo seeds. **Needs approval before production:** the migration (columns, the strength function and its triggers, the view redefinition, and the one-off backfill of every drink with a spec). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
Found on the Pi 5 with gtk4-widget-factory under the #40 example.

- toplevel tiled on every edge instead of always `maximized`: still borderless, and the client's maximize button now asks for maximize (it offered restore); clients below xdg-shell v2 are still told maximized
- `WaylandToplevelController.windowState` / `ihs_wl_view_state` (`IhsWlWindowState` maximized 1, fullscreen 2): the app grants the state, typically in `onWindowRequest`; creation params carry it. An unanswered fullscreen request left GTK's F11 toggle firing fullscreen/unfullscreen bursts
- a window larger than asked (widget-factory's min width 1337 in a 1280 view) is scaled down to fit, input mapped back; its right edge (the window buttons) was cut off
- Dart: `resize` on `flutter/platform_views` when the laid-out size changes. `PlatformViewLink` only creates; nothing ever told the shell a new size, so a view never followed a layout change on hardware (mock-shell tests call the resize callback directly)

Pi 5, drm-kms-vulkan: buttons (with GTK's button layout set; this Pi's default is `appmenu:close`), maximize/restore, F11, minimize/Restore, Scale 800x600, Close all correct.

Not fixed here

author: clouddrove-ci
body:
Every app-side finding from the second audit (security, correctness, Slack copy and UX, dashboard), in one PR. Website and docs accuracy fixes are in their own repos (website #14, and a docs PR to follow).

## Security
- **Kudos:** the reason and the configurable kudos emoji were posted to Slack unescaped, so `<!channel>` or a disguised link worked. Broadcasts are now defused, labelled links show their real URL, and the emoji is validated.
- **Departed people:** dashboard sessions check that the member and installation are still active (at most once a minute). Sessions last 7 days and refresh while in use. A deactivated installer is no longer admin. MCP keys record who created them (migration 060) and stop working when that person is no longer an active admin. Bad bearer keys no longer cause a write.
- **AI summary:** defused and links neutralised before posting.
- **Visibility:** members see only standups they are in or whose channel they can see, in the standups list, reports and CSV export. Emails and private-channel membership are shown to admins only.
- **Zoom OAuth:** state is bound to the browser session and single use.
- **Workspace settings:** the manager digest email, AI settings and Jira URL need a workspace admin, not a standup admin.
- **Email and alerts:** HTML-escaped in every template, and install alerts to the operator channel are escaped.
- **Connect:** met and not-met answers are checked against match membership and team. Slots in the past or too far ahead are refused.
- **Email tokens:** the purpose is part of the HMAC. Legacy tokens still work for unsubscribe only.
- **Public feed:** the token is generated on the server and hidden from non-admins, and the feed shows only standups from public channels.
- **Rate limits:** a small in-process rate limiter covers the feed, email links, the OAuth callback and MCP auth failures. `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH` is 4 MB.

## Correctness
- **Streaks:** they were always 1. Now they count the member's scheduled working days, skip holidays, and reset after a missed day.
- **Low participation rule:** it fired before every standup. It now runs at report time for that standup, and the `participation.low` and `blocker.detected` webhooks are actually sent.
- **Analytics and reports:** they end on the team's local day, and reports use the chosen from and to dates.
- **Daily thread race:** there is no longer an orphan header. The loser adopts the stored thread and deletes its own header.
- **Sessions:** a standup session lasts 20 hours, so a late answer is not lost.
- **Members page:** the Slack user list is cached for 5 minutes and fetched with rate-limit retries.
- **Local "today":** remaining UTC uses (feed, MCP, connect, insights) now use the local day. Ruff `DTZ` is enabled for `app/src`.
- **Company holidays:** they now skip the standup DM, reminder, nudge, report and scheduled coffee rounds. Only the holiday list suppresses jobs; the default working week does not.
- **App Home changes:** pause, enable, delete and edit take effect within about 15 seconds (the scheduler polls for changed schedules). Before, the web worker called a dead copy of the scheduler.
- **Edit setting:** "until the report is posted" now works. Answers close at that standup's report time, or at the end of the day when the standup allows edits after the report. Before, it meant no limit.

## Slack copy and UX
- **Welcome DM:** no longer promises daily pings before a standup exists.
- **App Home:** one rule decides who can manage standups, both for showing the button and for the check. Other members see who to ask. "Edit my answers" edits today's answers instead of starting a new standup. The configuration modal is titled "Standup settings".
- **Create-standup modal:** it validates before closing and shows errors next to the fields, and the creator gets a DM if saving fails.
- **Help:** a single source for DM help, `/help`, the App Home help and `/morgenruf help`. References point at `/morgenruf help`.
- **Copy fixes:**
  - Coffee chat pause and resume wording is consistent, and intros name the channel they came from.
  - Celebrations copy is fixed.
  - Previous standups show only that standup.
  - One set of default questions.
  - "Time for X", and threads titled "X · Tue 29 Sep".
- **Delivery failures:** they are DMed to the installer instead of posted in the channel.
- **Plain language:** webhook and API errors, sentence-case digest subjects, and unused email senders removed.
- **Version:** `APP_VERSION` is set at build time, so the API and MCP report the real version.
- **Em dashes:** removed from user-facing Slack, manifest and email text.

## Dashboard
- **Confirmation dialogs:** publishing the public feed, turning a feature off, role changes, removing a grant, deleting a coffee chat, and discarding unsaved edits.
- **Undo toasts:** pausing, pool changes, removing a holiday, removing a question.
- **Errors:** each failed action is reported once. Celebrations and kudos have error states.
- **Empty states:** each one says what to do next, and Members has "Clear filters".
- **Consistency:** one date and time format, one participation threshold (75%), consistent coffee chat wording, correct plurals, British spelling, and a member picker instead of typing a Slack user ID.
- **Accessibility:** meaning no longer depends on colour alone, and missing values show "n/a" with a label.

## Checks
2171 backend tests pass, and ruff (now with DTZ) is clean. On the frontend, format, API check, lint, build, typecheck and 278 unit tests pass. Both e2e suites pass: 77 and 7.

## Deploy notes
- Migration 060 adds `mcp_api_keys.created_by`. Keys created before this have no creator and keep working until revoked.
- Rate limits are counted per pod.

author: saintjalon
body:
Adds `SaintTrades-RejectionBlock-Strategy.pine`, the Strategy Tester twin of the rejection block indicator merged in #7. It's built the same way as `crt_ict_strategy.pine`. `rejection_block_README.md` gains a strategy section.

## What it does
- **Same signals as the indicator.** The indicator's code decides whether and where to trade, copied unchanged:
  - levels, the rejection candle, the zone, CE and stop
  - displacement, grade and filters
  - invalidation, the 16:00 expiry and the CISD-after-tap trigger

  A diff against the indicator shows only the order handling, inputs, table and header changed.
- **Broker fills.** One entry type is traded:
  - **CE limit** or **body-edge limit** go in on the close of the bar the RB is found on.
  - **CISD after tap** sends a market order on the trigger bar's close, filled at the next bar's open.
- **Bracket.** T1 (TP1 + stop) for the partial and T2 (TP2 + stop) for the rest. It is re-sent every bar while the order works or the trade is open. T1 is never re-sent after it fills, which would otherwise open a new exit on the rest.
- **Management.**
  - 50% off at TP1, then the stop moves to breakeven.
  - Flat at 16:00 NY, with no new orders until the 18:00 roll.
  - One position at a time: working limits share one OCA group. An RB that forms during a trade gets its order once flat, if its zone is still untouched.
  - Entry window (08:30–16:00 NY), direction filter, max trades per day, daily loss limit in R.
- **Sizing and costs.** Auto size is 2 MNQ or 1 NQ; there's also fixed contracts or risk %. Costs are Topstep MNQ commission ($0.61/side), 1 tick of slippage and margin 0, matching the CRT strategy.
- **Table.** R from broker fills after costs: expectancy, net R, win rate, TP1 hit rate, profit factor, longest losing streak, today, and results by grade. Labels show each trade's R; a skipped RB's tooltip says why it wasn't traded.

## Testing
- Syntax passes the `pynescript` parser.
- Runs end to end in PineTS's strategy engine on synthetic data, with no runtime errors, across:
  - all three entries
  - opposing-liquidity TP2 and "Never" expiry
  - risk sizing, direction filter, 0% and 100% partial, 3 fixed contracts, no breakeven, no loss limit
  - required displacement and minimum grade A+
  - 1m→5m, 1m→15m and 15m→1H

  In every run, orders filled = trades closed = broker trades, and nothing was left open.
- Known-answer scenarios, calculated by hand first:

  | Scenario | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Bearish PDH sweep, CE limit | Filled at 100.5, TP1 97, breakeven, TP2 93.5 → +1.32R after costs |
  | Same, body-edge limit | 98 → 92 / 86 → +1.39R |
  | Same, CISD after tap | Market at the 19:25 open, TP1 89.9, TP2 82.85 → +1.41R |
  | Open at 16:00 | TP1, then the rest flattened at the 16:00 open → +0.96R |
  | Bullish mirror | Same result as the bearish case |

- **Random-data check.** With same-bar exits ruled out, random prices give −0.08R to +0.11R over 16–30 trades, and CISD entries give −0.19R. Those are no-edge numbers, as they should be.
  - PineTS's emulator can fill a TP1 on the entry bar before the entry itself, which inflates results. That's a test-engine quirk, so PineTS was used to check logic only.
- **Bugs the tests caught and fixed:**
  - Two orders filling on the same bar could leave one trade unbooked.
  - CISD market orders sent with `limit=na` never filled in PineTS; they now go in as plain market orders.
  - PineTS dropped exits sent only once before the entry fills; brackets are now re-sent every bar.
- **Not yet compiled in TradingView.** TradingView was blocked from the build environment. The first compile and Strategy Tester run still need to happen in the Pine editor; the README has a validation checklist.

body:
## Summary

`compare` checks the live site and then the copy in the same browser tab. When it leaves the live site, many sites send a last analytics ping, and `compare` counted those pings as requests made by the copy.

Every Substack page failed this way: "copy requested 2 external host(s): substack.com, www.derekthompson.org". Loaded on its own, the copy makes no outside requests at all.

The fix loads a blank page between the live site and the copy, so the pings go out while nothing is listening.

## Testing

- New test: a live page that pings as you leave is no longer blamed on the copy. It fails without the fix.
- New test: a copy that really does load something from the live site is still caught.
- On a real Substack capture, the false failure is gone.
- `npx vitest run` and `tsc --noEmit` pass. One unrelated cleanup test failed once under full-suite load and passes on its own.

author: nitjsefnie
body:
## Summary
A service stop during a long single-statement ingest phase (the reprice clean restamp, a rollup rebuild) now aborts the run instead of leaving its row unfinished and its statement running past exit; forked parse workers no longer outlive the service holding its port, database sessions and the ingest advisory lock; and a run whose advisory-lock session dies mid-run stops as an abort instead of continuing unlocked.

## Related Issues and Pull Requests
Fixes #372
Fixes #373
Fixes #374

## Changes
- Lifespan teardown (`backend/app.py`) cancels the viz pool's in-flight statements right after the abort request (`backend/db.py`: checkout registry in `viz_conn`, new `cancel_viz_queries`); the run classifies the driver's QueryCanceled raised under the shutdown request as the abort arriving (`ingest._shutdown_cancel`), and when the bounded wait still times out, teardown closes the open `ingest_runs` row itself (`ingest_runs.close_open_run`, writing only a still-open row) — a stop never leaves `finished_at` NULL.
- The parse process pool's initializer (`ingest_fetch.parse_worker_init`) restores SIGTERM/SIGINT to SIG_DFL, arms prctl PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (best-effort), and exits any worker whose parent is not the one that forked it; an abort also cancels the pools' queued work. Forked workers die with the service instead of holding its port, sessions and ingest lock.
- `backend/ingest_lockwatch.py` (new): `_db_run_lock` arms a one-slot guard with the lock connection; the bounded steps consult `check_lock_alive()`, which aborts the run (`IngestAborted("lost ingest lock")`, recorded in the row's error text) when the advisory-lock session died or no longer holds the lock. The abort cause now rides the IngestAborted message into the row's error.
- Size split: the listing scan moved to `backend/ingest_scan.py` (seam-preserving), so `ingest.py` stays under its baseline entry; `.github/ci-thresholds.json`'s entry tightened 735→676 via the loader's own writer — **this PR is a gate-definer** (rule 14) and merges in a manager window.

## Testing
Full `pytest tests/ -q` green against a private Postgres (2889 tests, incl. 14 new: lost-lock abort, dead-session bounded-step check, cancelled-statement-closes-aborted, fallback row close idempotence, teardown cancel of an in-flight pg_sleep, parse-worker SIG_DFL/SIGTERM-death/orphan-exit, plus review-pinned guards: queued persist half cancelled on abort, QueryCanceled without a shutdown closes fatal, live-but-unlocked session aborts). pylint, pycodestyle, pyright, eslint, secrecy-check clean. End-to-end on a private instance: SIGTERM mid clean-restamp (800k-row corpus) → run row closed `aborted: shutdown requested`, statement cancelled, fast exit. New tests proven red on unfixed code before the fix.

## Footer
Generated by GLM-5.3-Flash (implementation, verification, review)

Moves the normal outbound transport toward Stalwart without changing production behavior yet.

Changes:
- Adds `OUTBOUND_RELAY=stalwart` as a supported production relay.
- Adds a Stalwart JMAP relay that submits the already-persisted Stalwart Email object via `EmailSubmission/set`.
- Keeps the existing GSW queue/undo/retry flow: the worker still runs after the undo window, but the transport can now be Stalwart instead of Resend.

- Adds config coverage proving Stalwart relay does not require `RESEND_API_KEY`.

Production remains on Resend until `OUTBOUND_RELAY` is switched after service-account JMAP access is verified.

author: ryanduguid
body:
## Summary

A failed `execute()` can leave rows and metadata from the previous statement available to callers. Clear the existing result fields after closing the previous query handle, before binding parameters or sending the next statement. The update incorporates main through `ac1406e`, including the fetch-page error, CALL/NULL decoding and connection recovery fixes.

```text
close previous handle -> clear old result and held page error -> bind and send
failed close          -> retain buffered result and held page error
undecodable new reply -> retain its newly opened handle for cleanup
```

## Changes

- Move the existing reset in both cursor implementations, including `_page_error`; preserve paging, generation checks, async handle ownership and INSERT identity handling.
- Keep the original failure cases and add seven cases combining a real packet-decoding page error with failed re-execution, failed close or cancellation. Bound the cancellation await with `wait_for` while retaining the `CancelledError` assertion.
- Synchronise the English and Korean API references, changelog and PATCH classification, then regenerate the documentation aggregate.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation update

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the project's style.
- [x] Ran `make check-all` and `make test` on the integrated source.
- [x] Added regressions and reproduced them on untouched pinned-main production code.
- [x] Updated the affected behaviour and API documentation.
- [x] Synchronised the Korean API reference; README translations are unchanged.
- [x] Recorded limitations and remaining checks below.

## Validation Evidence

Linux WSL, Python 3.13.15, CUBRID 11.4.6.1963, pinned main `ac1406e`:

- Untouched pinned main passes 2,829 offline tests with 97.63% coverage. Adding the page-error interaction tests gives five failures and two passing close-preservation controls. All four live SQL/binding regressions also fail on the pinned base.
- The integrated source passes 2,851 offline tests and 251 subtests, with nine skips, one expected failure and 97.65% coverage. All 152 focused cases pass.
- All four live SQL/binding regressions pass. The regular live suite passes 551 cases, skips 51 and fails two invalid UTF-8 cases. Untouched pinned main passes 547 cases and reproduces the same two failures: `test_invalid_value_raises_data_error[sync]` and `[async]`, both reporting `DID NOT RAISE DataError`.
- `make check-all`, all pre-commit hooks, the public API check, changelog check and strict documentation build pass. The build has the same 202 informational link messages as pinned main. Regeneration matches the staged files, and the root index matches its canonical source byte for byte.
- Aikido scanned all five changed Python files. Its five findings concern unchanged guarded procedure-name formatting and an internal assertion. No finding occurs in the changed code; no suppression or unrelated repair was made.

## Merge danger

The change is reversible and affects ordinary cursor execution. Fetching after a failed replacement statement now raises the existing no-result-set `InterfaceError`. A failed close retains buffered results and their page error, subject to connection invalidation or reconnect handling. An undecodable replacement reply can still open a new handle that must stay tracked for cleanup. INSERT identity-cache handling is unchanged.

## Unverified

The full live suite is not green because of the two failures also reproduced on pinned main. The offline replay case for #551 is an unchanged expected failure on both trees. Other Python, operating system and CUBRID versions; the skipped offline and live cases; CUBRIDdb differential, Docker broker-control, EUC-KR, slow and TLS lanes; distribution builds and installed-package checks for this updated tree; upstream CI remain unverified. Transport and cancellation regressions use mocked connections with real cursor methods; page-error interactions use real packet decoding. `wait_for` is a cooperative timeout and does not guarantee a hard deadline. Whether the updated head clears the public CodeQL annotation remains unverified.

## Related Issues

Addresses #373. The reset retains the close-before-clear boundary used by the merged batch fix in #380.
