author: manhpv-3661
body:
## Vấn đề và behavior sau thay đổi

Trước PR này, 5 route auth công khai không có giới hạn nào: kẻ tấn công có thể thử mật khẩu không giới hạn ở `POST /auth/login`, spam mail reset vào hộp thư người khác ở `POST /auth/forgot-password` (dù `api-requirements.csv` đã ghi AUTH-04 trả `429 vượt rate limit`), và mọi response đều lộ `X-Powered-By: Express`, không có security header nào.

Sau PR:

- `register`, `verify-email`, `login`, `forgot-password`, `reset-password` bị giới hạn theo **IP** (mặc định 20 request/60s) và theo **email trong body** (mặc định 10 request/900s), mỗi route có ngân sách riêng. Vượt ngưỡng trả `429`, message i18n và header `Retry-After` chuẩn. **Đúng mật khẩu nhưng đã vượt ngưỡng vẫn bị chặn.**
- Mọi response có security header của `helmet`, không còn `X-Powered-By`.
- Client không còn tự đặt được `X-Request-ID` tuỳ ý để giả mạo trường trong log.

## Requirement

- Requirement/bug IDs: AUTH-03 (đăng nhập), AUTH-04 (`429 vượt rate limit` cho forgot-password); mục "rate-limit review" trong `docs/process/release-checklist.md`; CODING_STANDARD mục 14 đã ghi rate limiting/security header là việc "làm ở pull riêng về hardening".
- Acceptance criteria đã xử lý:
  - Vượt ngưỡng theo email hoặc theo IP → `429` + `Retry-After`; hết cửa sổ thì dùng lại được.
  - Email được chuẩn hoá (trim + lowercase) trước khi đếm nên đổi cách viết không né được.
  - `X-Forwarded-For` giả không né được giới hạn theo IP (mặc định không tin proxy).
  - Redis lỗi không làm login trả `500`.
  - Log đúng một dòng ở lần vượt ngưỡng đầu tiên của mỗi cửa sổ, không chứa email.
- Ngoài phạm vi PR: CAPTCHA hoặc khoá tài khoản bằng DB/backoff luỹ tiến, rate limit toàn API, chỉ đếm lần đăng nhập thất bại, anti-cache header (Sunlint S037), CORS, rate limit cho WebSocket.

## Thay đổi kỹ thuật

- API/module:
  - Module hạ tầng mới `src/rate-limit/` (phẳng, cùng kiểu `redis/`): `RateLimitModule`, `RateLimitGuard`, decorator `@RateLimited()` (tự khai `429` trong Swagger), `FailOpenThrottlerStorage`, `buildThrottlerOptions()`. `AuthController` chỉ gắn `@RateLimited()` lên 5 route (không gắn `logout`).
  - `configureApp()` thêm `helmet` và `trust proxy`; `RedisModule` export thêm `REDIS_CLIENT`; `RequestIdMiddleware` chỉ nhận `x-request-id` khớp `[\w.:-]{1,64}`.
  - i18n en/vi: `errors.tooManyRequests`. Biến môi trường mới trong Joi schema, `.env.example`, `.env.test`.
  - Dependency mới: `@nestjs/throttler` 6.7.1, `@nest-lab/throttler-storage-redis` 1.2.0 (MIT, chỉ phụ thuộc `tslib`, maintainer npm `jmcdo29`), `helmet` 8.3.0 (MIT).
- Database/migration: không có, không đổi entity.
- Queue/file/integration: bộ đếm nằm ở Redis qua Lua script của `@nest-lab/throttler-storage-redis`, dùng chung `REDIS_CLIENT` nên không mở thêm connection. Key được băm SHA-256 nên email không nằm dạng rõ trong Redis.
- Security/RBAC/ownership:
  - Hai bộ đếm `ip` và `account` chạy song song; `account` tự bỏ qua route không mang email (`verify-email`, `reset-password`).
  - Redis lỗi thì cho request đi qua và ghi `warn` (`login`/`register`/`forgot-password` không phụ thuộc Redis, không để rate limit làm chúng ngừng hoạt động).
  - `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` mặc định `0`: `X-Forwarded-For` do client gửi bị bỏ qua (có e2e chứng minh).
  - Helmet giữ CSP mặc định (Swagger UI vẫn chạy, đã kiểm bằng Edge); chỉ đổi `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` thành `cross-origin` để web frontend khác origin nhúng được ảnh sản phẩm.
  - Sửa lỗi có sẵn phát hiện khi làm log mới: `x-request-id` từ client trước đây đi vào log nguyên văn nên giả mạo được các trường khác trong dòng log; nay ID không hợp lệ bị thay bằng UUID.
  - Log không chứa email; log của guard chỉ ghi route, IP, giới hạn, cửa sổ và `requestId`.
- Performance/query: không có query DB. Mỗi request tới 5 route trên tốn thêm 1 lệnh Redis `EVAL` cho mỗi bộ đếm (tối đa 2), các route khác không bị ảnh hưởng. Log chỉ ghi ở request đầu tiên vượt ngưỡng của cửa sổ để không ngập log khi bị tấn công.

## Kiểm chứng

```text
npm run lint:check         → pass (0 warning)
npx prettier --check .     → pass
npm run build              → pass
npm run test:cov           → 385/385 pass (51 suites); src/rate-limit 100% statements/branches/functions/lines
npm run test:e2e           → 228/228 pass (18 suites); 16 test mới:
                             rate-limit 10, rate-limit-window 1, rate-limit-untrusted-proxy 1, security-headers 4
npm run lint:sunlint       → 0 errors (263 warning); file mới chỉ có C014/C035/S056, đã ghi lý do ở CODING_STANDARD mục 14
migration:generate         → không áp dụng (không đổi entity)
```

Test case quan trọng (unit + e2e trên Redis/PostgreSQL thật):

- Login: 3 lần sai rồi lần 4 bị `429` kể cả đúng mật khẩu, kèm `Retry-After` 1..60; email viết hoa hoặc có khoảng trắng đếm chung một tài khoản; email khác không bị ảnh hưởng; một IP thử nhiều email bị chặn ở lần thứ 6; message tiếng Việt qua `Accept-Language: vi`.
- forgot-password: 3 lần `202` rồi `429`; ngân sách tách riêng khỏi login; register cũng bị giới hạn theo email; verify-email chỉ bị giới hạn theo IP.
- Cửa sổ hết hạn: TTL cấu hình bằng giây thật sự thành cửa sổ đúng thời gian (chặn trong cửa sổ, cho qua ngay sau khi hết).
- Proxy không tin cậy: đổi `X-Forwarded-For` mỗi request vẫn bị chặn ở lần thứ 4 (IP limit = 3).
- Guard: `Retry-After` chuẩn, log đúng một lần, log không chứa email, fail-open khi store lỗi.
- Header: helmet có mặt trên response thường và lỗi 404, không có `X-Powered-By`; `x-request-id` hợp lệ được giữ, chuỗi giả mạo bị thay bằng UUID.

Về lần chạy e2e: một lần chạy đầy đủ trước đó có **1 test fail** ở `order-lifecycle.e2e-spec.ts` (ORDER-02, "only returns orders owned by the current customer") mà không lưu được chi tiết lỗi; chạy riêng spec đó pass 19/19 và chạy lại toàn bộ pass 228/228. Chưa xác định được nguyên nhân, code của test đó không liên quan tới thay đổi trong PR này, nên ghi lại để reviewer biết chứ không kết luận là flake.

Bằng chứng thao tác tay qua Swagger UI và `curl`: khung hướng dẫn ở `docs/testing/pr20-manual-test-guide.md`; **evidence chạy tay chưa đính kèm**, sẽ bổ sung trước khi xin merge.

`npm audit` (dependencies production) báo 6 lỗ hổng mức moderate ở package có sẵn (multer, platform-express, swagger, js-yaml, exceljs, uuid); ba package mới không thêm cảnh báo nào. Không xử lý trong PR này.

## Release và rủi ro

- Config/secret mới: `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` (mặc định 0), `THROTTLE_AUTH_IP_LIMIT`/`_IP_TTL_SECONDS`/`_ACCOUNT_LIMIT`/`_ACCOUNT_TTL_SECONDS` (mặc định 20/60/10/900), đều có default nên không bắt buộc đặt. Không có secret. `.env.test` nâng trần lên 100000 để e2e không tự chặn mình; CI lấy giá trị này từ `.env.test`.
- Backward compatibility: response mất `X-Powered-By` và có thêm security header; `login`, `forgot-password`, `register`, `verify-email`, `reset-password` giờ có thể trả `429`; `x-request-id` không hợp lệ bị thay bằng UUID. Không đổi body hay status của các trường hợp bình thường.
- Deploy/migration order: không có migration. **Khi deploy Railway (PR19) phải đặt `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS`** (dự kiến `1`, chưa xác nhận số hop thật). Để `0` sau proxy làm mọi client dùng chung một IP nên giới hạn 20 request/phút theo IP thành giới hạn cho cả hệ thống; đặt cao hơn số proxy thật thì client giả được IP. Cần kiểm `req.ip` qua log sau khi deploy.
- Rollback/forward-fix: revert PR là đủ; các key đếm trong Redis tự hết hạn theo TTL.
- Known limitations:
  - Bộ đếm theo email tính mọi request, không chỉ lần thất bại, và theo email toàn cục: kẻ biết email nạn nhân có thể khoá đăng nhập của họ tối đa 15 phút (đánh đổi thường gặp).
  - Nhiều người sau cùng một NAT dùng chung IP nên dùng chung ngân sách 20 request/phút theo IP.
  - Khi Redis chết, giới hạn tạm thời không có hiệu lực (fail-open, đã chọn có chủ đích).
  - Khi demo bằng Swagger có thể chạm `429` (10 request/15 phút cho mỗi email); nâng các biến `THROTTLE_*` nếu cần.
  - Chưa kiểm Swagger trên Safari với `http://localhost` (CSP mặc định có `upgrade-insecure-requests`); cloud dùng HTTPS nê

body:
## Problem

Part of #128799 (open). PM-generated runtime workspaces omit non-package resources. This PR preserves the shipped plugin/MCP catalogs and bundled/optional skills; it does **not** claim to resolve the issue's locale symptom.

## Root cause

`pm.workspace._copy_core_inputs` gates directories on setuptools package roots. The runtime readers resolve these resource directories beside the generated code, but they are deliberately not Python packages. Consequently the plugin and MCP catalogs become empty, `OptionalSkillSource.list_local()` loses shipped skills, and `sync_skills()` cannot seed bundled skills in a fresh home.

## Change

Retain `plugin-catalog/`, `optional-mcps/`, `skills/`, and `optional-skills/` in the existing copy branch. Preserve exclusions, symlink handling, copy-error propagation, wildcard behavior, consumer fallbacks, and caller-selected resource overrides. No new environment variable, loader fallback, or dependency.

The original plugin-catalog increment was followed by MCP retention (`32f275cb671062928a070037ee55e19bff0b90f1`) and skill retention (`c61c02da67d37fbf6cc3ff70d93ee3c20b617d55`) on this same PR.

## Verification

Native Windows; product imports/runs used temporary HOME, USERPROFILE, HERMES_HOME, APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA. No installation, production state, or service restart.

- Original plugin-catalog RED at `7b384285fa281d0d843cddf4f00c243b92f44b60`: **1 failed, 2 passed**.
- MCP RED at freshly fetched main `bddd22be7c2e5f7630c3d90507e6e7280ff092e3`: **2 failed, 2 passed**.
- Skills RED on that same current main: **4 failed, 4 passed**. Exact failures: bundled seeding returns `[]`, optional catalog returns `[]`, and omitted resources never reach their copy errors. Wildcard controls already pass.
- Focused GREEN at current head: **16 passed** across the three snapshot-resource files.
- Broader skills/snapshot suites: **160 passed, 1 skipped**, including real skill synchronization and hub behavior. Boundary coverage includes local fetch, missing-skill remote fallback preservation, configured overrides, user customization retention, absent resources, exclusions, and copy exceptions.
- Fresh-interpreter integration against an actual generated checkout snapshot, using default resolvers with no resource overrides: **152 optional catalog entries**, **148 locally vendored skill bundles fetched offline**, and **58 bundled skills seeded into a fresh temporary home**. Repeat sync seeds nothing again. Module origins were verified inside the snapshot; network was denied in the consumer process.
- Earlier real snapshot integrations verified the plugin entry/removal-list readers and all **65 MCP catalog entries**. The sparse checkout was materialized before the full-resource runs; no dependencies were installed.
- Known adjacent prerequisite blocker: the legacy workspace-member test requires unavailable `tomli_w`; that leg is **not** claimed green.
- Codex CLI 0.153.4 (`gpt-5.6-sol`), exact head `c61c02da67d37fbf6cc3ff70d93ee3c20b617d55`: **STATIC PASS**.
- Claude Code 2.1.280 / Opus 5.5 exact-head review: **blocked/pending**. Both the preceding-head and exact `c61c02da67d37fbf6cc3ff70d93ee3c20b617d55` attempts returned repeated service HTTP503 and timed out. This is not a second-engine PASS; retry after the recorded cooldown.

Commands used the existing interpreter via `HERMES_PYTHON` and `bash scripts/run_tests.sh`:

```text
tests/pm/test_workspace_skill_resources.py -q                         # RED on isolated current main

 tests/pm/test_workspace_mcp_resources.py
 tests/pm/test_workspace_skill_resources.py -q                         # broader coverage
```

## Ownership / remaining acceptance / continuation decision

Full issue/PR comments and timelines, four semantic search groups, owner-function follow-up, and fresh pre-push checks found no pre-existing implementation of the selected skill-retention contract. Actual related diffs were inspected in qualification:

- **Delivered here:** plugin catalog/removal list, MCP discovery, bundled skill seeding, and local optional-skill discovery/fetch in new workspaces.
- **Already on main:** nested `pm/uv.lock` retention; unchanged.
- **External owner:** #128803 handles `locales/`, not these resources. #122460 handles source refresh/install metadata, not missing resource inclusion. Shared files are partial overlap, not duplicate behavior.
- **Excluded:** old-generation repair, TUI/web built outputs, resource-policy redesign, and new remote/download/install behavior.

**Continuation decision: continued on this PR** through two independently verified same-root increments. Catalog/skills coverage is now complete for the chosen boundary; remaining work is exact-head second-engine review and any substantiated findings. Do not absorb the locale or refresh owners or merely copy unverified TUI build outputs. This remains **Part of #128799**, not Fixes.

author: kayceesrk
body:
Adds `MMTK::is_collection_requested()`, which reads `GCTrigger`'s request flag.

The flag is set before a user-requested collection is scheduled (`GCTrigger::request`) and cleared in `notify_mutators_paused`, after the binding's `stop_all_mutators` has returned. A binding whose `block_for_gc` waits on its own "pause active" state can use this to cover the interval between the request and `stop_all_mutators`: without it, `block_for_gc` can return before the requested collection has started, so a VM-level "collect now" call comes back with the collection still to run.

The load is `Relaxed`; a binding orders it against its own pause state, for example by reading it under the lock its `stop_all_mutators` takes.

Two small additions, no behaviour change in mmtk-core itself: `src/mmtk.rs`, `src/util/heap/gc_trigger.rs`.

Needed by ocaml-mmtk to make `Gc.major` / `Gc.full_major` / `Gc.compact` / `Gc.minor` return after their collection (its ROADMAP open item 22). Verified there: with the binding change, the collection counters move before the call returns on GenImmix, Immix, StickyImmix, SemiSpace, GenCopy, ConcurrentImmix, Bactrian and LXR, native and bytecode; full ocaml-mmtk testsuite runs on the combined change: GenImmix 1448 passed / 0 failed, debug runtime 1448 / 0, Immix 1448 / 0, Bactrian 1448 / 0 (macOS arm64).

body:
## Summary

What o3co/auth.provider#762, #768 and #769 did for the provider, done here: comments state what holds now, not history. The E2E tests, the compose file, the provider fixtures, the Dockerfiles, the Makefile and the workflows said why a setting or an assertion exists by citing the component issue that changed it or the release it landed in. They now say it in terms of what each component does, checked against the component at the revision the Makefile pins (and at its develop where it differs).

Only comments change.

## Passes

- [x] **Comments state what holds now** (b3175e4). Issue and pull request numbers, versions a change landed in and "used to" go. The "Old and new names" block keeps the state it describes: both names are set until `PROVIDER_REV` pins a provider that reads only the new ones.
- [x] **Comments agree with the components** (23882b9, d45eee1, b784955). Among the corrections:
  - `/authorize` admits only first-party clients because this rig configures no consent store; with one, another client goes through the consent page.
  - The provider requires PKCE of every authorization-code client and accepts only S256 unless a registration sets `allowPlainPkce`, which none here does.
  - The Dockerfiles' frozen installs refuse a workspace file whose `overrides` differ from the lockfile's; `onlyBuiltDependencies` is not in the lockfile, so without it the provider install passes and skips bcrypt's install script. The `npmrc` build secret mounts the host's `~/.npmrc` without writing it into a layer; nothing resolves from GitHub Packages.
  - `typ` is all that keeps a refresh token out of `/verify`, so a relaxed `at+jwt` pin is caught by the refresh-token test and the hand-signed `typ` case; the id_token is refused for its `typ` first, and its audience (the client id) would refuse it too.
  - The scopeless ABAC case is refused by the scope rule (`invalid_scope`), not by an empty rule set.
  - The login JSDoc states the provider's current CSRF rule (a same-origin or trusted `Origin`), not one it was to adopt.

Comment lines (`//`, `/*`, `*` and `#` in the JavaScript, YAML, HOCON, Dockerfiles and Makefile): 729 → 699.

## How to check

- JavaScript: `comment-only-diff.cjs` from o3co/auth.provider#762's description — no code change.
- YAML: every changed document parses to equal values at the base and at the head.
- Makefile, Dockerfiles and `tests/abac/application.conf`: the lines that are not comments are unchanged.
- The pins (`PROVIDER_REV`, `VERIFIER_REV`, `PROXY_REV`) do not move. `test-e2e` passes.

Reviewed before publishing by two reviewers, one of them adversarial (it tries to falsify each rewritten claim against the pinned component source, and ran pnpm to check the frozen-install claims), and the fix commits again; every finding was checked against the source and applied, Minor ones included.

## Found along the way, not changed here

- `tests/dockerfiles/provider.Dockerfile`'s hand-maintained package list has no line for `packages/mfa`, which provider develop has and the pin does not. The develop template does not depend on it yet, so the nightly develop run still passes; the line belongs with the pin bump that brings the package in.
- When `PROVIDER_REV` moves past o3co/auth.provider#786 (the old variable name alone refuses boot), the compose comment that a renamed setting "would fall back to its default silently" needs rewording.

- `docs/claims-contract.md` still calls `typ` the only discriminator between the three token kinds, which the corrected test comments no longer say of the id_token; `docs/` is outside this PR.

## Not in this PR

- Values, variable names, recipe lines, test names and `docs/`.

author: nkramber
body:
PR-26, Stage B of the mobile proposal, narrowed by the owner's answer to OQ-67 (D-1004): a web push through Firebase Cloud Messaging, with one event. When a deck build ends after the user left the page, each device that opted in gets a notification, and a tap opens the deck. The email digest, the legality event, and the new-cards event wait for later pull requests.

## Session

- Role: author
- Branch: `feat/return-channels`
- Base: `b0a44cd`

## What changes

- **Proto.** `proto/mtg/v1/push_service.proto` adds `PushService`: `RegisterDevice`, `UnregisterDevice`, `GetDevice`. A device is a Firebase Installation ID. Both SDKs deprecate the token path (D-1005).
- **Store and sender.** `go/internal/push` keeps the devices under `users/<uid>/push_devices`, at most 10 for each user, oldest out. `FCM.Send` sends a data message by `Fid`. A device that Cloud Messaging calls unregistered leaves the store.
- **Trigger.** `agentsvc.storeDeck` calls `WithPush` after it stores the deck, only when the stream context is done. So a user who reads the stream gets no push. A revised deck counts as a finished build.
- **Wiring.** `go/cmd/api/main.go` mounts `PushService`, and it turns on the sender on Cloud Run alone.
- **Web.** The account menu gets "Notify me when a deck is ready" (owner choice). `web/apps/web/src/features/push/push.ts` asks for the permission before its first await, because Safari needs the gesture. A sign-out removes the device, and each start refreshes it. `web/apps/web/public/push-handler.js` joins the PR-25 worker through workbox `importScripts`, so the app keeps one worker. It shows each push and keeps a tap on the app.
- **Build.** `cloudbuild/web.yaml` and the fallback `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` pass `VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID`, the project number. With no sender id, the app shows no toggle.
- **Emulator lane.** `go/internal/push` joins the CI Firestore step and `make store-check`.

author: nicolasrufino
body:
## Summary
These are the five backend items from the codebase audit. Implementation by Codex, reviewed and adjusted by me.

1. **Upload type check on the server.** Previously only the browser limited types. Now the file extension **and** its magic bytes must match an allowed type: resumes accept PDF/DOCX/DOC, and event materials accept PDF/PPTX/PPT/DOCX/PNG/JPEG. The stored MIME is normalized, and filenames with control characters are rejected.
   - *Review change:* the browser's claimed MIME is no longer part of the check. It's unreliable (`.docx` often arrives as `application/octet-stream` on machines without Office), and extension plus contents is the real proof. Added a test for that case.
2. **Safe download filenames.** New `lib/content-disposition.ts` sends an ASCII fallback plus an RFC 5987 `filename*` and strips quotes, backslashes and control characters, so a quote in a filename can't break the download.
3. **No caching of resumes and materials.** Downloads now send `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `nosniff`.
4. **Notifications are best-effort.** A failed notification after a post, material or speaker update is logged instead of returning 500 after the save, which used to cause duplicate posts on retry.
5. **Size limits.** Posts are capped at 5,000 characters, matching the frontend's `maxLength`. Form answers must be a plain object of at most 50 KB.

No schema, migration, auth, cookie or env changes.

## Note
Event materials used to accept any file type. They're now limited to the types above; say if the board needs others, like `.xlsx` or `.key`.

## Test plan
- `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass: 329 passed, 21 DB tests skipped locally and run in CI.
- New tests cover magic-byte spoofing (HTML claiming PDF), each accepted format, `.docx` arriving as `octet-stream`, hostile and unicode filenames, the post length limit, a failed notification still returning success, and the form payload cap.

author: urassh
body:
## 目的・変更

README に「Web フロントを足す場合は `frontend/`」とだけ書かれていた枠を実装で埋める。
**iOS と同じレイヤ分け・同じダミー接続の仕組み**にしてあるので、片方を読めばもう片方も読める。

構成: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4 + TanStack Query + React Router (SPA)

```
frontend/src/
  app/       Provider の組み立てと DI 登録 (container.ts だけが data/ を知る)
  core/      config / connection / tokenStore / repositories / session
  domain/    エンティティと Repository の型。何にも依存しない
  data/      apiClient・レコード型・API 実装・ダミー実装・OpenAPI 生成型
  feature/   画面 (auth / users / shared)
```

- 依存の向きは `app → feature → core → domain ← data`。**DI の登録は `app/container.ts` だけ**で、画面は `useRepositories()` で型だけを見る
- **ダミー接続を dev の既定にした**。backend を立てずにログイン〜一覧〜更新〜削除まで動く。切り替えはログイン画面 / ヘッダの「接続先」(dev のみ表示) で、選択は localStorage に残る。JWT は接続先ごとに別のキーで持つ
- 通信の口は `data/apiClient.ts` だけ。失敗は全部 `DomainError` に畳む。ログイン系はトークンがレスポンスヘッダで返るので `sendReceivingToken`
- サーバー由来の状態は TanStack Query が唯一の持ち主。ログイン状態も `me` クエリのキャッシュなので Context の Provider は置かない

周辺の配線:

- `web` は **`compose.override.yaml` にだけ**置いた。base の `compose.yaml` には入れていないので、`infra/` 経由の Lightsail デプロイ (`compose.yaml` + `infra/compose.deploy.yaml`) には含まれない
- `Makefile`: `front-logs` / `front-sh` / `front-lint` / `front-build` / `front-types`
- `Dockerfile` は dev(Vite) / builder / runtime(nginx, SPA フォールバック) の3段
- 規約は `.claude/docs/frontend.md`。README / AGENTS.md / docs/project.md も更新

## 仕様・接続への影響

- **API・DB の変更なし**。`backend/` は 1 行も触っていないので、Swagger の再生成も不要 (`make front-types` で再生成しても `frontend/src/data/generated/api.ts` に差分なしを確認済み)
- **環境変数 (新規)**: `VITE_API_ENDPOINT` (既定 `http://localhost:3000`)、`VITE_CONNECTION` (`dummy` | `api`)。ひな形は `frontend/.env.example`、読むのは `core/config.ts` だけ。`VITE_` で始まる値はビルド時にバンドルへ埋め込まれるので秘密は置かない
- **iOS への影響なし**
- **CI**: `frontend` ジョブを追加 (lint / build=型チェック込み / 生成型の鮮度)。既存の backend の 2 ジョブは、トップレベルの `defaults.run.working-directory: backend` を job 単位へ移しただけで挙動は変えていない
- **Docs**: Google Docs URL は未設定のままなので、Docs 確認は行っていない。本 PR は README の既存方針 (「`frontend/` として直下に並べる」) を根拠にしている

## 確認結果

`npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` はいずれも成功。

加えて、ローカルの Chrome を headless + CDP で動かして実ブラウザで通した (使い捨てスクリプトなのでリポジトリには入れていない)。

- ダミー接続: ログイン → 一覧 → 詳細 → 更新が一覧へ反映 → 削除が一覧へ反映 → ログアウト
- 実 API (`make up` した backend): ログイン → 一覧 → トークン保存
- 壊れたトークン: ログイン画面へ戻し、トークンを破棄
- console のエラーは、意図的に壊したトークンによる 401 のみ

API 契約は curl でも確認した。CORS preflight が通り、`Authorization` が expose され、`POST /api/v1/login` のヘッダのトークンで `/api/v1/me` と `/api/v1/users` が 200。エラー形 (`{error}` / `{errors}`) も実装の想定どおり。

Docker: dev イメージのビルド、nginx イメージで `/` と `/users/1` が 200 (SPA フォールバック)、`VITE_API_ENDPOINT` がバンドルに埋まることを確認。`make front-types` / `make front-lint` もコンテナ経由で実行できることを確認。

この過程で実装バグを1つ見つけて直した。ログアウト時に `localStorage` を読むだけでは React が再描画せず画面が切り替わらなかったので、`tokenStore` を購読可能にして `useSyncExternalStore` で見るようにした (別タブのログイン / ログアウトにも追従する)。

新規テストは追加していない (AGENTS.md の方針)。CI の結果はまだ見ていない。

## 残課題

- **web のデプロイ先は未配線**。`infra/` は API だけを載せる構成なので、公開するなら `Dockerfile` の `runtime` ステージをどこかに載せるか、`dist/` を静的ホスティングに置く (`.claude/docs/frontend.md` に記載)
- `typescript` は `~5.9` に固定した。TS 7 だと `typescript-eslint` の peer (`>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`) が解決できずインストールが通らないため。対応後に上げられる
- トークンは localStorage に置いている (XSS で読める)。ハッカソンの土台として割り切った。本番に持っていくなら httpOnly Cookie + CSRF 対策へ寄せる旨をコードのコメントに残した
- 画面は `users` の CRUD のみ。実プロダクトの機能は載せていない

author: gurajani-aws
body:
## Summary
NVIDIA/AMD GPU families in `modernization_mapping` mapped their Graviton target to `g5g` (Graviton2 + NVIDIA T4G). T4G is not a like-for-like substitute for A10G (`g5`), L4 (`g6`), L40S (`g6e`), or the AMD Radeon Pro in `g4ad`. As a result these families were reported as Graviton-`Eligible` and inflated On-Demand eligible savings in `graviton_ec2_view`.

## Change
- Blank `latest_arm` and `graviton2` for `g2, g3, g3s, g4ad, g5, g6, g6e, g6f, gr6, gr6f` (and the `g5g` self-row). With no Graviton target, `default_grav_price` is null/0 so `graviton_ec2_view.ineligibility_reason` becomes `No equivalent graviton instance` with `$0` eligible savings.
- Retain `g4dn -> g5g` as a valid like-for-like T4 -> T4G mapping.
- Only the GPU family rows change; C/M/I/R/T/D/X families and the analytical views (`graviton_mapping`, `graviton_ec2_view`) are untouched.
- Bump dashboard to `v3.0.3` and add a changelog entry.

## Validation
- YAML parses cleanly.
- Confirmed via view wiring that `graviton_mapping` joins `modernization_mapping` on `SPLIT_PART(instance_type,'.',1) = family` and exposes `latest_arm` as `default_grav_instance_type`; blanking it routes these families to the existing `No equivalent graviton instance` branch.
- Windows usage and oversized targets (e.g. `g6.24xlarge`) were already handled correctly and are unaffected.

Post-deploy check:
```sql
SELECT ineligibility_reason, COUNT(*) rows, ROUND(SUM(default_g_savings_potential),0) savings
FROM graviton_ec2_view
WHERE SPLIT_PART(existing_instance,'.',1) IN ('g2','g3','g3s','g4ad','g5','g6','g6e','g6f','gr6','gr6f')
GROUP BY 1;
```
Expected: these families no longer appear as `Eligible`; `g4dn` remains eligible.

author: assem2002
body:
## Summary

Adding any label to a PR that already carries `Tests::Run-Exhaustive` re-ran
the whole exhaustive suite and cancelled the run already in progress. This
fixes both halves of that.

## Why the `if:` guards changed

The workflow subscribes to `labeled`/`unlabeled` so that adding the label
starts the suite. GitHub emits one event per label and `on:` cannot filter by
label name, so every label change dispatched a run. The guards then tested
only whether the PR's label *set* contained `Tests::Run-Exhaustive` — which
stays true once the label is present — so an unrelated label re-ran everything
on an unchanged head SHA.

The guards now test the label that triggered the event
(`github.event.label.name`) together with `github.event.action`, so only
`labeled` with `Tests::Run-Exhaustive` starts the suite. `opened`, `reopened`
and `synchronize` still run whenever the PR carries the label. `unlabeled` is
excluded by omission.

## Why the concurrency group changed

The group is keyed on the PR number with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and
GitHub picks the group *before* any job's `if:` is evaluated. So a run for an
unrelated label would cancel the running suite and only then skip all of its
own jobs — leaving the suite unfinished with nothing explaining why.

The group now splits on the triggering label: runs for other labels get a
separate group and cannot cancel a suite. `github.event.label.name` is null on
push/opened/reopened/synchronize, so those keep the shared group and a new
commit still supersedes a running suite. Adding or removing
`Tests::Run-Exhaustive` also keeps the shared group, so removing the label
still stops a running suite.

## Verification

Evidence of the bug in run history — PR #13871 got three labels in one action
at `02:44:24Z` and produced three runs at `02:44:27Z`, two `cancelled` and one
`skipped`:

```
$ gh api repos/lfortran/lfortran/issues/13871/timeline
2026-09-30T02:44:24Z  labeled  enhancement
2026-09-30T02:44:24Z  labeled  parser
2026-09-30T02:44:24Z  labeled  tokenizer
```

Locally: the file parses as YAML, all 10 gated jobs carry one identical
expression, and `concurrency.group` folds to a single line.

Expression evaluation cannot be exercised locally, so the behaviour was
reasoned per event type rather than observed. Worth confirming on this PR: add
`Tests::Run-Exhaustive`, then add a second label while the suite is running —
the second run should skip without disturbing the first.

author: rdvankck
body:
Follow-up to #390/#392 in the frontend/MF template sweep: the shell scaffolded by `create --microfrontend` was broken at **every stage after generation** — 20 strict-TS errors, a dead routing file at a doubled path, and a production build that could not even resolve its loader. CI never sees this because the scaffold-and-typecheck job only covers `create --backend` templates, not the `--microfrontend` surface.

## Findings (fresh `create --microfrontend` scaffold)

| Stage | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | **20 errors** (implicit-any handlers/params, `getElementById` null, `module.hot`, undeclared webpack runtime globals) | **0 errors** |
| `webpack --mode production` | **fails** — `Can't resolve 'ts-loader'` (used by the shell webpack override but not a declared dep) | exit 0, emits `dist/main.js` + `dist/index.html` |
| Routing | written to doubled `src/src/Routing.tsx`, **imported by nothing** — shell could never route to remotes | `src/Routing.tsx`, wired into `App` |
| `npm run start` | `webpack serve` with no `webpack-dev-server` dep, and no `HtmlWebpackPlugin` → no page | dep added + plugin restored |

## Fixes

**`commands/create.ts`**
- `generateShellRouting`: write routing to `src/Routing.<tsx|jsx>` (was `src/src/…`, a doubled segment — same for the vue variant) and overwrite the App component to actually render it, so remotes appear at their routes.
- `generateReactRouting`: `@ts-ignore` on the remote lazy imports — they are resolved at runtime by Module Federation, so the strict tsconfig would reject them as TS2307.
- `ReactModuleFederationShellTemplate.generateShellWebpackConfig`: the shell override had swapped the base template's babel-loader (with `@babel/preset-typescript`) for ts-loader **without declaring the dep**, and dropped HtmlWebpackPlugin plus the css/asset rules. It now mirrors the base loader/plugin setup with the shell's Module Federation wiring on top (`historyApiFallback`, CORS headers, `publicPath`).

**`templates/frontend/react-module-federation.ts`**
- `webpack-dev-server: ^4.15.2` devDependency (the `start` script runs `webpack serve`).
- Types for the previously implicit-any params, using the `src/types` declarations that the template already generated but nothing consumed: `CounterProps`, `RemoteComponentProps`, typed `CustomEvent` handlers (cast kept TS-only — the JS variant stays plain).
- `bootstrap`: null-check the root container; `module.hot` accessed through a narrow cast instead of undeclared on the module.
- `api.ts`: `declare const __webpack_init_sharing__ / __webpack_share_scopes__` + a `RemoteContainer` interface; `fetchRemoteComponent` now **re-reads** the container after `loadScript` and throws an actionable error instead of silently returning `undefined` when the container registered late.

## Verification

Fresh headless scaffold (`create mfshell --microfrontend --yes`, combined with #392 for the non-interactive path):
- `npm install` exit 0
- `tsc --noEmit` → **0 errors** (was 20)
- `webpack --mode production` → exit 0, `dist/index.html` + `dist/main.js`
- `webpack serve` → dev server up, `/` returns 200 with the app HTML
- `tests/unit/create.test.ts`: wizard-path assertions now pin `src/Routing.tsx` (and absence of the doubled `src/src/`), the App wiring, the `@ts-ignore`, and that the shell webpack config references html-webpack-plugin but **not** ts-loader — 27/27
- Full suite: **5777 passed / 0 failed** (known main flake in `template-engine.test.ts` untouched — fix is open in #382)

Note: the vue/svelte/angular MF shell variants still carry their own ts-loader-based webpack configs (out of scope here; spotted while fixing the react one).

## Problem The `dependabot-repair` loop starts its worker with a prompted `rimz agents` launch inside a check. RimZ makes that launch a loop-owned supervised run, and that run opens in the `rimzd` loop zone. The worker runs for hours and starts subagents, and the subagents open next to it. As a result, the worker and its subagents fill the loop panel in `rimzd`. ## Change - `loops/dependabot/dependabot.py::launch` adds `--new-tab` to the worker argv. `run_placement` checks `force_new_tab` before `loop_zone`, so the worker opens in its own tab. The loop still applies the timeout and pane cleanup, and `-p` still returns the report to the coordinator. - The loop test asserts the new argv. A new Rust assertion in `loop_check_launch_is_blocking_bounded_and_owned` makes sure that `--new-tab` stays set after `into_loop_check_request`. - `docs/contributing/dependabot-loop.md` tells where the worker opens, and why. - `docs/internals/harness/loops.md`: the sentence "a manual `rimz loop fire` splits beside the caller" applies only to `Spawn` tasks. A prompted agent launch from a check uses the loop zone on scheduled and manual fires, unless the launch passes `--new-tab`. The doc now says this. body:
Fixes #253.

Over open ocean, Esri's Dark/Light Gray Canvas tiles stop at zoom 12. From z13 on, Esri returns its "Map data not yet available" placeholder with HTTP 200, so the layers' `maxNativeZoom: 16` showed that placeholder at sea. Near the coast the data goes to z16, which is where 16 came from.

This PR sets `maxNativeZoom: 12` on both canvases in `www/app/templates/default/js/mapBaseLayers.js`, so Leaflet enlarges the z12 tile past that point. That's the same approach the Esri Ocean Basemap already uses at z10. The trade-off is that land and coast lose real tiles at z13–16, where the canvases have little detail anyway.

**Testing**
- ESLint passes.
- Manual check still needed: in the Data Dashboard map, switch to each gray canvas and zoom past 12 over open water. The placeholder tile should no longer appear.

## Phase 4 — Quantum Simulator

### Overview

This PR implements **Phase 4 — Quantum Simulator**, building on the canonical quantum circuit model and Quantum Lab established in Phase 3.

The simulator allows users to execute valid quantum circuits, calculate the resulting quantum state, determine measurement probabilities, and perform multi-shot measurements directly within the platform.

### What's Included

#### Quantum Simulation Engine

* State-vector based quantum simulation
* Complex-number arithmetic for quantum amplitudes
* Initial `|00...0⟩` quantum state
* Circuit execution based on the Phase 3 `QuantumCircuit` model
* Numerical normalization and floating-point tolerance handling

#### Supported Gates

* X gate
* Y gate
* Z gate
* Hadamard (H) gate
* S gate
* T gate
* CNOT gate

#### Measurement & Probabilities

* Quantum-state probability calculation
* Single-shot measurement
* Configurable multi-shot simulation
* Measurement counts
* Probability distributions
* Basis-state representation

#### Quantum Lab Integration

* Run Circuit functionality
* Simulation status indicators
* Configurable number of shots
* Execution summary
* Final state-vector display
* Probability distribution visualization
* Measurement histogram
* Clear simulation results
* Stale-result detection after circuit modification
* Error handling for invalid/unsupported circuits

#### Testing

Added tests covering:

* Single-qubit gate simulation
* H → H behavior
* CNOT basis-state transformations
* Bell-state simulation
* State normalization
* Measurement sampling
* Measurement counts
* Invalid circuit handling
* Phase 3 circuit integration

### Integration

Phase 4 directly consumes the **existing Phase 3 `QuantumCircuit` representation** rather than introducing a separate circuit schema.

The architecture is:

```text
Phase 3 Quantum Circuit
          ↓
       Validation
          ↓
   Quantum Simulator
          ↓
     Final State
          ↓
   Probabilities
          ↓
 Measurements / Shots
          ↓
  Simulation Results
          ↓
     Results UI
```

This keeps the simulator reusable for future phases, including the planned AI explanation/tutoring functionality.

### Validation

Before merging, the implementation should be verified with:

* [ ] All existing project tests pass
* [ ] Phase 4 tests pass
* [ ] Lint passes
* [ ] Typecheck passes (if configured)
* [ ] Production build passes
* [ ] X gate verified
* [ ] H gate verified
* [ ] H → H verified
* [ ] CNOT verified
* [ ] Bell state verified
* [ ] Measurement sampling verified

### Important Demo Cases

#### Hadamard

```text
q0 ── H ── M
```

Expected approximately:

```text
P(0) = 50%
P(1) = 50%
```

#### Bell State

```text
q0 ── H ──●── M
          │
q1 ───────X── M
```

Expected approximately:

```text
P(00) = 50%
P(11) = 50%
P(01) = 0%
P(10) = 0%
```

### Documentation

Added Phase 4 integration/documentation covering:

* Simulator architecture
* State-vector representation
* Gate execution
* Measurement model
* Probability calculation
* Simulation result structure
* Numerical considerations
* Testing
* Phase 5 integration considerations

### Scope

This PR focuses specifically on the **classical quantum simulation layer**.

It does not include:

* AI tutor/chatbot
* AI-generated explanations
* Quantum hardware execution
* IBM Quantum integration
* Advanced assessment functionality

### Target Branch

```text
develop
```

### Source Branch

```text
feature/phase-04-quantum-simulator
```

author: waywardmonkeys
body:
Homogeneous numeric arrays currently store one `Value` enum per element. Opening, cloning, editing and consuming mesh data therefore allocate and copy much more than the native elements require. This change retains shared native buffers through import, composition, sparse edits, interpolation and saving, then lets schema readers copy native elements directly when callers request an owned vector.

The three commits cover native storage and formats, direct schema adapters, and retaining decoded ownership before layer assembly. `Value::TypedArray` uses `Arc<Vec<T>>` with copy-on-write edits; the existing heterogeneous `Value::Array` remains available. Empty buffers preserve their kind, authored guards preserve float bits and kind distinctions, and half/quaternion/matrix values retain their existing semantics.

```rust
use layerstack::{TypedArray, Value};

let points = Value::from(vec![[1.0_f32, 2.0, 3.0]; 1_000]);
let snapshot = points.clone(); // Shares the native buffer.
if let Value::TypedArray(TypedArray::Vec3f(buffer)) = &snapshot {
    let points: &[[f32; 3]] = buffer.as_slice();
    assert_eq!(points.len(), 1_000);
}
```

Representative measurements on the same workloads before and after:

| Workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Payload for one million float3 elements | 40 MB | 12 MB |
| Resolve, retain and scan one million float3 elements | 5.95 ms | 0.749 ms |
| Shared-buffer sparse write | 2.97 ms | 0.189 ms |
| Owned `Mesh::points()` read of one million elements | 7.21 ms | 0.180 ms |
| Materialized USDC import, 262,144 floats | 0.496 ms | 0.453 ms |

Native slice reads avoid enum expansion. Owned schema getters still copy into their returned vectors; document-writer boundaries can also copy native data. Authored sparse-program saving remains explicitly unsupported.

Fresh review found and fixed native empty-point bounds, expression-variable list conversion, and tuple-component authoring regressions. Regression coverage also includes bit preservation, kind-aware empty arrays, copy-on-write ownership, sparse/interpolation parity and USDA/USDC saving. Each commit passes the fast gates and workspace Clippy; final workspace tests, schema regeneration, MSRV 1.88, no_std/wasm and feature checks pass using an isolated build target.

author: xiechimon
body:
#462 症状 1 根治：m5-web-e2e 的 CI 间歇红不是「环境慢」，是**产品级缺陷**——SSE 边沿触发 + 服务端无重放 + 客户端无重连补偿 ⇒ 任一次性事件在断连 gap/哑连接窗口内丢失 = 对应查询永久陈旧（相位 chip / plan 卡停更直到整页重载）。CI 只是放大器；生产用户同样会看到「任务卡住不动，刷新才好」。

## Summary

```text
apps/web/src/api/sse.ts（team/conv 两流共用 connect()）
+ 重连 resync：onopen（非首开）→ queryClient.invalidateQueries() 全量
+   （SSE 本就只是 invalidate 提示信号；resync = 把断线窗口丢失的提示补成一次全量重取）
+ 静默看门狗：OPEN 态 20s 无任何事件（含心跳）→ close + 重建（触发 resync）
+   —— 覆盖 onerror 永不触发的哑形态（服务端写链静默停摆）；生产心跳 15s < 阈值恒不误触
  边界保全：CONNECTING（浏览器自重连中）与 fatal CLOSED（#253 401 门页恢复流）不接管

integration/test/helpers.ts
  pingIntervalMs 1h → 15s（= 生产 TEAM_STREAM_PING_INTERVAL_MS 同源缺省）——测试环境保真
```

**不动**任何断言/超时/retry；不动 web e2e fixture 面（fixture 模式不建 SSE 流）。

## Evidence

- **根因证明（故障注入环）**：服务端按 UA 掐断浏览器侧 SSE 真 TCP——基线代码**精确复现全部三种 CI 签名**（test1 `Expected /确认/ Received "规划中"` 300 polls ≈ CI 303；test2 `方案 · v1` 63 polls ≈ CI 64；conv-only 掐断 = #464 run 签名）；修复版同注入 **mac + ubuntu 容器双端全绿**（trace 可见 `subs=0` 丢失 → 重连 → resync 逐个挽回）。
- **排除表**（10 假设，H1-H8 全排除带证据）：CI 慢/CPU 竞争被双峰分布否定（红/绿 ~10s vs 182s+ 无中间态；红 run 卡死窗口 runner 空闲）；daemon 卡死被 test2/test3 行为否定（test1「卡死」后 31s 内走完两个完整 daemon 轮）。
- **自然矩阵 67 轮全绿**（mac 裸跑/全核燃烧/QoS 8-16× 减速/进程树冻结混沌/ubuntu noble 容器 ×23）——CI 原始触发源未自然复现，**明写未复现**；但「丢失即永久陈旧」是红的必要环节，修复后无论触发源是什么丢失都被补偿（自愈 ≤ ~24s ≪ 30s/150s 预算）。
- 车道终验：根 `pnpm test` **913 passed / 1 skipped**；m5 最终树 mac 10 轮 + 容器 2 轮全绿；插桩零残留（grep 验证）。
- **主线独立复验（merge 最新 main 839f59e 后，零冲突）**：lint 0 error、typecheck 五包绿、web vitest 绿、**m5 三轮 3/3 绿**；sse.ts diff 亲审（看门狗只在 OPEN 态、每事件重置；resync 只在重连不在首开；401 语义零变化）。
- 附带修正两处 #462 记录错误：签名 A（ECONNREFUSED 8787）实为 web e2e 步骤的 vite preview 继承 proxy 噪音（→ #483）；「#459 push-run m5 两连败」实为 shared 快照真红。

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way（2 commits + merge；回滚 = revert，回到「丢失即永久陈旧」旧语义）

**Blast Radius:** 全站 live SSE 实时面（team/conv 两流）

- 健康连接零行为变化（心跳 15s 恒重置看门狗；resync 只在真重连时发生）；
- 重连成本有界：invalidateQueries 仅活跃查询真发请求，SSE 事件语义本就是提示信号；
- fixture/e2e 面不建流，完全不受影响；integration 心跳对齐生产（913 测试全绿实证零波及）；
- 遗留：CI 原始触发源未钉死（预期不再红；若复发，带桩配方在车道报告 §8）；flight.claim 死代码 → #482；preview proxy 噪音 → #483。

Closes #462

（症状 2 已随 #465 根治；症状 3 双跑去重的 concurrency 建议在 #483 顺带裁决）

- Disable the old installer and its mise task before dependencies, binary/shortcut replacement or process launch. Preserve the previous script in Git history.
- Keep offline previews available, and record isolation, rollback and manual prerequisites. No hardware support or setter behavior is expanded.

## Validation

`mise run ci`: formatting, strict Clippy, 124 library + 2 CLI + 3 capability + 6 catalog integration tests, release build and CLI help passed. `ci-preview`: strict feature Clippy, 130 library + 2 CLI + 9 editor + 3 capability + 6 catalog tests passed. All 30 mise tasks validate. Production and editor Windows x64 MSVC cross-builds passed without launching.

Tests seed legacy config, alias-library and immutable-baseline sentinel bytes and prove development loads/saves leave them untouched; the pure production launch gate rejects. The disabled install task returned exit 1 before build or Windows invocation. PowerShell installer received source review only. Independent review confirmed the startup finding is resolved and reported no further material issues.

## Gates

Keep draft. The installed executable, configuration, startup and mouse state were not operated on. No GUI, installer or HID command ran. Manual Windows behavior remains unverified. author: marcelroozekrans
body:
Fixes #132

## Root cause

The `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` transforms returned `FeatureInfo` and `ReducerInfo` holding `INamedTypeSymbol` and `IMethodSymbol`, and the output also combined with `CompilationProvider`. A symbol belongs to one compilation, so the models never compared equal across edits. Every edit reran every step and regenerated the store, dispatcher and DI sources, including edits to files with no `[Feature]` or `[Reducer]`.

## Fix

- **Value-equal models.** The transforms read the symbols and return models with no `ISymbol` or `Compilation` in them: fully-qualified names, the bare type name, flags, the InitialState factory name, and the diagnostics that concern one model alone (ZFLUX003, ZFLUX004, ZFLUX005).
- **Cache-safe diagnostics.** They are held as `DiagnosticInfo` with a `LocationInfo(SyntaxTree, TextSpan)` in the model's equality, using the same pattern as Telemetry. They are rebuilt with `Location.Create(tree, span)`, so `#pragma` suppression and IDE navigation still work. `DiagnosticLocationTests` still passes unchanged, including the pragma test and the edit-moves-the-diagnostic test.
- **No CompilationProvider.** ZFLUX004's `IServiceProvider` lookup now uses `ctx.SemanticModel.Compilation` inside the transform, so the output no longer combines with `CompilationProvider`.
- **Name-keyed dispatcher.** `DispatcherEmitter` groups reducers by action and state name instead of `SymbolEqualityComparer`.
- **One validation path.** `FluxValidation` runs the cross-model checks, ZFLUX001 and ZFLUX002, for the generator. The test-only `FeatureDiscovery.DiscoverFromCompilation` and `ReducerDiscovery.DiscoverFromCompilation` walks, which duplicated the rules, are deleted. The tests now get their models from the generator's tracked steps through a small `Discovery` helper, and validate them with the same `FluxValidation`.
- **Tracking names** on the transform, collect and combine steps.

Generated output is byte-identical: no snapshot changed.

## Also fixed: duplicate locals in the fan-out

This is a defect in the fan-out code this PR touches. Each store local was named after the feature's bare type name. Two features with the same name in different namespaces, or one feature reduced from two reducer classes (ZFLUX002 only forbids duplicates within one class), emitted two `store_CounterState` locals. The generated code then failed with CS0128. A repeated name now gets a suffix. `GeneratedCodeCompilesTests` covers both cases by compiling the generated code, and both tests fail without the fix.

## Tests

- `IncrementalityTests.UnrelatedEdit_LeavesEveryTrackedStepAndOutputCachedOrUnchanged`: the fixture has both feature kinds, an InitialState factory, a fan-out, and one diagnostic of each id ZFLUX001 to ZFLUX005. After an edit to an unrelated file, every tracked step and every output step is Cached or Unchanged, and the sources and diagnostics are identical. With tracking names alone, before the model change, this test failed on `step Features output was Modified`.
- `IncrementalityTests.EditToAReducer_RegeneratesTheOutput`: renaming a reducer produces a Modified output and the new call.
- The full suite passes locally on net8.0 and net10.0. The AOT smoke publishes and passes on win-x64, and the sample builds.

perf: make the generator's pipeline models value data so unrelated edits hit the cache
fix: give each store local in the dispatcher fan-out a unique name so the generated code compiles

author: daawesomepwner
body:
## Problem
A JVM that never initialised AWT could hang forever at exit. The `preferences-shutdown` hook (registered by `PropertiesManager`) calls `PreferencesStore.shutdown`, whose EDT guard used `SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()`. That call loads the default toolkit. `WToolkit`'s `AWT-Windows` thread then fails to register its own shutdown hook (`IllegalStateException: Shutdown in progress`), `WToolkit.<init>` waits forever, and `ApplicationShutdownHooks.runHooks` never returns. This showed up as Gradle test workers that never exited, for example `test --tests assets.AssetRecoveryTest` run on its own.

## Fix
`requireOffEdt` now identifies the EDT by its thread class (`java.awt.EventDispatchThread`), so it never touches the toolkit. The guard still rejects blocking `preload`/`shutdown` calls on the EDT.

## Tests
- New `PreferencesStoreTest.shutdownHookInAJvmThatNeverStartedAwtSavesAndExits` starts a child JVM that never uses AWT. The child saves a preference and then exits through a shutdown hook that calls `shutdown`. Before the fix, the child hung and the test failed with the `AWT-Windows` "Shutdown in progress" trace. With the fix, the child exits cleanly and the preference is on disk.
- The existing EDT-rejection test now also checks the new helper on the EDT and on a plain thread.
- Local: `test --tests util.PreferencesStoreTest` passes (12/12). `cleanTest test --tests assets.AssetRecoveryTest` passes and the worker now exits.

author: aljohri
body:
Makes `libcrypto.a` and `libssl.a` byte-identical when the same sources are built from different directories or at different times. Today every object differs between two checkouts. Three independent commits, so any of them can be dropped:

- **`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` defaults to `0`.** Without it, `mkbuildinf.pl` embeds the current time as `built on:`. A value from the environment still wins.
- **`MODULESDIR=/usr/local/lib/ossl-modules`** (non-Windows targets). The default is under `--prefix`, which is the build directory, so libcrypto embedded a build-machine path that is usually writable. Same issue as #141 for `OPENSSLDIR`; this uses OpenSSL's documented default. Installed `.pc`/`.cmake` files are unchanged.
- **`-ffile-prefix-map=<build dir>=.`** when the compiler accepts it (not MSVC), so debug info no longer records the build directory. It goes on the `make` command line via `CPPFLAGS` rather than to Configure, because Configure's flags are embedded in `OpenSSL_version(OPENSSL_CFLAGS)`.

Behavior changes:

- `OpenSSL_version(OPENSSL_BUILT_ON)` reports `built on: Thu Jan  1 00:00:00 1970 UTC` unless `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set.
- The compiled-in default modules directory is `/usr/local/lib/ossl-modules` instead of a path under `OUT_DIR`. `OPENSSL_MODULES` still overrides it.

Tested on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, two checkouts at different paths:

| build | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| GCC, dev | 985/985 `libcrypto.a` objects differ | identical |
| GCC, release | 2/985 differ | identical |
| Clang, dev | 965/985 differ | identical |

`testcrate` passes in debug, `--release` and `--all-features`. Not tested on Windows, macOS or cross targets.

author: ascorbic
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the flaky bubble-menu browser test "keeps text typed after an applied link outside the link" (added in #3630). It failed in the Browser Tests job of unrelated runs, for example [36638964838](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/actions/runs/36638964838) on docs-only #3667 and [36659412602](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/actions/runs/36659412602).

**Cause: a race in the test.** The product code from #3630 is not at fault, so this PR changes only the test.

After clicking Apply, the test sent `{ArrowLeft}{End} for more information` as back-to-back CDP key events. Two ProseMirror behaviours make that unsafe right after the editor refocuses:

- ProseMirror only learns about native caret moves through the async `selectionchange` event. When the first typed character is processed before End's `selectionchange`, the caret move is folded into the text-input transaction. `LinkBoundaryExit` handles only selection-only transactions, so it never removes the inclusive link mark. The typed text then joins the link. This matches the CI failure: correct text, but all of it inside `<a>`.
- For 20ms after focus (`handlers.focus` in prosemirror-view), ProseMirror resets any DOM caret move it hasn't observed yet. Apply refocuses the editor in a `requestAnimationFrame`, so End sometimes arrived inside that window and was undone. The text then landed before the "d" (`Hello worl for more informationd`).

I reproduced both locally by running the test hundreds of times. It failed about once every 200–1500 runs, and I captured the DOM selection writes and transactions with stack traces showing the reset coming from ProseMirror's post-focus `selectionToDOM`.

Neither path affects people typing at human speed. Both need a caret key and the next input within milliseconds of each other or of the refocus.

**Fix.** Wait until the editor has focus, move the caret away from and back to the link end with `editor.commands.setTextSelection`, then type natively. Those moves are the same selection-only transactions `LinkBoundaryExit` handles, and ProseMirror records the DOM selection it writes, so no pending event or timer can undo them. The assertions are unchanged.

author: gggfox
body:
## Summary

The five highest-impact findings from the UI/design audit.

**1. Diners can read the menu and reserve without an account**
- `/r/:slug/menu`, `/r/:slug/:lang/menu` and `/r/:slug/reserve` render signed out. The sign-in prompt moves to the order bar ("Sign in to order"). The menu queries and `reservations.create` were already anonymous-safe, so there is no backend change.
- Pages that need a visit (orders, order status, checkout, closeout) keep the sign-in card, with corrected copy and a back-to-menu link.
- An unknown or inactive slug returns an HTTP 404 with "We couldn't find this restaurant". `loadBranding` now tells "missing" apart from "timed out", so a Convex blip never shows a diner a 404.
- Diner pages are titled with the restaurant's name. Loading shows a loading state instead of "No active session".
- The header sign-in is trimmed to one quiet link, so it doesn't compete with the order bar. The reserve form now scrolls on phones, and the reservations-unavailable state links back to the menu.

**2. The URL language wins after hydration**
- Root cause: TanStack reuses the server's `beforeLoad` result during hydration, so the client i18n instance kept the detector's cached `en-US`. The server rendered Spanish, the client English, and React logged a hydration mismatch.
- The detector now reads the diner URL's `:lang` first. `supportedLngs` normalises `en-US`/`es-MX`.
- Visiting a diner link does not overwrite the saved cookie or the account language.
- An unsupported `:lang` redirects (307) to a supported one.

**3. Money follows the restaurant's currency**
- `formatMoney(minorUnits, currency, language)` and `useFormatMoney`, built on `Intl.NumberFormat` with `narrowSymbol`, replace the literal "$" at about 34 call sites and three competing staff formats.
- `MoneyCurrencyProvider` sits in the customer and staff layouts. Billing is pinned to `PLATFORM_SUBSCRIPTION_CURRENCY`; payouts and disputes use each record's own currency.
- The team drawer revenue was printing cents as pesos (100× too large).

**4. Schedule**
- Day headers named the previous day west of UTC ("Lun · 27 sept" in the week of 28 sept). They are now formatted from the date itself.
- Overnight shifts: an end before the start means the next day. The drawer shows an "Ends next day" hint and the chip shows "+1". The backend already allowed this.
- Week navigation steps by calendar days (DST-safe). A skeleton replaces the empty week while loading, and "+" stays in cells that already have a shift (split shifts).

**5. Diner order-flow dead ends**
- New `orders.saveDraftFromMenu`, one atomic mutation. It replaces the draft's lines, table and notes, or changes nothing and returns a stable code.
  - Validates availability, restaurant ownership, quantity (≤ 99) and line count (≤ 50).
  - Retires an open payment attempt through the existing `invalidateActivePayment` / `standDownSupersededIntent`.
  - Rejects with `ERROR_PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` while a PaymentIntent create is still in flight.
- The menu reopens holding the draft's picks. Submit errors show inline, with "remove it from my order" when a dish is refused. Previously the submit had no `catch`, so any failure passed silently and re-ordering after going back duplicated the lines.
- An order that is missing or not yours shows not-found instead of "Loading order…" forever. The order page scrolls, and unpaid orders get "Continue to payment".
- Checkout shows "Confirming your payment" after the diner confirms, including after a reload or a 3DS return, with no pay button. After 25s it tells the diner not to pay again and to show staff the order reference. A failed 3DS shows a retry.

## Deploy note
**Convex must be deployed before or with the frontend:** `orders:saveDraftFromMenu` is new and `orders:addItem` now shares `priceOrderLine`. Until then the menu submit shows the generic error.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm test`: 235 files, 2968 tests pass (en/es parity included)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` for the app and for `convex/`: 0 errors. `eslint` on changed files: 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in `admin/schedule.tsx`)
- [x] Checked in the browser (local dev, same data before and after):
  - Signed-out `/es/menu` with `en-US` saved renders the Spanish menu with the order-bar sign-in
  - `/r/does-not-exist` returns 404; `/fr/menu` returns 307 to `/en/menu`
  - Reserve opens signed out
  - Schedule headers read 28 sept–4 oct
  - 18:00–02:00 shows the next-day hint
  - A bad order id shows not-found
- [ ] e2e specs touched (`pivot-surfaces`, `settlement-flows`) not run locally. They now expect a 404 and restaurant-name titles.
- [ ] `saveDraftFromMenu` live, after a Convex deploy: go back from checkout (picks restored, no duplication); switch a dish off, then submit (refused with a remove button)
- [ ] Payment confirming state with a blocked webhook, and a failed 3DS card (`4000 0027 6000 3184`)

## Follow-ups found (not in this PR)
- The dashboard active-orders widget sums cents and formats them as whole units (100× too large); two similar widgets probably have the same bug.
- The AI menu importer writes English "(price not listed)" into descriptions with a $0.00 price (`convex/menuImport.ts:84`).
- A server-side "diner confirmed payment" signal, so the confirming state works across tabs and devices.
- One draft per session is shared by everyone on the visit.
- Picks made before sign-in are lost on return.
- `convex/shifts.ts` uses a fixed `ONE_WEEK_MS` (harmless without DST).
- Convex hides the message of errors thrown as plain `Error` in production, so thrown codes may reach users as generic text (not verified).

author: cryo2010
body:
Fixes the five issues the cloud review of #449 raised, one commit each.

## Fixes

- **#450 (bug, low)** A `-d:naviHttp3` build compiles again with `--threads:off`. The sync WebSocket-over-h3 pump (its `Channel`/`Thread` state and procs) now sits behind `when compileOption("threads")`, matching the gate `websocket.nim` already had, and the `wkH3` transport arm carries no state on a threadless build. The CI compile matrix now runs `nim check -d:naviHttp3` over the three native entries in both thread modes so the gap cannot reopen; the http3 workflow path filter also picks up `private/websocket.nim`.
- **#451 (bug, medium)** An h3 IP-literal origin is bound with `X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_ip_asc` against the certificate's iPAddress SAN and is no longer offered as SNI (RFC 6066 section 3), mirroring `bindExpectedIdentity` on the TCP backends. Bracketed IPv6 literals are handled. Note on the premise: on OpenSSL 3.5 a plain `127.0.0.1` already verified by accident (`SSL_set1_host` tries the IP matcher first), so the user-visible bugs were the leaked SNI and bracketed literals falling through to the DNS matcher. New http3 interop probes on all three clients assert the SAN match, the absence of SNI (via a Caddy echo route), a mismatched-IP rejection and that DNS origins still send SNI.
- **#452 (bug, medium)** The sync backend's whole establish (TCP connect, SOCKS5 or CONNECT handshake, TLS handshake) now spends one wall-clock budget, matching the async backends' single `withTimeout`. The tunnel drivers re-arm `SO_RCVTIMEO`/`SO_SNDTIMEO` per syscall with the remaining time and raise the connect `TimeoutError` when it is spent; a bounded TLS handshake is driven non-blocking against the same deadline (a per-recv timeout cannot bound a handshake); `connectAcross` bounds its re-race loop once. Unit tests with a proxy that trickles the CONNECT and SOCKS5 replies one byte per 100 ms against a 300 ms budget: before the fix they ran 4.0 s and 6.9 s and surfaced the wrong error.
- **#453 (enhancement, low)** One `openH3Tracked` template in `core/altsvc.nim` does the mark-broken/mark-working Alt-Svc bookkeeping for all three h3 openers (sync `h3Transport`, `getH3Conn`, `stream_download`). Behaviour is byte-identical. The ws-over-h3 opener is deliberately left alone: it never consulted the Alt-Svc cache and has no h2/h1 fallback to protect. Four unit tests cover the template.
- **#454 (enhancement, low)** `navi_h3_new` no longer rebuilds the `SSL_CTX` per connection. A process-wide cache in `h3client.cpp` (mutex-guarded, 8-entry LRU, keyed by the owning `contextStore` plus every input the context is built from including size/mtime of file inputs, `SSL_CTX_up_ref` per connection so a context outlives every SSL made from it) hands back a shared context; `close` releases the client's entries. `NAVI_H3_CTX_CACHE=0` restores the per-connection build. Also fixes the password callback userdata outliving the call. Micro-measurement in the h3 image (50 connects with caFile plus a PKCS#12 credential): 0.557 ms to 0.025 ms per connection. The h3 stress `requests` cell is unchanged because Caddy fronts the h3 leg and `NAVI_RECYCLE` only churns the backend, so it never exercises the connect path.

## Validation

- `checkmate` on the integrated head: 46/46 suites, 1017/1017 tests.
- `nim check -d:ssl -d:naviHttp3` over `navi`, `navi/asyncdispatch`, `navi/chronos` with `--threads:on` and `--threads:off`: clean.
- `tests/interop/http3` image built and run on the integrated head (all probes including the new IP-literal and context-cache ones, leak and ASan/UBSan checks): see the result section below.
- Stress smoke `NAVI_PROTO=all NAVI_CLIENT=all NAVI_SECONDS=10 NAVI_REPORT_SECONDS=2 nimble stress`: see the result section below.
- Each fix was additionally validated in isolation by its own worktree (unit suite, and the h3 interop image for #451, #453, #454; the happy_eyeballs and http_connect interop scripts for #452).

## Results on the integrated head

- h3 interop image (`tests/interop/http3`) on the integrated head: exit 0. All probes green, including the new IP-literal probes on sync, asyncdispatch and chronos, the SSL_CTX cache probe with the cache on and off, the fd/heap leak check and the ASan/UBSan check.
- Stress smoke `NAVI_PROTO=all NAVI_CLIENT=all NAVI_SECONDS=10 NAVI_REPORT_SECONDS=2 nimble stress`: all five workloads report `all cells passed`, 49 of 49 cells (requests, ws, sse, streamUpload, streamDownload over h1/h2/h3 on sync, asyncdispatch, chronos, plus js on h1), no `err`, mismatch, checksum or panic signatures.
- CI: the Windows badssl job failed once on the third case (verify off against self-signed.badssl.com) with a handshake failure on the blocking handshake branch, which this PR does not change; the rerun passed. Treated as a badssl.com network flake (the job has 12 consecutive passes on earlier branches).

Closes #450
Closes #451
Closes #452
Closes #453
Closes #454

author: gwendall
body:
## Why

The generation benchmark's full run rendered 188 generations, every one from a prompt asking for original music. Scored against the known-melody gate as it shipped, **59 of them (31%) reached 0.40**: in production each would have been refused after the paid model call.

## What was wrong

- **Four of the five public-domain reference rhythms were wrong.** They had been hand-encoded from memory with only pitches checked. They are now read from published scores (Wikipedia scores for Ode to Joy, Für Elise, Symphony No. 5 and Twinkle; thesession.org setting 24502 for Korobeiniki). `fur-elise` and `korobeiniki` are the scores' first 16 notes. Korobeiniki's invented all-equal rhythm alone caused 42 of the 59. A new test recomputes every reference from the score's note names and lengths.
- **The NSF-corpus check could not fail.** NSF capture pitches are fractional (68.81, not 69), so no interval ever equaled a reference's integer one: 0.000 was an artifact. `tokenize` now rounds pitches to the semitone. Generated scores are already integer (`score.ts`), so production scoring is unchanged by this. Measured properly, the eight songs score up to 0.467.

## The threshold

With the references corrected, 15/188 still reached 0.40. Every top match was a false positive on inspection (for example a chord part's B B A A oscillation against Twinkle). The threshold was re-derived from the real generations. The rule was written down before scoring:

- odd prompt numbers are the calibration half, even numbers the held-out half;
- the threshold is the lowest 0.05 step at least 0.05 above the calibration max.

The calibration max was 0.571, so the threshold is **0.65**. The held-out max was also 0.571, so 0/94 are flagged.

| Threshold | References | Real gens flagged (188) | NSF flagged (8) | Synthetic positives (cal / held) | Synthetic negatives flagged (46) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.40 | as shipped | 59 | 3 | 43/48, 45/48 | 0 |
| 0.40 | corrected | 15 | 3 | 46/48, 46/48 | 0 |
| 0.60 | corrected | 0 | 0 | 35/48, 40/48 | 0 |
| **0.65** | corrected | **0** | **0** | **29/48, 33/48** | **0** |

Trade-off: synthetic paraphrase recall drops to 62/96.
- Every one-change copy is still caught (16/16), and an exact transposed or re-timed copy is always 1.0.
- What passes is mostly two changed notes plus an ornament (5/32 caught), and the 6-token Beethoven motif.
- The structural fix, weighting each reference's distinctive intervals, is filed as NEXT-27.

## Changes

- `similarity.ts`: rounding in `tokenize`, `KNOWN_MELODY_THRESHOLD = 0.65` with a rewritten doc comment.
- `known-melodies.ts`: corrected references and sources.
- `scripts/melody-negative-corpus.mjs`: `--gen-bench <run-dir>` writes `test/melody-negatives-gen-bench.json.gz` (the 188 generations' pitched notes, delta-encoded, 42 KB) and reports both real sets.
- `test-known-melody-similarity.mjs`:
  - score check, rounding check;
  - new confusion matrices, plus a check that every one-change copy is caught;
  - real-generation checks: the threshold follows the rule from the calibration half, and the held-out half has no false positive.
- `test-gen-bench.mjs` and `test-generation.mjs`: fixture values moved above/below the new threshold.
- Docs (EN and JA):
  - decision 56 amendment;
  - GENERATION-BENCHMARK "The full run": per-console results, cost $50.29, latency, 53% `abrupt_ending` on non-loops, failures;
  - BACKLOG: GEN-01/05, GEN-04, NEXT-21, new NEXT-27;
  - GENERATIVE-COMPOSITION.

The run stopped at 232/250 when the OpenAI account ran out of credit. Resuming it and rewriting the fixture re-applies the same rule.

## Tests

- `node test-known-melody-similarity.mjs`: PASS, 0/188 flagged.
- `node test-gen-bench.mjs`: PASS.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `python3 docs/check-translations.py`: OK.

author: tokeiito
body:
## Problem

The Bot Manager opens from the Pilot Hangar with nobody in the client, but its **New bot** and **Edit** buttons were greyed out there ("Bring a pilot into the client to write or edit a bot"). The Bot Builder took a pilot's whole `AppFlow` and could only open on a pilot's desktop, so a player with every pilot signed out could list their bots but not write or change one.

## Why a pilot is not needed

- The bot library is platform-wide, and the Bot Manager already reaches it as an **account** (`app/pilotReach.ts` `libraryOptions`).
- The station search (`/api/map/find`) and ore families (`/api/ore/families`) are static data behind the same account-level `requireAuth`.
- What a pilot adds is only help with the pickers: their saved fittings, bookmarks, fitted modules, cargo, corp hangars and accessible structures.

## Change

- `bots/builderFlow.ts`: `BuilderFlow` is the slice of `AppFlow` the Builder and its pickers call. A pilot's flow satisfies it unchanged, so the desktop Builder is untouched. `StationPicker`, `CorpHangarPicker` and `BotInspector` take `Pick<AppFlow, ...>` of what they call.
- `createPilotlessBuilderFlow` rides the account sign-in for the library, the map search and ore families.
  - A character's fittings and bookmarks come back empty.
  - Corp offices come back as "could not check", never as "no offices".
  - A `dockable` search asks for stations only, because which Upwell structures a pilot may dock at depends on a pilot.
- With nobody in the client, App floats the Builder on the global layer over the hangar (`HangarBotBuilder.svelte`, with an empty store).
  - It is **not** a global tab, so it stays off every pilot's desktop and needs no launcher.
  - It is not restored on reload.
  - While it is open it stays the New/Edit target even after a pilot signs in, so two builders never race for one `builderTarget` request.
- The Bot Manager's pilot gate on New and Edit is removed.

## Exercised

- On the running companion (Docker, before this rebase) with no pilot signed in:
  - Bots → **New bot** is enabled.
  - Clicking it opens the Bot Builder over the hangar with its plan, examples and Save, and no console errors.
  - That browser knew no account, so the Builder showed its existing "Could not reach the saved bots" note, as intended.
- `docker build --target web-build` (tsc + vite) passes on this branch.
- `node --test "web/src/**/*.test.ts"` in that image: 5748 tests, 33 failing. **The same 33 fail on `master` at 7c5d540** (compared by name: the repair-module, loot-container and cargo-drain bot suites). None are new.
- New tests:
  - `bots/builderFlow.test.ts`: the account-backed calls, the empty character reads, corp offices as "could not check", and `dockable` as stations only.
  - `globalWindow.test.ts`: the Builder can float, and is not restored on reload.
  - `botManagerPanel.test.ts`: New bot is enabled with no sessions.
  - `botBuilderPanel.test.ts`: `GlobalPanel` draws the Builder with nobody in the client.

body:

Scheduler slow servicing probes run only for due, fast-eligible work; local WUA `IsBusy` supplies positive busy evidence, and a fresh input/owner/session check and mutation fence precede admission. CLI key creation uses a protected TokenUser-only DACL at CREATE_NEW and reads it back before writing any seed. author: okxint
body:
TypeScript 7 changed how it resolves circular mapped types. `VitestAssertion`'s mapped-type traversal of `Chai.Assertion` now drops the `not` property, so `expect(x).not.toBe(...)` produces `TS2339: Property 'not' does not exist on type 'Assertion<void, string>'` at type-check time. Runtime is unaffected.

Adding an explicit `not: Assertion<R, T>` to the `Assertion` interface shadows the mapped-type version and resolves correctly under both TS 5 and TS 7.

Fixes #11144

author: wahabshaikh
body:

_Requested by **Wahab** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WKk2qXLdGZYeZwLKawRR6c?thread=cmsg_01WKk2qXLdGZYeZwLKawRR6cQfiS5gpNbBvUXfPCS4cgDb)_

## What changes

Before: PR previews wrote to the production R2 bucket, ran from `pull_request_target` (so workflow changes couldn't be tested in the PR that made them), and were the only place checks ran. Production deployed through the dashboard's Workers Builds from a repo-root copy of the build, with no checks and no migrations. Several dependencies were `"latest"`, and public vars lived only in the dashboard.

After: one Worker, every binding and public var declared in `apps/web/wrangler.jsonc`. Each PR gets its own D1 database and the shared `halalfood-world-evidence-preview` bucket, so previews never touch production data. `ci.yml` runs typecheck, tests and build on every PR (forks too). `deploy.yml` deploys production on push to `main`: checks, then D1 migrations, then `wrangler deploy`.

- **Previews** (`preview.yml` + `apps/web/scripts/preview.mjs`): `pull_request` trigger, one job, the workers.dev subdomain is read from the API instead of hardcoded, GitHub deployment via `environment: preview`, cleanup on close. Unit tests guard that no preview keeps a production binding.
- **Config:** `EMAIL_FROM` and `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` (both public) are now in `vars`. Workers Logs are on for every request, with 5% of requests traced.
- **Repo:** pinned `"latest"` ranges to the lockfile versions; removed `scripts/stage-cloudflare-build.mjs` and the root build copies; added `.node-version`, `.editorconfig`, `apps/web/.dev.vars.example` (Turnstile test keys), Dependabot, a PR template, CONTRIBUTING and SECURITY.
- **Docs:** the Cloudflare sections of the README moved to `docs/cloudflare.md`, which covers bindings, secrets, environments, rollback and new-account setup.

## How it was verified

- [x] `npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` (463 tests pass)
- [x] `wrangler deploy --dry-run` on the generated config lists DB, R2, ASSETS and the three vars
- [x] The same dry run after the preview rebinding shows `halalfood-world-pr-*` and `halalfood-world-evidence-preview`
- [x] `wrangler d1 migrations apply --local` against the generated config finds all 17 migrations
- [ ] This PR's own preview run (the new workflow runs here, since it uses `pull_request`)

## Notes for review

Dashboard steps before or at merge:
1. **Disconnect Workers Builds** from the `halalfood-world` Worker (Settings → Build). Production now deploys from `deploy.yml`, and Workers Builds would fail without the root staging script.
2. **Check `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`** has *Workers R2 Storage: Edit* as well as Workers Scripts and D1 edit, so previews can create the preview bucket.
3. If `EMAIL_FROM` or `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` are stored as **secrets** on the Worker, delete those two secrets (they're now public vars and the names would clash).
4. Optional: delete the unused KV namespace `VINEXT_KV_CACHE`; nothing binds it.

During this PR only, the old `pull_request_target` preview from `main` runs alongside the new one on the same `pr-<n>` alias; that stops once this merges.

author: aflordelis
body:
## Description

Closes #3513

Forced retrieval's relevance pick of candidate files had its own copy of the Atlas gate and called `fabfilechunks.vectorSearch` directly. It now uses the same gate and the same `atlasVectorSearch` path as Data Lake semantic search, so a gating or backend change in the seam reaches both. Ranking behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- `atlasVectorSearch.ts`: new shared `isAtlasVectorSearchAvailable` gate (Atlas backend + both ANN repo methods; the `EnableDataLakeVectorSearch` read stays with each caller), plus an optional `includeText` passthrough.
- `annVectorSearch.ts`: forwards `includeText` only when set, so existing callers still send exactly `{ limit }`.
- `semanticDataLakeSearch.ts`: inline `canUseAtlas` now uses the shared gate (same truth table).
- `ChatCompletionFeatures.ts`: `canSelectCandidatesByRelevance` / `rankCandidatesByAnn` go through the gate and `atlasVectorSearch`. Kept: `includeText: false`, the 3s deadline, no score floor (`minScore: -Infinity`), and every by-name fallback.
- Tests: gate on/off Atlas and missing methods, `includeText` forwarded/absent, no-floor pick, and a fallback when every hit names a file outside the listing.

## Guide for Testers

Backend-only refactor with no UI change. Regression check only:

1. Open a notebook that has a Data Lake with more files than the forced-retrieval candidate cap attached.
2. Type `Summarize what these files say about onboarding` and send it.
3. Expected: a response arrives with no errors and cites files from the Data Lake.

**What NOT to test:** self-host OpenSearch (forced retrieval stays on the by-name pick there, unchanged), and any UI.

## Additional Information

- The "every hit is outside the listing" fallback is defensive only. The real repository already filters by file id, so users won't see it. It guards against a misbehaving adapter.

<details>
<summary>Verification and open P3s</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @bike4mind/services typecheck`: pass
- `pnpm --filter @bike4mind/services test`: 500 files / 9045 tests pass, 13 skipped
- `pnpm lint:check`: pass
- The new outside-listing fallback test fails on the pre-change code and passes after. The no-floor test fails if `minScore` is set to `0`.

Open P3s for the reviewer:
- [ ] The gate test doesn't cover the `USE_DOCUMENTDB_COMPATIBILITY` branch of `supportsAtlasVectorSearch()`. That branch belongs to db-core.
- [ ] The seam's `2s-1` normalization can tie raw scores within about 1e-16, which then order by id. Cosmetic.

</details>
