body:
Goal: close the package gaps that block AISL from adopting `community_base.coursework` for course projects (AI-Shipping-Labs/website#1696 phase 2). Closes #350.

## What changed

| Change | Files |
|---|---|
| Nullable `Project.module` FK to `cb_curriculum.Module` (`SET_NULL`, `related_name="projects"`), mirroring `Homework.module` | `coursework/models.py` |
| `Project.commit_id_field` (default `True`); `ProjectSubmission.commit_id` is `blank=True`; `ProjectSubmission.clean` requires it only when the toggle is on; `submit_project` stores `""` when off; the package project page hides the input when off | `coursework/models.py`, `coursework/projects.py`, `templates/coursework/project.html` |
| `CourseworkConfig.ready()` registers the Studio section only when `COMMUNITY_BASE["COURSEWORK_STUDIO_ENABLED"]` and imports `api_views` only when `COMMUNITY_BASE["COURSEWORK_MEMBER_API_ENABLED"]`; both default `True` | `coursework/apps.py`, `kernel/conf.py` |
| Migration `cb_coursework.0006_project_module_commit_id_field` (after `0005`, depends on `cb_curriculum.0004`) | `coursework/migrations/` |
| Tests | `tests/coursework/test_adoption_toggles.py` |
| Docs | `coursework/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/02-architecture.md`, `docs/plan/phase-5.md`, `docs/plan/STATUS.md` |

### Ambiguity resolved

The plan offered gating on `apps.is_installed("community_base.accounts")`. DTC does not install `community_base.accounts` (it has its own `accounts` app), so that gate would drop DTC's coursework Studio section and member API. I used the two `COMMUNITY_BASE` settings instead, which default to today's behaviour. They are kernel `COMMUNITY_BASE` keys rather than runtime `community_base.config` keys, because `ready()` reads them once at startup, where a database override could never take effect.

`models.py` was already over the 300-line limit. It grows by the three model fields plus one 5-line `clean`: framework constraint, since fields and model validation live on the model.

## Verification (worktree off `origin/main` `eb2f3e3`, `uv sync --all-extras`)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `uv run ruff check .` | All checks passed |
| `uv run ruff format --check .` | 885 files already formatted |
| `testproject/manage.py check` | no issues |
| `makemigrations --check --dry-run` | No changes detected |
| migrate from empty SQLite | `cb_coursework.0006_project_module_commit_id_field... OK` |
| reversible: `migrate cb_coursework 0005`, then forward | unapply OK, reapply OK |
| `pytest tests/coursework tests/test_boundaries.py tests/kernel tests/homework_steps tests/studio tests/curriculum` | 986 passed |
| full `uv run pytest` | 2390 passed |
| `scripts/plan.py check` | OK: 184 issues |

No data loss: `sqlmigrate` shows two added `cb_coursework_project` columns (`commit_id_field` backfilled to `1`, nullable `module_id`) and a no-op for `commit_id` (`blank=True` is validation only). No existing row changes value.

### Mutation proof (each new test fails on a deliberate break)

| Mutation | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| `ProjectSubmission.clean` never raises | `test_commit_id_is_required_by_default`, `test_full_clean_requires_commit_id_only_when_the_project_asks_for_it` |
| `ready()` ignores both settings | `test_site_can_install_coursework_without_studio_or_member_api` |
| template always renders the input | `test_project_page_shows_the_commit_id_input_only_when_asked[False-False]` |
| `submit_project` stores the commit id when the toggle is off | `test_a_commit_id_is_not_stored_when_the_project_turns_it_off` |

The gating tests boot a fresh process without `community_base.accounts` (the AISL shape) and count the coursework Studio sections and API routes: `studio=1 api=3` by default, `studio=0 api=0` with both keys `False`.

## Done when

- [x] A project can belong to a module and survives the module's deletion.
- [x] A project with `commit_id_field=False` accepts a link-only submission; the default still requires a commit id.

author: rcownie
body:
Closes #2656

## The gap
`plugin.ValidateManifest` checks a manifest's own internal consistency only — name/version format, that type references inside the manifest resolve. Nothing cross-references a `HostFuncDef`'s `Input`/`Output` `TypeDef` against the real Go request/response struct fields the host function actually uses. `plugins/llm` is the only plugin that maintains a `plugin.json`, and it had drifted: `chat_input`'s manifest was missing `api_key` (added for cleat#1988), and `chat_output` described a flat `response`/`tool_calls`/`finish_reason` shape while `providers.ChatOutput` actually returns a `choices` array plus `cost`/`model`/`estimated_cost`.

## The mechanism
`plugins/llm/manifest_type_parity_test.go` adds `TestManifestTypesMatchGoStructs`: a reflection-based structural comparison between each host function's manifest `TypeDef` and the real Go struct it describes, recursing through arrays/maps/objects and named type references. Checker over generator — smaller verified mechanism, falsifiable on its own without also taking on "what does codegen from Go types look like" as a design question.

Run against the real (pre-fix) manifest, it found **seven distinct drifts**, not just the two the issue cited: the `message`/`tool`/`tool_call` nested shapes also disagreed (a Go `Tool` is `{type, function: {name, description, parameters}}`, the manifest had it flat), and `embed_output` was missing `usage`/`cost` while declaring `model`/`total_tokens` fields that don't exist on `providers.EmbedOutput`.

**`list_models` is explicitly out of scope**, not silently skipped: its response is assembled from `map[string]any` and a function-local anonymous struct, not a named Go type, so there's no stable `reflect.Type` to point the checker at. Its own manifest fields (`models`, `providers`) are untyped opaque `object`s with no nested `Fields` either, so there's nothing structural for a checker to compare there regardless — the same "an object with no declared Fields is opaque by the manifest's own choice" rule the checker applies everywhere else.

## The manifest fix
`plugins/llm/plugin.json` corrected to match `chatRequest`/`providers.ChatOutput`/`embedRequest`/`providers.EmbedOutput` as they exist today (all now verified by the test above). One thing worth flagging rather than fixing here: I initially drafted `chat_output.usage` and `choice.message` as references to a named type (`usage_info`, a new `choice_message`), but `plugin.ValidateManifest`'s `validateTypeDef` only resolves named-type references at the array-item level (`items: {"type": "some_named_type"}`) — a field's own `.type` pointing directly at another named type is never validated and silently passes through unchecked either way. Inlined both instead, matching the convention the rest of the file already used. Didn't fix `validateTypeDef` itself since it's a separate, adjacent gap in manifest validation semantics that affects every plugin, not just llm's drift — flagging in case it's worth its own issue.

## Falsification
Removed `chat_input`'s `api_key` field, confirmed the checker fails naming exactly that field, restored, verified the restore against a backup byte for byte.

## Prior art checked

author: senamakel
body:
Adds `crates/tinyruntime-pyserver`, a pure library (no bus, no module) that keeps one Python interpreter warm and serves named backends over a private JSON-lines stdio protocol. It is extracted from OpenHuman `runtime/python_server` (the persistent spaCy + Kompress worker).

- `PythonServer`: spawn, handshake, request with one restart-and-retry, status, idle check.
- `ServerSlot`: the process-wide cache: one shared worker, rebuilt when the backend set changes or a named backend idles, five-minute back-off after a failed start. The host passes a lazy future that prepares the `ServerLaunch`.
- `ServerLaunch`: interpreter, script, backend ids, env, timeouts. The host builds it from its own config; this crate reads no host setting.
- `SERVER_SCRIPT` / `write_script`: the worker script, embedded so its protocol revision matches the crate.
- Wire and status types are unchanged from the OpenHuman originals (literal-JSON fixture tests included).

No change to the `tinyruntime` module, the bus contract or the ABI. Tests use `sh` scripts as the fake interpreter; per-file line coverage is at least 96 percent (`cargo llvm-cov`, gate is 90).

Based on `main` (= v0.2.7). OpenHuman pins the identical commits on `oh-pyserver-on-v0.2.7`.

body:
Kate asked to recover the current DO work, audit what is actually built and reduce the confusing homepage. Recent Personal DO PRs are merged, but repeated entry points and device-local checklists make the experience fragmented.

This change keeps the approved atelier and Living Brief, gives Pursuit/DO/Studio one compact explanation, moves extra demos behind optional controls, and makes Personal DO the main DO destination. One composer is visible at a time, examples are optional and guests can start a local checklist immediately.

Signed-in people can explicitly save/open/remove a private checklist collection across devices. Full schema validation, session-scope matching, RLS and a service-only expected-revision RPC protect account isolation and stale overwrites. Empty snapshots retain revision tombstones. This is manual save/restore, not automatic chat sync or reminders. No user data was seeded.

The audit also found an unverified background worker: production heartbeat NULL and nine 401 cron responses in the inspected window. The UI now distinguishes missing/stale heartbeat from configuration. Authentication is preserved. Repairing the Vercel cron configuration and proving a real owner/provider run remains necessary before claiming always-on operation.

Validation:
- Standard full pnpm build passed: compilation, TypeScript and 206 static pages.
- Standalone typecheck, focused ESLint, brand/front-door/macron guards passed.
- Full DO core selection: 1,257 tests passed, two skipped by the existing suite. Twelve local PostgreSQL checks passed.
- 94 real-page browser checks passed: 22 for the new flow plus 72 for existing customisation, call lifecycle and assistant behavior. Fixtures are fictional; the real anonymous cloud endpoint denied with 401. 375/320px, explicit consent, save/restore, conflicts, cancellation/deletion and no runtime errors verified.
- The old example/disclosure assertions were updated for the intentional simpler navigation. CI now also exercises snapshot browser and SQL boundaries; no security test was removed.
- Additive migration 20260930063926 applied to Assembl-prod; actual RLS/grants checked. No production user records created.
- Local staged tree exactly matches the uploaded Git tree.

Audit and evidence:
- docs/ASSEMBL-DELIVERY-AUDIT-20260930.md
- docs/evidence/do-refinement-20260930/
- scripts/review-do-refinement.cjs
- scripts/test-do-personal-checklists-sql.cjs

Limits: no verified real signed-in provider run, physical phone proof, bank OAuth, automatic push, household sharing, signed iPhone distribution or changes to separately hosted client hubs. These are explicitly ordered in the audit. Native iOS PR #1417 remains draft. Live trading remains disabled.

Rollback: revert the application change; preserve the private snapshot table for export/removal rather than dropping user data. Kate's prior explicit push/merge permission covers this delivery; merge only after reviewing current-head checks.

Release repair: clean CI reproduced the pre-existing Turbopack Google-font query failure in Air NZ operations and Contact Energy. Those two lockups now use a bundled Cormorant Garamond 4.001 asset with its OFL licence, existing variables/weight range and complete character coverage. FontTools verified identical character mapping, horizontal metrics and axes to the official source. No framework/dependency upgrade or design change. See lib/fonts/assets/README.md and docs/evidence/do-refinement-20260930/font-proof.json.

External checks: Supabase Preview is blocked by the older duplicated migration version 20260716090000, not this additive snapshot migration. Actual schema/grants and isolated PostgreSQL tests provide the snapshot evidence. Cursor/Vercel automated reviews could not run due to usage/credit limits; they are not represented as successful reviews.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces owner-scoped private data persistence and a new authenticated API with revision semantics; mitigated by RLS, session binding, and broad tests, but cross-device saves affect real user checklist data.
> 
> **Overview**
> This delivery **simplifies the public homepage and DO entry** while adding **explicit, consent-based private checklist snapshots** for signed-in Personal DO users.
> 
> **Homepage & routing:** The atelier hero and Living Brief stay; repeated product sections become three compact product doors, with Pursuit research and the DO film behind optional expanders. ## What & why
Closes #26

**Stacked on #143 (#122) → #138 (#121).** The diff shows their commits until they merge.

M1 Registration and M2 Approval pending (PLAN §8 mechanics, §10.0, §12.2; wireframes M1, M1·Ind, M2). A new mechanic registers either as a **workshop** or as an **independent** mechanic, and lands in admin approvals (A2) as `pending`. After that, onMechanicRegistered (#101) sets their claims.

### M1 Registration (`LaneFlowScaffold`, "Step n of 4")
1. **"Do you have a workshop?"** (workshop / independent) + **city** (the rules let only admins change it later).
2. **About you:** name + profile photo; then
   - **workshop:** shop name, shop address, shop photo;
   - **independent (M1·Ind):** years of experience, base area, travel vehicle + plate (normalised, e.g. `GJ16CK4471`), **2–5 toolkit photos**.
3. **Your work:** vehicle types (chips) + services (`ProblemTile` grid).
4. **ID and payment:** ID proof + UPI ID / name; independents also add a **selfie holding the ID**, **address proof**, and an optional **reference** (name + E.164 phone; half a reference is an error).

- **Validation** uses `roadside_core`'s `mechanicProfileErrors` / `mechanicKycErrors`, the same rules Firestore enforces (#99). Errors show on Next, per field, and clear as they're fixed. Each type writes **only its own fields**.
- **Photos:** picked from camera or gallery (`LaneSheet`), then ≤ 1600 px / ≤ 500 KB JPEG with **EXIF stripped** (same pipeline as `customer_app`).
  - Profile / shop / toolkit go to `mechanics/{uid}/shop/…`, stored as download URLs.
  - ID / selfie / address proof go to `mechanics/{uid}/kyc/…`, stored as **Storage paths, never URLs** (§8).
- **Submit:** profile + KYC in **one batch** (the KYC rule reads the profile via `getAfter`), with timestamps via `stampNew`; the KYC phone always comes from Auth. Then **`getIdToken(true)`** picks up #101's claims.
  - A failed upload or save shows a plain message; the retry **skips photos already uploaded**.
- Back keeps answers; each step opens scrolled to the top.

### M2 Approval pending (`LaneStatusScaffold` on the ThreeUI still)
- **Workshop:** "We're checking your details. Usually within 24 hours." Checklist: shop details ✓ received, ID proof checking.
- **Independent:** "**We'll call you for a short verification**, usually within 24 hours." Checklist adds the verification call.
- **Blocked:** "Your account is on hold", with Call support.
- Call support (when configured) + Help.

### Routing
After first run: **M1** until registered → **M2** while pending or blocked → **home** once approved. The router re-runs when the profile changes, so an admin's approval moves the app on by itself. Help, the privacy notice and permission explainers stay reachable from M1 / M2.

### Data seams (until Firebase is wired)
- `RegistrationRepository`: `InMemoryRegistrationRepository` is the default; `FirestoreRegistrationRepository` is written and tested with `fake_cloud_firestore`. It needs an `AuthSession` (uid, phone, `refreshClaims`), which lands with login (#123).
- `MechanicPhotoUploader`: the fake returns Storage-shaped values; the Firebase Storage uploader lands with #120 (it must set `contentType: image/jpeg` for the rules).
- New deps: `image_picker`, `flutter_image_compress`, `cloud_firestore` (same versions as `customer_app`); dev: `fake_cloud_firestore`.

### Notes
- **Base area location:** `baseArea.geopoint` is the **city centre** for now (checked against `firebase/seed`), with the locality text saying where exactly. Dispatch never uses it (live location, §10.0). "Use my location" can come with M3 (#27) when location lands.
- **Local widgets:** `PhotoSlot` and `FieldError` are new `_local_ui` widgets, candidates for `lane_ui` (@CODER7657).
- **hi / gu:** the M1 / M2 strings are mine and need the glossary review (#55). Problem types, vehicle types and validation messages reuse `customer_app`'s wording.

## Screenshots / recording
Pending: no local Android build yet (see #143). The flows are covered end to end by widget tests below.

## Checks (local, Flutter 3.47.5)
- `dart format`: clean · `flutter analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings`: no issues
- `flutter test`: **66/66**, 29 new:
  - **Draft:** every step for both types; workshop vs independent requirements; experience / plate / toolkit / UPI / selfie errors; half a reference; **each type writes only its own fields**; city centres match the seed.
  - **Submit:** workshop and independent upload paths (`shop/` URLs vs `kyc/` paths); **upload failure → retry doesn't re-upload**; save failure → retry; a missing field jumps to its step; backing out of the camera changes nothing.
  - **Firestore:** one batch, `status: pending`, only independent fields, **phone from Auth**, claims refreshed, `watchProfile`.

  - **Screens:** unregistered → M1; Next shows what's missing; **workshop path end to end → M2**; **independent path end to end → M2** (incl. the toolkit-minimum error); Back keeps answers; **approval moves M2 → home**; blocked wording; **320 px × 200%** (gu step 1 + independent step 2, hi M2).

body:
## What

- `scripts/dev/entra_live.sh`: a person step with real secrets, no duckdb-acl. The person is an administrator by the `secrets_admin` app role and holds `analysts`.
  - The person creates `entra_live`, grants `use` to `role:analysts` and `role:nodes`, and revokes it from `role:analysts`.
  - DuckDB's `which_secret` finds the secret only while it is granted: never before the grant (an admin role gives no `use`), and not after the revoke.
  - The node steps then find the secret through `role:nodes`.
  - Every step checks the lines it must print (`grep -xE`), and the script exits nonzero when one is missing.
- `website/docs/entra.md`:

author: senamakel
body:
## Summary

- Add persistent advisory file locks for transcript mutations. Generation creation holds the successor lock from its existence check through the first successful write, so concurrent compactors cannot both claim the same generation and a crash cannot leave an empty reservation.
- Validate each turn append baseline against the latest logical transcript under the lock; stale sessions now receive a persistence error rather than hiding another writer’s turns with a compaction.
- Add thread and subprocess race tests, and document lock-file placement and behavior. Lock files live under the workspace `.transcript-locks/` directory and are retained to keep waiters on one lock inode.

Fixes #198

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-session` (166 unit tests and 2 doctests)
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-runtime` (64 unit tests)
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-harness` (1446 unit tests; 43 doctests passed, 3 ignored)
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-graph` (508 unit tests; 3 doctests passed, 2 ignored)
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-registry`
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-orchestration`
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-definition`
- `cargo test -p tinyagents-integration-tests`

The network-gated live tests were left ignored. The implementation treats a stale turn baseline as a persistence conflict; callers must reload the session before retrying.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved reliability when multiple processes update transcript history at the same time, preventing conflicting writes from overwriting one another.
  * Creating the same next transcript generation concurrently now allows only one attempt to succeed.
  * Turn appends based on outdated transcript history now return an error, preserving newer recorded messages.
  * Writes to a transcript generation are rejected if its successor has already been committed.

author: gafferongames
body:
## What this is

IT24 of `design/EVENT-DRIVEN-TICK-v2.1.md`: `tla/SprintEvents.tla`, the TLA+ model of layers 3 to 8 of nova-sprint (events, due times, rules, the tick, the verbs), written from section 5 with plan and apply as separate actions for every rule and verb, R17 included. It stands on the guarantees the layer 1 and layer 2 models prove (`tla/SetTable.tla`, `tla/SetTableLog.tla`, both now on `sprint/foundation`) and says so at the top. `tla/README-SprintEvents.md` has the model, the properties, every run, and the findings with their traces.

Third round: the model's `Fixes` match errata 3 to version 2.1 with its amendment 2 (04:35): the model's forms of H2, H3, H8 and H11 confirmed, H14, H15 and H16 decided and repaired, the H13 gap closed, and the error step carrying the lease generation. The branch is rebased once onto `sprint/foundation` f8125e65a (SetTable, PR 4775, and SetTableLog, PR 4780); every row of both sides of `tla/CASES.tsv`, `tla/RUNS.tsv` and `tla/README.md` is kept.

## Checked

- 111 gated cases in 14 `sprintevents*` groups, recorded by `tlacheck run` on the bench (two workers for a case expected to pass, one for a counterexample, 110 s a group); the largest group takes 83.3 s of TLC time on the loaded bench. `tla/RUNS.tsv` is the merge of those runs onto the records already there; `tlacheck groups --stale` prints `[]`.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/ci/` passes (with `TestTLCRecordsCoverCurrentModels`), and, run separately, `./internal/tlc/` and `./tools/tlacheck/`.
- The bench runs (`tla/sprintevents-bench/`, 900 s cap), on this round's module: FullOps2 (drops with two op names, resume, abort, crash, error, stop and start, rank, ack; every repair, the three new ones included) passes at 7,662,264 distinct states; FullLive passes; FullDesign meets H13 in 10 states; GoalFlap shows H12 (a 59-state lasso); GoalFlapStable, with the H12 repair, shows H15 (a 129-state lasso, 5,623,278 distinct states); RepairFlapStable, with the H15 repair (`unplaced`, `MaxPlaceTries` 3), passes `Progress` at 5,591,976 distinct states (715 s); Full2 (every repair, 2 verbs) did not finish: no violation in 14,359,942 distinct states at the 900 s cap, which is not a pass. No instance reaches section 5's (4 primaries, 3 readers, step bound 3, 6 actions): the README states the gap and owes that run.

## This round

| change | goal (fails without it) | passes with it |
|---|---|---|
| `dropcond` also leaves out `add n` while n's stream is being dropped (amendment 2, H8) | GoalDropAdd: `Answerable`, 4 states, on `Fixes = {}` (and with the second round's `dropcond`, a manual probe) | RepairDropAdd |
| `stoprearm` (H16): a close of the STOPPED judgment clears `raised`; R17 raises once per span and close | GoalRearm: `ProgressScoped`, a 26-state lasso, with `stopclose` (H16 is a hole in that repair: on `Fixes = {}` nothing closes the judgment and GoalRearm passes, a manual probe) | RepairRearm (`ProgressScoped`, `StoppedStaleCloses`, `StoppedOnce`) |
| `stopinputs` (H14): R17's step also guards on the version of what its dry plans read, as the revision of every card | GoalStaleRaise: `StoppedRaiseFresh`, 12 states, with `stopclose` (the same on `Fixes = {}`, a manual probe) | RepairStaleRaise |
| `unplaced` (H15): R6's 30 s entry restarts on a take, not a deal; a card dealt and withdrawn `MaxPlaceTries` (3) times without a take raises "this card cannot be placed" | GoalPlace: `UnplacedNamed`, 18 states, with `seenfresh` and `stablesince` (the count a ghost); bench GoalFlapStable: `Progress` (H15) | RepairPlace; bench RepairFlapStable: `Progress` holds (5,591,976 distinct states, 715 s) |
| `rankclose` covers the sentinel's own rescore (the H13 gap) | GoalRankSelf: `Answerable`, 7 states, on `Fixes = {}` (and with the second round's `rankclose`, a manual probe) | RepairRankSelf |
| `freezefirst`: a refused part returns the verb to read again, at most 2 times | GoalFreeze (H11, as before) | C13, Drop2; FreezeReach, a probe, shows a part applied after the fresh read |
| the LIMIT and bug error steps write only under the lease generation (1.3.5) | the same configuration on the second round's module fails `LeaseSafe` in 7 states (manual probes, both branches) | LeaseErr |
| W5Reach is said to break reach and unreach (the nit) | | |

## Holes

H1 to H13 are in the design as written; H14, H15 and H16 are in repairs errata 3 decided, and amendment 2 decides each (repaired above); H9 is wording. One new hole, found this round:

- **H17** (in amendment 2's decision for H14): `stopinputs` covers the cards, as the decision words it ("the streams' heads and the sentinels' scores"), but a dry deal also reads the fleet. GoalStaleFleet (12 states, with `stopclose` and `stopinputs`): STOPPED, p1 ready, m1 the only member up, so a dry deal is due; a look sets `due_since`, a unit passes, the next look plans the raise; `fleet down m1` applies (no member up, no move due, no card changed); R17's step applies and raises with no move due: `StoppedRaiseFresh` fails. With `stopclose` the stale judgment lives at most one look. A repair would add the fleet table's revision to the version. Not decided, not patched.

Every counterexample on the unbroken model was checked by hand against the design; the traces are in the README (Findings).

## Not modelled

The same list as at the top of `SprintEvents.tla` and in `README-SprintEvents.md`:

- R5 (cross), R7 (level), R12 (overdue), R15 (done), R16 (held) and R18 (behind). R16's table is the invariant `NothingSilent` instead (with a row for R6's 30 s entry under `stablesince`); the held queue with its cap, and `HeldDrop`, are not kept.
- Quarantine: a refusal naming a card is a layer-1 bug, and layer 1's model shows it does not happen.
- Clear, epochs and remove, so `EpochSafe` is not checked; CI, return, merge stops and resume; reader add; add in parts and insertion's anchors (an insertion is an add at an odd score); `ask --another`; the coordinator's `accept` verb (R9, the machine's accept, is modelled).
- R11's `idle:s` kind (a notice, no judgment), and R1's strangers (a beat from a member with no fleet row).
- The `askwait` index, and I3 for it and for `fresh` above sigma: `HeadActionable` checks `elig` below sigma, deal's heads and `wait:n`.
- `NoLostWork`'s "parked (and named)": a parked key counts as owed without the check that its judgment is open. `Named` does check a parked key per card.
- Byte and read budgets other than the step bound; the tick's step budget (a tick applies every request it planned); R19's one step a tick.
- The rules' reads as separate snapshots: a tick plans every key on one snapshot, then applies request by request, with every outside action free to run between two requests.
- A note line that queues no key is not written.
- The order of two keys of one priority in the round robin is the one TLC's `CHOOSE` gives; the design leaves it open, and a trace that needs the other order needs another scenario.
- The row of "this card cannot be placed" (H15's judgment): its decisions are not decided; the model prints `drop` only, and the judgment is neither held nor acked.

author: ognjhunt
body:
A follow-up to #2471 (Phase 3b PR 4). This PR closes the review's last item, which was low-severity and pre-dated its final commits.

The remote episode-compilation collector read three records with `_read_record`, which returns `None` for any open failure. The collector took that `None` to mean "absent", so one EMFILE or EIO could:
- **Leave a pointer permanently unsealed.** In `_reseal_pointer`, the lease turned `completed` while the pointer kept `provider_zero_proven: false`.
- **Skip a settlement.** In `_close`, a provider-zero attempt with an unreadable teardown was skipped as "settled elsewhere". This failed safe, because the worst case stayed charged against the caps, but the attempt was never settled.
- **Re-prove a sealed teardown.** In `_seal_teardown`, an unreadable record sent the collector back to prove provider-zero again, and the rewrite then hit a record conflict.

## The fix
- **`_read_json_present`** returns `None` only when the record is absent (`lstat` gives ENOENT). Any other failure raises a typed `remote_cpu_record_unreadable:<name>`. Those failures include EMFILE, EIO, a link, a special file, or a mode the collector can't trust. The next run then retries the step rather than taking it as done.
- **`_close` skips a provider-zero attempt with no teardown record only when that attempt is already settled.** Every provider-zero teardown, the allocator's or the collector's, is sealed at `teardowns/<attempt>.json` before the lease says so. A record missing before settlement therefore raises `remote_cpu_teardown_record_missing`: the attempt stays charged at its worst case and the problem is surfaced.

Other `_read_record` callers keep their meaning.

**Review of this PR:** a counterexample, fixed in `63159b4f3`. The strict read made `_close` read every provider-zero attempt's record before checking `_settled()`. So a persistent EACCES on a *settled prior* attempt's record raised on every run, and the current attempt was never torn down: its slot stayed held. Now:
- a settled attempt with no reseal due is skipped before anything is read;
- each attempt's teardown, settlement and reseal runs on its own, and a failure is raised only after every other attempt has had its turn.

## What the first deploy after merge does
Nothing changes in `host` mode, which never reads these records. With remote compilation enabled, a failed read is retried by the next run instead of skipped.

## Verification
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| The reviewer's counterexample as a test: attempt 1 settled with its record unreadable, attempt 2 compiled. It was stuck with a slot held; it now completes with 2 settlements and 0 slots | passed |
| Three new tests, each failing before the change: EMFILE on the pointer read, then resealed by the next run; EMFILE on the teardown read after a failed settlement, then settled exactly once; a teardown record missing before settlement, surfaced and the lease left open | 3 passed |
| After the second fix: the episode-compilation suites, slow tests included | 91 passed |
| The episode-compilation, allocator, lease, records and census suites | 215 passed. One inherited failure: the allocator line budget, 7,465 > 7,456 on `main` |
| `-m slow` on the episode-compilation, worker and transport suites: parity, byte identity ×4, runtime closure | 12 passed |
| 49 test files covering remote CPU, episode compilation, scene compilation, disk and storage, systemd, the volume move, lane governance, the env guard, the chain preflight and the object store | 1,164 passed, 1 skipped. The same inherited allocator failure |
| CI's own impacted selection for this PR, 10 tests and files, sentinels included, run locally | 120 passed |
| `ruff check` | clean |
| `scripts/verify_source_governance.py` | only the inherited allocator budget |

## Review and CI
- **Review:** the PR 4 reviewer's final item. A re-review of this PR found the settled-prior-attempt counterexample, and the fix was then APPROVED at `63159b4f3`. Its 48-hour EACCES probe passes in every variant, a BaseException crash still propagates, and all 23 earlier probes pass.
- **CI:** `Impacted tests and sentinels` and its gate pass. The full suite was not required for this 2-file change.

author: aidenarokij
body:
Closes #4 — in a lighter form than asked.

**What.** A fifth AI tab, **«Разбор задержания»**. After a detention the officer tells — typed or with 🎤 — what they did and in what order. Each step is weighed against the server's laws:
- **По закону** / **Нарушение** (with «Как надо») / **В законах сервера не нашлось**, each with its article, opened with a click;
- **Не сделано** — duties the found articles require that the story lacks;
- «По закону: N из M · нарушений · не сделано», a one-line summary, and **«Скопировать разбор»** as plain text for the academy.

**Why not the recording the issue asked for.** Recording the whole detention would take other players' voices (detainee, lawyer, others) without their consent, and they come from the game or Discord — the whole computer's sound would have to be captured. A 10–30 minute recording is also costly for the AI and poorly recognised in noise. So the officer tells it themselves: nothing is recorded, only their own text goes to the AI, as in the other modes (PRIVACY.md lists the mode).

**Grounded like the rest.** Only found articles are sources. A step called a violation, or a missed duty, must cite one of them (`citedIn`); otherwise the step is shown as «В законах сервера не нашлось» and the missed duty is dropped — the AI cannot make up a violation the officer did not commit.

**Code.** `src/ui/detention.ts` (the hook, the prompt, `grounded()`), `src/ui/DetentionView.tsx`, the tab in `AiView.tsx`, Enter / voice / placeholder / hint in `Overlay.tsx`. Built like «Требования адвоката».

**Tests.** `src/ui/Detention.test.tsx`: steps and verdicts, a violation citing an article the laws don't have is not shown as one, a missed duty without a found article is dropped, the counts, the copied text, what the AI is sent; and a story the AI makes nothing of. `npm test` 409/409, `npm run typecheck` clean. Checked the tab in the preview — five tabs fit.

author: okxint
body:
Vitest runs Vite with `command: 'serve'` and `mode: 'test'`, so the `annotateSourceFile` condition was `true` during `AstroContainer` tests. After `@astrojs/compiler-rs@0.5.1` (shipped in Astro 7.3.5) started implementing `annotateSourceFile`, `experimental_AstroContainer.renderToString()` began emitting `data-astro-source-file` and `data-astro-source-loc` attributes on every element in tests — breaking any test that asserts exact HTML markup.

Adding `viteConfig.mode !== 'test'` excludes test runs from source annotation while keeping it enabled in normal dev server use.

Fixes #18162

author: yamihatsukoi
body:
## Changes

### Dungeon feel
- **Movement:** constant-speed gliding, 0.15 s per tile. The next step starts just before the current one ends, so held keys and tap paths move without stopping. Previously each step eased in and out.
- **Companions** glide along the trail instead of jumping between tiles.
- **Camera** follows more tightly and positions snap to device pixels.
- **View:** sight radius 6 → 8, and the default zoom is one step wider.
- **Rendering:**
  - terrain is pre-rendered into 16×16-tile chunks (one per water frame, LRU cached);
  - fog is a one-pixel-per-tile overlay, and only the visible part is drawn;
  - lighting and vignette are pre-rendered.
  - Result under 4× CPU throttle: 19 → 45 fps (60 fps unthrottled).
- **Trees and tall obstacles** now stand in the middle of their tile, on dungeon floors and on the sanctuary's forest border.
- **Floor 4:** pines are now the main obstacle and book stacks only occasional.

### Economy
- The dock button becomes 💰 **Bán** and only sells. Buying needs a trip to a dungeon town or the **Market** building, whose stalls grow with its level:
  - level 1: general store, seeds, produce;
  - level 2: + apothecary;
  - level 3: + smith, tailor;
  - level 4: + arcane, jeweler.
- New gold sink, **forge enhancement** (a button in the Lò Rèn panel):
  - each gear slot can go from +1 to +10, and each level makes the item in that slot 6% stronger;
  - the level stays with the slot when gear is swapped;
  - cost grows steeply with the level and with the deepest floor reached;
  - success chance falls from 100% to 30% at the top levels; a failure only costs gold.
  - Enhancement shows on party gear tiles.

### Party screen
- Compact header: portrait, name, class and level, thin HP/MP/EXP bars, appearance and roster buttons.
- Four tabs (Trang bị / Chỉ số / Kỹ năng / Nội tại), each with a badge (upgrade hint, unspent points, skill slots, passive slots).
- Gear is a grid of icon tiles with short names, enhancement level and ⬆ hints; full stats show when a tile is opened. A key-stat summary sits above the grid.
- Much less always-visible text; explanations moved into tooltips.

## Testing
- `vitest`: 51 tests pass, including a new forge enhancement test (cost, failure, cap, the level staying with the slot).
- `tsc` and `vite build` succeed.
- Playwright: walk FPS measured with and without throttling; party screen checked on desktop and mobile.

Refs #127

**`biffo-plugin-idea-scout` has `scripts/error_branch_coverage.py` present (shared-sync delivered it) but never runs it, and its coverage config excludes the directory it lives in.**

Diagnosed while re-verifying `keiranholloway/biffo-template#1603` against real current state (2026-09-04). The template's own distribution half is done and confirmed: this repo's `scripts/error_branch_coverage.py` blob is byte-identical to the template's (`0d5972c2`). What's missing lives entirely in this repo, not upstream, so a template-scoped session cannot fix it directly.

Confirmed by reading this repo's own files via the GitHub API on 2026-09-04:

1. `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.coverage.run]` has `source = ["src"]` — `scripts/` is not measured, so an uncovered `except` there produces no signal even if the gate ran.
2. None of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` or `.github/workflows/release-guards.yml` (nor any other workflow file) invoke `error_branch_coverage.py --check` or generate the `--cov-report=json` it needs. The script sits present and inert.

**What closes it**, mirroring the working shape in `biffo-plugin-marketing#184` (cited as reusable in `biffo-template#1603`):

1. Widen `[tool.coverage.run] source` to include `scripts` alongside `src`.
2. Add pytest's `--cov-report=json` flag wherever coverage already runs in CI.
3. Add an `Error-branch coverage` step calling `error_branch_coverage.py --check` in `release-guards.yml` (or wherever this repo's other required gates live), with a ratchet baseline so pre-existing uncovered branches don't block — only new ones should fail.

Until this lands, an uncovered `except` added to this repo's `scripts/` today goes undetected exactly as it did in `biffo-plugin-marketing` before that repo adopted the gate.

Part of keiranholloway/biffo-template#1603

Implemented by biffo-fleet-v2's implementer agent.

WP-2 de `docs/plans/WP-POS-STATION-DEVICE-CUSTODY-2026-09-29.md` (o plano vive em `dsh/go-live-acceleration-20260929`), na postura da **D-007**: vários dispositivos no mesmo terminal, **com visibilidade**. Avisa e pede confirmação, nunca recusa.

- Tela (`operator-kit`, `OperatorStationSetup`): a opção de cada balcão diz "N dispositivos já usam este balcão · caixa aberto"; no 409, a mensagem aparece como aviso e o botão vira "Usar este balcão também".

`cashman.Entry` / `SessionEvent` (WP-6), a regra de custódia (um turno por terminal) e migrações: nenhuma.

Beads: **sim-jbt.2** (epic sim-jbt)

## Summary
- **`[profile.wasm-release]`** in `Cargo.toml`: inherits `release`, with `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = "fat"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `debug = false` and `strip = "symbols"`.
- **`index.html`** points trunk at it for release builds only (`data-cargo-profile-release="wasm-release"`), and turns on binaryen `wasm-opt -Oz` (`data-wasm-opt="z"`; it was `"0"`) with `--enable-bulk-memory --enable-nontrapping-float-to-int --enable-sign-ext --enable-mutable-globals`. Trunk 0.21 downloads wasm-opt (version_123) itself, locally and in CI.
- **Untouched:**
  - Native `cargo build --release`: `[profile.release]` is unchanged.
  - Dev `trunk build` / `trunk serve`: dev profile, no wasm-opt.
  - The CI workflow: `trunk build --release` picks the profile up from `index.html`, so the workflow file needs no change.
- No code, gameplay or asset changes.

## Sizes (local `trunk build --release`, `gzip -9`)
| | wasm raw | wasm gzipped | build time |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Before** (master, `data-wasm-opt="0"`) | 132.3 MB | 19.9 MB (Pages measured 20.5 MB) | 181 s |
| **After, `opt-level = "z"`** (this PR) | **25.9 MB** | **8.2 MB (−59%)** | 368 s |
| Tried, `opt-level = "s"` | 31.4 MB | 9.8 MB | 440 s |

`"z"` is used: it's 1.6 MB smaller gzipped, and `"s"` sits only just under the 10.25 MB target, leaving little room as the game grows. **Tester:** please watch for any frame-rate drop in the browser, since `"z"` trades some runtime speed for size. If play feels worse, switch to `"s"`: one line, still under target.

## CI time
- Master's web job: **60 s** (warm cache).
- This PR's web job: see its CI run. Expect several minutes, because fat LTO and `codegen-units = 1` rebuild Bevy, plus a wasm-opt pass (about 5 min of the 368 s local build). Later runs benefit from rust-cache for dependencies, but LTO still re-links everything.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] PR records wasm size before and after, raw and gzipped; gzipped after is 8.2 MB, under 10.25 MB.
- [ ] After deploy, the Pages wasm `content-length` with gzip matches. *(Pages gzip level may differ a little from `gzip -9`; check after merge.)*
- [ ] Web smoke test: menu → start → serve → break bricks (explosive + particles) → pause → game over, with no console errors. *(Tester, in the browser.)*
- [x] Native `cargo build --release` uses unchanged settings; the size profile is web-only.
- [ ] CI's web job passes and deploys; duration noted above, pending this PR's run.
- [x] `cargo test` (135), clippy `-D warnings` and `trunk build --release` pass.

## Possible further savings (not done, per spec)
Trimming Bevy features (for example `bevy_audio`, `bevy_gilrs`, `bevy_gltf` and other formats this 2D game doesn't use) could cut more, but it needs a careful per-feature check against the game.

author: ktalons
body:
Adds an adapter for the Heimdall Data Format, the third Phase 2 slice (ADR 0013). HDF is what InSpec's `json` reporter writes and what `saf convert` writes from Nessus, Trivy, Burp, and other scanners, so one adapter covers native InSpec and CINC Auditor runs, the STIG baselines published as InSpec profiles, and every converted scanner report. `complyroll ingest` and the three `report` commands accept it beside the STIG checklists and SARIF logs.

Dispatch keeps every existing artifact where it was. A name ending `.hdf.json`, in any case, goes to the HDF adapter. A bare `.json` file parses as before and goes to it only when the parsed root has no `stigs` member, a `profiles` array, and a `platform` object, so every checklist keeps its dispatch. A checklist saved under a `.hdf.json` name is refused, and the message names its `stigs` member and says to read it under a `.cklb` or `.json` name.

Each control that survives overlay shadowing becomes one observation of source type `hdf`, keyed by its id under the root profile's name, on `platform.target_id` or, when the document declares no target, on the scan and root profile name. Identity uses the ADR 0002 recipe unchanged. A result reads OPEN when it failed, PASS when it passed, NOT_REVIEWED when it was skipped, and ERROR when it errored or carries a backtrace, since InSpec writes a check that raised as its RSpec status plus a backtrace. A control takes its highest-ranked result with OPEN first, so an errored sibling never hides an observed failure. A control with no results is ERROR. Impact 0 is NOT_APPLICABLE, with an INFO line naming what the results would have read.

Waivers and `saf attest apply` attestations are recorded as metadata with a warning and never change a disposition. Severity comes from the `severityoverride` tag, the `severity` tag, or InSpec's impact bands, and it is evidence only: it never sets PAIN. `observed_at` is the earliest result `start_time`. Converted documents write `""` there, so they need `--detected-at` or `cases attest-detection` like any clockless artifact, and the examples README walks through that on both paths.

Overlays decide the design. The wrapper profile lists every control with `results: []`, and only the profile at the bottom of the `parent_profile` chain holds results. The adapter walks `parent_profile` rather than `depends`, whose entries are local aliases. The copy with results shadows the empty copies, and a dangling parent or a cycle refuses the artifact. A waiver or attestation that only an empty wrapper copy carries passes whole to the surviving copies, outermost wrapper first, so the warning that says it is recorded stays true. Copies that fold into one observation take each group whole from one copy and never mix two.

Every document is untrusted. It is read through the existing bounded JSON reader and the existing limits: `max_results_per_run` bounds the controls in a profile and the results of a control, `max_observations_per_artifact` bounds the observations, and the per-observation ceiling and per-artifact byte budget apply as they do for SARIF. The one new bound is 64 profiles per document. An identity input past its cap is refused with an ERROR and never truncated, evidence is cut and marked, and an impact that is not a number from 0 to 1 is warned about and ignored before any arithmetic, so a 400-digit integer cannot crash the run.

Also in this PR:

- The SARIF helpers HDF shares move to `adapters/common.py` behind public names; `sarif.py` binds them by alias, and a test asserts every binding.
- The shared CVE and CWE patterns now end on a token boundary, as GHSA already did, so `CVE-2024-1234evil` names no identifier. This narrows SARIF extraction and KEV matching for such a token; no fixture carries one and no existing golden moves. It is recorded in an ADR 0011 amendment.
- A `description` whose title already leads with the record id is no longer prefixed twice. The rule sits in the shared record compiler, so the VDT, AVI, and historical reports all take it. No existing golden has such a row.
- A duplicate JSON object key is quoted and cut in the refusal message for every JSON adapter, so an untrusted key cannot write a control character to the terminal.
- `stigroll` skips an HDF document with a warning, and prints `could not parse` for an HDF or SARIF file that fails to parse instead of hiding the refusal behind the skip line.

Memory: a 3.3 MB document of 50,000 controls peaks at about 330 MB RSS in the adapter, 515 MB for a stateless `report vdt`, and 810 MB for a persisted `ingest`. ADR 0013 records these numbers.

Verification:

- 1581 tests OK on Python 3.11, 3.13, and 3.14 (215 in `tests/test_hdf.py`); ruff, mypy, and notation-check clean, and `ruff format` clean on the files this PR adds.
- Four synthetic fixtures and two new goldens, `tests/golden/vdt-hdf.{json,md}`. The stateless path, the persisted path, and the replay reader give the golden bytes in all six ingest orders of the three golden fixtures. The twenty existing goldens are byte-identical.
- Review: a Claude verify workflow (six lenses, one refuter per finding, plus a mutation run) and an eight-leg cross-vendor Forge audit, then a second Claude verify workflow over the fixes. Every confirmed finding is fixed, and every code finding has a test that fails without the fix. Each of the 44 mutants in the review's table fails a named test on 3.14 and 3.11.

Docs: ADR 0013, the ADR 0011 and 0012 amendments, README, BUILD_PLAN, ARCHITECTURE, DATA_MODEL, SECURITY, the FedRAMP mapping, the examples README, and CHANGELOG under Unreleased.

Commits: the first four move the shared helpers, add the reader, add the goldens and the front doors, and add the docs. The fifth folds the review fixes into the files the first four add or touch.

author: nicolas-bracigliano
body:
## Why

Two chrome problems:

- **The day/night toggle changed width with the theme.** The label swaps between "day" and "night" ("día" / "noche"), so the pill grew ~9px (58.3 → 67.3px) when switching to night and shoved the language toggle and the rest of the chrome sideways.
- **The desktop header didn't fit between 721px and ~901px.** The mark, the six-item nav, and the jump-to + lang + day/night group need ~901px in Spanish once the gutters are respected. Narrower, the row overflowed the viewport by up to ~100px (ES, 740px) and pushed the theme toggle off-screen. From ~845px to 901px it didn't scroll, but ran up to 17px into the right gutter. Below 720px the compact header took over, which is why phones were fine.

## What changed

**`fix(chrome)`: toggle width** (`base.css`)
- The longer word renders invisibly in `::after`, stacked in the same grid cell as the visible `::before`, so the pill is always sized to "night" / "noche". It measures the real text, so it holds if the font changes. A fixed `ch` width would be wrong under small caps.
- `text-align: start` overrides the button's centring, so the gap from icon to word stays constant.

**`fix(chrome)`: compact header below 920px**
- The compact header (compact mark, icon-only search and day/night, nav in the bottom foot-rail) now takes over at **920px** instead of 720px. That's where the desktop row fits with ~19px of slack. These move together:
  - `base.css`: the chrome + foot-rail block
  - `cmdk.css`: the magnifier-only search pill
  - `chrome.ts`: `MOBILE_BREAKPOINT`, so the foot-rail's hide-on-scroll switches at the same width
- Page layouts keep their own 720px split. Nothing else assumed the foot-rail only existed below 720px.
- Removed the ≤880px nav-gap rule, since the nav is hidden there now. `tokens.css` now documents 720 (page layouts), 880 (two-column layouts) and 920 (chrome split).

I considered keeping the top nav on tablets by compacting it (icon-only controls, tighter gaps, smaller mark). It only fit by letting flex crush the search and theme buttons, or by cramming the row, so the existing compact header won.

## Verification

- **Toggle:** the same width in all four states (EN/ES × day/night), 67.3px in Chromium and 68.2px in WebKit, at 1280 and 800px. The language toggle and nav no longer move.
- **Header:** swept every 4px from 700 to 1300px in EN and ES, both themes, Chromium and WebKit. At every width there's no horizontal scroll, the chrome never runs into the gutters, no control is crushed, the top nav and foot-rail are never shown together, and the nav keeps ≥16px of clearance.
- `verify:fast` and `verify:slow` (build, html-validate, 162 e2e, lhci) pass.
- Firefox is not verified.

Checked the switch with a throwaway debug line at startup, removed before committing. With `--spring.profiles.active=dev` both the DEBUG and WARN lines print and `library.environment` resolves to `dev`. With `prod` the DEBUG line is gone and only WARN prints. `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=dev` as an environment variable gives the same result as the command line flag, which is the mapping the container uses.

### Typed configuration

Added `library.borrow.max-books-per-patron=5` and `library.borrow.loan-period-days=14`, bound through `BorrowProperties` in `com.example.library.config` with `@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "library.borrow")`. Nothing injects it yet, that comes in Phase 6.

Verified with a temporary test asserting the bean binds to 5 and 14, and separately by running `Phase1GradingTest`, which passes both of its checks. Neither test file is part of this commit since Phase 1 does not ask for tests.

### Packaging

`mvn clean package` builds `target/library-service-0.1.0.jar` and `java -jar` starts it standalone. Tomcat comes up on 8080 and `curl localhost:8080/` returns 404, which is right since there are no endpoints until Phase 2. `jar tf` shows 35 dependency jars nested under `BOOT-INF/lib/`, which is what makes it runnable on its own.

### Container

Multi-stage `Dockerfile`: `maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17` builds the jar, `eclipse-temurin:17-jre-jammy` runs it, so no Maven, no sources and no `~/.m2` cache end up in the final image. Added a `.dockerignore` so the build context skips `target` and `.git`.

Docker is not installed on this machine, so the image build and the `docker images` size comparison against the single-stage version are still to do. Everything else above was run and checked.

### Also

Created the empty `com.example.library.service` package with a `.gitkeep`, as Module 1 asks.

Existing test suite stays green: `mvn clean package` runs `LibraryServiceApplicationTests` with no failures.

Round three of the tab bar redesign, bonsplit side. **Stacked on #5** (base `tab-bar-qol`); rebase onto `main` once #5 merges. The c11 side is the paired PR (linked below): it bumps this submodule and fills the new detail model.

## What changes

- **Fixed-grid sheet.** 46pt two-line rows: `Tab N` · activity mark · title (the only flexible column, min 260) · agent (150) · status (104) · one column per clock (78) · close (22, space always reserved) · grip (24). Header row, footer (`N tabs`, `K need you` in amber). An empty cell shows `—`; text truncates inside its column; tabular numerals; nothing moves when text changes or a clock ticks. Width comes from the columns, clamped to the screen. Relative times refresh once a second and only while the sheet is open.
- **Host-provided detail, bonsplit stays generic.** `BonsplitTabDetail` (full title, agent label, subtitle, status + since, named clocks) rides on `Tab`/`TabItem`. The host sets it with `updateTab(_:detail:)` and `tabDetailProvider` refreshes it as a sheet opens; `sheetClockOrderProvider` orders the clock columns (unknown names ignored; `seen` renders `—` until the host supplies it).
- **Count cell on every tier.** `TabCountCell` (`N ▾`, fixed 54pt, background-waiting dot) is pinned at the left of the full tier's trailing chrome and folded into the tier math (`needFull`, `needMedium`, the chrome width), so thresholds stay exact. In the full tier the sheet's right edge anchors to the cell; collapsed tiers stay flush-left under the bar.
- **Palette.** `TabBarColors.sheetPalette(for:)`: near-black family for the sheet, collapsed header block and count cell; near-white equivalent when the chrome background is light. Gold rules stay.
- `BonsplitController.setTabSheetOpen(_:inPane:)`: opens/closes a pane's sheet without a click (automation seam).
- 21 new strings in all 7 locales (en, ja, ko, ru, uk, zh-Hans, zh-Hant).

body:
## Description

Closes #472

CI installed other kubebuilder and kind versions than `.tool-versions` pins, and Renovate could not move them because they sat in `run:` scripts. Each workflow step now reads its version from `.tool-versions`, so the Renovate `tool-versions` update moves CI in the same pull request. The Makefile `renovate` pin now gets one update per release, not a minor branch and a patch branch.

## Changes

- Chart and Release workflows: kubebuilder comes from `.tool-versions` (4.16.0, was 4.13.1).
- Chart workflow: kind comes from `.tool-versions` (0.33.0, was 0.31.0). The kind cluster uses the v1.37.0 node image of kind 0.33.0, which matches kubectl 1.37 in `.tool-versions`.
- e2e workflow: kind comes from `.tool-versions`, not from `dl/latest`. Today latest is 0.33.0, so the e2e cluster does not change.
- `renovate.json5`: the `renovate` rule sets `separateMinorPatch: false`, as #456 does for helm.

## Challenges

The kind node image in the Chart workflow stays pinned by digest, as before. Renovate does not move it with a kind update. A kind release that drops support for the pinned image fails the Chart job on the Renovate pull request, and the pin then moves by hand. The comment above the step says to bump both together.

## Related

- #456 adds the helm rules next to the `renovate` rule in `renovate.json5`. The two diffs touch neighbouring lines, so the second merge can need a small conflict fix.

## Testing

- `make helm-generate IMG=controller:latest` and `make helm-verify` pass with kubebuilder 4.16.0. No tracked file changes.
- `make lint-renovate` passes. `actionlint` passes on the three workflows.

author: dayvidpham
body:
The first live boot exposed three things the static checks could not:

1. **All four slots autostarted** at boot (microvm.nix defaults `autostart = true`),
   each holding ~4.3 GiB with no jobs. The pool is meant to start slots on
   demand from the dispatcher; now `autostart = false` per VM.

2. **The guest image load failed** — `[FAILED] Failed to start Load the baked
   runner image into podman.` followed by `[DEPEND] Dependency failed for Run
   one GitHub Actions job...` — and because `runner-job` never started, its
   poweroff `ExecStopPost` never ran, so the slot wedged instead of powering
   off. `runner-image-load` now carries `OnFailure = [ "poweroff.target" ]`,
   and its output streams to the guest console (`journal+console`), which the
   host captures in the unit journal, so the next failure is diagnosable from
   the host.

3. **Container storage sat on the tmpfs root** (`/` is `size=50%` of the 4 GiB
   guest) while the runner image is ~1.4 GiB uncompressed — no room for
   `podman load`, and overlay-on-tmpfs besides. Each slot now gets a 6 GiB
   sparse ext4 volume at `/var/lib/runner-vm/disks/runner-vm-N.img` mounted at
   `/var/lib/containers`; the store is reset and the image reloaded every boot,
   so fresh-state-per-slot is preserved.

Validated statically: `microvm.autostart` is empty and the VM option `false`;
the guest mounts the volume at `/dev/vdb` (ext4); the runner payload creates
and formats the slot image; `runner-image-load` reports
`OnFailure=["poweroff.target"]` and `journal+console`.

After merging and rebuilding, verify with one slot:
`sudo systemctl start microvm@runner-vm-1` (no JIT) should boot, load the image
(visible via `journalctl -u microvm@runner-vm-1`), then power the guest off by
itself. The currently running wedged slots can be stopped first:
`sudo systemctl stop microvm@runner-vm-{1..4}`.

author: jacklightchen
body:
Add CAV 2016–2020 initial regular-paper deadlines and normalize the existing 2021 deadline to the repository's 23:59:00 default where the source gives no clock.

Original sources:
- 2016: https://i-cav.org/2016/call-for-papers/ — mandatory abstract registration January 24 and full paper January 29, both explicitly 16:00 EST (UTC-5). Main conference July 20–23, Toronto.
- 2017: https://web.satd.uma.es/pipermail/ecoop-info/2017-January/007767.html — original CFP posted by publicity chair Mikaël Mayer, January 24 AoE; explicitly no separate registration deadline. https://i-cav.org/2017/program/ places regular paper sessions July 25–28; July 24 consists of a separate workshop, tutorials and reception.
- 2018: https://i-cav.org/2018/cav-2018-call-for-papers/ — January 31 AoE; main conference July 14–17, Oxford.
- 2019: https://i-cav.org/2019/call-for-papers/ — February 7 AoE; main conference July 15–18, New York City.
- 2020: https://i-cav.org/2020/call-for-papers/ — January 28 AoE. Final online main conference July 21–24 is explicit at https://i-cav.org/2020/virtual-attendance/.
- 2021: https://i-cav.org/2021/call-for-papers/ — January 28 AoE for new submissions. February 4 is expressly an update-only window, not an extended initial submission deadline. Artifact abstract registration is excluded.

For AoE dates without a clock, 23:59:00 is the repository convention, recorded in comments. The 2016 clocks are stated explicitly. The archived originals were read through the web renderer; direct downloads of several old i-cav pages now return 404, so no claim of current live availability is made.

Deferred: 2015 abstract January 30 and full paper February 6 AoE are verified at https://i-cav.org/2015/call-for-papers/, but the recovered homepage gives the July 18–24 umbrella span. Its original schedule and important-dates links could not be recovered to establish the main-session span, so no 2015 edition is inserted yet.

Validation: YAML schema and unique IDs; all 2022+ entries remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Full remote diff and exact-head CI checked separately after publication.

Related to #1907.

body:
## Summary

Closes the "no real money behind the ledger" gap from `docs/LIVE_VALUE_RUNBOOK.md`: the unified value pipeline now reports how many **real** dollars back the ledgers, and the GCP runtime turns on the fiat funding and payout gates. Fiat only. No `THIRDWEB_*` / `STABLECOIN_*` / `SPRITZ_*` / `TRUST_POLICY_*` flag is touched.

**Pipeline (`osEngine.js` `unifiedPipeline`)** gets a new `spendable` stage (`stages` ends `..., 'payment_gateway', 'spendable'`) built by `spendablePosition()`:

```js
spendable: settle({
  summary: {
    realSpendableCents,        // = ReserveEngine.coverage().attestedReserveCents (never a ledger balance)
    ledgerCashCents, unbackedCents, backingStatus,
    stripeBalanceCents,        // CashEngine.getAccount('CA-STRIPE-BALANCE')
    payerSourceSpendableCents, // PayerOsEngine.readiness().fundingSource.spendable
    fundingRailReady,          // TreasuryFundingBankEngine.status().ready
    treasuryBankEnabled,
  },
  treasuryBank, stripeBalance, payerSource, reserve,  // each { ok, value } | { ok:false, error }
  gaps: [...],  // missing module / failed source / unverified treasury bank / unbacked ledger cash
})
```
Each engine is loaded with `tryRequire` and wrapped in `settle`, so a missing or failing source shows up in `gaps` and the pipeline keeps running. `realSpendableCents` is **only** the attested reserve. Ledger cash with nothing behind it goes in `unbackedCents` and is not counted.

**Trust admin workflow `funding` stage.** When `TREASURY_BANK_ENABLED=true` (read through `TreasuryFundingBankEngine.getConfig().enabled`), this stage now reports `TreasuryFundingBankEngine.status()`, which fails closed until the mandate is verified. Otherwise it reports `TreasuryOdfiBank` as before. Without this, turning on the Betterment/Stripe rail would still have shown ODFI readiness.

**infra/gcp**
- `variables.tf`: `TREASURY_BANK_ENABLED`, `PAYMENT_PROCESSOR_LIVE`, `PAYMENT_GATEWAY_LIVE`, `ENTERPRISE_NETWORK_LIVE`, `PRIVATE_PAYMENT_NETWORK_LIVE` and `CANONICAL_FUNDING_LIVE` change from `false` to `true`. `TREASURY_BANK_ID/NAME/ACCOUNT_HOLDER/REGISTER_SETTLEMENT` and `PAYMENT_PROCESSOR_DEFAULT=lili` already had the requested values. Every `REQUIRE_*` flag stays `true` and `PRIVATE_PAYMENT_NETWORK_MFT_LIVE` stays `false`.
- `CANONICAL_FUNDING_SAVINGS_ACCOUNT_ID` is left `""` because the real Fineract savings account id is deployment-specific. It belongs in the git-ignored `terraform.tfvars`. While it is empty, each source ledger account's linked Fineract account is used, and an unlinked account blocks the payout.
- `secrets.tf`: new `live_rail_secret_names` adds the Secret Manager containers each enabled rail needs (existing `*_secret_names` locals) to `runtime_secret_names`. Values are still added out of band with `gcloud secrets versions add`. No literals. **Deploy note:** Cloud Run refuses a revision that mounts a secret with no version. Seed these secrets first, or list them in `unseeded_secret_names`.

**Docs:** runbook §3 (how to read the `spendable` stage), §2a, and a new §8 flag change log. The checklist gets a new B13 row ("real dollars back the ledgers") and a flags note.

This makes the rail **capable** of moving money; it moves none. Real dollars reach `CA-STRIPE-BALANCE` only after the trustee runs runbook §4 (link, verify micro-deposits, explicit pull).

**Tests:** new `tests/unifiedPipelineSpendable.test.ts` checks the stage, the attested-vs-ledger math and gap reporting. The other pipeline stages are stubbed because calling them unstubbed crashes the vitest worker in better-sqlite3 teardown, which also happens on `main`. `paymentGatewayOsEngine.test.ts`'s trailing-stages assertion now includes `spendable`.

Validation: `npm run lint` (0 errors), `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run tests/engineWiringReadiness.test.ts tests/payerOs.test.ts tests/unifiedPipelineSpendable.test.ts tests/fixedIncomeBankRail.test.ts` (63 passed), `terraform validate`. `paymentGatewayOsEngine.test.ts` / `paymentProcessorOsEngine.test.ts` have 4 failures that also happen on `main` (engine counts 14 vs 46), not caused by this PR.

Separately noted and not changed here: `variables.tf` sets `LILI_ORIGINATOR="nacha"`, while runbook §2b describes Lili payouts as `stripe_payout`.

## Summary of Changes

本 PR 聚焦于后端全局性能优化与高频读写路径的资源开销治理，主要涵盖以下 5 项改进：

### 1. API 调用埋点改建为内存有界缓冲与周期批量落库
- **背景**：此前 `ApiUsageMiddleware` 为每个请求通过 `asyncio.create_task` 独立分配 DB Session 异步落库。高并发或流量突增时容易引发数据库连接池耗尽与写锁竞争。
- **优化**：
  - 引入有界双端队列 `_buffer = deque(maxlen=API_USAGE_BUFFER_MAX)`（默认上限 5,000 条），请求处理路径仅做 O(1) 内存写入；
  - 后台常驻 `_flush_loop` 任务以固定周期（5s）单次批量事务刷入最多 500 条记录；
  - 注册 FastAPI 启动与优雅停机（`startup_api_usage_flush` / `shutdown_api_usage_flush`）钩子，确保停机时尽力清空缓冲区。

### 2. 数据库查询优化与 N+1 消除
- **用户已报活动批量查询**：
  - `EventRepository` 新增 `list_by_ids` 方法（基于 SQL `IN` 语句一次性获取）；
  - `EventService.list_user_registered_events` 替换原本遍历报名记录逐条 `get_by_id` 的 N+1 查询，并保留原有报名记录排序语义。
- **活动签到码批量插入**：
  - `EventCheckinRepository` 新增 `create_many` 方法；
  - `EventService.generate_checkin_codes` 改造为单次 `flush` 批量入库，消除逐条创建的写放大。
- **RBAC 角色用户数聚合**：
  - `RBACRepository` 新增 `count_users_by_role`，以单条 `GROUP BY` SQL 统计各角色关联用户数；
  - `RBACService.list_roles_admin` 不再逐角色执行查询，彻底消除管理员角色列表接口的 N+1 性能瓶颈。
- **用户管理角色筛选下推到 SQL**：
  - `UserService.list_users_admin` 角色筛选改由 `User.roles.any(Role.name == role)` 下推至 SQL 执行；
  - 修复此前在 Python 分页后内存过滤导致的 `total` 统计失真和单页返回条数不足问题。
- **活跃管理员数量单条 SQL 聚合**：
  - `UserService._active_admin_count` 优化为 `func.count(func.distinct(User.id))` 聚合查询，避免将全量活跃用户及角色模型拉取至内存。
- **社区公开标签 SQL 原生展开**：
  - `community.list_tags` 使用 PostgreSQL `func.jsonb_array_elements_text(CommunityPost.tags)` 与 `DISTINCT` 查询，消除全量拉取帖子标签列表在 Python 内存去重的读放大。

### 3. HTTP 响应 GZip 压缩
- 在 `app/main.py` 注册 `GZipMiddleware`，对大于 1KB（`GZIP_MINIMUM_SIZE_BYTES = 1024`）的响应进行压缩，降低大 JSON 与长列表的传输体积与延迟。

### 4. 静态资源 HTTP 强缓存
- 头像服务（`serve_avatar`）与社区图片服务（`serve_community_image`）响应头添加 `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`；
- 由于资源文件名均携带毫秒时间戳且内容不可变，配合客户端本地缓存与 FileResponse ETag 机制，大幅减少重复图片请求的带宽消耗。

### 5. 第三方抓取超时与降级策略
- `ContributionService` 的 GitHub 贡献图抓取超时时间调整为 `GITHUB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 3`（原为 8s），在外部依赖网络抖动时快速失败并安全降级返回陈旧缓存，避免长时间挂起请求。

---

## Verification

- **自动化单元与集成测试**：
  - 运行全量测试套件 `PYTHONPATH=. pytest`，**381 passed, 86 skipped**，无新增失败用例。
- **接口兼容性**：
  - 所有 API 返回结构保持与前端现有契约完全一致。

author: mvanhorn
body:
Add a small pure commit-message cleanup function to the existing `AICommitsUtils` object and call it from `LlmClientConfiguration.setCommitMessage`, making the function part of the production path. Remove exact lowercase `<think>` reasoning blocks non-greedily across newlines, including an unclosed block through the end of the current response, before applying the existing user cleanup regex and final trim; recognize an opening tag with optional attributes only at a real tag-name boundary, leaving `<thinking>` and escaped tags unchanged. Suppress a trailing incomplete opening-tag prefix in cumulative streaming text so token splits such as `<thi` do not flash markup, and recompute from each cumulative input without introducing persistent parser state.

Issue #506 reports that MiniMax responses through the OpenAI client contain literal `<think>...</think>` reasoning in the generated commit message on plugin 2.19.1. Another participant confirms the problem and supplies a multiline cleanup-regex workaround, making the issue actionable without retrieving the attached image. The current `LlmClientConfiguration.setCommitMessage` only applies the configured cleanup regex, which defaults to empty, and then trims the result. `LlmClientService` sends both cumulative streaming responses and the final response through this setter, so incomplete reasoning blocks also need to be handled.

Complete single-line and multiline reasoning followed by a conventional commit message produce only the message, preserving its internal newlines and punctuation; Multiple adjacent reasoning blocks, optional opening-tag attributes, CRLF input, and whitespace between reasoning and message are handled without greedily deleting answer text between closed blocks.

Fixes #506

author: clattribe
pblumer
body:
## Merge this immediately before tagging, not earlier

`chart-release.yml` publishes the Helm chart as soon as `deploy/helm/atlas/Chart.yaml` changes on `main`, and OCI tags are immutable. Merging this PR therefore publishes chart **0.8.0** right away. Its default image, `ghcr.io/pblumer/atlas:0.8.0`, only exists once `v0.8.0` is tagged. Merge this PR and push the tag together:

```bash
git tag -a v0.8.0 -m "Atlas v0.8.0"
git push origin v0.8.0
```

Before merging:
- **Changelog.** Move any entry that has reached `[Unreleased]` on `main` since this branch into `[0.8.0]`. As of `481660da` there is none; pblumer/atlas#1166 added no entry.
- **Date.** The heading says `2026-09-30`. If the tag is set on a different day, change the date and run `make whats-new`.
- **Windows test.** Test the Windows artifact from a manual `release.yml` run (`workflow_dispatch`, which builds and publishes nothing) on the target Windows Server. Run it as a service, deploy a process, start an instance, stop the service and start it again, then check that the instance is still there. That is the failure this release fixes, and no CI job runs `atlas.exe` as a service.

## Summary

This closes `[Unreleased]` as **0.8.0** and puts the version in every place a release carries it. It follows the pattern of the 0.7.0 release commit (d9998468).

The section holds 31 entries: 14 features, 2 changed behaviours, 14 fixes and 1 under Security. The preamble covers three topics:

1. **Atlas on Windows.** 0.7.0's `atlas.exe` could not start a second time: the WAL reopened its newest segment append-only, and Windows will not truncate through that handle. The first Windows CI runs then found four more defects:
   - a record being read blocked deleting or saving it,
   - a store directory replaced by a file read as an empty store,
   - the generated vault key kept the data directory's access rights,
   - a script's timeout ended only the interpreter (pblumer/atlas#1162).
2. **A catalogue product as one lifecycle process** (ADR-0425, ADR-0427, ADR-0428), including directed triggers.
3. **`latest` resolving at run time again.** This reverses what the 0.7.0 summary announced, and the preamble says so.

It is a minor bump under the pre-1.0 policy. The preamble's "Read this before upgrading from 0.7.0" list names what acts on an existing installation:
- 409 for an untriggered create into a process with several start events and no none start event;
- processes deployed under 0.7.0 keep their frozen decision version until redeployed;
- a decision service refuses an input of the wrong type, on running instances too;
- a deploy refuses a `versionTag` binding;
- a client draining a version has to pass `nextCursor` back;
- a script that leaves a program holding its output fails instead of waiting, on every system;
- the Windows vault key a 0.7.0 install generated;
- the still-open pblumer/atlas#1123;
- records 0.7.x cannot replay (`TriggerReceived`, `TriggerReceiptsPruned`), which make the upgrade one-way.

## Changes

- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** a `[0.8.0]` heading with the preamble, an empty `[Unreleased]` left in place, and extended compare links. No bullet in the upgrade list starts with bold, because the feed generator reads any `- **…**` under a version heading as an entry.
- **Versions:** `api.Version` and `mcp.serverVersion` set to `0.8.0-dev`, with the `-ldflags` examples in their doc comments following.
- **Helm chart:** `version` and `appVersion` set to 0.8.0, and the install commands in the chart README.
- **Install commands:** the download, checksum and Windows service commands in `README.md` and `docs/install.md`. The sentence "releases up to and including 0.7.0" about the vault key stays, because it describes history.
- **What's New feed:** `api/web/whats-new.json` regenerated. The twelve entries carry 0.8.0.
- **Merges of `main`:** two merge commits bring in entries that landed after the release commit. Two came from pblumer/atlas#1160 and pblumer/atlas#1165, and one from pblumer/atlas#1162, which the release waited for.

Left alone on purpose: `docs/runtime-contract.md` still says 0.6.x, for the reason the 0.7.0 release gave. Moving that line would assert a check nobody made.

## Checks run

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are clean.
- `go test -race -timeout=45m ./...` is green locally on the release commit and on this head, `fe23532d` (78 packages, 0 failures).
- CI on `fe23532d` is green, including `windows · storage` and `windows · api`, which now runs the Worker Types too.
- `GOOS=windows go vet` over the storage, `api`, `connector` and `engine` trees is clean.
- `go test ./scripts/whats-new/... ./docs/adr/`, the changelog and feed tests in `./api`, and `go test -race ./connector/script/` pass.
- Every relative link added in the preamble resolves to an existing file.

## What this cannot show

- The CI Windows jobs run the packages on Windows Server 2025, not the binary as a service. The save-while-reading fix relies on a POSIX-semantics rename, which Go falls back from on systems without it. Whether that fallback applies to the target server's version (Windows Server 2016 is the likely case) is unverified.

author: musyg
body:
## What

Two recipes went red under load, each for one root cause. Both causes belong to one class:
concurrent runs of the suite shared state they did not own.

- `tests/tunnel_par_coeur.rs` (Linux): the working directory had a fixed name. With two runs
  started 2 s apart, 12 out of 12 went red; the core relaunch of one run executed the other
  run's wrapper. It now uses a per-process directory, and the recipe requires that the core
  listening on its API is its own child.
- `coeurs::port::port_sans_personne` (Windows): the function returned a port number that was
  bound and then released. Windows hands that number out again, either to another bind or as
  the source port of the next connection, which then connects to itself. It now returns a
  `PortSansPersonne` that HOLDS the port (a bound socket, never listening, without
  `SO_REUSEADDR`). The recipe requires the refusal itself. Its bound goes from 2 s to 10 s,
  because on Windows the refusal takes 2.0 s and the old bound expired before it (40 timeouts
  out of 40).

## The class

- The facade, switch-over, transport and relay recipes released a port the same way; the
  facade went red 2 times in 314 suites.
- Six fixed temporary paths in recipes, and the probe copy of `check` on Linux, now carry the
  process id.
- New guard `partage_entre_executions.rs`: it reports `temp_dir()` without a pid or unique
  label outside named exceptions, a number read from a released listener, and a held port not
  consumed in place.

## Verification

- Red rates before and after, under the same load:
  - Linux, two staggered runs: 12/12 -> 0/12, then 0/40.
  - Windows, the exact recipe shape under allocator pressure: 7/80000 -> 0/80000.
  - Windows, full suites run in pairs: 3/314 -> 0/314.
- Counts (`scripts/recettes-strict.sh`, announced/abstentions/ignored/red/real):
  - Windows dev host: 1371/19/0/0/1352 -> 1375/19/0/0/1356
  - Linux test host (git clone): 1391/25/1/0/1366 -> 1395/25/1/0/1370
- Falsifications: 4 on Linux and 8 on Windows, each red observed before being written.
- Independent adversarial verification: PASS. It reproduced 12/12 red before and 0/12 after,
  and replayed four falsifications, all red.

## Not measured

- CI.
- The window in `liberer` before a third-party child binds.
- The daemon's fixed default ports (out of scope here).

author: cent-dave
body:
closes #646 

Title:
perf: unify Horizon health polling into useHorizonHealth and pause when tab hidden

Description:
## Summary

Consolidates two independent periodic Horizon health check pollers (`TopBar` and `OfflineBanner`) into a single source of truth via a new `useHorizonHealth()` hook and `HorizonHealthProvider`. 

Prior to this change, `TopBar` polled `HORIZON_URL` every 15 s (treating status < 500 as online) while `OfflineBanner` polled `${HORIZON_URL}/` every 30 s (treating only `res.ok` as online). Neither poller paused when backgrounded, causing an idle open tab to send ~6 requests/minute to Horizon indefinitely and allowing the two indicators to disagree.

The unified poller resolves this by implementing:
1. A single source of truth reading `HORIZON_URL` with a standard `res.ok` (200–299) success rule and a 3 s abort timeout.
2. Background tab pause: clears timers and aborts in-flight requests while `document.hidden`.
3. Immediate re-check on `visibilitychange` (when returning to the tab) and on window `online` events.
4. Intelligent backoff: polling starts at 15 s, backs off to 60 s after 2 consecutive successes, and resets back to 15 s immediately upon any failure or offline state.
5. Deduplication and cleanup: a reference-counted singleton store (`HorizonHealthPoller`) backed by `useSyncExternalStore` ensures only one poller and timer ever runs regardless of how many consumers mount it, with clean lifecycle management under React StrictMode.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix / Performance improvement
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Localization (i18n)
- [ ] Accessibility
- [ ] Smart contract / on-chain wiring
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Acceptance Criteria Mapping

| Acceptance Criterion | Implementation Details |
|---|---|
| Only one periodic Horizon health request exists in the app | Unified in `HorizonHealthPoller` singleton store. `TopBar` and `OfflineBanner` consume `useHorizonHealth()` and share the same timer. |
| No health requests are sent while the tab is hidden | `document.hidden` clears pending timers, aborts in-flight requests, and guards against scheduling new requests. |
| TopBar indicator and offline banner always agree | Both components read `isOnline` from the exact same hook and state snapshot. |
| Unit tests for the hook cover visibility pause/resume, backoff, failure reset, and online/offline events | 11 comprehensive tests in `src/hooks/useHorizonHealth.test.tsx` verifying all lifecycle transitions, interval adjustments, and consumer agreement. |

## Verification & Testing

- `npm test`: 81/81 test files passed (794 tests total), including all 11 new tests in `src/hooks/useHorizonHealth.test.tsx` and all tests in `src/shell/TopBar.test.tsx` and `src/shell/TopBar.network.test.tsx`.
- `npm run typecheck`: Passed clean with 0 errors (`tsc --noEmit`).
- `npm run build`: Production build completed cleanly across all 20 routes with Next.js Turbopack.
- Prettier formatting validated on all touched files.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run build` passes locally (builds + type-checks)
- [x] `npm test` passes locally (full suite passes with 0 failures)
- [x] Follows the design system and repository conventions
- [x] Accessible & clean teardown on unmount
- [x] No secrets committed
