body:
## Summary
- Add `manifests/oauth2-proxy` (Deployment + Service): oauth2-proxy acts as a reverse proxy in front of demo-nginx, using Keycloak's `home` realm (with Google as an Identity Provider) as its OIDC provider.
- Add `localargo/apps/oauth2-proxy.yaml` so it's GitOps-managed like the other apps.
- Change `demo-nginx`'s HTTPRoute backendRef from `demo-nginx:80` to `oauth2-proxy:4180`, so `demo.focus4.net` now requires Google login (via Keycloak) before reaching demo-nginx.

## Prerequisites (already done manually)

author: sergii
body:
## What

Implements the first hosted reverse relay vertical slice without coupling ORTYO core to a cloud vendor or tunnel transport.

- makes exposure mode/access explicit through `CreateExposure`
- routes forward and relay exposures through separate providers
- adds deterministic relay URLs for relay-mode exposures
- adds transport-neutral `RelayRequest` / `RelayResponse` envelopes
- adds `RelayBroker` request claim/completion semantics
- routes relay work through the existing local HTTP Boundary
- correlates `relay_request_id` and `exposure_id` into Interaction evidence
- proves raw request body + signature header preservation
- models unavailable and disconnected runtime failure semantics
- documents the ACCESS2 protocol boundary

## Proof

```text
RelayBroker ingress
      |
      v
registered runtime
      |
      v
proxy_relay_request
      |
      v
HTTP Boundary
      |
      +--> Interaction(origin=proxied)
      |
      v
local target
      |
      v
RelayResponse
```

The transport remains intentionally undecided. WebSocket, HTTP/2, QUIC, and deployment provider selection can now be implemented behind this protocol rather than inside the domain.

Tracks #9.

body:
Owner, 30 Sep: the Personal Pic folder (Final Edited Photos > Based on Excel Sheet > Personal Pic) files six pictures as CO-240001 to CO-240006. The ask: "update the art code to website".

## Codes

Each picture was matched to its product on the website by picture, compared against all 536 current products. All six were on temporary codes.

| File | Product | Was | Match |
|---|---|---|---|
| CO-240001-3825 | #33278 The Golden Sardar | TMP-1162 | the same photo, 346 matching points |
| CO-240002-3050 | #25358 Dancers in Ocean Light | TMP-1248 | the same photo, 237 |
| CO-240003-3050 | #25779 Dancers by the Lamp | TMP-1250 | the same photo, 164 |
| CO-240004-5030 | #25840 Dancers in Duet | TMP-1251 | the same photo, 246 |
| CO-240005-3050 | #33302 Sunset Shore Dance Duet | TMP-1170 | the beach picture, printed on a stand; the only product that shows it (#25358 shares only the two dancers, set in water) |
| CO-240006-0000 | #28778 Dancer on Stage | TMP-1276 | the same dancer, pose and costume, 114; the file has the backdrop changed to the Nataraja |

In `tools/artcode-corrections.csv`, four rows replace the file's `NONE` rows (#25358, #25779, #25840, #28778) and two rows are new (#33278, #33302). The two rows added this morning in c4fe63e ended in LF; they now end in CRLF like the rest of the file. Content is unchanged.

CO is outside the art-code book, like AC and CP:
- `af_artcode_book_code` and `af_artcode_full_code` return nothing for it.
- Corrections and renumbering leave it as written.
- The SKU is the code: `af_sku_code_part('CO-240001-3825')` gives `CO-240001-3825`.

## Not changed

Five products show these dancers in photos taken at an event. They stay on their temporary codes, and the owner has been asked whether they should share the artwork's code:
- #33292 and #33300: the duet print on a stand.
- #33298: the lamp picture on a stand.
- #33296: two prints on stands.
- #33294: the stage dancer with a second dancer.

## Tests

- All suites pass:
  - `test-artcode-book` 79
  - `test-renumber-writes` 37
  - `test-corrections-chain` 53
  - `test-temp-artcodes` 28
  - `test-sku-follows-code` 29
  - `test-art-code-display` 17
  - `test-sku-swap` 37
  - `test-sku-code-part` 20
- Deploy simulation on the live catalogue of 30 Sep, 07:22 UTC (536 products, health check): corrections, renumbering and the temporary-code pass change exactly these six codes. 102 products stay on temporary codes.
- The real SKU pass, run twice over the same catalogue:
  - The first run changes exactly the six SKUs, TMP to CO. There are no duplicates and no product without a SKU.
  - The second run changes nothing.
  - #8474 keeps TP-050004-5030B, since the product named for that page, #229, has been removed.

## Also carries

`tools/export-thumbs.mjs` prints every product's main picture as a small JPEG to the log, read from the public Store API. It is used through `qa-personas.yml` for the picture-to-picture duplicate checks. The server-side `diag-artcode-thumbs.php` runs only inside a full deploy, which would also run every catalogue pass. This one is read-only.

## After merge

Only `tools/` changes, so the push to main does not deploy by itself; `deploy.yml` is dispatched by hand. Then `tools/verify-co-codes.mjs` checks the six live as a first-time visitor:

author: doldori7
body:
## 무엇을 · 왜

저장소 규칙("반복·시스템 실수는 세션이 끝나기 전에 재발방지 대책을 코드·태스크로 등재하고, 사고는 사고 대장에 적는다")에 따라 2026-09-30 `/drive` 세션에서 반복된 두 가지를 대장에 올린다. **코드·스키마·설정·시크릿 변경 없음** — 대장 파일 3개(태스크 1 · 사고 샤드 1 · 세션 이벤트 샤드 1). 판정 기준 main `fff5b74a`. `MEMORY.md`는 건드리지 않는다 — 이 PR이 다루는 충돌의 원천이 바로 그 파일이라, 사고를 MEMORY.md가 아니라 사고 대장에 적었다.

1. **`MEMORY.md` 동시 append가 GitHub 서버 병합에서 충돌** — 태스크 `HARN-210-memory-md-concurrent-append-github-dirty`(P2 · 설계 판정이 먼저) + 사고 대장 계열 `memory-md-append-github-dirty` 1회차.
   - 실측(main `3bc9fb2e` 시점 — 태스크 acceptance의 정정 항 참조): `MEMORY.md` 3,368,672바이트·11,689줄 · main 커밋 24시간 21건 중 10건·7일 101건 중 51건이 `MEMORY.md`를 건드렸다.
   - 이 세션 사례: PR 1396이 2회 · PR 1385가 1회 GitHub에서 `dirty`(충돌)로 보였고, dirty PR에는 GitHub가 CI 런을 만들지 않았다(각 PR 본문에 기록). main `fff5b74a`(EOS-154)가 다시 `MEMORY.md` 끝을 바꿔 두 PR이 같은 조건이 됐고, 로컬 git의 union 병합으로 해소했다(충돌 0 · 삭제 0줄).
   - 같은 계열(공용 append 파일 × GitHub 서버 병합)의 이벤트 대장은 `HARN-46`, 사고 대장은 `HARN-130`이 샤딩으로 풀었는데 `MEMORY.md`를 맡은 태스크는 없었다(태스크 제목·본문 검색 기준). 기존 자동 재동기화(`.github/scripts/pr_auto_resync.sh`)도 충돌(409)은 사람 몫이라 이 계열을 풀지 못한다(스크립트 헤더를 읽어 확인).
2. **태스크 번호 중복(`HARN-200`)** — 사고 대장 `task-id-collision` 13회차. PR 1385의 `HARN-200-push-time-mirror-head-notice`와 [PR 1377](https://github.com/kiki-s-broom/WhyMath/pull/1377) 브랜치(`claude/harn-180-424n4m`)의 `HARN-200-runbook-self-containment-waiver-cleanup`이 같은 번호를 쓴다. 실측: 원격 예약 대장의 소유는 PR 1385 브랜치(예약 커밋 `5b968d4c` · 2026-09-29 10:26:44Z)이고 상대 세션은 예약 없이 등재했다(`add` 이벤트 10:26:48Z) — 그 브랜치 트리(`541f2043`)에 `HARN-111`의 `number_guard.py`가 없었다. 머지 큐가 막기 전에 PR 1385 쪽을 `HARN-209`로 개명했다(그 PR의 커밋 `708610f4`). 이 PR은 그 사고의 기록만 남긴다.

## 검증 — 무엇을 돌렸고 결과가 무엇인가

- 대장 정합 5종(`validate` · `audit-deps` · `rules lint` · `rules render --check` · `jit check`) + `incident report` **전부 exit 0** — 태스크 959건 · 게이트 97건 · 규칙 85건(산문 29/기준선 29 그대로) · 적시 주입 후보 364건 · 사고 대장 774건.
- 등재한 태스크·사고 줄을 YAML/JSON으로 다시 읽어 대조했다 — acceptance와 notes의 핵심 식별자(`fff5b74a` · `merge=union` · 수치 · `pr_auto_resync.sh` 등) 누락 0. 백틱이 든 산문은 파일 경유(`"$(cat …)"`)로 넘겼다.
- **CI 미러**(`ci_mirror.py run --prepend-path <파이썬 3.12> --diff-base origin/main` · 커밋 `b11bb153` · 이 PR 자신의 3파일 → 도구가 5잡 선택): `infra-contracts`(`pytest tests/infra` 587.6s) · `infra-shell` · `policy-guard` · `harness-integrity`(하네스 테스트 531.4s) · `declared-unwired-audit` **전 잡 exit 0 · ✔ 33스텝 · 실패 0 · 미실행 스텝 0건** · 마지막 줄 `✔ 전 잡 통과`(래퍼의 `MIRROR_RC=0` · 결과 파일의 커밋이 HEAD와 같다). 미러 뒤 작업 트리 변경 0건(하네스 테스트의 이벤트 샤드 누출 없음).
- **그 뒤 커밋 `f8c037a7`**: 태스크 acceptance에 측정 기준 main 표기 정정 1항을 `backlog.py amend --acceptance`로 덧붙였다(수치가 `fff5b74a`가 아니라 `3bc9fb2e` 기준이었다). 이 커밋 뒤에는 **대장 정합 5종만 다시 돌렸고 CI 미러는 다시 돌리지 않았다** — 대장 텍스트 1항 추가이고, 최종 판정은 PR CI가 한다.
- 세션 이벤트 샤드의 `policy_warn` 12줄은 `add`가 낸 **실제** `path_overlap` 고지다(`id`가 `HARN-210-…` · `other`가 겹친 태스크 · `mode: warn`) — 하네스 테스트가 남기는 가짜 누출(`id: "-"`)이 아니다.
- [x] CI 잡이 이 변경을 실제로 실행한다 — 대장 변경이라 `harness-integrity` 계열 잡이 대상이고 미러에서 실행을 확인했다.

## 변별력 — 무엇을 *깨뜨려* 확인했는가

새 검증 장치를 만들지 않는 기록 PR이라 뮤테이션은 없다. 태스크 `HARN-210` ④가 픽스처와 뮤테이션을 요구한다('MEMORY.md를 건드리지 않는 PR'을 대조군으로 두어 전부 충돌로 계상하는 과잉 수정을 막는다). 이 PR에서 변별력이 있는 것은 읽기 대조뿐이다 — 기록한 값이 실제 저장소 상태와 같은지(수치는 `git log`·`git show`로, 번호 중복은 원격 전 ref 스캔과 `harness-claims` 예약 대장으로 다시 잰 값이다). 그 대조에서 측정 기준 표기 오류 1건이 나와 정정 항으로 고쳤다.

## 정직한 공백

- **머지 큐가 `MEMORY.md` 동시 append로 실제 이탈시키는지는 재현하지 못했다.** 사고 대장 파일의 MERGE_CONFLICT 이탈(`HARN-130` — [#1255](https://github.com/kiki-s-broom/WhyMath/pull/1255) · [#1363](https://github.com/kiki-s-broom/WhyMath/pull/1363))은 실측이고 같은 기제라고 읽어서 추정할 뿐이다 → 태스크 ① 픽스처가 재현한다.
- 이 세션의 dirty 횟수(PR 1396 2회 · PR 1385 1회)는 각 PR 본문과 세션 기록에서 센 값이고, 과거 시점의 GitHub 상태를 다시 조회해 확인한 것이 아니다.
- **번호 중복 원인 중 '상대 브랜치가 낡은 main 사본을 병합했다'는 확정하지 못했다.** 측정한 것은 (가) 그 브랜치 트리(`541f2043`)에 `number_guard.py`가 없었다는 사실 (나) `HARN-111` 착지 `b2b0c1e6`(main 08:57Z)이 그 커밋의 조상이 아니라는 사실뿐이다. 상대의 마지막 main 병합 메시지는 `c08c58c4`(07:59Z)까지였다.
- 상대 브랜치(PR 1377)는 다른 세션 소유라 고치지 않았다 — PR 1385 쪽만 개명했다. PR 1377이 머지되면 `HARN-200`은 그 태스크의 번호가 된다.

author: ysmr3104
body:
#22 の残り。**原因にかかわらず、星の中心を投影位置（またはクリック位置）のまわりで取り直してから開口測光する。** #22 ではフィクスチャの画素が上下反転していて、開口が約 7 px 外れていた（フィクスチャは直した）。

## 変更

- `refineStarCenter(image, ch, cx, cy, aperture)`（SkyQualityAnalyzer.js）
  - 背景: 半径 `aperture+5`〜`aperture+25` のアニュラスを sigmaClippingStats に通した mean / std（MAD は使わない）
  - 重心: 半径 `aperture` の中で `値 − mean > 3σ` の画素だけの重み付き平均（画素中心 +0.5）
  - 検出の条件: ピーク ≥ 10σ かつ有意な画素 ≥ 5（WCS テストの判定と同じ値）
  - 反復: 移動 < 0.1 px か 3 回で止める
  - 元の位置から `aperture/2` を超えて動いたら、別の星に引かれた可能性があるので取り直さない
- 数値の判定は純粋関数 `significantPixelCentroid()`（sqm_math.js）に切り出して Node で検査。閾値は `CENTROID_*` の名前付き定数
- `aperturePhotometry()` は中心を決めた直後に取り直す。戻り値に `projectedX/Y`（取り直し前）と `centroidShift` / `centroidRefined` / `centroidReason` を追加
- `runAnalysis()`: 1 フレーム 1 行の出力に移動量を出す。**3 px を超えて動いたフレーム、取り直せなかったフレームは結果の警告に出す**
- specs.md §8.4 に手順と閾値を追記
- クリック位置のダイアログは変えていない（取り直しは測光のときだけ）

却下した案: 画像全体から一番明るい星を探す（別の星を拾う）、取り直しを WCS の補正として他のフレームに伝える（フレームごとに解があるので不要、誤りが伝播する）、PSF フィット（ぼかした星のドーナツ像に合う PSF が無い）。

## テスト（98cfb8a）

| テスト | 結果 |
|---|---|
| Node test_sqm_math | 112/112 |
| test_wcs_transform | 11/11 |
| test_read_frame_metadata | 12/12 |
| test_measure_background | 8/8 |
| test_aperture_photometry | 11/11 |

**独立な正解を持つ検査（合成画像）**: 1 チャンネルの浮動小数画像に、背景 0.10、ガウスノイズ σ=0.002（種固定）、中心を小数で決めたドーナツ像（中心 (100.37, 80.61)、内径 4、外径 10）を描く。
- 開始位置を真値から 0 / 3 / 7 px ずらす → すべて真値との差 **0.0022 px**、`converged=true`
- 星を 1 つだけ置き、開始位置を +10〜+22 px ずらす → すべて取り直さず `code="too_far"`、位置は元のまま
- 40 px 離れた 2 つ目の星の近くから始める → その星に収束（差 0.0031 px）
- 合成像は 8×8 の副標本で面積を求めて描く。画素中心だけで硬い縁を評価すると、それだけで重心が約 0.1 px ずれ、テスト自身の誤差になる（Node で確認）

実データ: HD 136919 は投影から 1.9 px、Kochab（飽和）は 6 フレームで 0.73〜1.37 px 動いて取り直せた。HD 136919 の投影を (+20, 0) ずらすと `too_far`。

## レビュー対応

- 取り直さなかった理由をコード（`no_star` / `too_far` / `edge`）で区別し、コンソールと警告を出し分ける。**`too_far`（星は見つかったが 7.5 px 超離れている）は、星から外れた開口で測ったフレームがフィットに入るので、別の警告にした**
- 3 回で収束しなかったときはコンソールに 1 行出す（`converged`）
- 0.3 px ずらしのテストの名前を実態に合わせた

author: karimghabra
body:
This adds NCBI as a second source of full-text XML, which you approved on 2026-09-30.

Europe PMC's REST service serves full text only for the open-access subset. For an NIH author manuscript it answers `fullTextXML` with HTTP 500. PMC holds those manuscripts, and NCBI's E-utilities give them out by PMCID.

## What changes
- **`fetch` gets a new step** (`parser/litrag_parser/acquire.py`). The order is now: Europe PMC's XML, then NCBI's `efetch` by PMCID, then the bulk-area PDF, then `needs-pdf`.
  - Only the PMCID goes out.
  - The article is taken out of its `<pmc-articleset>` byte for byte, and must contain a `<body>`. NCBI answered a publisher's closed deposit (PMC9469745) with HTTP 400 in the morning and with 200 and front matter only an hour later. Both cases must end as `needs-pdf`.
  - NCBI is asked for every PMCID that Europe PMC didn't serve. Rows found before this change have `has_xml = 0` stored, and re-running a search never overwrites a stored value.
  - Requests are spaced at least 0.34 s apart.
  - `LITRAG_NCBI_URL` redirects the calls. `LITRAG_NCBI_EMAIL` and `LITRAG_NCBI_API_KEY` are sent only when set.
- **`has_xml` counts author manuscripts**, so the Search tab shows "open XML" for them.
- **A `needs-pdf` candidate can be fetched again from the Search tab** (`app/src/renderer/search.ts`). This lets existing libraries pick up the new route.
- **`wanted`, and so the Collect PDFs window, goes most-cited first.** This was the one unmet point of #1's spec.
- **The e2e fixture now also stands in for NCBI** (`app/tests/e2e/epmc-fixture.ts`, `studio.spec.ts`). Otherwise the suite's made-up PMCID would be sent to the real NCBI.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` invariant 1 now names NCBI; AGENT.md, README and PIPELINE describe the new fetch order.
- **Records:**
  - CHANGELOG's Unreleased section gains NCBI, the post-0.3.1 commits from #23, and a line for #24, which had no entry.
  - BACKLOG: the other XML sources checked live, and what's still stranded on `collect-mode` and `ingestion-generalization`.
  - NOTES: the NCBI standing decision and today's measurements.
  - `campaign/STATUS.md` no longer says "Phase 4, EXAM never scored".

## Verified
- `npm run check:all` on the merged tree: CLI 46, app 10 plus typecheck and build, parser 446.
  - 5 new acquire tests: an author manuscript fetched from NCBI, NCBI's refusal and front-matter-only answers both ending as `needs-pdf`, extracting the article from the set, contact fields sent only when set, and `wanted`'s order.
  - No test touches the network.
- **Live, against the real services:**
  - On `"electrochemically aligned collagen" AND genipin`, 14 of 22 hits are author manuscripts. 19 of 22 now have XML to fetch, against 5 before.
  - The real app under Xvfb, with live Europe PMC and NCBI, Docling on the CPU and Ollama's embedder: one paper fetched from Europe PMC and two from NCBI, all three read into trees with their methods found; the publisher deposit became `needs-pdf`.
- **Not run:** `npm run e2e:studio`. It needs the two archive PDFs on your machine. The fixture change only adds the NCBI stand-in, which answers 404, so the suite still takes its PDF route.

## Conflicts resolved
Merging `main` (#24, #25) conflicted only in CHANGELOG.md and NOTES.md, where both sides had added a newest-first entry. Both are kept, with #25's section under its own heading so its "not yet measured" caveat stays attached.

author: git-on-my-level
body:
## Problem

Firestore composite index creates ran synchronously in a loop, so each missing index held the migration workflow until its build completed. Large gaps could take hours serially and block backend deploys at the Firestore readiness gate.

## Change

- Pass `--async` to each composite-index create and issue all missing creates before the existing readiness poll checks the full expected set.
- Treat `ALREADY_EXISTS` in gcloud stderr as an accepted concurrent create; other failures still raise with the affected index named.
- Keep reconciliation create-only and preserve the dry-run output.
- Increase both index workflow readiness waits from 1 hour to 3 hours. Give both jobs a 4-hour GitHub Actions limit so the readiness window has time for checkout, authentication, and command overhead.

The longer wait accounts for large production collections where an individual index build can exceed an hour. Async creation allows all missing indexes to build concurrently, while the three-hour poll window gives that batch time to converge and the four-hour job limit retains operational headroom.

## Verification

- `BACKEND_UNIT_TEST_FILE_LIST=/Volumes/Ephemeral/scratch/worktrees/omi/omi-lane-idx-reconciler-async-upstream-keep-clean/.agent-brief/d1-tests.txt bash test.sh` from `backend/`: 156 passed, 1 deselected across the four requested suites plus the workflow contract suite.
- No live Firestore project was queried or mutated; index operations used unit-test doubles only.

## Product invariants affected

- INV-DATA-1 — workflow timeout configuration only; project selection and serving authorities are unchanged.

## Failure class (fixes)

Failure-Class: new

author: latand
body:
Studio stopped any song longer than 600 s at decode ("songs must be between 1 and 600 seconds"). This PR raises the bound to 40 minutes and keeps memory flat for long songs.

## Why 600 s existed
The bound came with the first commit, with no reason recorded. Of the steps a long song goes through, only Demucs grows memory with length. `apply_model` keeps all four sources of its whole input in RAM several times over (the bag of four models, the random shift): about 4 MB per second of song. pYIN already works in 25 s blocks, torchcrepe in 1024-frame batches, and lyric alignment reads only the vocal stem.

## What changed
- **Windowed separation** (`studio/prepare_song.py` `separation_windows`, `separate`). A song longer than 5 minutes is split into equal windows. Each window hears 8 s past its edges (one Demucs segment) and cross-fades linearly into the next over 4 s. The weights add up to 1 at every frame. Normalisation uses the whole song's mean and std. A song up to 5 minutes goes through the same single run as before.
- **Upper bound of 40 minutes** (`MAX_SECONDS`). The trainer sets it: it embeds all four stems as base64 in one script, 8.7 MiB per minute of song. Chromium's longest string is 2^29 − 24 characters (checked in headless Chromium), which a trainer passes near 58 minutes. A longer file gets a Ukrainian message, e.g. `Пісня триває 42 хв 7 с. Luma Studio готує пісні від 1 секунди до 40 хвилин: довший тренажер був би завеликим для браузера. Обріж файл або розділи його на частини.` It is refused before decoding when ffprobe knows the length.
- The trainer's `validateSong` accepts the same 2400 s. The Studio drop zone now says "до 40 хв · до 1 ГБ". Uploads are streamed to disk in 1 MiB pieces, up to 1 GB (a 40-minute 48 kHz / 24-bit WAV is under 700 MB). Imports go up to 512 MB.
- Docs: PIPELINE, TARGET_MAP_SCHEMA, AUDIO_QUALITY (the old 200 MB import note), README.

## Verification
- **The failing 608 s file**, full `prepare_song.py` with `--no-lyrics` (no paid Soniox call): 423 s, exit 0, 3 windows, 759 notes (523 ok), comparable 34.2 %. Peak RSS for the whole pipeline: 3.9 GB. The 88 MiB trainer opens in headless Chromium, plays from 588 s and logs nothing to the console.
- **Separation alone on the same file:** one run 5,491 MiB peak RSS, windowed 3,894 MiB. The two vocals differ by −20 dB overall. At the seams the difference is −21 and −25 dB, and inside a window it is −14 dB, so the seams add nothing beyond the run-to-run noise from Demucs's random shift.
- **The bound itself:** the same audio looped to exactly 40:00 prepares end to end in 33 min (separation 9 min, pYIN 17 min, CREPE 3.5 min). Peak RSS is 4.4 GB; one run would have needed about 12 GB for separation. The 349 MiB trainer opens in Chromium in 6 s and plays from 2380 s with a clean console.
- `tests/e2e/run.sh`: exit 0, with all eight browser suites and all Python suites. New tests:
  - `tests/separation_test.py`: the window plan, weights adding up to 1 with context around every weighted frame, stitching that matches one run even when a stand-in model corrupts window edges, the Ukrainian message, and an overlong file refused before decode.
  - `tests/studio_test.py`: a streamed upload arrives whole with no `.part` left, the size limit, and a body cut short.

Not covered: the Soniox lyric step on a long song, which was left out to avoid a paid transcription. It sends one MP3 of the vocal and polls for up to 15 minutes.

author: widgetii
body:
xm-uart was written by trial and error. This PR audits it with `uart-bridge` (#30) against the stock firmware of an **HI3516EV300_85H50AI** camera and its real lens board, fixes what was wrong, and writes up the measured protocol in [`xm-uart/PROTOCOL.md`](xm-uart/PROTOCOL.md), with the captures it rests on in `xm-uart/captures/`.

### How it was measured
- **Ground truth:** the stock firmware, driven through DVRIP `OPPTZControl` (python-dvr) while bridged. Every PTZ command's UART frame is in `captures/e1-stock.jsonl`.
- **What the board accepts:** the host acts as the camera and sends frame variants. The effect is read from the board's zoom reports, and from RTSP video (ffmpeg `blurdetect` for focus, `signalstats` for iris).
- **xm-uart itself:** built natively and run through the new `bridge --cam pty`, before and after the fixes.

### Board rules this established
- Only sync `C5` is accepted. The checksum, address and `5C` trailer are **not checked**, for zoom and focus alike.
- **The parser has no inter-byte timeout.** `A5`/`C5` starts an 8-byte frame, so a stray byte silently swallows the next command.
- Stock sends one frame per action, and checksum = sum % 256.
- Presets, queries, zoom speed, iris and pan/tilt bits have no effect on this board.
- Replies are `EF 01 type len payload`: zoom reports `"X1.4 "` about every 225 ms, then a blank report about 6.7 s later.

### xm-uart fixes
| was | now |
|---|---|
| checksum % 100 | % 256, as stock sends it |
| `h`/`l` sent right/left | left `04`, right `02`, as stock |
| `z`/`x` the opposite of stock's FocusNear/FocusFar | stock bits (physical direction unverified; see the spec) |
| compile-time `AUTO_FOCUS` sync `FF`/`C5` | fixed `C5` (the board ignores `FF`) |
| reply parser looked for `'X'` at byte 0 of each `read()`, so it never worked | `EF 01` framing across reads: `Zoom X1.4` |
| stop after `while(1)` was unreachable, and the terminal was never restored | `q`, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM/SIGHUP and stdin EOF all send stop and restore the terminal |
| unchecked `write()` | whole-frame `write_all()` |
| `init[]` (a stale `A5` frame) | removed |
| shared `main.o` across variants | per-variant compile, plus a `host` target |

d9cbf71 attributed "focus does nothing" on the 85H50AI to checksum validation. That does not reproduce on the same board. Every checksum value moves focus, tested with a stop-frame null control and in monotonic single-direction steps. Focus backlash after a direction reversal is a plausible cause of the original symptom.

### uart-bridge changes
- `bridge --cam pty` lets a tool under test play the camera.
- **Bug fixed:** camera bytes are now forwarded only from a frame boundary, and the frame in flight is finished on exit. Before this, every capture started mid-frame and passed a stray byte to the board.
- **Bug fixed:** the pty path is announced only once forwarding runs. Before, the tool's first write was discarded by the stale-input drain.
- The codec now matches the spec: % 256, iris bits, Pelco-D extended commands.
- `scripts/xm_uart_audit.py` (`stock`, `accept`, `tool`, `focus`, `restore`, `refocus`) reproduces the experiments and puts the lens back.

### Verification
- `uv run pytest`: 30 passed, locally and on the rig.
- xm-uart compiles warning-free with `-Wall -Wextra` plus the CI `-Werror=` set on gcc 16, `arm-linux-gnueabihf-gcc`, and the OpenIPC musl toolchain.
- On the rig, the fixed xm-uart's frames match the stock firmware byte for byte for zoom, focus and stop. The one exception is pan/tilt speed (`3F` at 100% vs stock `27` at Step 5), which the board ignores.
- SIGINT or `q` in the middle of a zoom sends stop at once (`e2-exit-paths.jsonl`).
- The rig was left as found: zoom X1.2, the camera OSD showing X1.2, and focus sharpness at least as good as the starting state.

author: jflavan
body:
Fixes #14

## Root cause
`finishRemoteMerge` called `syncMain` but ignored whether the sync actually brought the merge into local main. It then went on to `finishMerge`: status `merged`, the health check, and on the next tick the done-check against a stale main.

`syncMain` already rebases Loopstra's bookkeeping commits onto a diverged `origin/main`. It skips or fails in only a few cases:
- the main checkout has unsaved tracked changes. The reporter's later `--autostash` suggests this is what happened, and a `merge-approved` saved but not committed, which the README allows, has the same effect;
- the root is on another branch;
- the fetch fails;
- the rebase clashes outside `intent/`.

Separately, `gh pr merge --delete-branch` also deletes the local branch. That fails while the change's worktree has the branch checked out, so a merge that went through was reported as an error.

About point 4 of the issue: Loopstra only ever runs `git fetch --quiet <remote>`, which never writes into a checked-out branch. The "fetch updated the current branch head" warning comes from `git pull` noticing that HEAD moved during the pull. That fits Loopstra's sync rebasing root main at the same moment as the person's pull. This PR does not change that race (see Review notes).

## Fix
- **`finishRemoteMerge`** (`src/stages/merge.ts`):
  - First commits the change's own `intent/<slug>/` folder, when root is on main. The local merge path already does this, so a saved but uncommitted status no longer keeps the sync from running.
  - Then syncs.
  - Then records the merge only when local main contains the PR's merge commit (`gh pr view --json mergeCommit`), or, when gh names none, the branch's changes (the old check).
  - Otherwise it **waits** and retries each tick. It traces the wait once, and the `main_sync` signal already tells the owner why. It waits rather than blocks because the common causes (unsaved changes, GitHub unreachable) clear up by themselves.
- **`GitHub.merge`** no longer passes `--delete-branch`. After gh reports the PR merged, `mergeOnGitHub` deletes the remote branch itself (`git push <remote> --delete`, best effort), and cleanup deletes the local one as before.
- **`gh pr merge` exits 0 but the PR is not merged** (a merge queue): the step now waits and keeps the head branch. Deleting it would close the PR.
- **Docs:** README (GitHub section) and `docs/decisions.md` ("A merged pull request waits for main (#14)").

## Verification
- Reproduced first: 3 of the new integration tests fail against `main`'s `src/`.
- New tests in `tests/integration/remote.test.ts`:
  - "merged through gh while main here cannot be brought up to date: waits, and finishes once main has the merged commit". It also checks there is no `--delete-branch`, that the remote branch is deleted, and that the local branch is kept.
  - "a merge gh only queued waits with the branch kept, and is recorded once it merges"
  - "merged on GitHub, then main moved on in the same files: main has the merge commit, so the merge is recorded". Only the merge-commit check can pass this one.
  - "a person on the status line who saves merge-approved without committing it: merges and records it in one tick"
- `tests/unit/github.test.ts` now also reads `mergeCommit`.
- The fake gh reports `mergeCommit` and has a `LOOPSTRA_FAKE_GH_QUEUE` knob.
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.
- `bun run test`: 332 pass, 0 fail.

## Review notes
An independent reviewer went over the diff twice. The first pass found two real problems, both fixed in the second commit:
- A saved but uncommitted `merge-approved` would have made the step wait forever.
- The remote branch was deleted even when gh had only queued the merge.

The second pass was clean.

Worth a close look:
- **Other unsaved tracked edits in the main checkout** (another intent, or code) still make the sync skip, so the merged change waits until they are committed or undone. That is the existing sync rule (H1/H26), now visible here, and `main_sync` reports it.
- **A PR retargeted on GitHub to a base other than `main_branch`** would wait forever, since its merge commit never reaches main. Before, it was recorded as merged.
- **Merge queues are still not really supported.** While a PR sits in the queue, each tick runs `gh pr merge` again and traces a merge phase. If real gh exits non-zero for an already-queued PR, the step blocks.
- **If the PR lookup right after the merge fails,** the next tick records the merge through the "already merged" path, which does not delete the remote branch.
- **Not addressed:** Loopstra rebasing root main while a person runs `git pull` there (the warning in point 4).
- **Nits:**
  - The scheduler's log line for a waiting result still says "waiting for GitHub".
  - Cleanup still decides with `containsChanges`, so a branch changed on GitHub before a squash merge can stay behind locally. That predates this PR.

body:
Fixes from the end-to-end run of 3.13.0's runtime admin API against a live chain (the lifecycle script plus two independent Codex passes on the ThinkPad).

- A move off a shared dataset now rehomes the cursor name onto the remaining mount first, and a refused rename fails the move (#1549).
- The token is checked before the body is parsed: no token means 401, never 415/422.
- `/metrics` is served at the runtime root, including with nothing mounted.
- Route keys are per mount (#1565): default-tenant mounts serve by alias and every other tenant as `tenant/alias`, so a restart never moves a route.
- Names the runtime would refuse at boot are refused at the API with 400.
- A restart during a move resumes the move and never writes a staging mount to `mounts.toml`.
- Mount jobs are claimed atomically, so identical concurrent mounts all answer with one job, and that job ends `live`.
- A configured `default_tenant` spelled out (`acme/usdc`) is refused with 400 before a job starts.
- Mount records match by route key under the runtime's default tenant. This fixes two regressions of the per-mount keys above: default-tenant mounts on a configured tenant were not written to `mounts.toml`, and moving `usdc` rewrote `globex/usdc`'s record.
- A move whose incoming rename fails undoes the holder rename it made on a shared dataset (Jules's finding).
- `scripts/e2e-lifecycle.sh`: the 12-step lifecycle run used on the box.

author: evandempsey
body:
## Problem

The opt-in **QUICK TIP** discovery modal is meant to be a startup-only affordance, but it reappears after a thread reset: dismiss the tip at launch, run `/clear` (or `/reset`), and tip 1 shows again.

## Root cause

`_reset_current_thread` wipes the transcript (`self.conversation_entries = []`) and rebuilds a fresh startup entry. `_ensure_startup_entry` constructs that new entry with `startup_tip_shown=self._resuming_session and not self._discovery_tips_ready` — after launch `_discovery_tips_ready` is `True`, so the rebuilt entry is not marked as "tip shown", and the deferred `_maybe_show_discovery_tip` callback it schedules sees a fresh (empty-history) thread and pushes the tip. Thread reset is the only path that clears `conversation_entries`, so it is the only re-arm path; `/loop --fresh` shares it via `preserve_loop=True`.

## Change

Make the tip offer a **once-per-launch** event:

- Add a `_discovery_tip_consumed` latch on `KolegaCodeApp`, set when a tip is actually offered.
- In `_reset_current_thread`, set the latch before `_ensure_startup_entry(render=False)`, so the rebuilt startup entry and its deferred refresh callbacks are no-ops.
- The latch is checked in the *push* guard rather than an early return, so the existing "close an open tip when it becomes ineligible" branch (tips disabled / thread no longer fresh) still runs.

`startup_tip_shown` and the `_resuming_session` suppression are retained: they still dedupe within a startup entry and keep tips off resumed conversations. Enabling the setting while the initial startup thread is still fresh continues to show the tip once.

## Tests

- `tests/cli/test_discovery_tips.py`: the two tests that encoded the old re-show behavior now assert no tip after `_reset_current_thread()`.
- Added `test_clear_command_does_not_resurrect_dismissed_tip`, driving `/clear` through the composer after dismissing the startup tip and running a turn.
- `tests/cli/test_discovery_tips.py`: 40 passed.
- Related CLI/TUI suites (boot splash, startup card, recent sessions, sub-agent workflows, sidebar, loop/goal, persistence-history, terminal/logs): 241 passed.
- Full fast suite: 6357 passed, 5 skipped; the 7 failures are live-provider tests (`together`, `fireworks`) needing external credentials, unrelated to this change.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` / `pyright` clean on changed files; pre-commit hooks pass.

## Docs

`docs/src/content/docs/tui/interface.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` updated: the documented contract moves from "once per fresh thread … stays dismissed until the thread is reset" to "once per launch … clearing the thread does not bring them back".

author: yasserf
body:
Inside an addon, `getCredential('clockifyWebhookSecret')` came back `unknown`, so a webhook receive step couldn't read its signing secret off the wire without a cast. Three causes, all fixed here:

1. **Function types never saw the credentials.** `pikkuFunctionTypesSplit` reads the setup-only inspection, which doesn't visit `defineCredential`, so `credentials.definitions` was always empty there and every project (not just addons) got `type CredentialsMap = Record<string, unknown>`. `pikku all` now reruns the step after the post-scaffold state, when the credentials leaf exists and the cache holds the full inspection.
2. **`getCredential` / `getCredentials` were optional on `PikkuWire`**, though `runPikkuFunc` always sets them. They're now required; `PikkuRawWire` (what runners build) keeps them optional.
3. **Without a map, `getCredential<string>(name)` returned `unknown`.** `string` satisfies `K extends keyof Record<string, unknown> & string`, so the keyed overload swallowed it. With no map, only the generic signature is offered, with `NoInfer` so an untyped call still returns `unknown`.

Verified: core suite 2744 pass (only the API-report check needed regenerating, done); new type tests for required `getCredential` and `getCredential<string>`; the CLI change applied to 0.12.174's `all.workflow.js` makes clockify's function types import its `CredentialsMap`, and `getCredential('clockifyWebhookSecret')` types as `string`.

Unblocks pikkujs/addons#40 moving webhook secrets off `WebhookSigningSecret.fromCredential` singletons, which also bypassed `credentialOverrides`.

author: frenck
body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

## Description

<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

Four new actions for an entity's icon and aliases:

- **`homeassistant.set_entity_icon`** sets the icon of one or more entities, the same setting as in the entity's settings dialog. `null` takes it away, and the entity goes back to its integration's icon.
- **`homeassistant.add_alias_to_entity`**, **`remove_alias_from_entity`** and **`set_entity_aliases`**, the same trio Spook already has for areas and floors. Aliases are the names a voice assistant knows an entity by.

The one thing that makes entity aliases different from area aliases: they are an ordered list that can hold a marker for "the entity's own name", and every new entity starts with just that marker. That is how a voice assistant knows what to call an entity without any alias added. So:

- **add** appends at the end, in the order given, and does not add one the entity already has.
- **remove** only takes the aliases named. The marker is never one of them.
- **set** replaces the written aliases, and keeps the marker (up front, where the UI shows it) only if it was there.

Taking the entity's own name away is a different choice, which the UI already offers; these actions leave it as it was. Aliases are trimmed, and empty ones and repeats dropped, as core's own editor does.

All four are admin actions like the other registry actions, look up every entity before changing anything, and an entity without a unique ID gets its own explanation rather than "not found". Entity IDs are never touched.

## Motivation and Context

<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->

Asked for in discussions [#1112](https://github.com/frenck/spook/discussions/1112) (set an entity's icon, the sibling of `rename_entity`) and [#876](https://github.com/frenck/spook/discussions/876) (entity aliases, like the area and floor ones).

## How has this been tested?

<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, tests ran to see how -->
<!--- your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->

16 tests: setting and clearing an icon, a check against core that a new entity starts with its own name as its only alias, add, remove and set each pinned to the exact resulting list (marker included, in order), a bad entity late in a list changing nothing for all four, an entity without a unique ID explained, and a non-admin refused for all four. The actions were then broken nine different ways; two breaks passed at first. One was a test gap (repeats in the input to set), now closed. The other showed a guard in remove that could never matter, so it was taken out instead. Full test suite passes, ruff, pylint and prettier are clean.

## Screenshots (if appropriate):

<!-- A picture tell a thousand words -->

## Types of changes

<!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: -->

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Other

author: shadoukita
body:
## Why

Found during the pre-v0.1.0 security delta review (SHAA-715). The ZAP API scan in `dast.yml` authenticates with an administrator **API token**. The operations that refuse tokens answer 403 before reading the body (`backend/src/api/route.rs` session-only check), so ZAP's injection and SSRF payloads never reach their handlers. The job still passes, and the green result looks like coverage it doesn't have.

On `main` there are 26 such operations. 13 of them became session-only after the 2026-09-28 pentest baseline (`d864c61`):
- `POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/users…` and `PUT /admin/users/{id}/password`
- `POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/profiles…` and `POST /admin/profiles/{id}/clone`
- `POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/identity-providers…` and **`POST /admin/identity-providers/{id}/test`**, the only outbound-request endpoint and so the SSRF target
- **`POST /admin/config/import`**, the largest body parser

The other 13 were already session-only at the baseline: `/auth/me`, `/auth/password`, `/auth/mfa*`, `/admin/api-tokens*` and `DELETE /admin/users/{id}/mfa`. `pentest.spec.ts` covers all of them for authn, CSRF and authz, but no test sends them injection payloads.

## What

- `tools/dast/session-openapi.mjs` writes `openapi-session.json` with only the operations whose `security` has no `apiToken` alternative (25 today). It leaves out `POST /auth/logout`, which would end the scan's session. It fails if it finds none, so a change to the security schemes can't silently empty the scan.
- `tools/dast/session-openapi.test.mjs` (`node --test`, runs in the job before the scan) covers two things. A unit test checks the filtering rules: public, token and session operations, inherited top-level security, and path-level parameters. A test against `backend/openapi.json` pins that the identity-provider test, config import, user/profile writes, password and MFA routes are all included, and that no token-capable or session-ending operation is.
- `dast.yml` gets a second ZAP API scan with its own fresh session. `ZAP_AUTH_HEADER=Cookie` carries the session cookie, and a ZAP replacer rule adds `X-CSRF-Token` to every request. It is capped at 10 min.
- After the scan, `GET /auth/me` must still return 200 with that session. If it doesn't, the job fails, because a signed-out scan passes every rule. The verdict step now includes both new steps.
- `docs/security/pentest-v0.1.0.md` now describes the second scan.

No product code changes. CI-only, so there is no changelog fragment.

## Testing

- `node --test tools/dast/*.test.mjs`: 2/2 pass locally.
- `node tools/dast/session-openapi.mjs backend/openapi.json out.json` lists the 25 operations.
- The ZAP pass itself is verified by this PR's DAST run. Check the `session.md` step summary and the "The session scan kept its session" step.

﻿## Jira



- Issue: ENT-034 — Memory Governance Hub data model.

- Action-plan task/source: ENT-034 acceptance criteria; PR #78 review finding on head `925a417` for the agent/backend credential contract and plaintext lineage metadata.

- Corrected disposition: credential exchange, encrypted lineage, durable enrollment/revocation, and their integration tests are included. This branch is rebased onto `align/master` at `4bfe05592afdd13d71281c415c703db2165c83ce` (PR #77); the only rebase conflicts were resolved in the Terraform revision and backend dependency pins.



## Engineering rules and prerequisite



- T01 activation verifier: `.github/t01-activation.json`, PR #52 active; merged commit `1e40bdb5c8fd6b4e28c827035ab7d06645530ccb`; effective `2026-09-16T12:57:25Z`; live ruleset 21141288 active with zero bypass actors. Verified using `python scripts/repository_policy.py --verify-github` on 2026-09-30.

- [x] T01 is merged and effective before implementation.



## Scope



- [ ] Cross-owner approval is attached: current-head human owner and risk reviews remain pending; see Reviewer sign-off.

- [x] API/schema changes are documented in this PR and the lineage sample.

- [x] Tests cover the change; see Test evidence.

- Intended behavior: maintain a standalone tenant-owned governed-memory store, separate from sequential chat history, with authenticated owner, purpose, sensitivity, provenance, approval, retention, legal hold, export/deletion state, encryption, model-use policy, correction and supersession.

- Active path: after agent authentication, the agent signs a 30-second assertion over environment, agent tenant, and authenticated principal; the backend verifies signature/replay protection, resolves an administrator-enrolled mapping, and binds the mapped tenant/principal through a database security-definer function before retrieval. No caller bearer/API key is forwarded. `GovernedMemoryManager` scopes records by tenant, purpose, owner, approval, retention, deletion, supersession, and model-use policy. Agent retrieval remains opt-in (`GOVERNED_MEMORY_ENABLED=false` by default).

- The review findings warranted changes because an incomplete frozen route inventory hid new API boundaries, old PostgreSQL tests asserted a migration guard no longer reachable after migration 072, and dependency scans identified fixable high/critical advisories.

- [x] The work is one coherent ENT-034 change. The dependency baseline from merged PR #77 is retained; this PR keeps the tooling urllib3 lock consistent at 2.8.0.



## Customer impact



Tenants can persist reusable factual context with explicit governance controls. Sensitive content is encrypted, and model use remains disabled until an authorized approval enables it. The agent integration stays disabled by default; chat history behavior remains separate.



## Release notes



No customer-facing release note is proposed for this internal governance capability; publish release notes when the feature is enabled for customers.



## Schema and rolling-deployment compatibility



Migration 072 creates governed-memory principals and records with tenant-bound foreign keys and forced RLS; migration 073 adds the tenant-scoped agent-principal enrollment mapping and signed-exchange database binder. Neither migration backfills or reassigns chat rows. Apply `alembic upgrade head` before enabling agent retrieval, and keep `GOVERNED_MEMORY_ENABLED=false` until backend and agent are deployed together and the backend/agent-only `AUTHCLAW_AGENT_MEMORY_SECRET` is provisioned. Both migrations intentionally refuse downgrade; rollback binaries with the schema retained, disable the feature flag, and repair forward. No chat table contract changes.



## Existing-code reuse



Searched and reused `backend/app/core/auth.py` (tenant-scoped DB context and scope guards), `backend/app/core/crypto.py` (secret envelope encryption), existing Alembic/database grant patterns, and the existing agent gateway. `services/agent/memory.py` and `ChatSession` remain sequential chat history. A separate enrollment table, short-lived signed assertion, nonce replay guard, and database binder are necessary because agent and backend credentials are independently issued and cannot be forwarded or trusted across that boundary.



## New-line justification



A separate schema/API/service is required because chat transcripts have different semantics and retention from reusable, approval-controlled facts. Enrollment and revocation persist across fresh database sessions, and the test covers enrollment → retrieval → revocation → denied retrieval. The PR is rebased on master commit `4bfe055` (#77), which already contains the patched Next.js and runtime/test dependency baseline. GitHub reports 1,929 additions, 108 deletions, and 42 changed files in this PR diff. The repository calculator reports 1,824 positive non-prose lines across 42 changed files. The only dependency lock change unique to this diff aligns `requirements-tooling.txt` to urllib3 2.8.0.


- [x] AGENTS.md line budgets are respected by the repository Tokei gate.

- Semantic duplicates: N/A; no shared logic was merged or removed.



## Security and compliance



- [x] No secrets, personal data, tokens or keys were committed or logged.

- Trust boundaries: backend tenant/principal values come from authenticated server request state, never the request body; service API keys are limited to memory routes; shared/stage/CI/prod memory retrieval requires HTTPS. High/restricted records require encryption, and model-context queries exclude unapproved, expired, deleted, superseded, or disallowed records.

- [x] Audit/evidence behavior was considered: source lineage records source/creator/approval/correction; the sample reflects the stored shape.

- [x] Migration/rollback steps are documented above; downgrade is deliberately blocked to preserve data.

- Production-like fail-closed evidence: `GOVERNED_MEMORY_ENABLED` defaults false; missing authenticated identity/backend and insecure shared-environment transport reject retrieval; encryption key defaults are rejected in production-like settings. See `services/agent/smoke_tests/test_governed_memory_context.py` and `backend/tests/test_memory_governance.py`.



## Material line-growth exception



The repository per-file method reports 1,824 positive non-prose lines across 42 changed files (non-prose only; each file contributes `max(additions - deletions, 0)`, with prose exclusions from `scripts/repository_policy.py`). This exceeds the 100-line threshold because the separate model, migration, authorization service/API, agent integration, and cross-boundary security tests/evidence are required; reusing chat rows would violate the feature’s retention and governance contract. Generate the exact current-head review marker with `python scripts/repository_policy.py --pr-evidence 78` after the final body update and include it in each required component owner’s current-head approving review. No owner approval is claimed yet.


## Tenant isolation evidence



Tenant and memory-owner IDs are server-derived. Agent identity is matched by `(environment, agent_tenant_id, agent_principal_id)` to an existing backend principal through an admin-scoped enrollment endpoint; client request data cannot select the destination tenant or owner. Application reads filter by tenant and owner; PostgreSQL uses composite tenant foreign keys and forced RLS on governed-memory records, principals, and agent mappings. The security-definer binder rechecks active tenant/user state and establishes the RLS transaction context. Negative SQLite/HTTP tests reject forged/unmapped principals; `test_governed_memory_forced_rls_denies_cross_tenant_reads_and_writes` and `test_agent_memory_enrollment_is_rls_scoped_and_binds_only_mapped_identity` exercise tenant RLS and mapping enforcement in PostgreSQL CI. Export and deletion are represented as schema lifecycle states; this PR does not claim a user-facing export/del

author: ehsan-saradar
body:
Closes #5059

## Problem

The inpage `Ethereum` provider started with `chainId = '0x1'` and `networkVersion = '1'` and only changed `chainId` when an `evmChainChanged` event arrived from the background. It never asked the background for the real chain, so `provider.chainId` disagreed with `eth_chainId` when:
- the site had no session and the global `currentEVMChainId` was not Ethereum, or
- a new session was created directly on another EVM chain (the background events agent skips sessions that did not exist before).

`networkVersion` was never updated at all. dApps that read these synchronously assumed Ethereum.

## What changed

All in `clients/extension/src/inpage/providers/ethereum/index.ts`:
- **`setChainId`**: updates `chainId` and `networkVersion` together and emits `chainChanged` / `networkChanged` only when the value changes. The `evmChainChanged` listener now goes through it, so a background event that repeats the synced chain does not emit twice.
- **Sync on load**: the provider fetches the chain from the background once when created. The inpage script already calls the background on every page load (`getIsWalletPrioritized`, `hasChainInVault`), so this adds no new service-worker wake-up.
- **Sync after requests**: `eth_chainId` requests go through the same sync, so the response updates the provider and is returned to the caller. After `eth_requestAccounts`, `wallet_requestPermissions`, `wallet_switchEthereumChain` and `wallet_addEthereumChain`, the chain is fetched again before the request resolves. So `provider.chainId` is already correct right after `await`ing a switch, where before it was updated only when the background event arrived.
- **Stale responses**: a counter, captured before each background call, drops a response when a newer update (another sync, another `eth_chainId` request or a background event) came in first.
- **`request` is now an arrow field**: it uses `this`, and this keeps it working when called detached (`const { request } = provider`, `sendAsync`).

## Worth a reviewer's attention

- Sync failures are swallowed: a failed load-time sync keeps the previous value, and a failed post-request sync never fails the request that triggered it.
- Independent of #5058 (#5060). That PR fixes the background event for a session's first EVM chain; this one fixes the provider side. Either can merge first.

## Testing

- Six new unit tests in `ethereum-provider.test.ts`: sync on load (including `networkVersion`), `eth_chainId` update with a single emit, sync after connect, no duplicate emit when a background event repeats the synced chain, a stale load-time sync ignored after a newer event, and a stale `eth_chainId` response ignored after a newer event (from CodeRabbit's review). The first three fail on `main`, the last one fails on the first commit of this PR.
- `yarn check:all`: every step passes except `quality:audit`, which fails on existing `undici` and `brace-expansion` advisories. This PR changes no dependencies.
- Tested by hand on the extension, with the global EVM chain set to Polygon, on a never-connected `https` site:
  - After load: `provider.chainId` is `0x89` and `networkVersion` is `137`, matching `eth_chainId` (before: `0x1` / `1`).
  - After `eth_requestAccounts`: `provider.chainId` is `0x89`, with no redundant `chainChanged`.
  - `await` a switch to `0x1`, then read `provider.chainId`: one `chainChanged: 0x1` and the value is `0x1` right away.
  - Re-tested after the stale-response fix on another fresh site: connect, then switch to `0x89`: one `chainChanged: 0x89` and `provider.chainId` is `0x89` right away.

## Agent Metadata
- **Agent**: Claude Code
- **Issue**: #5059
- **Confidence**: high
- **Needs human review for**: none

body:
Unifies `reasoning_effort` behind a single `/effort` control and records the
architecture it created.

## What changed

- `/effort` becomes the one control for reasoning effort, replacing the
  per-tier `/low /mid /deep /max /ultra` writes. The old commands stay as
  aliases so existing scripts keep working.
- `MODELS[alias]["effort"]` is a per-rung map (`{rung: wire_value}`), not a
  flag, so a model that accepts `low/medium/high` but not `xhigh` simply
  lacks that key and the rung is never sent.
- `apply_effort` is the single write path. It also carries
  `preferred_worker` across, which fixes a pre-existing bug: every tier
  preset pinned the worker to `"auto"`, so an explicit `/worker <alias>`
  lock was silently undone while the worker menu — which reads the on-disk
  policy first — kept showing the old value.
- Split `core/commands/_effort_flow.py` and
  `core/commands/_model_picker.py` out of `provider.py` (a644e24).

## Why the AGENT.md merge needed care

This branch rewrote the Known Risks section into seven `### ` subsections
while #163 and #164 were both adding entries to the old flat list. Resolving
by taking either side wholesale would have dropped seven entries and left a
description of an already-fixed bug, so the merge keeps the new structure
and re-lands #164's four terminal entries and three testing-trap entries in
the new format.

Also corrected while merging: the Typed Island prose claimed the CI mypy
step "lists 44 paths" because it named `tests/test_e2e.py`. It does not — the
step passes 43 library modules and no `tests/` file. Verified against

author: mgth
body:
## Why

The Linux release zip is linked against the CI runner's Ubuntu 24.04 libraries (`libavcodec.so.60`, `libplacebo.so.338`, `liblua5.2.so.0`) and bundles none of them, so on any other distro mpv stops at `error while loading shared libraries`. Reported on Fedora 44 in mgth/Omniphony#605.

## What

- **`scripts/build-appimage.sh`**: packages the built `mpv` and the fallback `liborender.so.N` into an AppImage.
  - Bundled: the ffmpeg 6.1 / libplacebo / Lua 5.2 closure, plus `libfribidi` (on linuxdeploy's excludelist, but missing from a Plasma install without GTK apps).
  - Left to the host on purpose: libstdc++/libgcc_s (the host GPU driver is loaded into mpv), the Vulkan loader, libva (compile-time driver path and VA-API minor check), libpipewire (compile-time module path, daemon protocol), ALSA and Wayland.
  - `liborender` sits next to `mpv` in `usr/bin`, which the existing exe-dir candidate already covers. The Studio-deployed engine and `$ORENDER_LIBRARY` still take precedence.
  - linuxdeploy, appimagetool and the type2 runtime are pinned by sha256. The static runtime needs no libfuse2 on the host.
  - Floor: glibc 2.38 (Fedora 39+, Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 13, Arch). Size: about 91 MB.
- **`scripts/smoke-test-appimage.sh`**: runs the extracted image in a Fedora container that holds only desktop libraries. It checks that all libraries resolve, that the pipewire/pulse/alsa aos and gpu/gpu-next vos are built in, that the bundled ffmpeg can encode and decode E-AC-3, and that `ad_orender` loads the `liborender` shipped inside the image.
- **`release.yml`**: builds, smoke-tests and publishes `mpv-omniphony-<ver>-linux-x86_64.AppImage` alongside the zip. The release notes tell Linux users to take the AppImage and say the zip is for Ubuntu 24.04 only.
- **`integration-build.yml`**: same AppImage steps. This also fixes drift from `release.yml`: the Linux job did not install the X11 extras, Wayland or the audio dev packages, so meson silently dropped the windowed vo and every desktop ao (the #59 bug). It now installs the same set and forces those backends on.

## Tested locally

- Built in an `ubuntu:24.04` container with the same packages and meson options as CI.
- `smoke-test-appimage.sh` passes on `fedora:44`. Log line: `orender: loaded liborender ABI 0.8 0.6.0 v0.6.0 … from /app/usr/bin/liborender.so.0 (next to mpv)`.
- On an Arch desktop, the FUSE-mounted AppImage played a DD+JOC 7.1.4 clip through the bundled engine and harletty-bridge. The engine was ready in 0.13 s, output was 12 channels, and mpv exited at end of file. Audio went to `--ao=null` and no video window was opened, so nothing was checked by ear or by eye.

Not yet exercised: these workflows on GitHub Actions (a `workflow_dispatch` of `release.yml` on this branch builds everything without publishing).

author: dipeshbabu
body:
## Summary

Historical pass rates and shadow proposals cannot safely authorize optimization. Add an offline review and bounded canary lifecycle for built-in Python budget policies against a reviewed tracing-only baseline.

Proposals bind native ablation observations/decisions, calibration cohorts, capability evidence, exact versions, thresholds and rollout limits. Missing, synthetic, stale, mismatched or undersized evidence remains ineligible. Explicit operator approval and scope opt-in are required before canary admission; changed workloads/versions, unknown measurements, regressions, expiry and kill switches restore the reviewed baseline. Passing a canary never silently expands rollout. Native decision exports retain approvals, rejections, outcomes and rollback without activating any existing study candidate.

## Related issue

Closes #195.

## Validation

- 41 new promotion regression tests; 238 affected tests passed on Python 3.10 and 3.13.
- Full isolated Windows suite at the initial implementation head: 1,842 passed, 82 skipped in 163.92 seconds. Optional integration/database coverage runs in its configured CI jobs.
- `uv run --frozen pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: all checks passed.
- `python -m examples.policy_promotion`: synthetic fixture retained as ineligible; no enforcement authorized.
- Before PR creation: branch CI (all nine jobs), CodeQL, dependency review and replay self-test passed at 173addca5f075c47624245ce469c22688e064f55.
- PR CI exposed an existing routing fixture that invented 1 ms of provider work while a fast host could finish in less than 1 ms. The final test-only fix declares the fake instantaneous and deterministically checks zero/sub-millisecond host durations; 49 routing/promotion tests and all pre-commit checks passed. Final head: e9a06bf612a56e4e176266e1c08126d1486a94cc. The production runner, exporter and archived study evidence are unchanged.

## Compatibility and risk

Opt-in Unreleased APIs only, with no dependency, version or database change. Initial scope is static built-in budget caps against the exact reviewed tracing-only baseline; active-budget baselines and absolute process-clock deadlines are rejected. The host authenticates operator attestations, verifies source evidence, applies returned configurations and reports independent outcomes. Checksums are not proof of evidence authenticity. Canary limits are cooperative and affect future admission, not already-running work. No online learning, production activation, paid provider calls or empirical improvement claims are introduced.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused change without unrelated formatting, generated files or dependency upgrades.
- [x] Relevant tests and local checks pass; skipped validation is stated above.
- [x] Regression tests cover failed/missing quality and cost, shifted workloads/models, insufficient tasks, expired/mismatched approvals, native decision coverage, concurrent admission, cancellation outcomes, kill switches and rollback.
- [x] Behavior, supported scope and limitations documented; changelog updated.
- [x] Examples and unit data are explicitly synthetic/simulated and contain no private data.
- [x] No new dependency or third-party licensing obligations.
- [x] Substantial AI assistance: implemented with Codex, reviewed against the native ablation/calibration/harness contracts, and validated with the checks above.
- [ ] All required PR checks pass before merge.

- Cookie de session sans `maxAge` (+ `SameSite=Lax`) : effacé à la fermeture du navigateur (auparavant valable 7 jours).
- Déconnexion après **30 min d'inactivité** : `requireAuth` vérifie `req.session.lastSeen` à chaque requête et détruit la session au-delà du délai (API → 401 `{expired:true}`, pages → redirection `/login.html?expired=1`).

- Photo fournie (`public/assets/login-bg.jpg`, 350 Ko) à gauche, en transparence sous un voile aux couleurs du logiciel, léger zoom animé ; formulaire à droite. Sur mobile, la photo passe en fond plein écran.

body:
## Quoi

- **Workflow `Publication`** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`), déclenché par une étiquette `v1.2.3` (ou à la main avec une version, sans Release) :
  - version `1.2.3` + numéro de build croissant `10203` (Play et App Store l'exigent) ; versions à zéros initiaux refusées ;
  - **Android** : APK + AAB signés (clé en base64 dans les secrets, Gradle lit clé et version dans l'environnement) ;
  - **Windows** : NSIS, version passée par `--config`, signé si un `.pfx` est fourni (empreinte → `certificateThumbprint`) ;
  - **iOS** : archive par signature automatique d'Xcode (clé d'API App Store Connect, rôle Admin), export `app-store-connect` / `upload` vers TestFlight ;
  - chaque plateforme sans secrets est **sautée avec un avis** ;
  - Release GitHub avec l'APK et l'installateur Windows.
- **`android.yml`** (chaque PR) : construit aussi la version release signée avec une **clé jetable** et la vérifie par `apksigner`, donc le chemin de signature est éprouvé en continu.
- **Icône iOS 1024 aplatie** (RGB, sans alpha : l'App Store refuse la transparence).
- **Politique de confidentialité corrigée** : le lieu du ciel (arrondi à ~10 km) est gardé dans les réglages, donc synchronisé.
- `docs/publication.md` (comptes, clés, secrets, formulaires Play et App Store), ADR 21.

## Limites
Le chemin iOS n'est éprouvable qu'avec un compte Apple ; Windows et Android le seront dès la première étiquette (ou un lancement manuel).

author: jordanthejet
body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds a transport conformance harness for the daemon's RPC endpoint. One scenario list runs against the real `run_local_listener`, once per transport leg. Today there is one leg, the local endpoint: a Unix domain socket on Unix and a named pipe on Windows. Each scenario speaks NDJSON JSON-RPC the way an external client does. Only opening a leg's stream is platform-specific, so every scenario compiles on every target. The in-process leg can later be added as a second `Leg` variant beside the local one.
  - A separate gateway process will reach the core over this endpoint, and #11001 asks for evidence that the transports behave the same for initialization, identity, denial, version compatibility, endpoint discovery and streaming. Before this, most of that was tested only at the dispatcher level, and nothing tested a protocol-version refusal.
  - 19 scenarios: 17 run on every leg, 2 are Unix-only. The coverage table below maps each #11001 row to its scenario.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Test-only. No product code changes, and no refactor of the listener or dispatcher tests. The harness is one new test module; it reuses the existing test-only context constructors and the connection prompt fixture as they are.
  - Not in this PR:
    - the in-process duplex leg and the three-way endpoint-resolution check against the RPC client and zerocode (both need #11186's client)
    - the session-owned turn lifetime and attach/replay rows (#11185)
    - any change to version negotiation
- **Blast radius:** The runtime crate's unit-test binary gains 19 tests, under a second in total locally. The scoped-identity scenario starts a mock identity provider on loopback. Nothing outside tests is compiled differently.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11001. Related #11000.
- **Coordination:** `a_camel_case_protocol_version_is_ignored_and_read_as_version_one` pins master's behaviour. #11275 makes that spelling checked instead, so the assertion flips when #11275 merges; whichever of the two PRs lands second updates it.
- **Labels:** `release:v0.9.0`, `ci:windows` (the second requests the advisory Windows run that exercises the named-pipe leg).

### Coverage

| #11001 row | Scenario | Unix socket | Named pipe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initialize and the advertised method table | `initialize_binds_the_connection_and_advertises_every_method` | yes | yes |
| Refusal before initialize | `a_request_before_initialize_is_refused_and_initialize_still_succeeds` | yes | yes |
| Compatible version, omitted version | `an_omitted_protocol_version_is_read_as_version_one` | yes | yes |
| Incompatible version (`-32011`, nothing bound) | `an_unsupported_protocol_version_is_refused_and_binds_nothing` | yes | yes |
| Documented `protocolVersion` spelling (today: read as 1) | `a_camel_case_protocol_version_is_ignored_and_read_as_version_one` | yes | yes |
| Identity: paired token | `a_paired_token_binds_its_principal` | yes | yes |
| Identity: scoped principal from an explicit bearer | `a_scoped_principal_is_held_to_its_grants` (OIDC introspection) | yes | yes |
| Identity: kernel peer uid | `the_peer_uid_binds_its_roster_principal_and_its_grants_gate_each_call`, `the_daemons_own_uid_keeps_the_operator_path_when_trusted` | yes | n/a: a pipe carries no peer uid |
| Denial at the handshake (`-32010`) | `an_unpaired_token_is_refused_without_falling_back_to_the_endpoint`, `with_a_roster_a_local_caller_it_does_not_name_is_refused` | yes | yes |
| Denial of a method outside the grants (`-32012`) | `a_scoped_principal_is_held_to_its_grants` (both legs); the peer-uid scenario (Unix) | yes | yes |
| Endpoint discovery per data directory | `each_data_dir_gets_its_own_endpoint_and_the_daemon_reports_it` | yes | yes |
| Updates delivered while the turn runs | `a_turn_streams_its_updates_before_it_completes` | yes | yes |
| Terminal outcomes, exactly one each | the streaming, `a_provider_failure_mid_turn_ends_it_as_failed_once`, `a_prompt_on_an_unknown_session_ends_in_a_failed_turn_once` and `cancelling_a_running_turn_ends_it_as_cancelled` scenarios | yes | yes |
| Disconnect ends a protocol 1 turn; the session survives | `closing_the_prompting_connection_ends_its_turn_but_not_its_session` | yes | yes |
| Bounded buffering: an expired replay cursor | `an_expired_replay_cursor_is_told_where_to_resume_then_streams_live` | yes | yes |
| Bounded buffering: a live subscriber that stops reading | `a_live_subscriber_that_stops_reading_is_told_what_it_lost` | yes | yes |
| Viewer and agent lifetimes (session-owned turns) | with #11185 | — | — |

The roster refusal is one scenario with two mechanisms. On a Unix socket the peer uid is a credential the roster does not name. On a pipe the caller presents no credential, and with a roster configured there is no compatibility path to take.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's daemon listens on a local socket (Linux and macOS) or a named pipe (Windows) for clients such as zerocode, and later a separate gateway process. This PR adds tests that talk to that real endpoint the way a client does. They check that it:
- lets the right callers in, turns the wrong ones away, and holds a limited user to what that user may do
- refuses a client speaking an unsupported protocol version
- can be found from the data directory alone
- streams a turn's progress while it runs and ends it clearly, whether the turn completes, fails, is cancelled, or loses its connection
- tells a subscriber that falls behind exactly what it missed, without holding up anyone else

The same tests run on every platform, so a behaviour difference between the socket and the pipe shows up as a failing test instead of a surprise later. The tests record today's behaviour, including two things to be aware of:
- the `protocolVersion` spelling shown in the protocol docs is not the field the daemon reads
- closing a connection ends the turn it started

body:
## What
Two changes:

1. **One screen per section.** The home page is now a run of full screens. Every chapter part is a panel exactly one viewport tall, and scrolling pages from screen to screen like slides.
2. **Phone light-mode hero** (follow-up to #48, which merged before this was pushed): phones get a native portrait frame of the golden-hour scene.

## How: full-screen panels
- **Panels:** About, the "Selected systems." title card, Aperture's intro, each project (Benchmark, Fraud Detection, Ridgepoint), Engineering in public (profile and calendar, then repositories), the Credentials title, Philosophy, Beyond, Education, Technology, Writing and Contact.
- **Fitting** (`src/fullscreen.js`):
  - short content is centred under the navbar;
  - long content is scaled down with CSS `zoom` (so layout really is one screen), never below 0.8, or 0.72 on short laptop screens, with content pinned to its own width so canvases and aspect-ratio boxes scale with it.
  - Phones don't zoom: panels centre when short and grow when long.
- **Pager** (instead of CSS scroll-snap, which snaps to the *nearest* stop and sprang small wheel scrolls back):
  - when a wheel, trackpad or keyboard scroll settles, the page glides to the next stop in the direction of travel;
  - nudges settle back;
  - link and hash jumps settle on the nearest stop;
  - panels taller than a screen scroll freely.
  - Touch keeps native scrolling.
- **Pinned stages:** Aperture pipeline, credential wheel and Direction get a stop per screen and still advance step by step.
- **Stops are page-level markers,** because Chrome misplaces the snap position of zoomed elements.
- **Dense chapters:** repositories in two columns, the Philosophy diagram and Education map capped by screen height, and tighter Contact spacing (`src/fullscreen.css`).
- **Fixes along the way:**
  - panels keep their reveal but drop its clip-path, because IntersectionObserver honours a target's own clip, so a clipped-shut panel never revealed;
  - jump links land exactly on panel tops.

## How: phone portrait hero
- **Image:** `hero-day-portrait-1080.webp` (from a 940×1672 source) replaces the crop of the landscape shot.

- **Paging:** PageDown and 3-notch wheel scrolls land on a stop every time (14/14 each). Wheel-up, a 15px nudge that settles back, and a long flick all behave. The three pinned stages advance through every step.
- **Nav links:** About, Work and Contact land exactly on their panels.
- **Visual tours:** desktop and phone, no clipped content. Philosophy, Education and Contact render complete.

author: a1flecke
body:
Closes #1008

Refactor only — no gameplay, balance, cost, catalog, data or save change.

## Base

`origin/main` at `d10f35b8f` (`feat(logistics): Open Borders is passage, not supply ... (#870)`).

The branch was first authored on `c8cf1909844cfbb94f0dc7fbfd368a34034ab920` (the assigned snapshot) and rebased onto `d10f35b8f` after **#871/#870 (territorial access) merged mid-flight**. That PR touched three files this one also touches — `.claude/rules/game-balance.md`, `tests/app/architecture-boundaries.test.ts`, and `src/ui/notification-routing.ts` — and the rebase auto-merged cleanly. Both PRs' architecture blocks (#1008 at the top, #871/#870 below) coexist in `architecture-boundaries.test.ts`, and the `city-*` modules were untouched by #871.

## Stale issue reconciliation

#1008 was written at `9e3db8f6` (2354 lines / 35 exports / 37 importers). Current main had drifted:

- `city-system.ts` was **2532 lines / 39 exported symbols / ~42 `src/` importers** (+ ~60 test files).
- #984 **landed**: `production-cost-context.ts` is already the canonical `GameState` → cost-context adapter, and `ProductionCostContext` has all-required fields with a `CivilizationEra`-branded `era` (#1016/#1017). The issue's "coordinate with the World Age bug" note is moot.
- #1113 (chain-aware `isUnitObsolete`), #1107 (`civHasCoastalCity`), #1080 (uniquePerEmpire dequeue) had landed.
- #1019 canonical owned-city queries and #1011 decomposed diplomacy are the current architecture; neither is re-implemented here.

So the remaining genuine gap was purely structural: one module still owned definitions + pricing + availability + presentation + lifecycle + turn, and `production-cost-context.ts` had to import the pricing core *from* that kitchen sink.

## Before / after

Before: `city-system.ts` 2532 lines, owning all six responsibilities.

After:

| Module | Lines | Responsibility |
|---|---:|---|
| `city-building-catalog.ts` | 1177 | static `BUILDINGS` data (pure leaf) |
| `city-unit-catalog.ts` | 144 | `TRAINABLE_UNITS` + meta-lists |
| `city-local-infrastructure.ts` | 33 | local-infra families + healing query |
| `city-lifecycle.ts` | 104 | `foundCity`, coastal geography, razing |
| `city-availability.ts` | 171 | availability / obsolescence / trainability |
| `city-production-cost.ts` | 287 | cost types + pure pricing rules |
| `city-production-presentation.ts` | 343 | icons / display names / queue copy (UI-facing) |
| `city-turn.ts` | 347 | completion + per-turn `processCity` |
| `city-system.ts` | 83 | thin compatibility barrel |

The only module still large is the catalog, and it is one cohesive responsibility (definition data). No file was split to hit a line count.

## Dependency diagram

```
catalogs / definitions            city-building-catalog
                                  city-unit-catalog        (+ combat-role-definitions)
        ↓                         city-local-infrastructure (+ combat-role-definitions)
queries / availability            city-availability  ──► city-lifecycle
        ↓
cost / validation                 city-production-cost  ◄── production-cost-context.ts
        ↓
commands / turn orchestration     city-turn
presentation adapters             city-production-presentation (leaf-ward of all of the above)
```

Forbidden and now asserted: catalog→turn, cost→availability/turn/presentation, availability→cost/turn/presentation, presentation→turn/cost/availability, lifecycle→cost/availability/turn.

## Public API before / after

Unchanged. All 39 pre-split exports are still importable from `@/systems/city-system`, which is now an 83-line barrel re-exporting only that public surface. Internal helpers that were private before (`requiresResource`, `getBuildingDiscountMultiplier`, `getTechCostDiscountMultiplier`, `getNationalProjectDiscountMultiplier`, `normalizeProductionEra`, `NP_PRODUCTION_DISCOUNTS`) stay private — a regression test proves the barrel does not leak them.

## How `production-cost-context.ts` was incorporated

It is **not** duplicated. It now imports `createProductionCostContext` / `getProductionCostForItem` / `ProductionCostContext` from `city-production-cost.ts` instead of the barrel, so the state-derived context adapter consumes the pricing core directly. `getProductionCostForItem` still has exactly one implementation (`city-production-cost.ts`), enforced by test.

## Why cost behaviour is unchanged

Every extracted block is byte-identical to the original (moved with `sed`); only import headers and blank lines were added. `processCity` ordering — growth → tech/resource queue filter → NP build-window dequeue → uniquePerEmpire dequeue → coastal/training-building/unit-blocker guard → production accrual → completion → idle production — is preserved exactly. `buildProductionCostContext` still derives civ era, bonus, techs, NPs, resources, substitution and reward charges in one place (#984).

## Architecture tests

`tests/app/architecture-boundaries.test.ts` gains a `#1008` block asserting: catalogs are leaves; presentation imports no simulation module; cost/availability/lifecycle import directions; `city-turn` may consume transitions but not presentation; the city-* graph is acyclic; the barrel re-exports the full pre-split value surface and leaks no internals; one pricing implementation; presentation consumers import `city-production-presentation`. The `#984` "canonical path stays canonical" allowlist was updated to the moved files (invariant preserved, not relaxed). The #985 catalog→espionage source rule (both the hook and `scripts/check-src-rule-violations.sh`) now covers the whole `city-*.ts` family instead of one file, with new fixtures.

## Save decision

No change. State shapes live in `core/types`; the modules only read/return plain `City` objects. No serialization or migration was touched.

## Verification

- `scripts/check-src-rule-violations.sh` over all changed/new `src/` files — clean
- `yarn build` — pass
- Focused suites: architecture-boundaries, city-system, production-cost(s/parity/context), catalog-id-integrity, city-founding, city-territory, planning-system, espionage-buildings, strategic-launch, city-panel, city-grid, city-map-presentation, panel-actions-controller, notification-routing, city-panel-building-icon — all pass
- `tests/scripts/check-src-rule-violations.test.ts` + hook smoke tests — pass
- `yarn verify:pr` (build + durable full suite) — recorded below

## Adversarial findings

- No conditional, ordering, default, iteration-order or RNG-relative change; pure code movement.
- No cycle introduced: no city-* module imports the barrel; `city-system` imports the leaves only.
- The barrel is a compatibility facade, not a licence to reach internals — only the pre-split public surface is re-exported and a test guards it.
- Collision-sensitive work (#871/#870 movement/borders, #1192 shared-host tooling, #1125) was not touched.

author: prabhjotsodhi
body:
Hints always listed keyboard keys and pad buttons together, so a player had to guess which one applied to them.

The game now remembers which device sent input last (pad, keyboard or touch). This is tracked in the frame loop in `main.js`, outside scene `update()`, and only the UI reads it, so game state stays deterministic. `drawKeyHints` shows keyboard keys, generic pixel art pad glyphs, or a tap icon for touch. Pad glyphs show a face button by its position (the pressed spot is highlighted), plus a stick and a start pill. The title and player select panels show only the rows that fit the device. Every screen that draws hints uses the new hint format. The device switches on the next frame after input from a different device.

Tests cover the last-device pick, hint items per device and row filtering.

Closes #197

`MDAdd` only lowercased the key, so a key like "bad key" or a value with a newline went out as an invalid HTTP/2 header and the server reset the stream. Allow existing Bukkit/Paper plugins to transfer players and query player/server information through the standard BungeeCord plugin channel. Enable it with `rift.config.network = { bungeecord = true }`, or add the flag to an existing network table.

- Keep compatibility opt-in, reject ambiguous server names, document the supported subset, and add independent socket acceptance tests to CI. Forward, Message, and Kick subchannels remain unsupported.

- Formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, and all-target Rust tests in debug and release.
- 50 Python harness tests and 15 frontend tests using the V8 runner.
