body:
## Hotfix 0.7.1: Windows rule paths and start commands

Supersedes #16: that PR was closed when its base branch `add-orchestrator-verify` was deleted after the merge of #15. Same branch and commit `8b2951e`, code unchanged; this PR targets `main`.

**Field defect (Windows 11, Python 3.13).** `orch.py init` and `orch.py settings all` stopped at settings generation: `settings admin: allow: Read(/C:\<path>/**): an absolute path needs a double slash (//path)`. The generator prefixed a single `/` to a Windows path with backslashes, and the plugin's own validator refused the result. No settings file was written, so `dispatch` refused without `--no-settings`.

| # | Item | Done |
|---|------|------|
| 1 | One function for the absolute path of a rule | `session_settings.abs_rule_path`: `//<path>` on macOS and Linux; on Windows the documented POSIX form `//<drive letter, lower case>/<path with forward slashes>` (`C:\a\b` → `//c/a/b`, `D:/x` → `//d/x`); network (UNC) and relative paths are refused with a clear error, reported by `settings`/`init` as an orch error. It is used for the repository, the module paths, the workspace and both templates (the placeholders get the finished form). The validator still accepts only `//…`. |
| 2 | Bash rules with paths | The script paths use forward slashes (`python3 C:/…/scripts/orch.py *`). On Windows the orchestrator's settings also allow `python …` and `py -3 …` for `orch.py` and `safe_edit.py`. The `--settings` path in start commands uses forward slashes on Windows. The documentation says the rules match the command text, so commands must be written with forward slashes. |
| 3 | PowerShell start commands | `shell: bash\|powershell` in `orch.yaml`, default bash. `init --shell` is asked explicitly on Windows: `init` refuses there without it. With PowerShell, `init` and `dispatch` print `cd "<dir with forward slashes>"; claude …`. `lint` checks the value. Done within the hour; no deviation. |
| 4 | Tests without a Windows runner | `test_windows_paths` swaps `session_settings.is_windows` and uses Windows path strings: `C:\a\b`, `D:/x`, UNC and relative paths refused; valid `Read(//c/…/**)` and `Edit(//c/…/**)` with no backslash in any rule; the `python`/`py -3` forms; a UNC workspace refused; `init` on Windows without `--shell` refused. PowerShell commands are tested end to end. **On POSIX the output is byte-identical to 0.7.0:** the fixture `fixtures/settings-0.7.0/{module,orchestrator}.json` was generated with the unchanged 0.7.0 code and is compared byte for byte. |
| 5 | Documentation | README (EN/RU): a "Windows" section. The 3a statement about `.claude/settings.local.json` is corrected in `init.md`, the concept (EN/RU), the `orch.yaml` template, the READMEs and the `.worktreeinclude` hint: it holds on macOS and Linux only, and the plugin always passes the rules with `--settings`. Plugin and root CHANGELOG with backlog (a Windows runner in CI, PowerShell forms of Bash rules). Version 0.7.1 everywhere. |

`check.sh` passes, including `check-private-traces.py`. That guard caught a user-directory path in the new test fixtures; they now use neutral paths.

## Deviations

1. **Branch point.** The branch starts at the accepted 0.7.0 head (the head of #15) instead of `main` after the merge. #15 is now merged, the merge into `main` is clean, and this PR's diff against `main` is the hotfix only. #16 was stacked on #15 and closed when its base was deleted; no more stacked PRs from here on.
2. **The Windows host is simulated in tests** (`is_windows` replaced, Windows path strings), as the package allows: there is no Windows runner.

author: agentydragon
body:
## Summary

Two fixes to the session watch, both found by reading the real API's frames with the account owner's access token (read-only requests).

**1. A stale resume token opens a dead watch.** Watches opened with tokens of increasing age (each token taken from the list route, then used N seconds later):

| Token age | Frames received |
| --- | --- |
| 20, 45, 90, 150, 165, 180, 195, 210, 225 s | `added`, `sync`, then `changed` |
| 240 s, 400 s, and one of about five minutes held for 75 s | one keepalive, then nothing: no `sync`, no `changed` |

The server answers the old token with a `200` and an open stream, not a 410, so nothing tells the client the watch is dead. The follower reused the id of the last `sync` frame across reconnects. `sync` recurs every 100-120 s on a live connection, so that id is at most about two minutes old while connected; but after any reconnect (the retry backoff alone reaches five minutes), an id older than about four minutes would have opened a watch that stays "connected" on the page and delivers nothing. Page size does not matter, and neither does an `Accept: text/event-stream` header.

Every connection now takes a fresh token from the list route (one request). `WatchCursor` is gone and `watch_sessions` takes the token. Changes in the gap reach the store through discovery, as before. A watch held open for seven minutes kept delivering `changed` frames throughout, so a connected watch does not lapse.

**2. The watch's keepalive was logged as an unknown frame.** The deployed sync logged `ignoring server-sent frame of an unknown kind: message, 0 bytes of data` seconds after connecting: the watch sends a frame with no `event:` name and no data. An unnamed frame without data is now ignored; one that carries data is still reported by its shape.

## Tests

- `test_each_watch_connection_takes_a_fresh_resume_token` (`test_live.py`): the server ends the first watch after a `sync` frame; the follower reconnects and has taken two tokens. The reused cursor would have taken one.
- `test_watch_yields_session_changes` (`test_api.py`) sends a keepalive frame first and asserts nothing is logged.

## Deliberately left out

- No idle detector for a watch that is open but silent: a quiet account legitimately has no `changed` frames, and the keepalive arrives every 12-15 s either way.
- The `delivery_update` handling for client-event stamps (see the follow-up PR on the TODO for it).

author: glslang
body:
Steps 1 and 2 of item 103 step 9, following [#425](https://github.com/glslang/windbg-mcp/pull/425)'s feasibility gate. **The read is built and the walk holds at run time.** Nothing was raised, no intercept was installed and nothing was written anywhere, so this is the confirmation that gate could not give — not the arm.

## The instrument

`h3probe.sys` gains `IOCTL_H3_VIDVP` (`0x80A`), returning the per-VP markers and `[P+0xB68][0..7]` together. Three guards keep it from being an arbitrary root kernel read:

1. **It takes a partition id, never a pointer.** The context is resolved through `H3ReadPair`, under the same `WinHvpPartitionArrayLock` and behind the same `winhvr.sys` build check S5q step 2 established.
2. **The registered routine must land inside the loaded `Vid.sys`**, or the context is not a VID partition object and the offsets mean nothing — `STATUS_OBJECT_TYPE_MISMATCH` rather than a plausible answer.
3. **Every dereference goes through one helper** — kernel-canonical address, `MmIsAddressValid` per page, `__try`/`__except`, `APC_LEVEL` or below. That does not make the read *safe*; it turns the likely failures into a reported status instead of a bug check.

Plus a `Vid.sys` build check of the **loaded** image (`TimeDateStamp` `0xE1E29EBE`, `SizeOfImage` `0xDC000`), reported either way, and a self-validating walk: `[V+0x00]` is the back-pointer `VidHandleExceptionIntercept` loads on its own first instruction.

## What it read

| | partition `0x2` | partition `0x3` |
|---|---|---|
| routine Hyper-V holds | `Vid+0x4170` (`VidInterceptIsrCallback`) | the same |
| `[P+0xAA8]` VP count | **2** | **2** |
| VP 1 at array + `0x980` | yes | yes |
| `[V+0x00]` back-pointer | equals `P` on both VPs | equals `P` on both VPs |
| `[P+0xB68]` vectors 0–7 | `FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF` | `FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF` |

**`[P+0xB68][3]` is `0xFF` — unclaimed.** That is the byte S5k named and the "was the slot claimed?" section has been asking for since; this is the first time it has been read at all. With no intercept installed, so it says the table reads and looks like a table, and nothing yet about an arm.

## The reading worth more than the back-pointer check

**The markers reproduce the type switch, live, on two message types and two partitions.** The feasibility gate read the jump table at `Vid+0x3D137` and the `lea`/`mov esi` pairs it dispatches to. The live markers agree without being told:

| `[V+0x30]` type | `[V+0x158]` handler | `[V+0x200]` reason | predicted statically? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x80000000` `UnmappedGpa` | `Vid+0x26040` `VsmmHandleMemoryIntercept` | `7` | yes |
| `0x80010000` `X64IoPortIntercept` | `Vid+0x3460` `VidHandleIoPortIntercept` | `5` | yes |

The back-pointer says *we are walking the right object*; this says *the object holds what `VidInterceptPreprocess` was read to put there*.

**Two corroborations from outside the instrument.** `[P+0xAA8]` read `2` per partition and Hyper-V's own management view reports **2 vCPUs** per guest — an oracle with nothing to do with these offsets. And the copied message's sender field carries the partition id (`02` on `0x2`, `03` on `0x3`).

**One caveat the output made plain**: `[V+0x68]` is the exception vector **only** for type `0x80010003`. On the IO-port message it read `0x71`, which is payload. Read the type first.

## Bench state

Driver started, four VPs read across two partitions, driver stopped. Host uptime continuous at 2h31m, **no bug check since boot**, both guests running with unbroken uptime. Nothing written, no intercept installed, no chain slot touched.

## What this does not do

Nothing was raised, so no exception intercept has been observed and the delivery question is exactly where the feasibility gate left it — including that a raw-arm negative would mean *no arrival observed at the convergence point*, not *not delivered*. What this retires is the **risk** in the arm rather than the arm: the walk is confirmed, the guards are exercised, and the markers are known to carry live state rather than zeros, which is what would have made a first arm's reading uninterpretable.

The driver and its client are bench work this repo does not ship; what is recorded here is the result and the design.

author: celino
body:
`BaseMoonScan`, `BaseMinmusScan` and `BaseDunaScan` never load when SCANsat is installed. Their `HiResScannerUnlocked` requirement uses `type = OR`, which isn't a Contract Configurator requirement type (the "one of these" type is `Any`), so CC rejects the whole contract:

```
CONTRACT_TYPE 'BaseMoonScan', REQUIREMENT 'HiResScannerUnlocked' of type 'OR': Unknown requirement 'OR'.
Errors encountered while trying to load CONTRACT_TYPE 'BaseMoonScan'
```

This changes `OR` to `Any` in `13-SurfaceBases.cfg`: 3 places in the stock contracts and 12 in the GPP version.

Tested in KSP 1.12.5 with CC 2.13.4.0 and SCANsat: the three contracts now load without errors.

author: danielch26
body:
Refs #51

## Resumen

Cierra los 8 fallos de contraste que quedaron de #64. Seis líneas, tres archivos.

## El problema

`--score-low/mid/high` se diseñaron como **relleno de fondo** (profundos en ambos modos, con `#fff` encima). Varios componentes también los usaban como **color de texto**, lo que en modo oscuro cae entre 1.54:1 y 3.26:1 — por debajo del 4.5:1 que WCAG exige para texto normal.

Los tokens pareados `-ink` ya existían y estaban medidos. **Los componentes simplemente no los usaban.**

## Cambios

| Archivo:línea | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| `EnergyBadge.svelte:36` | `color: var(--score-low)` | `var(--score-low-ink)` |
| `EnergyBadge.svelte:41` | `color: var(--score-mid)` | `var(--score-mid-ink)` |
| `EnergyBadge.svelte:46` | `color: var(--score-high)` | `var(--score-high-ink)` |
| `StrengthsGapsList.svelte:58` | `color: var(--score-high)` | `var(--score-high-ink)` |
| `profile/+page.svelte:767` | `border-color: var(--score-high)` | `var(--score-high-ink)` |
| `profile/+page.svelte:768` | `color: var(--score-high)` | `var(--score-high-ink)` |

**Los seis `background:` de `HistoryList` y `ScoreCard` son correctos y quedaron intactos** — esos son rellenos y ya pasan.

## Contraste medido después del cambio

| Par | Claro antes → después | Oscuro antes → después |
|---|---|---|
| `EnergyBadge:36` | 4.13 → **5.53** | 2.73 → **6.95** |
| `EnergyBadge:41` | 6.43 → **6.43** | 1.54 → **8.27** |
| `EnergyBadge:46` | 4.76 → **6.67** | 2.08 → **7.49** |
| `StrengthsGapsList:58` | 5.48 → **7.68** | 2.67 → **9.60** |
| `profile:768` | 5.48 → **7.68** | 2.67 → **9.60** |
| `profile:767` (borde, 3:1) | 5.48 → **7.68** | 2.67 → **9.60** |

Los diez pares pasan.

## Dos notas que cambian cómo leer los números

**1. `EnergyBadge` no está sobre `--surface`.** Su fondo es un tinte translúcido (`rgba(239,68,68,0.12)` y similares), así que la superficie real es ese alfa compuesto sobre `--surface`. Medir contra el token plano habría estado mal. Sobre esa superficie, `EnergyBadge:41` da **6.43 antes y después** — el token ink es byte-idéntico al fill en modo claro, así que esa línea es **solo un fix de modo oscuro**.

**2. El borde de `:767` usa `--score-high-ink` y no un token neutro**, porque ese borde y la etiqueta al lado señalan el mismo estado. Un borde gris perdería el color de "completado". Los bordes hermanos en `:772` y `:777` ya pasan y quedaron intactos — pasan porque esos tokens sí se voltean por modo, que es exactamente lo que `--score-*` deliberadamente no hace.

## Corrección aparte: un comentario que mentía

`app.css:59` documentaba `node contrast-audit.mjs frontend/src/app.css` como la forma de re-verificar el contraste. **Ese script nunca se commiteó.** Probablemente sea la razón por la que 8 fallos de componente sobrevivieron a una capa que sí midió 42 pares de paleta: el comentario leía como una red de seguridad existente.

El comentario ahora dice que los pares fueron medidos y que **no hay check automatizado todavía**, y pide re-medir tras cualquier edición que cambie un valor de color, un par o un modo.

Vale la pena construir el script de verdad en algún momento, para que esto no vuelva a pasar en silencio.

## Nota de producto (reportada, no tocada)

`es.json` y `en.json` usan **"JD"** en copy user-facing (~10 strings por locale, ~20 en total), y el español usa **"CV"** donde la regla pide *hoja de vida* (~20 strings). El primero que ve el usuario es `es.json:4` — el tagline: `"Match JD ↔ Perfil"`.

También: `es.json` mezcla voseo (`Pegá`, `Subí`) con usted formal (`Adjunte un PDF…`, línea 240). Es una decisión de estilo, no de la regla que diste.

**No toqué nada de esto** — es copy y amerita su decisión aparte.

## Plan de pruebas

- [x] `npm run check` → **0 errores** (1 warning preexistente en `HistoryList.svelte:6`, archivo no tocado)
- [x] `npm test` → **48 tests pasan** (7 archivos)
- [x] `npm run build` → **✓ built in 16.10s** (con `PUBLIC_API_URL` definida; el guard de prebuild la exige)
- [x] Confirmado que el CSS compilado emite `var(--score-*-ink)`

## Rollback

Un commit, cuatro archivos. Revertir devuelve los tokens de fill a los usos de texto.

## 这个 PR 是什么

`09-29-multi-agent-collab` 任务（工单 01–13）的全部产出，外加同分支上的 Composer 行内块改造（Tiptap 输入、Skill block）。两个任务都已验收归档。

## 内容

- **Composer 行内块（ADR 0005）**：Web/Electron 输入换成 Tiptap；@ 选中的文件、目录、图片和选中的 skill 在输入框里显示为行内块，草稿、排队编辑、发送失败恢复、Rewind 都保留；用户气泡与 Queue track 从文本渲染行内块。行内块以普通文字存在消息里，协议不加字段。粘贴按 DOM 选区插入，不再覆盖整段。
- **@ 提及智能体（ADR 0004 agent-mention）**：@ 列表新增智能体分组，Agent mention 为 provider/profile 两段式；提及由当前智能体通过 `create_agent` 派发，消息附加 Routing block，按 profile → Mention defaults → 运行时默认逐字段解析。
- **Mention defaults**：按 provider 存进 daemon 配置；设置 → Host → Agents 新增卡片，即时保存模型、思考档位与模式。
- **派发可用性**：agent 快照与 provider 快照下发 `canCreateAgents` 与原因码，@ 分组和新建界面据此置灰并给出开启入口。
- **派发组**：时间线里连续的 `create_agent` 调用合成派发组，实时显示子智能体状态、时长与等待批准，点开复用 track 的打开处理。`create_agent` 子智能体带 `paseo.parent-tool-call-id`，OpenCode/Pi/OMP 的工具名规范为 `paseo.create_agent`。
- **provider 子智能体**：provider 自带的子智能体调用也进派发组，行点开只读面板；其权限按 `metadata.providerSubagentId` 归属到父会话，track 与派发组行显示等待批准，只读面板里可直接批准。
- **子智能体权限交给用户**：通知改为勿代批，权限 attention 放行，工作区与 track 显示等待批准。

## 协议

新字段全部可选，新能力都挂在 `server_info.features` 上并带 `COMPAT(...)` 标签：`agentMentions`、`subagentCallLinks`。

## 与 main 的合并

已把 `origin/main`（第三方接口、提供方安装指引、0.12.0）merge 进本分支（`fca2be5aa`）。7 处冲突都是两边在同一位置各加了可选字段或 feature 开关，均两边保留：

- `protocol` 的 `agent-types.ts`、`messages.ts`，server 的 `agent-sdk-types.ts`：`canCreateAgents` / `createAgentsUnavailableReason` 与 `isModelListAuthoritative` / `activeApiEndpoint` 并存；features 里 `agentMentions`、`subagentCallLinks` 与 `apiEndpoints` 并存。
- `agent-manager.ts` 的 `registerSession`：`createAgentsCapability` 与 `apiEndpointId` 并存。
- `.atw/spec/server/backend/rpc-and-protocol.md`：两边各自新增的 Scenario 小节按先后拼接。

## 验证

- 合并后 `build:server`、全仓 `typecheck`、双方都改过的 22 个文件 `lint` / `format:check` 通过。
- 定向测试：protocol 5 个文件 51 项（providers-snapshot、api-endpoint、provider-subagents、wire-compat、snapshot-codec），server 4 个文件 316 项（agent-manager、agent-projections、create-agents-capability、provider-snapshot-manager）全部通过。
- 各工单在开发期间已按 `docs/qa.md` 做过 Web/Electron 验收；原生端无模拟环境，未做实机验收。
- 全量测试交给本 PR 的 CI。

## 备注

`docs/adr/` 下有两个 0004：`0004-api-endpoint-rewrites-cli-config.md`（main 已有）和本分支的 `0004-agent-mention-dispatched-by-parent-agent.md`。本 PR 未改名。

body:
RegExpRouter (the first router tried by the default `Hono` app) crashes when a route param uses a custom regex that can match an empty string:

```ts
const app = new Hono()
app.get('/api/:id{[0-9]?}', (c) => c.text(`id=${c.req.param('id')}`))

await app.request('/api/')
// TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')
```

### Cause

Each route terminal in the compiled RegExp is marked with an empty capture `$()`, and the matcher locates the handler with `match.indexOf('', 1)`. When a param regex such as `[0-9]?`, `[0-9]*`, `a{0,3}` or `(?:a|)` matches an empty segment, its capture is also `''` and comes first. The matcher then picks the param slot instead of the handler slot, returns `undefined` handlers, and `hono-base.ts` throws on `matchResult[0].length`.

#4329 (fixing #4325) handled this for the literal pattern `.*` only. This PR generalizes that check: any param pattern that matches the empty string now throws `UnsupportedPathError` in RegExpRouter (and PreparedRegExpRouter, which shares the same `Node`). SmartRouter then falls back to TrieRouter, which already matches these routes correctly (for `/api/` it gives `id === ''`). Behaviour for `{.*}` is unchanged.

### Tests

- `reg-exp-router/router.test.ts`: `{[0-9]?}`, `{[0-9]*}`, `{(?:a|)}` and `{a{0,3}}` throw `UnsupportedPathError`, and `{[0-9]+}` still works.
- `hono.test.ts`: with the default app, `/api/` returns `id=`, `/api/5` returns `id=5`, and `/api/55` returns 404. Without the fix, the `/api/` case fails with the `TypeError` above.

## What's in it
- `core-patch/class-devourer.patch`, diffed against azerothcore-wotlk `7f12e89` (Playerbot branch). It changes 5 files:
  - `SharedDefines.h`: `CLASS_DEVOURER = 10` and bit `0x200` in `CLASSMASK_ALL_PLAYABLE`. Talent tabs, quest, condition, item and achievement class checks depend on this mask.
  - `enuminfo_SharedDefines.cpp`: adds the new value to `EnumUtils<Classes>`. Without it, `.lookup player` would throw on class 10.
  - `StatSystem.cpp` and `Player.cpp`: the class-10 slot in the miss/parry/dodge/diminishing and dodge-from-agility tables was `0.0f`, which gives NaN for miss and dodge. It now uses warrior values.
  - `ObjectMgr.cpp`: `BuildPlayerLevelInfo` gives class 10 the warrior stat growth.
- `core-patch/playerbots-class-devourer.patch`, diffed against mod-playerbots `7bae1b5`:
  - Random bot creation skips class 10.
  - The equip cache skips class 10.
  - A config switch can't do this: `CharacterCreating.Disabled.ClassMask` would also block real players from creating the class.
- `apply.ps1` / `revert.ps1`:
  - Both patches get a dry run first. Nothing changes unless both pass.
  - A tree that is already applied (or already reverted) is detected and skipped.
  - They use `--ignore-whitespace` so CRLF checkouts work.

- Warrior-like attack power, armor and shields are left out of the core on purpose. They go through `Player::IsClass`, which calls the `OnPlayerIsClass` hook first, so the module (task 002) handles them.
- The README also lists the class-10 data that task 003 must provide. Missing `player_class_stats` for a class that has `playercreateinfo` rows crashes the server at startup. Zero `gt*` rows make ratings and crit worthless.

2. `build-server.ps1` builds. Expect a near-full rebuild because SharedDefines.h changed.

5. Random bot creation makes no class-10 characters. Only applies if bot accounts get created or refilled.

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5.5
Harness: Claude Code

Effort: Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code

# Subset: the promoted `fb6f5a8f` record with `QSB_DIVSTEP_LOOKAHEAD` 1 and the exact device switch `QSB_CODE_ROLL` 2, chosen from the ranked in-run probe `f70a9cbd`

## What this entry is

This entry is the promoted subset record `fb6f5a8f` (cefika; source `ff27a2b`, which is kshitij-hash's `e6715658` plus cefika's contiguous-epoch co-grinder walk) with two device switches turned on and the native image rebuilt:

- `tests/gpu_epochs/tree.cu`: `QSB_DIVSTEP_LOOKAHEAD` 0 -> 1. This switch is already in the record's tree, off by default. It is the lookahead form of the warp-0 divstep root inverse and is exact by construction (the record's own replay check covers both forms).
- `subset.cu`: `#define QSB_CODE_ROLL 2` before the tree is included. This is one of the exact device switches that cefika's in-run multi-arm probe `f70a9cbd` time-sliced on the ranked card against the record's own image. Paired round by round against the probe's two control arms, this arm reads the highest of the six switches, but the probe's own A/A check failed (see below), so that reading is not evidence. **This entry is a single-switch measurement. We give no point estimate.**
- `tests/gpu_epochs/tree.cu`, `tests/gpu_epochs/pair_shared.cuh`, `tests/gpu_epochs/window_schedule_shared.cuh`: the code of the probe's device switches, ported without the probe framework. That means `QSB_CODE_ROLL` and `QSB_WSEC_L1LAST` (ercumentyildirim's, first public in `dea321f0`), `QSB_DIGEST_MINB` and `QSB_SM_SKEW_NS`, plus the host-only switch `QSB_HP_SKIP`. Every one of them stays at the record's default unless it is the switch named above. With all of them at their defaults, the device code compiles to the same instructions as the record-plus-lookahead image. Only the image's knob string is longer, because it now lists the new keys.
- `qsb_carrier_sm89.h`: the native sm_89 image rebuilt for this tree.
- `subset.cu`, line 1: an inert `#define` tag that nothing references and that is not a carrier knob.

The co-grinder (`CpuGrindSubset.h`), the host producers, the gate, the recovery path and the table are the record's bytes. The multi-arm probe framework (the probe loader and the time-sliced schedule) is **not** part of this entry. This is a normal single-image run.

## The device image

- The image was rebuilt with `build_carrier.sh 24` from a clean export of this commit, with a CUDA 12.8 toolkit. Its cubin sha256 begins `5505f27a20a6ab72`.
- Positive controls, each run with the same toolkit from a clean export:
  - Rebuilding the committed tree of the record-plus-lookahead entry reproduces its committed image `3860ba97…` byte for byte.
  - Rebuilding this tree with the lookahead forced back to 0, once with each probe arm's flag, reproduces **all seven distinct arm images** that `f70a9cbd` committed, byte for byte: `a299b14f…` (control), `698775bc…` (`QSB_Q_SPREAD` 1), `fc2be370…` (`QSB_TREE_UNROLL` 1), `4a18d4d9…` (`QSB_GATHER_L1_POLICY` 1), `da65c084…` (`QSB_CODE_ROLL` 2), `f38e136d…` (`QSB_WSEC_L1LAST` 1), `e4554092…` (`QSB_DIGEST_MINB` 1). So the device code this entry runs for the switch is exactly the code the probe measured. The only difference is that this entry also has the lookahead on.
  - With every ported switch at its default, the image's SASS is identical line for line to the record-plus-lookahead image `3860ba97…`.
- The image's embedded knob string is byte-identical to the knob string compiled into this tree's host binary. The native image therefore passes the carrier's fingerprint check and loads natively instead of falling back to the JIT path.
- The rebuilt header from a second clean export of the final commit is identical to the committed header.

## Why this switch

The probe `f70a9cbd` ran eight digest-kernel images in about 0.7 s slices over disjoint epoch ranges within a single ranked run. There were eight arms and 224 slots per arm. Arms 0 and 3 are the record's image (an A/A pair). Arms 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are the six switches listed above.

I read its public hit list as follows:

1. The GPU hits are the hits in the late window's 128 triples.
2. For each hit, take the lexicographic rank of its first six skip indices. The arm is rank // A and the slot is (rank − k·A) // S, where A = floor(C(137,6)/8) and S = floor(A/224).
3. The work of each (arm, slot) is the highest GPU-hit rank in the slot minus the slot start.
4. For each round, divide an arm's work by the mean of the two control arms' work in the same round.

I excluded the first round (warm-up), the last two rounds (cut by the harness), near-full slots and thin slots. The decoder was checked on patternrecognition9-del's earlier seven-arm probe `9b2fbb14`: it reproduces that probe's published reading, including `QSB_Q_MIX` 2 at about −1.2%.

My own gate for a switch, written down before the probe scored:

- the A/A pair must agree within 0.30%;
- the arm must read at least +0.30% and at least twice its standard error;
- the arm's median ratio must be positive.

The probe failed the first condition: its two control arms, which run the same image, disagreed by 1.44%. With the A/A pair that far apart, no arm reading from this probe can be used. This arm's pooled reading against the mean of the two controls was +0.95% ± 0.23%, the highest of the six, and we report it only for completeness. The switch has never been measured on its own on the ranked card. That is what this entry does.

## Why nothing else is added

I reviewed every ranked subset run of the day, including rejected and cancelled ones. The GPU part was measured by the rank of the last GPU hit, which has no Poisson term; its remaining noise is machine state. The co-grinder part was measured by its own hit count.

- The runner drifts. Code-identical draws of the record-plus-lookahead image read 6.152e9 (16:37 UTC start), 6.074e9 (17:05) and 6.057e9 (20:19) GPU epochs, against about 6.146e9 for the same class of image around midday. Two code-identical draws in consecutive slots differed by 1.3%. A single draw therefore cannot resolve a switch below about 1%. That is why this entry relies on the in-run probe, which pairs arms within the same seconds, and not on single draws.
- **Host producers off** (`QSB_HOST_PRODUCERS` 0 / `QSB_HP_SKIP` 1). The co-grinder part rose by about 1–3% in every run that had the producers off. The GPU part of the one clean draw with this change (plus a co-grinder change), however, sits 0.6% below the plain draw in the next slot. The GPU part is about nine tenths of the score, so the net sign is not established. The switch is ported here but left off. Three later ranked draws that carried it (with the lookahead on) read about −0.4% on the GPU part and about +3% on the co-grinder, a net close to zero.
- `QSB_Q_MIX` 2, `QSB_ROOT_LUT_SMEM`, `QSB_SHA_CONST_PEEL` and `QSB_PSI_HOIST` 2 were already read ≤ 0 on the ranked card by the probes `9b2fbb14` and `8df5c413`. They are not carried.
- The co-grinder changes published today (a SHA-NI digest bridge, split MRG chains, adaptive table geometry, a KH16 feed-forward) show no co-grinder gain above the ±1% Poisson noise of one run in any ranked draw so far. They are not carried.
- `QSB_DIVSTEP_LOOKAHEAD` 1: the ranked draws and probe arms of this switch, pooled against same-hour plain draws, give about +0.05% ± 0.10%. It is exact and costs nothing, so it is kept.

## How to read this entry's result

- GPU part: take the rank of the last GPU hit and compare

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a standalone local CLI tool (`analyze.py`) that complements the existing Streamlit webapp. The tool reads HubSpot Excel exports directly without requiring API access, performs the same DIRS21 sales intelligence analysis, and exports results to Excel. Both tools now share the same fachliche logic in `logic/`.

## Key Changes

- **New `analyze.py`**: Local CLI entry point that orchestrates the analysis pipeline
  - Reads companies from Excel files via new `logic/excel_import.py` module
  - Processes each company through the existing analysis logic (website crawling, DIRS21 detection, scoring, recommendations)
  - Exports results to Excel with automatic timestamped filenames in `exports/` directory
  - Implements robust error handling: individual company failures don't break the overall analysis
  - Supports `--limit` flag for testing and `--config` for custom configuration paths
  - Saves intermediate results at configurable intervals to prevent data loss on interruption

- **New `logic/excel_import.py`**: Excel import module
  - Reads HubSpot Excel exports and maps columns via `config.yaml` (no hardcoded column names)
  - Handles missing optional fields gracefully
  - Validates required fields (hotel_name, website) and documents issues in pruefhinweis
  - Skips completely empty rows while preserving row numbers for traceability

- **Updated `config.yaml`**: Restructured to support both data sources
  - New `excel.columns` section for mapping internal field names to actual Excel column headers
  - Moved `adressgruppe_mapping` to top level (shared by both tools)
  - Added `analysis.save_interval` for intermediate Excel saves in CLI mode
  - Clarified which sections apply to which tool (Excel vs. HubSpot API)

- **Updated `README.md`**: Comprehensive documentation
  - Explains both analysis paths (CLI with Excel vs. optional Streamlit with HubSpot API)
  - Step-by-step guide for local CLI usage
  - Clarified Excel import requirements and optional fields
  - Updated project structure and error handling sections

- **Updated `app.py`**: Minor refactoring
  - Changed `config["hubspot"]["adressgruppe_mapping"]` to `config.get("adressgruppe_mapping")` to use shared top-level mapping

- **Updated `.gitignore`**: Added entries for generated files
  - Excludes `exports/` and `data/*.xlsx` (can contain customer data)
  - Keeps `.gitkeep` files to preserve directory structure

- **New `.streamlit/secrets.toml.example`**: Template for HubSpot token (app.py only)

## Implementation Details

- The CLI tool maintains the same output column structure and fachliche logic as the Streamlit app
- Error handling is comprehensive: network timeouts, malformed HTML, missing fields, and API errors are all caught and documented in `pruefhinweis` without stopping the analysis
- Excel column mapping is entirely configuration-driven, allowing the tool to work with different export formats without code changes
- Intermediate saves prevent data loss during long-running analyses of large company lists
- Progress is displayed in the terminal with `[current/total]` format for transparency

author: xeriomy
body:
## What

First real patches for this collection, replacing the no-op placeholder:

- **Change app name** — writes the user's value into the `app_name` string
  resource. Verified against Spotify 9.1.84.2231: `app_name` is declared once,
  in `res/values/strings.xml`, with no per-locale variants, and 29 manifest
  elements reference it, so one edit renames all of them consistently.
- **Clone app** — renames the package so the patched app installs alongside the
  original.

## Why it is shaped this way

Both patches are resource patches. Neither modifies bytecode, so
`Fingerprints.kt` stays empty — and a patch that needs no fingerprint cannot
break when Spotify is obfuscated differently next release.

Renaming a package is not just the `package` attribute. Four groups of
package-derived values have to move together, or Android rejects the install:

| What | Failure if left behind |
|---|---|
| 8 provider authorities under `<application>` | `INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER` |
| 4 custom permissions, in all 3 places each appears | `INSTALL_FAILED_DUPLICATE_PERMISSION` |
| `media_provider_authority` string resource | `INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER` |
| process name | `AssertionError: The process name ... is not allowed to start` |

The process name is handled from the manifest via `android:process`, rather than
by patching Spotify's startup allowlist. Two installed apps may share a process
name — processes are keyed by name *and* uid — so the clone and the original
coexist, and `getPackageName()` still returns the new package.

## Verified on device

- Clone installs with the original present, launches, and signs in
- Custom app name applied

## Not yet verified

- Share sheet, profile picture and playlist artwork (these depend on Spotify
  deriving its authorities from `getPackageName()` at runtime — the suffix
  strings exist standalone in the dex, but the call sites were not read)
- Android Auto on the clone (the `<queries>` entry is deliberately untouched)

## Verified against the APK

Derived from Spotify **9.1.84.2231**, versionCode **146291969**, which is now
pinned in `Constants.kt`. `res/values/strings.xml` was checked for 728
quote-delimited raw strings, 682 containing apostrophes and none with an
unescaped inner quote, which is the rule the name escaper implements.

## Also in here

author: pkarw
body:
Specyfikacja **VCAL** — kalendarz wizyt w module `patient` oraz kontrola dostępności terapeuty i gabinetu. Dokument projektowy, **bez implementacji**: PR dokłada 16 plików w `.ai/`, nie rusza `src/`.

Rozszerza [VIS — wizyty pacjenta](.ai/specs/2026-09-29-patient-visits.md) (zależność: faza VIS-1).

## Najważniejsze ustalenie

Dostępności nie trzeba budować — jest w platformie, a moduł `patient` po prostu jej nie czyta:

- `planner:planner_availability_rule` — `subject_type` = `member` \| `resource` \| `ruleset`, `rrule`/`exdates`, `kind` = `availability` \| `unavailability`
- **`staff.leave-requests.accept` ustawia `status='approved'` i sam zakłada reguły `kind='unavailability'`** z powodem kadrowym (`staff/commands/leave-requests.ts`, `createUnavailabilityRules`) — urlop i zwolnienie są już w tym samym strumieniu co grafik, więc nie trzeba czytać tabeli wniosków
- gabinet: `resources_resources.availability_rule_set_id` + `is_active`
- scalanie okien: `plannerAvailabilityService.getMergedAvailabilityWindows()` — ta sama funkcja dla siatki i dla walidacji serwerowej, więc nie mogą się rozjechać

VCAL nie dodaje żadnej tabeli grafiku ani relacji ORM między modułami. Kontrola siedzi **w komendzie zapisu**, nie w komponencie — dlatego działa identycznie z kalendarza, z listy wizyt i przez API.

## Zakres projektu

- **Macierz dziesięciu kodów konfliktu z wagami.** Nieobecność kadrowa (`member_absence`) i nieaktywny gabinet (`resource_inactive`) blokują zapis; poza grafikiem, ręczny wyjątek i podwójna rezerwacja ostrzegają; brak grafiku to informacja, nie ostrzeżenie.
- **Kontrakt nadpisania** z sygnaturami konkretnych kolizji, wymaganym powodem i feature'em `patient.visits.override_conflict`. Zmiana sytuacji między podglądem a zapisem unieważnia zgodę.
- **Cztery pola audytu** na `patient_visits` (powód szyfrowany, autor, czas, kody) + dwa indeksy częściowe pod wykrywanie nakładania.
- **Dwie trasy API:** `GET /api/patient/visits/calendar` i `GET /api/patient/visits/availability-check`.
- **UI na `ScheduleView`** z `@open-mercato/ui/backend/schedule` — prymityw design systemu, którego używają już `planner`, `staff` i `resources`. Ekran kalendarza CRM jest wewnętrzny dla modułu `customers` i nie jest publicznym kontraktem, więc go nie kopiujemy.
- **Dziesięć testów integracyjnych**, traceability, rollout, ryzyka, kryteria akceptacji.

## Fazy

| Faza | Wynik | Wdrażalna osobno |
|---|---|---|
| VCAL-1 | Kontrola dostępności na ścieżce zapisu — działa na istniejącym formularzu VIS, bez linijki kodu kalendarza | tak |
| VCAL-2 | Widok kalendarza, filtr terapeuty i gabinetu, wizyta z wolnego slotu | tak, po VCAL-1 |

## Makiety

11 ekranów: `.ai/specs/assets/vcal-ui-mockups.html` + PNG, render przez `node .ai/specs/assets/render-vcal-mockups.mjs`. Tydzień terapeuty z pasmami grafiku i urlopu, wizyta ze slotu, ostrzeżenia, nadpisanie z powodem, odmowa przy urlopie, to samo sprawdzenie w formularzu z listy, miesiąc/gabinet, karta wizyty, lista z przełącznikiem, komplet stanów UI, 360 px.

## Do decyzji recenzenta

Brama Open Questions została rozstrzygnięta **w trybie autonomicznym**. Cztery założenia są wypisane w sekcji `Resolved assumptions (autonomous defaults)`, każde odwracalne i z opisaną ścieżką odwrócenia:

1. jedna specyfikacja z dwiema fazami zamiast dwóch dokumentów,
2. dwie wagi konfliktu zamiast „wszystko blokuje” lub „wszystko ostrzega”,
3. „zajęte” = reguły `planner` + własne wizyty; wydarzenia kalendarza CRM poza zakresem,
4. `ScheduleView` zamiast odtwarzania ekranu CRM.

Status dokumentu pozostaje `Draft`. Do `Ready for implementation` potrzeba potwierdzenia tych założeń, a sama implementacja i tak czeka na fazę VIS-1.

## Weryfikacja

- 25/25 sekcji szablonu `SPEC-000-template.md` obecnych
- wszystkie odnośniki do makiet i specyfikacji rozwiązują się
- każde `capabilityId` → `sourcePaths` zgodne z `src/modules/example/references/surface-inventory.json`
- `node scripts/check-lessons.mjs` — zielony

Bez zmian w `src/`, bez migracji, bez nowych zależności npm.

body:
The `RoverExploreWhyren` contract never loads:

```
CONTRACT_TYPE 'RoverExploreWhyren': Error parsing scienceSubjects
NotSupportedException: Can't parse identifier for type ScienceSubject in class ContractConfigurator.ExpressionParser.SubjectParser - not supported!
```

`scienceSubjects = @scienceSubjectsTemp2.Add(RoverScienceExperiment)` adds an experiment name to a list of science subjects, and CC can't turn that name into a subject. This drops the `.Add(...)`, so the contract picks 1 to 3 subjects from the experiment list, which already includes `RoverScienceExperiment`.

(Side note: even with a valid value, CC's list `Add()` currently returns the list unchanged, so the extra subject would never have been added. I'll report that on the Contract Configurator side.)

author: lhj6102
body:
## Problem

CCDD users ask their own agents to build per-project `views.agentTools`. Nothing in the docs said how to keep those tools small. A downstream project (a game damage simulator) found that one tool per data projection cost 50.6 KB of tool definitions per request and that reviews spent most of their tokens on dumps.

## Change

- New `docs/reviewer-tools.md`: what reaches the model, surface (few tools, explicit inputs, `select`, batching, per-Artifact `enum`s), output (no echoes, duplicates or internal detail; warnings always), descriptions, authored errors, structural enforcement of a checking order with the exact schema dialect and its limits, how tool changes affect review identity, measurement with `tools check`, `run show` and executor telemetry, a short case study, and a ready-to-paste agent brief.
- One-line links from the README next steps, `docs/builder-workflow.md` and `docs/reviewers.md`. The root README is also the `@ccdd/core` package README.

No code, example or package version changes.

## Validation

- Each mechanism the guide names was checked against `src`: tool naming and scope (`src/tools/runner.ts`), the system prompt and final schema (`src/executors/pi.ts`, `src/response-schema.ts`), the schema keyword set (`src/tools/schema.ts`), authored and generic tool errors (`src/tools/diagnostics.ts`), repair diagnostics (`src/executors/final-result.ts`), identity inputs (`src/project/identity.ts`) and telemetry (`src/broker/index.ts`, `src/project/store.ts`).
- Both JSON snippets were run through the built `validateSchema`, `validateResponseSchema` and `validateFinalResult`: valid input is accepted; an invalid selection, a duplicated option and a missing item are rejected. `contains`, `$ref`, `if`, `format`, `prefixItems`, type arrays and empty `enum`s are rejected as stated.
- The `tools check --json` fields were checked on a copy of `examples/custom-text-reader`.
- Relative links and anchors in the edited docs resolve.
- `npm test` (Node 22.23.2, WSL2): the language check and build pass; 556 of 557 tests pass. `resources.test` "dead owner cleanup retains the slot until its tracked child group is no longer running" times out here, also when run alone. Repair diagnostics are always category-only in real reviews. `finalResultSchema` wraps both branches in a top-level `oneOf` (`src/response-schema.ts:17-24`), and `supportsBoundedErrors` rejects any schema with `oneOf` (`src/executors/final-result.ts:100-105`), so the repair prompt never names a path. `docs/contracts.md` (around line 452) implies simple schemas get paths.

body:
## Problem

Meson release builds pass `-O1` to ELD, producing an unrecognized-option warning and failing links that use `--fatal-warnings`.

## Root cause

The shared GNU option table has no `-O` definition, so optimization-level arguments reach the unknown-option diagnostics.

## Fix

Recognize joined and separate forms, such as `-O1` and `-O 2`, as ignored compatibility options. Reuse `JoinedOrSeparate`, the existing compatibility group, and `getUnsignedInteger` to validate every occurrence before discarding its value. The separate `--lto-O` behavior is unchanged.

Add regression coverage using the existing command-line fixture and help test. Cover valid and repeated levels, malformed/missing values, and preservation of unrelated unknown-option warnings.

## Validation

- Built ELD against LLVM main; 54 focused test runs passed across x86-64, Hexagon, AArch64, ARM, RV32, and RV64 using Clang 24. Six expected `PrintHiddenHelp` skips.
- The `-O1 --fatal-warnings` smoke link passed and produced byte-identical output to the link without `-O1`.
- Verified that `-O` and `--lto-O` remain independent, including rejection of an invalid LTO level.

The full test suite was not run.

Fixes qualcomm/eld#1940

body: ## Summary Adds `@data-agent-ontology/ontology-mcp`, an optional MCP host adapter beside `withOntology`. It does not replace the library or `ontology-server`. One process owns the Ladybug file. The CLI constructs `new Ontology(new OntologyStore(() => new Date(), file))` and `new LocalOntologyClient(ontology)`, and closes the store on shutdown. - `--transport stdio` uses `StdioServerTransport`. No port and no token. - `--transport http` uses Streamable HTTP (`StreamableHTTPServerTransport`) at `POST /mcp`. A non-empty bearer token is required (`ONTOLOGY_TOKEN` or `--token`). Missing or wrong tokens get 401. `--port` defaults to **8788** so it does not collide with `ontology-server`. `--host` / `HOST` defaults to `127.0.0.1`. - `--file` or `ONTOLOGY_FILE` is required and must be a `.lbdb` path. Tools, mapped onto `OntologyClient`: `context`, `lookup`, `check_sql`, `record_sql`, `note`, `list_proposals`. Notes and traces file proposals and do not change trusted knowledge. `submitScope`, `revise`, `revert`, `rollback`, `acceptProposal`, and `rejectProposal` are not registered. Curator accept stays on the library or the existing HTTP service. `check_sql` / `record_sql` do not auto-submit a scope. SDK pin: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0` (1.30.1 and 1.31.0 are inside the 7-day `minimumReleaseAge` window). ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm --filter @data-agent-ontology/ontology-mcp test` (9 tests) - [x] `pnpm --filter @data-agent-ontology/ontology-mcp exec tsc --noEmit` - [x] `pnpm exec eslint packages/ontology-mcp` - [x] `pnpm knip` - [ ] CI on this draft PR

body:
Depende de #605. Esta branch parte de `fluxo0/01-conta-gratis`; o PR aponta para `main` para executar os workflows existentes. Até #605 entrar, o diff inclui também os commits do ticket 01. O ticket 02 deve ser revisado no intervalo `1c73e5ef..HEAD`.

O Estrategista recebe as últimas 20 mensagens anteriores à atual, com corte de 2.000 caracteres por texto e cards resumidos. A resposta pode trazer até três iscas na mesma chamada de modelo; clicar registra a frase como mensagem da pessoa, com `payload.fromSuggestion=true`. Iscas de confirmação, aprovação e autorização, inclusive os imperativos Aprove/Publique/Autorize/Confirme, são filtradas antes de aparecer ou persistir. Iscas antigas ficam desabilitadas quando Equipe é desligada.

As sugestões concluem a resposta depois das demais ferramentas autorizadas da mesma chamada, preservando comandos pagos independentemente da ordem. Falhas de ferramenta ou de comando são devolvidas ao modelo; o limite de iterações permanece.

Na conta grátis, ficam só as ferramentas de consulta, sugestões e oferta: pedidos pagos usam o card do plano, e a recusa pelo teto também entrega esse card, sem chamar o provedor. A oferta e o contato comercial exigem `diagnostic.recorded`; falha ou ausência de fonte não libera o plano. O card não exibe preço. “Assinar o plano” usa `request_support` com `purpose:"plan"`, abre uma exceção comercial com prazo e confirmação na conversa, e reutiliza o pedido ainda aberto ou assumido, identificado pela finalidade no evento, mesmo quando a nota muda. O evento de abertura carrega a finalidade opcional, validada pelo schema existente: só `purpose:"plan"` recebe a confirmação comercial; exceções automáticas e eventos antigos sem a chave mantêm a mensagem geral. “Agora não” envia a frase para continuar no grátis.

Anexos no chat free recebem uma recusa clara na conversa, antes de qualquer chamada ao agente; a rota encaminha somente a presença validada do anexo. O texto orienta a enviar a mensagem em texto ou usar a leitura do site. O teto grátis após o diagnóstico leva ao card do plano; antes dele, a resposta não sugere reinício mensal. A mensagem mensal permanece para contas pagas.

O limite grátis reutiliza o contrato do 01: 2048 tokens por padrão, configuráveis; bound conservador do payload completo em bytes UTF-8 + 4096, declarado em cada chamada. As fixtures PostgreSQL derivam o uso do request, verificam concorrência entre dois pools, custo exato e teto vitalício sem depender do tamanho antigo do payload. Nenhum gate do ledger foi afrouxado. O prompt foi versionado como `equipe-prompts/v3`.

As listas fixas das telas vazias estão disponíveis no catálogo/componente reutilizável. A integração nas superfícies e o consumo de `/?suggestion=` ficam com o ticket 09, conforme decisão do coordenador. Nenhuma home, página, rota nova, dependência ou migração foi adicionada.

Validação local do HEAD `ac98717e`: 123 testes passaram em 7 arquivos, cobrindo as regressões dos seis threads de revisão; 8 falhavam antes da correção. Typecheck, ESLint focal (um warning de img preexistente), gate de destinos e `graphify update .` (AST, sem LLM) passaram. Os artefatos Graphify permanecem locais, fora deste diff.

[CI Node 22 do HEAD `ac98717e`](https://github.com/jhowtkd/adscale/actions/runs/36745704894) verde nos cinco jobs: 10.131 testes passaram e 25 foram pulados; lint, typecheck, convergência e build passaram. Os gates E2E passaram com 14 testes de acessibilidade, 17 layouts (4 skips) e 4 jornadas críticas do Studio, além das quatro matrizes.

Os seis threads de revisão atribuídos ao ticket 02 foram respondidos e resolvidos. O novo P1 em `ledger.ts`, herdado do ticket 01 e fora do diff `1c73e5ef..HEAD`, permanece aberto e foi encaminhado ao mediador/dono do PR 605.

Evidência visual: componente real com CSS do projeto e dados sintéticos; conferido contra a D2 v4. O placeholder de preço foi removido por requisito. Os prints abaixo não representam jornada autenticada nem aceitação humana. Nenhum fornecedor real, produção, merge ou deploy foi acionado.

## Was und warum

<!-- Kurz: was ändert sich, welches Problem löst es, welcher verworfene Weg. -->

## Sicherheit — Durchsicht nach `docs/SECURITY_STANDARD.md`

Diese Liste erzwingt nichts. Sie erinnert an die Fragen, die eine Durchsicht
stellen muss; erzwungen wird nur, was das Qualitätstor prüft (`npm run
security:check`, `npm test`, `npm run e2e`). Nicht Zutreffendes streichen,
nicht einfach ankreuzen.

- [ ] **C1 Anmeldung** — Sitzung auf dem Server geprüft; Gerätesperre (`allowDuringHandoff`) beachtet
- [ ] **C2 Rechte** — `permissions` am Endpunkt, Registry `scripts/openapi-routes*.ts` gleich, Seite/Knopf/Endpunkt einig
- [ ] **C3 Mandant** — `organizationId` im `where`; fremde ID = unbekannt; Fall gegen `fremdeOrganisation()`
- [ ] **C4 Eingaben** — Zod-Schema aus `src/lib/validation/`, Obergrenzen
- [ ] **C5 Injection** — kein Unsafe-SQL mit Werten, kein Prozess, kein Pfad aus der Anfrage
- [ ] **C6 XSS** — fremder Text nur als React-Text; keine fremde Adresse als Link/Weiterleitung
- [ ] **C7 CSRF** — kein schreibender GET; Origin-Prüfung über die Routenfactory
- [ ] **C8 SSRF** — ausgehende Verbindungen an konfigurierbare Ziele nur über `pruefeZiel`
- [ ] **C9 Rate-Limit** — Kontingent passend zum Rateproblem
- [ ] **C10 Geheimnisse** — nichts im Code, Log, Protokoll, `NEXT_PUBLIC_`
- [ ] **C11 Personendaten** — geschwärzt im Protokoll; keine in Codes, Links, Dateinamen
- [ ] **C12 Dateien** — Ticket, Abschluss, Typ/Signatur, Malware-Prüfung
- [ ] **C13 Öffentliche Tokens** — nur `PublicAccessToken`; neuer öffentlicher Endpunkt in `security/oeffentliche-endpunkte.json` begründet
- [ ] **C14 Geld** — Decimal, Preis vom Server, Belege unveränderlich
- [ ] **C15 Invarianten** — in der Datenbank (Index, Sperre); Gleichzeitigkeitsfall; neue Schranke in `security/datenbank-schranken.json`
- [ ] **C16 Protokoll** — fachliche Änderungen protokolliert, ohne Geheimnis
- [ ] **C17 Webhooks** — Signatur, Zeitfenster, idempotent
- [ ] **C18 Abhängigkeiten** — neue Laufzeitabhängigkeit in `docs/LIEFERKETTE.md`; Advisory bewertet und befristet
- [ ] **C19 Fehler** — über `toErrorResponse`, nichts Internes nach aussen
- [ ] **C20 Prüfungen** — Pflichtfälle aus C20 vorhanden

## Nachweis

- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run docs` (keine Abweichung)
- [ ] `npm test` gegen `npm run test:server`, **ohne** zusätzliche Wiederholungen, Überspringen oder entfernte Zusicherungen
- [ ] `npm run e2e` (bei Oberflächenänderungen im Rahmen zusätzlich `npm run e2e:stress`)
- [ ] `npm run security:check` ohne blockierenden Befund; neue Unterdrückung begründet
- [ ] Migration: additiv, SQL gelesen, handgeschriebene Regeln mit Begründung

body:
Follow-up to #79. On `--agent-engine v3` (KAS, the default since #79), kiro-cli records every MCP tool call with `toolName: "tool_call"`; the real identity is in `title` (`@aws-mcp/aws___run_script`), `actionType` (`mcp_aws_mcp_aws___run_script`) and `_meta.kiro.serverName`. The KAS converter copied `toolName`, so every MCP call in `trajectory.json` is a function named `tool_call` with no server, and MCP usage is invisible in v3 trajectories. Built-in tools (`execute_bash`, `fs_write`) and KAS meta-tools (`tool_load`, `disclose_context`) were already named correctly.

```json
{"type": "tool_call", "toolCallId": "toolu_bdrk_015FesafxZC5CcxMQMD1UZv6", "toolName": "tool_call",
 "actionType": "mcp_aws_mcp_aws___run_script", "title": "@aws-mcp/aws___run_script",
 "_meta": {"kiro": {"serverName": "aws-mcp", "toolOrigin": "default"}}, "args": {"code": "..."}}
```

**Change** (`aws_bench/agents/kiro_cli.py`)
- `_kas_tool_call(payload) -> ToolCall`: keeps a real `toolName`; for a generic one takes the tool from `title` (`@<server>/<tool>`), else from `actionType` with the `mcp_<server>_` prefix stripped, else `unknown`. Sets `extra["mcp_server"]` when the server is known, and `extra["disclosed_context"]` (skill name/uri) for `disclose_context`. Parses JSON-string `args`.
- The v1/v2/v3 store parsers build `ToolCall` directly instead of tuples that `_build_trajectory` re-wrapped; v1/v2 output is unchanged.

**Tests**: `TestKasToolCallNames` (10 tests, payload shapes as recorded by KAS). `make check` green (3191 passed). Also checked on real v3 sessions (kiro-cli 2.24.0–2.25.0, several models): MCP calls resolve to `aws___run_script` with `mcp_server: aws-mcp`, built-in and meta-tool names are unchanged, nothing is left unresolved.

author: edridudi
body:
## Summary

A support ticket for the v2.7.1 Chrome freeze (fixed in #1132–#1134, shipping in 2.7.2) also showed `Uncaught (in promise) AxiosError: timeout of 15000ms exceeded` from `get24hrTicker`, repeating every 30s. The freeze itself is not caused by this. The Strike timeouts happened because the browser UI thread was stalled; `api.strikefinance.org/price/v2/ticker/24hr` answers in about 0.2s. But `useStrikeMarket` turns every failed poll into an unhandled rejection. That is console noise that makes tickets harder to read, and it hides a real gap.

`src/modules/market/composables/useStrikeMarket.ts`:

- **No unhandled rejections.** The initial load (`Promise.all(...).finally(...)`) and the 30s refresh had no `catch`. Fetches now run through `Promise.allSettled`, failures go to `debugLog`, and the last good tickers and funding rates stay in place.
- **Exchange info retried.** It was fetched once. If that first request failed, the perps symbol list stayed empty until the page was reloaded. The refresh now retries it until it loads.
- **Polling stops on unmount.** The interval ran for the life of the page once any perps component had mounted. It is now ref-counted per component scope (`onScopeDispose`), stops when the last consumer unmounts, and restarts on the next mount. Calls made outside a scope keep the old run-forever behaviour.

The public return shape is unchanged. No other file calls `fetchTickers`/`fetchFundingRates`.

## Test plan

- [x] New `useStrikeMarket.spec.ts` (4 cases). On the old code it fails 3 of 4: an unhandled rejection is caught, the symbol list stays empty after a failed initial load, and the poll keeps running after the last consumer is disposed. The 4th case, which keeps last good tickers on failure, guards the new code path.
- [x] `npx vitest run src/modules/market src/api`: 13 files, 151 tests green.
- [x] ESLint clean on touched files. Pre-commit design ratchet and contrast checks pass.
- [ ] Not run in the extension. Manual check: open Perpetuals in the side panel, block `api.strikefinance.org` in DevTools, and confirm no `Uncaught (in promise)` after 30s. Then navigate away and confirm Strike requests stop.

Note: this spec is not in the CI-named spec list (`dev-bundle-gate.yml`), so CI does not run it.

author: alpergundogdu
body:
## Summary

Operators had no denominator for chain-RPC health: `decdn_rpc_healthy` is a 0/1 probe, and the other RPC counters only see failures on specific paths. This adds per-request metrics at one choke point.

- **Tower layer on the alloy RPC client** (`crates/node/src/rpc_metrics.rs`). `ProviderFactory` becomes a value holding the URL and the metrics handle, and every role (read-only, shared head, seller wallet, buyer wallet, deployment preflight) builds its client through `metered_http_client`. No call site changes. The layer uses `ClientBuilder::default().layer(..).http(url)`, which is what `connect_http` does, so alloy's localhost poll default is unchanged (the existing `provider_factory_preserves_role_polling_policy` test still pins that).
- **`decdn_rpc_requests_total{method,outcome}`**:
  - `method` is a closed set of 15 JSON-RPC names plus `other`.
  - `outcome` is one of `ok`, `reverted`, `rpc_error`, `rate_limited`, `transport_error`, `timeout`. `timeout` covers a reqwest timeout and a request whose caller dropped it, which in this node means the per-call `timed` deadline fired. A drop guard records it.
  - Batch replies are matched per request by id.
  - All 96 pairs are exported at zero from startup.
  - The URL is never a label.
- **`decdn_rpc_request_duration_seconds{method}`**: buckets 10 ms to 10 s, with the top bucket at `DEFAULT_RPC_CALL_TIMEOUT`. A dropped request records no sample.
- These metrics live in a separate `RpcMetrics` group. `DecdnMetrics` derives `Deserialize`, and a labelled histogram family cannot deserialize, so they can't go there.
- The rate-limit predicate moves from `multiplexed_poller` into `rpc_metrics::is_rate_limit`, so the poller and the metric share one definition.
- **Monitoring**: `dashboard-chain.json` gets a "Chain RPC provider" row with request rate by method, error ratio by method (plus all methods), failures by outcome, and p95 latency by method. `prometheus-alerts.yml` gets `DecdnRpcErrorRatioHigh`: ratio over 10m > 10% for 15m, excluding `ok` and `reverted`, with a volume guard of > 0.05 req/s.
- **Docs**: `adr/appendix-observability.md` gets a new § Chain RPC Metrics (registry rows are gate-enforced) and a note that `outcome` meets the labelled-reason-split bar. `docs/runbook.md` § RPC unreachable covers the new alert.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p decdn-node`: 1502 passed. Includes the new classification unit tests, wiremock end-to-end tests (ok / reverted / 429 / dropped-at-deadline), the exposure test, `monitoring_selectors_are_exported` and `adr_registry_names_are_exported`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features`, `cargo fmt --check`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc`
- [x] pre-commit (crate edges, ADR hygiene, markdownlint, yaml)

body:
## 摘要

報名流程改為 Google 登入，新增大廳與活動專區的兩個遊戲，以及主持人後台。

## 參加者流程

登入 → 捏角色報名 → 大廳 → 活動專區

- **Google 登入**：一個帳號一個角色，在任何裝置登入同一個帳號都能修改；移除原本存在瀏覽器的 `edit_token`
- **大廳**：所有報名角色在跑道上跑，附全部名單與「我的角色」；已加入遊戲時顯示「繼續遊戲」
- **LINE 內建瀏覽器**：自動加上 `openExternalBrowser=1`，改用手機預設瀏覽器開啟（Google 不允許在 LINE 內登入）

## 遊戲一：搶答跑位

- 主持人建立場次並設定代碼，參加者輸入代碼加入
- 手機用十字鍵上下左右移動角色，站在哪一欄就是答案；可以跳躍、做 8 種表情
- 投影主持畫面顯示題目、倒數與所有角色，時間到自動公布答案並計分，最後顯示排名
- 斷線處理：答案送出失敗自動重送、重新整理回到原本的答案區

## 遊戲二：接力抽禮物

- 投影拉霸機：燈泡、滾輪減速、閃光、彩帶、合成音效（可關閉）
- 抽中的人由伺服器隨機決定；被抽中的人手機在動畫結束時跳出通知
- 接力抽，抽過的人移出籤池；沒有連線的人也會被抽到

## 主持後台 `/host`

- 題庫：是非題／選擇題、正確答案、作答秒數、排序
- 場次：建立代碼、開啟主持畫面
- 籤池：排除、手動加入沒報名的人、放回、重設
- 報名管理：顯示 Google email、改名、刪除

## 其他

- 遊戲中與投影畫面保持螢幕常亮
- GitHub Actions 每天查詢一次 Supabase，避免免費專案閒置被暫停
- 本機模擬模式支援開多個分頁測試（每個分頁是不同的人）

## 資料庫 migration（依序執行）

- `20261005000000_google_auth.sql`：`players` 改用 `user_id`，移除 `edit_token`
- `20261010000000_quiz_game.sql`：`admins`、`quiz_questions`、`games`、`game_players`、`game_answers`
- `20261015000000_gift_draw.sql`：`draw_entries`、`draw_state`
- `20261020000000_admin_players.sql`：報名管理用的 function

⚠️ 原有的報名資料會失去修改權限（沒有對應的 Google 帳號），上線前的測試資料可以直接刪除。

## 上線前設定

- [ ] Supabase：依序執行 migration，並執行 `insert into public.admins (email) values ('主持人 gmail');`
- [ ] Google Cloud：建立 OAuth client，同意畫面發布為正式版；Supabase 啟用 Google 登入
- [ ] Supabase URL Configuration：設定 Site URL，Redirect URLs 加上正式網址與 `http://localhost:5173/**`
- [ ] Vercel 環境變數：`VITE_SUPABASE_URL`、`VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`、`VITE_ROSTER_KEY`
- [ ] GitHub Actions secrets：`SUPABASE_URL`、`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`

詳細步驟見 README。

## 測試

- `pnpm test:db`：用 PGlite 跑所有 migration，測試權限與 function（登入、搶答、抽籤、報名管理）
- 本機模擬模式的端對端測試：登入報名流程、搶答完整一場（含斷線、重新整理、表情、上下移動）、接力抽籤完整一輪（含通知、放回、重設、報名管理）
- `pnpm build` 通過

**尚未驗證**：以上都在本機模擬環境測試，還沒接上真的 Supabase。Google 登入、Realtime 即時同步、螢幕常亮、音效需要部署後用實機預演確認。

author: kvnloo
body:
Downstream implementation of hurttlocker/o8#2228.

Harness:
- process-level TCP recorder loaded in the o8 test process and inherited by Node worker children through `NODE_OPTIONS`
- records surface + host + port + count before connect
- blocks unexpected non-loopback destinations after recording them
- excludes machine-local o8 IPC while retaining the configured local-provider endpoint
- drives one real delegated packet: dispatch → worker work → Brain → telemetry-off assertion → review → merge
- worker and Brain both make real HTTP calls to the fixture `O8_LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL`
- writes/prints `o8/local-egress-report/v1` with per-surface counts
- classified in the integration lane

This PR intentionally does not fix leaks found by the harness; any non-local contact is emitted with the responsible surface and fails the final assertion.

The first CI execution is the baseline source; its printed `[local-egress-baseline]` report will be copied back into this PR unchanged.

author: snapotter-hq
body:
Closes #1731

SCIM Users PATCH answered 200 for operations it never applied. The worst case: `{"op": "Replace", "path": "Active", "value": "False"}` left the user active, because the route compared paths exactly and RFC 7643 2.1 makes attribute names case-insensitive. An op other than add, remove or replace was skipped the same way.

`normalizeUserOps` now does all of this before any operation applies, so the route can keep matching exact strings:

- A known path is matched case-insensitively, trimmed, and with any `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User:` prefix removed (RFC 7644 3.10). The route gets its canonical spelling.
- The known keys of a path-less value object are canonicalised too, so `{"Active": false}` deactivates like `{"active": false}`. One attribute under two spellings is a 400 `invalidSyntax`.
- An op other than add, remove or replace is a 400 `invalidSyntax`.
- A `remove` with no path is a 400 `noTarget` (RFC 7644 3.5.2.2). A `remove` of `userName`, which is required, or of `active` is a 400, rather than a 200 that changed nothing.
- `remove` on `emails[type eq "work"].value` clears the address, since add and replace already accept that path.
- A path-less `{"active": null}`, which the route read as a deactivation, is refused, as the path form already was.

Unknown paths (`title`, `name.givenName`, `phoneNumbers`) are still ignored, on purpose: IdPs send attributes SnapOtter keeps no column for on every sync, and refusing them would break provisioning. A test pins that.

Deactivations through a cased path or key now apply, so they also have to meet the last-active-admin check. Both shapes are rows in its existing table.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/api/scim-bodies.test.ts`: case-insensitive, trimmed and URN-prefixed paths; canonical value-object keys; the duplicate-key, null-active, remove and unknown-op refusals.
- `tests/integration/platform/scim.test.ts`: cased `Active` and path-less `{"Active": false}` deactivate; both are refused for the last admin; an unknown op after a valid one applies nothing; cased removes clear `externalId` and the work email; `remove` of `userName` and a path-less remove are refused; an unstored `title` path still answers 200.

## Verification

On the unfixed code, a cased `Active` path and an unknown op both answer 200 having applied nothing. The targeted pair (`scim.test.ts`, `scim-bodies.test.ts`, `external-auth-race.test.ts`, base `6dc10f59` vs this branch, same host) is valid on both sides with no new failures, 167/167 on the change. `pnpm typecheck` is clean. Details and the review findings are in the comment below.

Groups PATCH has the same case-sensitivity and unknown-op gaps. That's #1683, which I'm taking next.

author: floraispretty
body:
## Summary
Most of #146 already exists on `main`: the `/dashboard/messages` page, conversation list and thread, send, empty states, a Sidebar link and badge, and the fan inbox from #419. The one acceptance criterion that **didn't actually work** was **"Unread count badge shows in navigation"**. This PR fixes it.

## The bug
- **The badge counted the wrong data.** The Sidebar badge used `messageService.getTotalUnreadCount()`, which summed that module's *legacy* fan mocks. But the Messages page's **Fans tab renders `FanInbox`, backed by `fanMessagingService`** (#419), a separate localStorage store. Reading a fan thread never changed the badge, and the badge counted fans that don't appear in the inbox.
- **It never refreshed.** The count was read once on Sidebar mount.
- **Artists-tab threads were never marked read** when opened.
- **The mobile bottom nav (`MobileNav`) had no badge**, so small screens had no unread indicator at all.

## Fix (commit 1)
- **`getTotalUnreadCount()`** now counts the **fan inbox store** (`fanMessagingService.getUnreadTotal()`, muted threads excluded, matching the inbox) **plus Artists-tab unread**. The signature is unchanged, so existing callers and spies still work.
- **`services/inboxEvents.ts`** adds an `audioblocks:inbox-unread-changed` event and a `subscribeToInboxUnread()` helper, which also listens to `storage` so counts sync across tabs.
- **`fanMessagingService.persist()`**, the single write path, dispatches the event. The new **`messageService.markConversationRead()`** dispatches it only when the count actually changes.
- **Sidebar** subscribes and updates live.
- **MobileNav** shows the same badge on the Messages tab, capped at `99+`, with screen-reader text ("4 unread messages"). It starts at 0 until mounted, to avoid a hydration mismatch.
- **Messages page:** opening an Artists-tab conversation marks it read.

## Tests (commit 2)
- New `inboxUnreadBadge.test.tsx` (7 tests) covers:
  - event subscribe and unsubscribe, including `storage`;
  - reading a fan thread lowers the total and notifies;
  - reading an artist thread lowers the total and notifies exactly once, with no repeat for an already-read thread;
  - the MobileNav badge, its screen-reader text, the 0-hidden and `99+` cases, and live updates;
  - the Sidebar badge updating live instead of only on mount.
- `messageService.test.ts`: the unread test pinned the old semantics (legacy mocks). It's updated to fan-inbox plus artist.

## Verification
- `inboxUnreadBadge` + `messageService` + `Sidebar` tests: **19/19 pass**. `tsc` reports no errors in touched files, and `prettier` is clean.
- `eslint`: 0 errors. The 3 warnings are on existing lines in `Sidebar.tsx` and `messages/page.tsx`, and `main` has them too.
- **Pre-existing, unrelated:** `FanMessaging.test.tsx` fails 7/7 **with and without this PR** under Node 26. Its bare `localStorage.clear()` resolves to Node's own `localStorage` global, which is undefined without `--localstorage-file`, instead of jsdom's. The new test uses `window.localStorage` to avoid that.
Closes #146
Closes #191
Closes #111 
Closes #129

author: alicialeo
body:
## User-visible change

Adds an opt-in setting under Settings > Advanced: "Use system proxy for relay upstream connections".

When enabled, the local relay routes its upstream proxy connections through the OS-configured system HTTP proxy via HTTP CONNECT tunneling, instead of connecting directly. This helps when the upstream proxy only accepts connections from a specific egress — e.g. when running behind a VPN client's system-proxy mode without TUN.

## Design

- Disabled by default; existing behavior is completely unchanged unless the user opts in.
- System proxy detection: Windows registry (`ProxyEnable` / `ProxyServer` / `ProxyOverride`), falling back to `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` env vars. PAC configurations fall back to direct (no PAC parsing in v1).
- The chained CONNECT preserves bytes arriving after the response headers, uses a 10s timeout, and includes loop detection plus bypass-list support.
- Toggling the setting requires a restart (the launcher reads it once at construction).

## Test results

- `bun run typecheck`: clean
- `system-proxy.test.ts` + `proxy-relay.test.ts`: 16/17 pass (the 1 failure — "abandoned CONNECT closes its still-waiting upstream socket" — also fails on unmodified upstream main)
- Verified end-to-end on Windows 11: with the OS system proxy pointed at a VPN client and TUN disabled, proxy check through an upstream HTTP proxy that rejects direct connections succeeded; the full chain relay → system proxy → upstream works.
