author: andste82
body:
Part of #239: Go gets its complete per-language list and a collision test.

## What broke

`reservedGoMethod` had drifted from corelib-go's `sofab.Visitor` interface:
- it still listed the old `UnsignedArray`/`SignedArray`/`Float32Array`/`Float64Array`;
- it missed nine names a generated type really carries.

Each of those as a field breaks the package, and the generator exits 0. Checked with `main`'s generator plus `go vet`:

| field named | result on `main` |
|---|---|
| `Serialize` | `field and method with the same name Serialize` |
| `EncodeTo`, `FixlenBegin`, `StringCheck` | the field replaces the method/embedded type the generated code uses: `cannot convert 0 …` |
| `ArrayBegin`, `ArrayEnd`, … (all array callbacks) | the field hides the promoted `VisitorBase` method: `*M does not implement sofab.Visitor` |
| `SetStringCheck` | **compiles**, but hides the promoted method. The message is no longer a `StringPolicyVisitor`, so the decoder never hands it its UTF-8 policy, and `WithStrictUTF8(false)` is silently ignored |

## What changes

- **`generators/golang/reserved.go` holds the whole list:**
  - the full `sofab.Visitor` interface plus the embedded `VisitorBase`;
  - the embedded `StringCheck` and what it promotes;
  - `Serialize`/`Encode`/`EncodeTo`.
- The struct path (`goFieldName`) and the union path both read it. A union adds only `Which`/`Clear`/`MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON`. The union-only `unionFixed` is folded in.
- Go keywords need no entry, because every field is exported.
- **Name folding:** `exported()` turns `a_b` and `aB` into the same `AB`, and `encode_` lands on the mangled `encode`. Such a pair used to produce a duplicate Go field; it is now a generation error naming both fields.

## Tests

- **Collision test:** every listed name is used as a message field, a nested struct field and a union option. Both types carry a string, so `StringCheck` is live.
- The package must `go vet`, build, and round-trip every value under its schema name against corelib-go.
- A test for the folding error.
- The Go conformance harness already runs the backend's gated tests, so the collision test runs in `lang-go`.

## Docs

- `docs/generator/go.md`: a new "Field names" chapter; the union paragraph now points to it.
- ARCHITECTURE §8: a list names inherited members too; folded names are an error.

## Not in this PR

#239's "shrink first" for Go would move the visitor callbacks off the message, so that `String`, `Bytes`, `Signed`, … stop being reserved. This PR does not do it:
- corelib-go's `MessageSeq` requires every element type to be a `sofab.Visitor`, so it needs a corelib-go API change;
- messages would stop implementing `sofab.Visitor`, which is a public API change;
- a separate visitor value risks an allocation per nested sequence, so it needs a bench measurement first.

author: vibe-code-repo
body:
## English

### Purpose (C2 · kit format, board card k40)
A *kit* (Bausatz) is a reusable group of objects with its own anchor and rotation, e.g. a whole village. C2 adds only format, validation and resolution in `shared`. Nothing in server, client or admin reads the new field yet: server reconciliation (C4a), rectangle flattening (C4b), the converter (C3, #174, built on these types) and the editor (C5) follow separately. Per Mike (29.09.): the start village is not converted, NPC figures stay single placements, `village1` is only a test piece.

### Changes
- `shared/src/bausatz/types.ts`: kit file (`bausatzVersion` 1, `grundflaeche`, optional `ebnung`, `gruppen`, `teile[]` with a stable part `id`, `dx/dz`, optional `dy`, `yaw/pitch/roll`, `scale` number or triple, optional `einebnen`/`gruppe`), instance (`id`, `bausatz`, `x`, `z`, `yaw`, `kennungen` = part id → existing placement id), limits, and the rotation contract for C4a as a comment.
- `shared/src/bausatz/sanitize.ts`: `sanitizeBausatz(MitBericht)` with a named message for unknown versions, canonical `bausatzText`, instance sanitiser and the write-path error list (`bausatzInstanzenFehler`, 9 rules).
- `shared/src/bausatz/aufloesen.ts`: `loeseBausaetzeAuf(layout, katalog)` → `{teile, unbekannt, fehler}`; resolved id `<instance>#<partId>` or the `kennungen` address; right-handed rotation about +Y; every field read once; shared guard `rohKennungen()`: only plain objects (class tag `[object Object]`, realm-independent; null-prototype and frozen objects count) are read as `kennungen`; strings, arrays, null, primitives, boxed String/Number/Boolean and objects with a `Symbol.toStringTag` count as none. `kennungen` is read exactly once, in the resolver and in `pruefeLayout`.
- `shared/src/worldlayout/zahlen.ts` (new): the world sanitiser's `klemm`/`koordinate` moved verbatim; kits use the same rules as placements (positions rounded to mm, angles and scale not rounded).
- `WorldLayout.bausaetze` wired into `worldlayout/{types,sanitize,layoutDatei,pruefung,ops}.ts`: 422 in the write path (`LayoutBausaetzeUngueltig`, `LayoutZuVieleBausaetze`), the same checks in `ops.ts` `wende`, `pruefeLayout(layout, katalog?)` findings (unknown kit, unknown part prefab, no own model, orphaned `kennungen` summarised per instance as a hint), `bausaetze` op collection.
- Tests: `shared/test/bausatz-format.ts`, `bausatz-aufloesen.ts`, `bausatz-welt.ts` (new), `shared/test/welt-ops.ts` (random walk includes `bausaetze`), entries in `scripts/kern/shared.mjs`.

### Paths (ownership)
`shared/src/bausatz/*` (new), `shared/src/worldlayout/{types,sanitize,layoutDatei,pruefung,ops,zahlen}.ts`, `shared/src/index.ts` (exports), `shared/test/bausatz-*.ts` (new), `shared/test/welt-ops.ts`, `scripts/kern/shared.mjs` (new entries).

### Evidence
- New tests red on the base `ee3031b6` (modules missing) and on each fix round's predecessor; green on the head. Mutation tables in the builder report: every surviving mutant from all review rounds now turns a test red, except documented equivalent ones.
- Legacy: `server/data/welten/dev.json` through the write path is byte-identical to `ee3031b6` (sha `c1b2a933…`); `pruefeLayout` findings for documents without `bausaetze` are unchanged; 4000 random `wende` operations give the same sha before/after.
- Weg A (keeping ZDO addresses): for all 243 placements of `dev.json` as kit parts, position, yaw, scale and fingerprint 243/243 equal, `eintrag()` key 237/237 byte-identical (6 with route/npc cannot be parts); requires instance yaw 0.
- Limits: 256 instances × 4000 parts resolve with a message instead of capping; 256 × 4000 orphaned `kennungen` → 256 findings in ~140 ms.
- Local rule B runs: typecheck, lint (0 errors), build, all affected test files, `pruefe-runner-liste`. Full run: GitHub CI.
- Reviews (Opus 5.5 against the Sonnet 5.5 builder): attack → N1, follow-up attack → N2, check N2–N3 → N4, check N4 → N5, check N5 → N6, small check N6 → N7 (realm-independent guard, read-once test for `pruefeLayout`), small check N7 → comment-only step. The small checks of N6 and N7 ran on Sonnet 5.5 because the DeepSeek checker aborted (model-family exception, noted in the reports). Reports under `Berichte/2026-09-30 C2 Bausatzformat — *.md`.

### Deviations
- 9 instead of 8 write-path rules (instance yaw that is not a finite number is refused, like placements).
- `klemm`/`koordinate` moved to `worldlayout/zahlen.ts` (verbatim, shared with kits).
- `pruefeLayout` gained an optional second parameter (kit catalogue); without it nothing changes. No production caller passes it yet.
- Orphaned `kennungen` are a hint (`art: 'welt'`), not an error.
- Out of scope, backlog card k172: `pruefeLayout` is quadratic for very many identical prefabs (pre-existing).

## Deutsch

### Zweck (C2 · Bausatzformat, Board-Karte k40)
Ein *Bausatz* ist eine wiederverwendbare Gruppe von Objekten mit eigenem Anker und eigener Drehung, etwa ein ganzes Dorf. C2 legt nur Format, Prüfung und Auflösung in `shared` an. Server, Client und Betriebsdienst lesen das neue Feld noch nirgends: Server-Abgleich (C4a), Rechteck-Ebnung (C4b), der Konverter (C3, #174, baut auf diesen Typen) und der Editor (C5) folgen getrennt. Nach Mikes Vorgabe (29.09.): Das Startdorf wird nicht umgewandelt, NPC-Figuren bleiben Einzelplatzierungen, `village1` ist nur Prüfstück.

### Änderungen
- `shared/src/bausatz/types.ts`: Bausatz-Datei (`bausatzVersion` 1, `grundflaeche`, optional `ebnung`, `gruppen`, `teile[]` mit stabiler Teil-`id`, `dx/dz`, optional `dy`, `yaw/pitch/roll`, `scale` als Zahl oder Tripel, optional `einebnen`/`gruppe`), Instanz (`id`, `bausatz`, `x`, `z`, `yaw`, `kennungen` = Teil-id → vorhandene Platzierungs-id), Grenzen und der Drehvertrag für C4a als Kommentar.
- `shared/src/bausatz/sanitize.ts`: `sanitizeBausatz(MitBericht)` mit benannter Meldung bei unbekannter Version, kanonisches `bausatzText`, Instanz-Sanitizer und die Fehlerliste des Schreibwegs (`bausatzInstanzenFehler`, 9 Regeln).
- `shared/src/bausatz/aufloesen.ts`: `loeseBausaetzeAuf(layout, katalog)` → `{teile, unbekannt, fehler}`; aufgelöste id `<Instanz>#<TeilId>` oder die Adresse aus `kennungen`; rechtshändige Drehung um +Y; jedes Feld wird einmal gelesen; gemeinsamer Wächter `rohKennungen()`: Nur einfache Objekte (Klassenkennung `[object Object]`, unabhängig vom Realm; Objekte mit null-Prototyp und eingefrorene zählen) werden als `kennungen` gelesen; Strings, Arrays, null, Primitive, String/Number/Boolean-Objekte und Objekte mit `Symbol.toStringTag` gelten als keine. `kennungen` wird im Auflöser und in `pruefeLayout` genau einmal gelesen.
- `shared/src/worldlayout/zahlen.ts` (neu): `klemm`/`koordinate` des Welt-Sanitizers wörtlich verschoben; Bausätze nutzen dieselben Regeln wie Platzierungen (Position auf mm gerundet, Winkel und Skala ungerundet).
- `WorldLayout.bausaetze` eingebunden in `worldlayout/{types,sanitize,layoutDatei,pruefung,ops}.ts`: 422 im Schreibweg (`LayoutBausaetzeUngueltig`, `LayoutZuVieleBausaetze`), dieselben Prüfungen in `wende` (`ops.ts`), Befunde in `pruefeLayout(layout, katalog?)` (unbekannter Bausatz, unbekanntes Teil-Prefab, kein eigenes Modell, verwaiste `kennungen` je Instanz zusammengefasst als Hinweis), Vorgangs-Sammlung `bausaetze`.
- Tests: `shared/test/bausatz-format.ts`, `bausatz-aufloesen.ts`, `bausatz-welt.ts` (neu), `shared/test/welt-ops.ts` (Zufallslauf enthält `bausaetze`), Einträge in `scripts/kern/shared.mjs`.

### Pfade (Besitz)
`shared/src/bausatz/*` (neu), `shared/src/worldlayout/{types,sanitize,layoutDatei,pruefung,ops,zahlen}.ts`, `shared/src/index.ts` (Exporte), `shared/test/bausatz-*.ts` (neu), `shared/test/welt-ops.ts`, `scripts/kern/shared.mjs` (neue Einträge).

### Nachweis
- Neue Tests rot auf der Basis `ee3031b6` (Module fehlen) und auf dem Vorgänger jeder Nachbesserungsrunde; grün auf dem Kopf. Mutanten-Tabellen im Bauer-Bericht: Jede überlebende Mutante aus allen Prüfrunden macht jetzt einen Test rot, bis auf dokumentiert äq

author: bnjthub
body:
## Résumé
- « Mes sons » passe juste après « Entendu… » ; le meilleur son devient un lecteur mis en avant (grand bouton `ClipPlayButton` en `mainAction`, ligne plus grande).
- « Ici en ce moment » garde sa courbe compacte de 12 barres mensuelles à côté de la phrase. La phrase est maintenant calculée sur les 48 semaines du géomodèle (seuil de la liste Explorer) : « Arrive début mars · repart fin septembre. » pour un migrateur, « Présent toute l'année. » pour un sédentaire. Sans scores hebdomadaires, on retombe sur l'ancienne phrase par mois.
- « Fais sa connaissance » : le filigrane de l'icône de la carte de contenu passe en haut à droite, et plus aucun débordement à 200 % de texte (libellé du bouton qui rétrécit, titre et compteur empilés au-delà de 1,6×).
- Nidification : champ optionnel `nesting` (« M-N », mois 1 à 12) ajouté au générateur de fiches IA (`tools/fork_species_sheets.py`, schéma, prompt, bundle, valeur invalide non livrée) et lu côté app (`NestingPeriod`). Pas de bande sur cette fiche : la carte du monde (#129) l'affiche (« Niche d'avril à juillet »).

## À faire (Benjamin)
Régénérer le bundle avec la nidification (tâche dans `fork/PLAN.md`, J4b), sinon la carte du monde n'a rien à afficher.

## Tests
- `here_now_card_test.dart` : sans débordement à 320/360/412 dp et 100/130/200 %, tap, goldens clair/sombre (Windows).
- `meet_species_block_test.dart` : sans débordement aux mêmes tailles.
- Modèle (semaines vers arrivée/départ/toute l'année), parsing de `nesting`, ordre des blocs, test Python du générateur.

author: isamu
body:
## Summary

Corpus round 12 (Refs #170).

- **Japanese papers.** The `academic/paper` preset's Japanese limits had been set from one article. This round adds four J-STAGE articles under CC BY 4.0. All four are URL only (see Items to Confirm).
  - Three 保健医療科学 (2025) pages that have an HTML version: a review, an original study with a structured abstract, and a policy comparison. Each page has a Japanese and an English abstract and a bilingual reference list, which also makes it the mixed ja/en stress case.
  - One 自然言語処理 abstract page.
- **Genres the corpus had few documents for.** Every genre in the priority list now has at least three documents.
  - `legal/contract` (ja): the Japanese legal code of CC BY 4.0, and デジタル庁's copyright policy.
  - `legal/patent` (en): US 6,285,999 and US 4,683,202.
  - `docs/faq` (en): NPS Yellowstone FAQs, and the NOAA AOML hurricane FAQ (URL only).
  - `speech/address`: a Federal Reserve speech with its notes (en), and the 施政方針演説 of the 221st Diet (ja).
  - `literature/*` (en): Great Expectations (fiction), Leaves of Grass (poetry), A Modest Proposal (essay) and Riders to the Sea (play).
  - `blog/tech` (en): an 18F tutorial post.
- **Stress cases.**
  - Long single documents: Great Expectations, Leaves of Grass and the AOML FAQ.
  - Mixed ja/en: the 保健医療科学 pages.
  - Tables: the AOML FAQ.
  - Footnotes: the Fed speech.
- **Fix: 「．」 closes a Japanese sentence after a word.**
  - Papers and university pages write 「，．」 for 「、。」. The Japanese adapter joins fragments that do not close a sentence. It counted only 。！？!? as closing, so every sentence on a line ran into one: an abstract became one sentence for `max-sentence-length`, and `no-nakaguro-parallel` counted its middle dots together.
  - 「．」 now closes a sentence after kana, kanji, 「ー」 or a closing bracket.
  - After a digit, 「．」 is a number or a decimal point, so 「１．はじめに」 and 「３．５％」 read as before.
  - The rule is a new pure module, `packages/lang-ja/src/sentence-close.ts`. The spec, the lang-ja README and the site's languages guide (ja/en) are updated to match.

## Items to Confirm / Review

- **J-STAGE pages are URL only, as in round 10.** Each article states CC BY 4.0, and the manifest quotes that line. But the page also carries J-STAGE's own interface text, which the licence does not cover.
- **AOML hurricane FAQ is URL only.** It is public domain, but it names individual contact persons with their phone numbers.
- **Committed, with the basis quoted in the manifest:**
  - CC BY 4.0 legal code (ja): CC0, which the page itself states; the notices around it are CC website content under CC BY 4.0.
  - デジタル庁 copyright policy and the Kantei speech: PDL1.0.
  - US patents: public domain (same wording as the existing patent entry).
  - NPS and the Fed speech: public domain; the Fed's Website Policies are quoted.
  - The 18F post: CC0, from the repository's LICENSE.md. Its front matter names the author's slug, a GSA byline under that same dedication.
  - Gutenberg texts: public domain.
- **Moby-Dick and Dickinson were replaced (Codex finding).** Codex pointed out that Moby-Dick (#2701) kept a transcriber's note naming Project Gutenberg, and Dickinson (#12242) kept an "End of Project Gutenberg's …" line. They were replaced by Great Expectations (#1400) and Leaves of Grass (#1322). Both are clean, which Codex confirmed on a second pass. Gutenberg's converter does not strip that older footer line: see follow-up 7.
- **Only one existing corpus line moved, as intended:** `utelecon-account-leave` max-sentence-length 10 → 5. That page writes 「，．」, and each sentence it no longer reports was two or more sentences joined.
- **A side effect to check:** `max-kanji-continuous` rises on the rehabilitation review. The rule reports a long kanji run once per sentence, and a reference entry such as 「日本作業療法士協会．…．日本作業療法士協会五十年史」 is now several sentences. The runs it reports are real.
- **Pinned URLs.** Every new source is pinned to a Wayback `id_` snapshot, except the 18F post, which is pinned to a commit.

### Triage of the new documents (after the fix)

| Group | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Real | AOML: "an amazing documentaries", "a tropical islands" (`agreement-slip`), "ocean ocean", "the the" (`doubled-word`) | real slips on a NOAA page |
| Real | jnlp: a 149-character sentence (`(1)…(2)…(3)…を得る．`); long kanji compounds in the 施政方針演説 (「政府安全保障能力強化支援」) and in J-STAGE affiliations | style rules doing their job |
| Real by the rule, register | Kantei: 「不可欠です」 (`empty-intensifier`), 「に取り組みます。」 ×9 (`ngram-repetition`); Fed: "It is … / There is …" (`expletive-construction`) | speech register |
| Real by the rule, register | CC legal code: 「〜すること。」 list items in a です/ます text (`no-mixed-desumasu`) | the form of legal drafting; follow-up 6 |
| FP, fixed here | 「，．」 text read as one sentence: `max-sentence-length` and `no-nakaguro-parallel` on all four J-STAGE pages and on utelecon | the fix |
| FP, remaining | English inside a Japanese document is not split at ". ": a whole English abstract counts as one sentence | follow-up 1 |
| FP, remaining | Fed speech: a note number glued to the sentence end (`recessions.1 Over the …`) joins two sentences; the section headings came through as plain lines | follow-up 2 |
| FP, remaining | US 4,683,202: `undefined-acronym` on Roman numerals ("Vol. XLIII", "Reactions II-VI") and on "FIG"/"FIGS" (both patents); `dangling-reference` on "35 CFR §122" / "37 CFR §1.14" (other laws); `numbering-gap` on a list of concentrations ("1.5 mM …" then "0.25 mM …") | follow-ups 3–5 |
| FP, remaining | Kantei: each line of the speech is a paragraph, but lines are joined without a blank line, so `max-paragraph-length` counts a section. A parenthesised subheading line 「（エネルギー・資源安全保障）」 joins the next sentence, which moves a finding to the subheading's line | follow-up 6 |
| Pipeline artifact | J-STAGE interface text (ISSN, 「BIB TEX形式」, affiliations): the J-STAGE acronym work is in another agent's batch; CC legal code: spaces around link text (`stray-space`) | not fixed here |
| Miss | デジタル庁 copyright policy: its headings go 「1.1.」 → 「1.4」, and `numbering-gap` does not report it | follow-up 8 |
| Miss | 18F post: "So, we needing realistic data" is not reported | follow-up 9 |
| Misdetection | CLI language detection reads two of the bilingual 保健医療科学 pages as English (the corpus run uses the manifest's `ja`) | follow-up 1 |
| Crash / hang | none; the long novel and the long FAQ add little to `yarn corpus` | |

Gutenberg texts are clean, as the literature presets intend.

### Follow-ups (prioritised)

1. **Mixed ja/en:**
   - Split English sentences inside a Japanese document at ". " + a capital letter, keeping the 「Dr. 田中」 guard.
   - Have language detection weigh body text over reference lists.
2. **Converter:** turn footnote reference numbers (`<sup>`/`<a href="#fn">`) into Markdown footnotes or drop them, and keep the Fed's section headings as headings.
3. **`undefined-acronym`:** Roman numerals after "Vol.", "Reactions", "Table", and ranges like "II-VI"; "FIG"/"FIGS" in `legal/patent`.
4. **`dangling-reference`:** "§ N" after an outside code's name (CFR, U.S.C.) is an outside address.
5. **`numbering-gap`:** a decimal followed by a unit ("1.5 mM") is a quantity, not an item number.
6. **Japanese speeches and legal lists:**
   - Treat each line of a speech (line breaks without a blank line) as a paragraph in `speech/address`.
   - A parenthesised subheading line should not join the next sentence.
   - `no-mixed-desumasu` could skip 「〜こと。」 list items in legal text.
7. **`gutenberg-text.ts`:** strip the older "End of Project Gutenberg's …" footer line.
8. **`numbering-gap`:** heading numbers written "1.1." then "1.4".
9. **Miss:** "we needing" (a subject pronoun + a bare -ing verb).

### Sources skipped

- **J-STAGE journals that are not CC BY:** 日本森林学会誌 (CC BY-NC-ND), 情報管理 (© JST), 日本公衆衛生雑誌, 人工知能学会論文誌, 日本教育工学会論文誌, 化学と生物, 心理学研究. 保健医療科学 before 2025 is © only.
- **J-STAGE HTM

author: reinder83
body:
Fixes #605. Part of #498 (part 4d of #395, parent #387). #498 is split in two. This PR covers full transfers and profile shares. Progress-only backups are #606, because a migrated profile no longer carries the handbook they would need, and the options for that are on #606.

## What changes

- **`public/transfer.ts`: `importableTransfer(data, load)`** runs `validateTransfer`. It then converts every `original` profile with `migrateOriginalProfile` (from #495/#497), using the profile's own `handbook`, `recipes.json` and the catalog's `pureLimits`. Calculated profiles are left exactly as `validateTransfer` returns them, and so is an already migrated export. `load` is only called when the import holds an original profile. If a handbook can't be converted, the import is refused with 400 before anything is written (see #609).
- **Docker:** `POST /api/import-saves` (`server/save-routes.ts`) calls it with `migrationData()`. That function is now exported from `server/persistence.ts`, which uses it for its own migration too. This part of the change is a pure refactor.
- **Pages:** `createBrowserApi` takes the store's `loadMigration` as an optional fifth argument, and `importSaves` calls `importableTransfer` outside the transaction. `recipes.json` is only fetched for an import that has an original profile.
- `MigrationData` moves from `browser-store.ts` to `handbook-migration.ts`, and `browser-store.ts` re-exports it.

Until now an imported original profile was stored as it was. It was only migrated on the next server start, or on the next browser connection. It is now stored converted. The unconverted data stays recoverable, because the imported file is the user's own copy. Since nothing original is stored any more, an import no longer triggers the start-up migration. A restart then changes nothing and writes no `workspace.json.pre-handbook` (tested).

AGENTS.md's paragraph on full transfers could mention the conversion on import. I left AGENTS.md alone because #600 has it open.

## Acceptance (#605)

- [x] A first-release export (2026-09-13: state version 1, `plan: null`, own handbook; new fixture `tests/fixtures/export-2026-09-13.json`) imports as a calculated profile in both editions. Every record is kept or ends up in `handbookOrigin.unmapped`, and a test checks this independently of the converter.
- [x] A profile share of an original profile imports the same way, without bringing back progress.
- [x] An export whose own handbook differs from the frozen copy is converted with its own handbook (tested with a different version and a changed Phase 3 recipe).
- [x] Skipped-version import: a version 11 state with factory groups and step links keyed by factory ids is re-keyed, and the ids it can't place are kept for review.
- [x] Re-importing an already migrated export changes nothing: the result deep-equals `validateTransfer`'s, nothing is loaded, and the copy in each store is identical.
- [x] A failed import (a partial handbook, or a failed recipe fetch) changes nothing in either edition.

## Verification

- `npm test` (334 node + 457 Vitest), `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `node build.ts`, and `browser-check.ts` with Edge: all pass.
- I imported the fixture through the Backup page in Edge, in both editions (the Pages build, and a temporary Docker server with its own `DATA_DIR`). Both stored a calculated profile at state version 12 with no handbook, the plan opens at Phase 4, and neither logged a page error. The notes page lists what couldn't be placed:

Pages:
![Pages: unplaced records](https://github.com/reinder83/satisfactory-planner/blob/9fc4be28bd7d6a540e2e1ec3002e321ba1794e90/issue-498/pages-unplaced.png?raw=true)

Docker:
![Docker: unplaced records](https://github.com/reinder83/satisfactory-planner/blob/9fc4be28bd7d6a540e2e1ec3002e321ba1794e90/issue-498/docker-unplaced.png?raw=true)

## Filed while working on this

- #609: an original profile with a partial handbook, imported before this change, blocks the next start-up migration in both editions. This PR closes the way in, because such a file is now refused at import. A record that already holds one is still affected.

author: awne8886
body:
A **PRO** card at the top of the classic sidebar (and a "pro studio" pill when the sidebar is closed) switches the site to its other side. The switch plays an ASCII "curtain" wipe. The other side is an image **and video** effects studio laid out like [Ladybug](https://app.theladybug.app/), in this site's own palette: black, cream, cheese yellow, pepperoni red and basil green. The photo open in the classic view comes along as the first layer. **Classic** in the rail, the top bar or the logo goes back. The route is `#/pro`, and the studio loads lazily, so the classic site's bundle doesn't grow.

## What's in it
- **Layout like the reference:**
  - top bar: undo/redo, project name, Main tab, help, New, Export
  - left rail: Add, Layers, Templates, Classic
  - stage with aspect/fps chips, selection handles (move, scale, rotate) and zoom
  - floating dock: Look · Move · Sound · 3D · Track · Layer | Canvas. With the canvas selected it shows Look · Finish · Scene | Canvas.
  - right inspector
  - transport bar and an expandable timeline
  - welcome dialog, templates gallery, shortcuts (`?`)
- **Video in, video out.** You can drop or pick videos, pictures or the webcam. Every frame goes through the looks, live in the preview and again frame by frame on export.
- **59 looks in the reference's ten families** (`src/pro/effects/`), each one a fragment shader:
  - Library with search, live thumbnails, presets and *Surprise me*.
  - Stacks of looks per layer or for the whole canvas, each with a blend mode, strength and "appears in" (brights, darks, centre, edges or the tracked object).
  - Number settings can loop between two values (◇) or follow the video layers' loudness (♪).
  - Saved looks.
  - The classic site's colour ASCII is the *ASCII* look.
- **Object tracking (Track tab):**
  - Draw a box around something in a video or the sample clip. It is followed through the whole clip, forwards and backwards from that frame.
  - The tracker is a normalized-cross-correlation template tracker with a multi-scale search. It runs on frame-accurate decoded frames (`src/pro/tracking/`).
  - Other layers can **follow** the object, optionally scaling with it. *Label that follows* adds a tag that rides above it.
  - Looks can appear only on the tracked object.
  - The tracked box and its confidence are drawn on the stage.
- **Layers:** pictures, videos, webcam, type, shapes and an animated sample clip.
  - Fit modes, placement, 12 blend modes and 3D tilt.
  - 12 motion presets that always loop seamlessly.
  - Clips can be moved and trimmed on the timeline.
- **Finish:** bloom, streaks and trails per layer or for the canvas; paper grain and a colour grade for the canvas.
- **Export:**
  - MP4 or WebM, encoded with WebCodecs through [Mediabunny](https://mediabunny.dev/) (MPL-2.0, lazy-loaded), with the unmuted video layers' sound mixed in.
  - A PNG of the current frame, or a PNG sequence as a ZIP.
  - Sizes from 720 px to 4K, with optional motion blur.
  - Browsers without WebCodecs fall back to a real-time MediaRecorder capture.
- **Other:** undo/redo, keyboard shortcuts, 12 templates, and autosave (`localStorage` + IndexedDB). Nothing leaves the device.

## How it's built
- `gl/renderer.ts` is a WebGL2 compositor.
  - Each layer's looks run at the size the layer covers, ping-ponging between mipmapped targets.
  - Each layer is then placed with a projective transform plus any follow shift (`geometry.placedQuad`) and blended onto the canvas.
  - Canvas looks, finish, grade and paper follow.
- The same renderer draws the preview and the export.
- `#/pro-sheet` (dev only) renders every look and preset and lists shader compile errors. It currently reports 0.

## Not replicated
Ladybug's **3D scenes and 3D models**, **components**, **vector SVG export**, and its account / Go Pro features. The 3D tab here offers tilt and 3D motions only.

## Testing
- `npm run check` passes: lint, format, typecheck, and 50 unit tests. The tests cover:
  - geometry, homography and follow shift
  - motion looping, modulation and media timing
  - the tracker, on a synthetic moving, brightening object
  - track interpolation
  - the ZIP writer and timecode
  - a registry check of every look's params and presets
- `npm run build` passes.
- Checked in headless Chromium (SwiftShader):
  - classic → curtain → PRO
  - video upload and playback
  - applying and stacking looks; the panels and templates
  - autosave restore after a reload; undo/redo
  - phone, 1024 px and desktop layouts
- **Tracking:** tested on a 30 fps clip of a moving ball. The track matched the true position to about 0.002 of the frame at every time checked, with confidence ≥ 0.93 throughout. The following label stayed on the ball, and a look limited to the tracked object stayed inside the box.
- **Exports** were decoded back to check them:
  - WebM: VP9 + Opus with a real picture
  - MP4: VP9-in-MP4, because this Chromium build has no H.264 encoder; Chrome picks H.264
  - PNG and the PNG-sequence ZIP: valid
- Only software GL was available here, so real-GPU performance is untested.

author: maxke24
body:
Closes #487.

The phone spin showed `e.message` for any failure, so network and parser errors reached the rider as raw text (URLs, parser internals). Spin's own dead ends are now a `SpinFailure` type that keeps its sentence. Everything else goes through `failureText("Spin", e)`.

## Before / after

Unit-tested in `ServersSyncStateTest` and `LoopSpinTest`.

| failure | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `IOException("Unable to resolve host photon.komoot.io")` | raw text | `Spin failed: it could not be opened. Check your connection and try again.` |
| `IllegalArgumentException("Unexpected JSON token at offset 41")` | raw text | `Spin failed: the contents were not what this app expected.` |
| "Not enough roads for a round trip — try a larger radius" | shown as-is | shown as-is (`SpinFailure`) |
| loop warning, roll threw HTTP 503 | `Server route failed (HTTP 503) — approximate loop instead` | `Server route failed: the server hit a problem. Try again later. Showing an approximate loop instead.` |
| fallback timeout after HTTP 503 | `Server route failed (HTTP 503); fallback timed out too` | `Server route failed: the server hit a problem. Try again later. The fallback timed out too.` |

## What changed

1. `SpinFailure : IOException` (`SpinPicker.kt`). Every curated spin throw now uses it: the LoopSpin fallback timeout, RoundTripPlanner "Not enough roads", RoadRoulette "No roads found within radius", PoiRoulette's two misses, and the `collectRolls` fallback. It is still an `IOException`, so every catch that moves on to the next server or sector behaves the same.
2. `spinFailureText(e)` sits next to `fileFailureText` and follows the same pattern. `SpinRun` uses it in place of `e.message`.
3. `failureText`'s reason table moved to `data/Http.kt` as `failureReason`. `failureText` now just prepends `"$action failed: "`. The move lets `LoopSpin` word the server error it embeds (`loopFailureReason`, the roll-level catch), because data/ may not import presentation/ (architecture.md §3).
4. versionName 3.6.5 → 3.6.6.

## Known limits

- When a loop roll fails with a GraphHopper 400 (`NoRouteException`), the warning now says "no road connects those points. Try moving them." A round trip has no points to move. It is mapped, but the advice is wrong.
- Not run on a device. The change is string mapping only and is covered by unit tests.
- PR #480 also sets versionName 3.6.6. Whichever of the two lands second needs to re-bump.

## Follow-ups

- #481: car `SpinScreen` and the other raw-text sites. It can now call `spinFailureText`.
- iOS `SpinModel.swift` still shows `error.localizedDescription`. It can adopt `spinFailureText`, but that needs an iOS build.

body:
Step 1 of #19: the reference and the output.

The reference is now `bin/cowsay` of `test/submodules/cowsay-org-cowsay` (tag `v3.8.4`), and `test/reference/` is gone.
The suite runs it with `COWSAY_ONLY_COWPATH=1`, so that it reads `COWPATH` alone, as this build does until step 2.

## Output

| | cowsay 3.03 | cowsay 3.8.4, and now this build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| balloon top and bottom lines | `" _____ "` | `" _____"` |
| empty message | `" _ "`, `"<   >"`, `" - "` | `" __"`, `"<  >"`, `" --"` |
| `-h` | usage on stderr, exit 255 (64 here) | help on stdout, exit 0 |
| `-n` with a message | usage on stderr, exit 255 (64 here) | help on stdout, exit 1 |
| missing cowfile | `Could not find nosuch cowfile!` | `Could not find cowfile for 'nosuch'!` |
| missing path with `/` | balloon without a cow, exit 0 (an intended fix here) | the same error, exit 2 |
| `-l`, stdout no terminal | `Cow files in DIR:`, names wrapped | names alone, one per line |
| `-l`, a directory it cannot read | dies | skipped, as is one without a cowfile |

`cows/` now holds the cowfiles of 3.8.4 beside `clawd`: `actually`, `alpaca`, `cupcake`, `fox`, `llama`, `mech-and-cow` and `sus` come in, `kiss` changes, and `satanic`, `sodomized` and `telebears` go.
The cowsay-org cases in the `submodules` section, and cowsay-org in `make check-third-party-cows`, go too, since `cows/` now covers those cowfiles.

## Intended fixes

- Gone: the missing path, which 3.8.4 fixes, and exit code 64, which nothing uses now.
- Changed: the help names this build (`cowsay version 3.8.4 (cowsay.wasm 0.2.0)`) and leaves out `-r` and `-C`, which this build does not have yet.
- Kept: `-W` below 2, `cowsay 0`, `-e 0`, ANSI escapes, and the `Wide character` warning; 3.8.4 keeps those bugs.

`--help`, `--version`, `-r`, `-C`, and subdirectories of a cowpath directory are outside the specification; `test/README.md` lists them.

## Snapshots

The snapshots under `test/fixed/` and `test/width/` change only in the trailing spaces of the balloon lines; the help snapshots are new.
`docs/clawd.svg` is regenerated.

## Checks

- `make check-native` and `make check-wasm` pass, 866 cases each, against 3.8.4 now; `make check-third-party-cows` and `make lint` pass.
- `-l` on a terminal matches the reference through a pty, directories left out included; the suite does not cover it, since it needs a terminal.
- `cowsay.wasm` is 95479 bytes, 6 kB more: the new cowfiles add 5 kB (`cupcake` alone 2.9 kB), and the help 1 kB.

author: randomm
body:
Closes #316

## Summary

Brief polish from QA 2026-09-29: two changes, both verified against the
operator decisions (binding) from the issue's gap resolution.

### De-dup: one row per agreeing axis

`state_block_for_version` (d33d/design_state.py) now collapses a param
row into its axis row when the param's value agrees with the axis's
measured extent within `max(BBOX_TOLERANCE_REL * extent,
BBOX_TOLERANCE_MIN_MM)`. The axis row keeps `kind: "axis"` and its name,
takes the param's label if present, and carries the param's current
provenance. Disagreeing params, params with no axis row, and
non-numeric params keep their rows.

The QA box (params W/D/H 40/40/12, bbox 40×40×12) now renders
Width/Depth/Height once each — the six-row repetition QA quoted is gone.

### history_missing flag + existing banner

`GET /api/projects/{id}/design-state` returns
`{"entries": [...], "history_missing": bool}` (envelope, not bare array).
`history_missing` reuses `_storage_field`'s `Path(git_repo_path).is_dir()`
predicate via the shared `repo_present` helper. The Brief's existing
`brief-saved-missing` banner fires when `history_missing === true` OR
`storage.repo_present === false`, rendered once. No new copy key.

### Envelope migration

api.ts `getDesignState` returns `DesignStateEnvelope` (not bare array).
App.tsx threads `historyMissing` to the Brief. All consumers updated.

## Test map

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|

body:
<!-- PR title must start with: [BugFix] [Enhancement] [Feature] [Refactor] [UT] [Doc] [Tool] [Others] -->

## Why

Dosi 0.1.12 (osi-engine #222) changed how a metric query filters. `where_sql` is now split by top-level `AND` conjunct: a condition on a selected metric filters the **result** rows (the HAVING that used to be refused), and in a window query a condition on group-by fields only also filters the result, so the kept rows keep the ranks and partition counts of the whole population. The new `context_filter` always filters the **input** rows and is the explicit way to rank within a subset.

Datus-agent pins `dosi-engine==0.1.12` since #1475 but exposed none of this: `query_metrics` had no way to scope the calculation population, the agent could not use HAVING, and a tenant scope written into `where` by a metric row policy now lands *after* ranking in a window query, so rank and partition count would still reflect every tenant's rows.

`time_ranges` (multi-window queries) was prototyped alongside this and deliberately left out; the design is captured in #1480.

## Solution

- **Runtime and tool**: `DosiRuntime.query_metrics` / `_build_query` and the `query_metrics` tool accept `context_filter` and put it on the engine query dict (the binding deserializes it directly; no engine change). The tool docstring and the `ask_metrics` prompt explain `where` versus `context_filter` (only window metrics tell them apart), the HAVING form, and how to act on the two new refusals.
- **Error mapping**: `result_filter_metric_not_selected` gets a structured `suggested_retry` that adds the missing metric to `metrics` (the engine only gives a text hint).
- **Explorer**: `MetricPreviewInput.context_filter`; `_narrow_by_metric_policy` hands both filters to the metric row policy transformer and reads both back, so a policy can scope the population through `context_filter`. The managed policy in Datus-backend still writes to `where` and needs a follow-up PR there.
- **Docs**: `metrics.md` / `.zh.md` parameter table; release notes list the feature and, under Upgrade Notes, the `where` behaviour change of Dosi 0.1.12.

Tradeoff: `where`'s new placement rules are the engine's contract, not something the agent re-implements; the tool layer only documents them and forwards the two filters as written.

## Test Cases

- **Acceptance (new, real engine + DuckDB)** `tests/integration/tools/test_dosi_query_filters.py` on the new fixture `tests/data/semantic_models/window_filters/` (a rank window metric and its partition count, mirroring the engine's `datus_window` corpus): the same predicate in `where` keeps the whole population's rank and N while `context_filter` rescopes to 1/1; `where` on a selected metric filters result rows; an unselected metric is refused with a `suggested_retry` that is then run successfully. Added to the PR acceptance list in `ci/run-pr-tests.py`.
- **Unit**: `test_dosi_runtime.py` (context_filter reaches the query dict only when set; structured retry for `result_filter_metric_not_selected`), `test_semantic_tools.py` (`TestQueryMetricsContextFilter`: pass-through, null-like values omitted, schema exposure), `test_explorer_service.py` (policy transformer receives and returns `context_filter` alongside `where`).
- Local: `ruff format/check` clean; `ci/run-pr-tests.py datus/main` 645 passed, 0 failed; `ci/audit_tests.py` P0=0 P1=0 on the changed test files; diff coverage of the changed lines with the mirrored unit tests plus the acceptance suite is 100%.

author: muhden
body:
Adds a skill that loads a documentation corpus into xmemory, starting from the questions it should answer. The docs go into new instances whose schema the agent writes from the questions and the XMD guide, or into an instance the user already has, after its schema is checked against the questions and extended only through a dry-run and the user's approval. The agent settles the scope, pilots a few sections for real and shows what each stored and overwrote, then writes the rest and reads the questions back. There are approval gates before creating instances or writing the pilot, before the bulk write, and before any schema change.

The bulk work runs in a bundled script, `skills/ingest-docs/scripts/ingest.py`, so the corpus never enters the agent's context. Markdown sources need only Python 3.9+; HTML pages are parsed by BeautifulSoup and lxml and rendered by markdownify, declared in the script and locked with hashes in `ingest.py.lock`, which `uv run` installs on first use. It reads a site root, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, a sitemap, page URLs or a folder of Markdown or HTML. Every chunk carries its page, section and source URL, and chunk boundaries stay put when a section changes, so an edit rewrites only its own chunk. A write log makes reruns skip what already landed and resume writes still in flight; a write that may already have landed is never sent twice on its own, and an exhausted quota stops the run cleanly. All calls go through xmemcli 1.5.1 or newer.

Tested end to end against a live instance, including a rerun that wrote nothing and a one-section edit that rewrote exactly one chunk. The script's own tests run offline: `uv run skills/ingest-docs/scripts/test_ingest.py`.

author: rajeshgoli
body:
Typing feedback in a document's review sheet inside the web Inbox closed the document: the first `e` ran Inbox **Done** (marking the item done and closing the panel), `f` went full screen, and Esc could close the panel.

Cause: the review sheet (`sm-doc-ui`) lives in a shadow root. A `keydown` listener on the document sees its textarea retargeted to the shadow host, so `e.target.closest('input,textarea,…')` missed and the shortcut fired.

Fix: one `typingIn(event)` helper in `ui.js` that reads `event.composedPath()[0]`, used by the reader (`e`, `f`), Inbox (`e`) and shell (Esc, `g` chords) shortcuts.

author: colochampre
body:
## What

This is the third and last slice of PR 10, unit 7s-scope (tasks 7s.1-7s.3). The Overview is scoped to one exchange at a time. PR 10 is complete with it.

### Exchange scope (`shared/scope/exchange-store.ts`)

- **Options.** The options are the distinct `exchange` values from `GET /api/pools`, in first-seen order. Disabled pools are included, so an exchange whose key was deleted stays visible (decision 22). The first option is the default.
- **Validation.** The pools body is validated row by row. A malformed body is an error, and never reads as "no exchanges".
- **Persistence.** A Zustand store persists the selection under `sm.exchange` through `safe-storage`. The stored value is only a preference: it is resolved against the live pool list, and a stale, wrongly typed or corrupt value falls back to the first option. A blocked or throwing storage never breaks the page.

### `ExchangeTabs`

- **Where it shows.** In `TopBar`, on scoped routes only: `/`, `/strategies`, `/strategies/:id`. `/settings` and the not-found page show no tabs and make no `/pools` request. Nothing is requested while the token gate is locked.
- **Layout.** From `lg` the tabs sit inline. On narrow screens they are their own horizontally scrolling row below the bar. The 10b contract still holds: no page-level scroll when the content fits.

### Bookings filtered by exchange (decision 3)

- `BookingsListView` in the Overview's decision rail takes the selected exchange and filters client-side on `proposal.exchange === exchange`: exact match, no prefix. `BookingProposal` already carries `exchange`, the same identifier `/pools` reports.
- **Pools loading or failing.** The tabs show a neutral "Loading exchanges" or a loss-coloured "Exchanges could not be loaded". The rail shows a message **instead of** bookings, and it does the same when no exchange is configured. It never falls back to unfiltered rows, because that would put an approve button on another exchange's proposal under a tab that claims a filter. The cost: while `/pools` is down, pending bookings are hidden.

### Deferred, and recorded in tasks.md

- **10c.4 (PR 13).** The read-only and no-key marks on the tabs (decisions 18 and 20). They need the `['credentials']` query that the Settings unit introduces.
- **7p.1 and 7p.2.** Owner polish: capitalised exchange display names, and brand-coloured tab text. 7p.2 carries an open question, because all three brand colours are amber/orange, the colour the design reserves for "needs your decision".
- The strategy detail page setting the scope goes to PR 12. The rail's amber pending count goes to PR 11.

## Checks

- `npm run lint`: exit 0.
- `npm test`: exit 0, 153 tests (65 new).
- `npm run build`: exit 0.
- Every new test failed first on an assertion, against stubs. Mutations seen red, among 19:
  - options not deduplicated;
  - the default not first;
  - the storage key changed;
  - a stale persisted value kept;
  - the filter removed, or matching by prefix;
  - tabs shown on `/settings`;
  - a pools failure or loading state showing unfiltered bookings;
  - a malformed pools body accepted;
  - raw `localStorage` instead of `safe-storage`.
- Owner review (local): one tab per exchange, and switching changes the rail; the choice survives a reload; no tabs on `/settings` or `/nope`; the narrow row scrolls sideways with no page scroll; a pools failure shows the message and never bookings.

## Deploy

Frontend only. It is not served while `PANEL_DIST_DIR` is unset, so the deploy is a pull as the `strategy` user, with no restart.

body: Linear: [COG-1141](https://linear.app/cog-gtm/issue/COG-1141/w0-testcontainers-mysql-harness-for-springboottest-boot-154-java-8) ## Summary This is the canonical Testcontainers MySQL harness: with it, `mvn verify` runs with only Docker and no local MySQL. Boot stays on 1.5.4 and Java on 8. - New `com.userFront.AbstractIntegrationTest`, with javadoc marking it as the entry point for the smoke suite: ```java @RunWith(SpringRunner.class) @SpringBootTest(classes = UserFrontApplication.class) @AutoConfigureMockMvc @ContextConfiguration(initializers = AbstractIntegrationTest.DataSourceInitializer.class) public abstract class AbstractIntegrationTest { protected static final MySQLContainer MYSQL = new MySQLContainer<>("mysql:5.7.44") .withDatabaseName("onlinebanking").withUrlParam("useSSL", "false"); // started once per JVM @Autowired protected MockMvc mockMvc; // DataSourceInitializer -> spring.datasource.{url,username,password,driver-class-name} from MYSQL, // spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update } ``` - `UserFrontApplicationTests` now simply `extends AbstractIntegrationTest`. - This class is a **superset of the ad-hoc copies in #106, #108 and #109**. It keeps the same class name and package, `@AutoConfigureMockMvc`, the inherited `protected MockMvc mockMvc`, and `spring-security-test` on the test classpath. Those PRs can rebase by deleting their own `AbstractIntegrationTest` and pom entries. - The initializer overrides every `spring.datasource.*` property, so it also satisfies COG-1158 (#333) `spring.datasource.password=${DB_PASSWORD}` and its fail-fast check. ### Non-obvious choices - **Image is `mysql:5.7.44`, not the ticket's 8.0 default.** The Boot 1.5 BOM ships Connector/J 5.1.42, which fails against MySQL 8 (`Unknown system variable 'query_cache_size'`) and cannot do `caching_sha2_password`. Move to 8.0 together with the W3 Connector/J bump (COG-1148 owns the version decision). This PR does not touch runtime dependencies. You can override the image without a code change: `-Dtest.mysql.image=...`. - **`useSSL=false`** is appended to the JDBC URL. Current Temurin 8 builds disable TLSv1/1.1, and that is what Connector/J 5.1 negotiates. - **Docker API version**: the docker-java shaded into Testcontainers 1.19.x defaults to API 1.32, which Docker Engine 25+ rejects (`client version 1.32 is too old`). When neither `api.version` nor `DOCKER_API_VERSION` is set, the base class sets `api.version = min(1.44, daemon max)`. The daemon max comes from `docker [--context default] version --format {{.Server.APIVersion}}`. `--context default` is only added when `DOCKER_HOST` is unset, so the CLI queries the same endpoint Testcontainers uses. If there is no CLI, it falls back to 1.44. Docker 24 (API 1.43) keeps working. - **`org.testcontainers:junit` does not exist** on Maven Central (404). JUnit 4 support ships in the core `org.testcontainers:testcontainers` artifact, so that is what the pom declares, with an explicit `1.19.7` like `org.testcontainers:mysql`. ## Verification (Temurin 8u504, Docker only, nothing listening on :3306) ``` $ mvn -B -f UserFront/pom.xml clean verify INFO tc.mysql:5.7.44 - Container mysql:5.7.44 started in PT6.707S INFO tc.mysql:5.7.44 - Container is started (JDBC URL: jdbc:mysql://localhost:32787/onlinebanking?useSSL=false) Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 - in com.userFront.UserFrontApplicationTests [INFO] BUILD SUCCESS ``` - **With COG-1149's CI workflow (#329) and COG-1158 (#333)** merged on top locally, the same command gives `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0`, BUILD SUCCESS. The GitHub Actions run of #329's Temurin 8 workflow is on the throwaway draft #342, which will be closed and not merged. - **Docker 24** was simulated with a fake `docker` CLI that prints 1.43: every request went to `GET /v1.43/...` and the build passed. **Sibling compatibility check:** I copied the smoke tests from #106 (`MoneyMovementSmokeTest`), #108 (`AppointmentSmokeTest`) and #109 (`AuthSmokeTest`) unchanged onto this branch, without their `AbstractIntegrationTest` copies. All three compile against this harness. ``` Tests run: 9, Failures: 0 - MoneyMovementSmokeTest Tests run: 4, Failures: 0 - AppointmentSmokeTest Tests run: 1, Failures: 0 - UserFrontApplicationTests Tests run: 5, Failures: 5 - AuthSmokeTest <- only when run in the same JVM as AppointmentSmokeTest $ mvn verify -Dtest=AuthSmokeTest -> Tests run: 5, Failures: 0 ``` The `AuthSmokeTest` failures come from test data, not the harness. All classes share one container and one cached context. #108 commits a user `smokeuser`, and #109 then tries to sign up the same username. `/signup` returns 200 ("user exists") where the test expects a redirect. One of those PRs needs to use unique usernames when it rebases. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4e949844d05d4a1a92421b67076d0628 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/4e949844d05d4a1a92421b67076d0628?variant=devin Requested by: @patrickbradley-cog --- #### Devin Review | Status | Commit | |---|---| | ⚪ Not started | — | > [Run Devin Review](https://staging.itsdev.in/review/cog-gtm/online-banking-with-java-spring-boot-angular-2/pull/335?analyze=true) ---

## Summary
Adds a complete research article: **A Feature-Optimized Explainable Ensemble Machine Learning Framework for Early Detection and Risk Stratification of Chronic Kidney Disease.**

## Deliverables
- `CKD_Explainable_Ensemble_ML_Manuscript.docx` — Word document with **12 figures embedded inline as JPG** at their in-text positions.
- `CKD_Manuscript.md` — source manuscript (~10,600 words) following the full requested 13-section layout + abstract + references.
- `ckd_figures/` — the 12 generated JPG figures.
- Pure-standard-library toolchain (no PIL/numpy/matplotlib): `jpeg_encoder.py` (baseline JPEG encoder), `generate_ckd_figures.py`, `create_ckd_docx.py`.

## Compliance with requirements
- **~10,000 words**: ~10,600 words total.
- **12 figures**: embedded as JPG, referenced in strict serial order (Figure 1 → 12), each cited 2–4 times.
- **6 tables**: each cited 2–4 times in strict serial order (Table 1 → 6).
- **43 references**: all cited throughout in strict serial first-appearance order (1 → 43).
- Deep analysis with comparison to prior literature (Related Work + Tables 1 and 6 + Discussion).

## Content coverage
Introduction, Related Work, Materials & Methods, Feature Optimization (MI/RFE/importance/correlation), 9 ML models, hyperparameter optimization, soft-voting + stacking ensemble, 11-metric evaluation, SHAP explainability, risk stratification, results & discussion, limitations, and conclusion.

body:
# Native request wait ownership

Owner: Arendt. Parent retains public activation. Base: 29bbe95d.

This continuation owns the installed native request journey from dispatch through
transport acceptance, first and later stream events, awaited native callbacks,
journal append and ACP publication. Historical 129.898-second evidence cannot
allocate the wait to the provider: it includes awaited local callbacks and lacks
dispatch, header and first-delta timestamps.

Mendel remains sole writer of PR453 native provider adapters and budget policy.
Request extensions there rather than implementing another adapter. Preserve the
existing diagnostic and NativePhase owners, original request/input/turn and owner
incarnation, accepted-stream no-replay semantics and valid unbounded model work.

Acceptance: controlled localhost provider delay versus blocked local publication
through the actual native/ACP path. If necessary, one short configured Sol/Off
call in an owned private fork with representative original history; no public
input, paid alternate model, parent settings changes or historical UNKNOWN replay.
Provider capacity is reported only when the transport supplies that evidence.

No new lifecycle store, retry owner, status mirror, timer or certificate cache.
Source and installed results will be recorded at their actual strength here.

## Concrete local publication defect and checkpoint

The original `SocketClient.session_update` awaited an observer's `drain()`.
The owner broadcast awaited each observer serially. Installed baseline05 proved
that one real non-reading Unix subscriber held an ACP publication for 1.029s
and an awaited native callback for 2.564s although the controlled provider wrote
its complete response in 15ms. This does not attribute the historical 129s.

The existing SocketClient now owns all its output handoffs: updates, permission
requests, result/ready records and error envelopes. It writes into the original
asyncio transport, yields to readers, and retires only that socket if its buffered
bytes exceed the transport's high-water budget. It retains the configured high
and low watermarks, reserving at least one burst from the actual kernel send
buffer. Kernel and transport overrides remain the resource owners. One
original saved snapshot's record size establishes the minimum byte budget for
that record. There is no second queue, whole-turn timer, copied transcript,
input disposition, or retry authority. Existing disconnection denies pending
permission futures and does not cancel the original turn.

Installed07 passed through actual Toad input clicks, ACP, worker and native Pi:
two originals, two localhost requests, both replies painted; a non-reading
observer retired while the controller, another fast observer and a temporarily
busy observer retained their attachments. Fresh recovery read the 392391-byte
canonical snapshot and matched its original content/frontier identity. Recovery
did not send another input. [Sanitized receipt](../../evidence/native-request-wait/installed07.json).
The final check below tightens this to a50ms pause after actual streamed text,
keeping the non-reading observer unread through native completion.

Run06 is a retained failed attempt: its premature complete flag is not acceptance.
The first watermark correction retired a healthy fresh reader of one large saved
snapshot; this caused the original-record byte-budget correction. All private
failed traces, journals and proofs are retained. Fixture daemon teardown was
also corrected to use the existing exact test-owner lifecycle; idle05/06/07
daemons were stopped through OwnerLifecycle after recording the receipt.

Thirteen focused phase, subscription and unsent-attachment controls pass. Native
request timing is attached to the original native ProcessIdentity and exact
turn/owner fence. Python append clocks are named recorded times, not ingress
times. Completed publication counters describe preceding completed operations;
they cannot be subtracted from native clocks without an original clock bracket.
Optional diagnostic I/O failure reports a warning and cannot change admission.

## Ready combined checkpoint

Mendel's adapter contribution `45521172` is normally integrated with merged453
`a4df9589`. Ten native stream adapters expose actual dispatch, available HTTP
headers, first raw parsed event and original iterator release through the same
request observation helper. Google SDK raw headers are unavailable; WebSocket
connection is not HTTP headers. Original retry attempts come from
`maxRetries - retriesRemaining`, with the original delay decision observed before
its existing abortable wait. No second counter or retry policy. Stream closure,
including cancellation/failure, does not assert successful commit.

Installed10 exits0 through actual Toad/ACP/worker/native:

- Two accepted originals and two provider POSTs; both replies visibly painted.
- Controller and fast reader retain the reply; a legitimate reader paused50ms
  after first streamed text retains its attachment and reply data.
- One observer never reads until native completion. Native settles, and only
  that observer is retired when its resource budget is exhausted.
- Both original input dispositions remain `started`; no UNKNOWN reconstruction.
- Fresh recovery reads the619196-byte canonical saved snapshot, matching its
  source/frontier content identity. Recovery sends no original again.
- Native dispatch→headers measures2023.30ms for the deliberately delayed provider;
  headers→raw event→consumed delta ordering has the same original native process
  and request/input/turn fence.
- Normal shutdown retires fixture children; bounded readonly census finds no
  remaining454 fixture processes. Zero paid/public calls.

[Authoritative sanitized receipt](../../evidence/native-request-wait/installed10.json).
Private `/home/ts/wt/aw454-10/receipt.json`, frames, journal, proof and diagnostics
remain retained. Failed08 caught false retirement of a genuinely busy reader;
the kernel burst allowance closes it. Failed09 resumed the observer before
publication finished and is not acceptance. Failed originals are preserved.

The original normal stock recipe passes zero-fuzz patches, exact pins and full
tree verification: selector `593b978a717ae8f6`, tree
`b7b2dc5693227740a91a09ac9aa9189519ca084e8fd9dfc71a9698aa65d76eda`.
Observation/adapters run after session-storage assembly, closing the constructor
crossing. Locked import-boundary preparation uses an owned npm cache; no global
package/source/default changes. The normal private Core wheel has no source
fallback; unchanged Toadb200/Text2e49/SDK0.12.1,68 compatible packages. Parent
owns final current-Toad pin/stage, affected entrypoint review and quiet cutover.

Historical129.898s stays unattributed. Ordinary requests now retain transport and
callback coordinates; direct compaction summaries keep their separate operation
and progress owner. Callback wall time is not CPU. Bedrock internal SDK socket
retries remain SDK-owned and unobserved.

`ModelWaitPhase.source` changes the live phase publication ABI. Release requires
matched owners and clients through the canonical idle batch; durable formats,
native journals, reservations, UNKNOWN receipts and original proof stores are
unchanged. Parent owns that cutover. Ready for review/merge, not publicly installed.

## Decisions

- Resolution home — put the new `resolveRoleFile` in `roles/plan.ts` (the I/O boundary that already hosts the loop's `resolveRoleDoctrineText`), not in `roles/resolver.ts`, which is deliberately pure (no `fs`, no config). The command and the review loop now share the exact same `buildRolePlan` → `resolveRoles` resolution, which is what makes `O3` hold by construction. Alternative considered: a synchronous resolver in `doctrine.ts` doing its own file reads to keep the command sync — rejected, because a second read/validate path could drift from the loop's and silently break the "same text" guarantee.
- Command is async now — `doctrineCommand` awaits the plan read, so `index.ts` awaits it and the in-process test harness (`captureStdout`) awaits too; the `--template` refusal test moves from a sync `toThrow` to `.rejects.toThrow`. Alternative (keep sync via duplicated I/O) rejected for the reason above. Every existing output path stays byte-identical — the default role still serves `roles/<role_id>.md` and its ack-token first line unchanged.
- Additive roles are served and listed under their render id (the post-`/` segment, e.g. `qa-lead`), never the namespaced config key (`acme/qa-lead`) — matching what every other renderer (`vinaya check --plan`, `DiagramModel`) shows.
- `apps/cli/specs/conformance.md` updated: the brief's `## Documentation` source named it "if it states what `vinaya doctrine --role` serves" — it did not state that before. Since this change carries a code surface at the brief's stated impact tier, the code-requires-docs contract needs a doc touch, so the matrix's `CLAUDE.md`/rules-hierarchy row (which owns "doctrine resolution") is updated to record that the command now serves configured overrides/additives through the shared role plan. author: alice39s
body:
Branch `feat/worker-proxy` → `feat/cors-direct` (stacked on #2).

## Why

The proxy lived in `server/proxy.ts` and only ran behind the site's own Pages Function, Vercel function or Vite server. Static deployments such as GitHub Pages had no proxy at all, and users who did not want their keys to pass through `lm.ikale.io` had no alternative.

## What

- Move the proxy into `worker/main.js`, a dependency-free Worker (`export default { fetch }`); the Pages Function, the Vercel function and the Vite middleware import its `proxyRequest`.
- Add CORS to the Worker for origins in `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (default `https://lm.ikale.io`), an `OPTIONS` preflight and a `GET` health check; keep the same-origin checks of the site proxy unchanged.
- Export only functions from the Worker module: workerd treats every named export as an entrypoint and refuses to start on a constant export.
- Add `worker/wrangler.json`, `worker/package.json` (binding description for the Deploy button) and `worker/README.md`; add `bun run dev:worker` and `bun run deploy:worker`.
- Add a Relay proxy setting to the API configuration: this site or an own Worker address (HTTPS, or local HTTP for `wrangler dev`), saved per browser as `{ mode, endpoint }`, with a health check.
- Block a run instead of falling back when Worker mode has no valid address (`proxy_missing`), and focus the address field.
- Key consent by proxy and upstream origin; name the Worker host in the dialog and state that the site cannot vouch for it.
- Add a Deploy to Cloudflare link and an Import from GitHub into the Playground button that builds the Playground's share link from the current `worker/main.js` on GitHub.
- Update `docs/deployment.md`, the READMEs and `web/design.md`.

## How verified

- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run build`: pass; `wrangler pages functions build` compiles the Pages Function.
- `wrangler dev --config worker/wrangler.json --var ALLOWED_ORIGINS:http://127.0.0.1:5174`:
  - preflight from the allowed origin: 204 with `Access-Control-Allow-*`; from another origin: 403 without CORS headers;
  - `GET`: health JSON; `POST` without a key: 401; `https://localhost/...`: 400; `PUT`: 405 with `Allow`;
  - SSE and JSON relay to a public upstream: 200, usage chunk intact.
- `wrangler pages dev web/dist`: same-origin health 200, cross-origin POST 403, SSE relay 200.
- Chromium via Playwright:
  - Tokenizer probe through a local Worker: 13 / 13 requests 200, `deepseek-v3` exact 99.3%; through `/api/proxy`: 13 / 13 requests 200.
  - Check proxy: ok (Worker), forbidden (page served from a non-allowed origin), unreachable (`http://127.0.0.1:9`).
  - Worker mode with an empty address and a remembered site-proxy consent: no proxy request, `proxy_missing` toast, address field focused.
  - Changing a saved address to an invalid one clears it; an address saved in another tab replaces the field.
- Decoded the generated Playground link with the Playground's own `getPlaygroundWorker` logic in Chromium: one module `main.js`, type `application/javascript+module`, content identical to `worker/main.js`, metadata from `wrangler.json`.

author: mrrr7
body:
## What & why

Fixes from a full click-through design critique of the live site, plus two requested additions: a proper loading state for generation and an independently scrolling shapes rail.

### Bugs fixed
- **Tour** died at step 3 (planner targets only mount after a campus is picked). The campus step now waits for a pick and auto-advances; "STEP X OF Y" and the dots count only visible steps.
- **Paste import** rejected every row: the validator required course name + credits the paste parser never produces. Defaults are applied before validating (same ones `addRows` already used); each row shows its real error; rows with no recognised slot code are flagged.
- **Disabled buttons** were indistinguishable from enabled ones (`disabled:opacity-60` on FPButton).
- **Export menu** now closes on Escape / outside click; **Share image** modal closes on Escape and uses fp primitives (fixes off-brand green).
- **Share** shows the link inline with Copy instead of relying on a toast after an await.
- **Swap** is a real `<select>` of the professors the layout allows, and briefly spotlights the swapped course.
- **Preferences** labels were raw keys (`start_after`); field groups are now real `<label>`s.
- **Contrast root cause:** `readableTextColor` used a 0.55 luminance cut, putting white on amber/teal at ~2:1. It now picks whichever ink has higher WCAG contrast. Removed an unused duplicate in `resultsVisuals.ts`.

### Flow / UX
- Planner rail: search first and full-width, short tab labels, VTOP banner moved below; **Tick all** per slot/course; Add disabled until something's ticked; "In plan · N profs" after adding; paste box clears after add.
- Live preview uses the same slot matrix empty or full (no layout swap on first course); blank empty cells.
- Preferences ends with ranking + Find my weeks; first-time banner hides once courses exist; busy cells actually visible; busy grid covers to 20:00.
- Zero results: **Drop** clears only the offending rule (was: reset everything); no duplicate sidebar/toast; clash-specific heading.
- Results: "score N" instead of "N / 100", Unverified badge explains itself, combo cards name the differing professor, single "Save & copy slots for VTOP" action, grid-first on phones.
- Landing: returning-user "Continue planning" CTA, distinct selected vs disabled campus cards, fuller hero grid, accordion FAQ. Compare highlights differing professors. Plain-language Settings copy; saved weeks named "Week N".

### Generate flow (requested)
"Find my weeks" now navigates to `/results` immediately. While the search runs, `/results` shows a loading screen (transitions.dev **matrix loader** + **thinking states**, live checked/found counts, Cancel), held ≥1.2s, then blurs out as the table blurs in (**skeleton reveal**). The worker lives at module scope in `useGenerator` and reports through a session-only `generation` store slice (not persisted), so it survives the planner unmounting. The old candidate-streaming animation in the planner preview is removed.

### Shapes rail (requested)
Sticky under the 57px header on desktop with its own scroll (`overscroll-contain`, thin scrollbar); the 3-shape cap / "N more" button is gone.

## Reviewer notes
- transitions.dev CSS lives in `src/app/fp-transitions.css` (snippets verbatim, tunables themed onto fp tokens).
- Known ceiling (marked `ponytail:` in `ZeroResultsFP.tsx`): dropping a busy-time rule clears all busy blocks, since findings carry the label, not the window id.
- `useGenerator` keeps its return shape so classic planner components still compile/work.
- Verified with `tsc --noEmit` and a browser walkthrough on a local dev server (tour, paste, search, zero-results drop, generate → loader → results, swap, export/share, compare, landing, 375px results). No lint config / test script in the repo. The share API 500s locally (Supabase insert) — the inline link UI was checked against a stubbed 201.

body:
## Problème

`kg_get_smart_maintenance_schedule` ramène tout libellé `diesel…électrique` au jeton `hybride`, puis ne retient que les nœuds `-essence`. La RPC sœur `kg_get_maintenance_alerts_by_milestone`, appelée par le même endpoint `/api/diagnostic-engine/calendar`, n'a pas ce repli : pour le même véhicule, l'une répond essence, l'autre diesel.

Lu en lecture seule sur la base le 2026-09-30 (corps live `md5 4a56e0a2…`, identique à `20260429_diag_maintenance_via_kg`) :

| types | `type_fuel` | avant | après |
|---|---|---|---|
| 338 | Diesel-Électrique | bougies-essence, vidange-essence | bougies-prechauffage, vidange-diesel |
| 191 | Diesel-Electrique | bougies-essence, vidange-essence | bougies-prechauffage, vidange-diesel |

Les 20 autres valeurs de `type_fuel` (hybrides essence compris) donnent un résultat identique.

## Correction

Migration `CREATE OR REPLACE` qui retire le repli et la branche `hybride` : le filtre carburant devient celui de la RPC d'alertes, à l'identique. Signature, `STABLE`, `SECURITY INVOKER`, `search_path`, droits et commentaire sont conservés. Aucune applicabilité ajoutée : le carburant thermique est lu dans `type_fuel`, comme pour les autres libellés.

Effet de bord documenté : un `p_fuel_type = 'hybride'` explicite ne renvoie plus que les 15 opérations génériques, comme la RPC d'alertes. Aucun appelant interne ne transmet cette valeur.

## Vérification

- `bash scripts/db/test-kg-maintenance-schedule-fuel-filter.sh` (PostgreSQL 17 jetable, sans réseau) : **21 réussis, 0 échec** — identité hors corps, périmètre exact du changement, idempotence, rollback au corps live verbatim.
- Défaut réinjecté dans la migration (`MIGRATION_UNDER_TEST`) : 6 échecs, exit 1.
- squawk 2.52.1 (`.squawk.toml`) : 0 issue. `--lint-markers` : OK. `--self-test` du moteur : OK.
- Invariants registry 6/6, empreinte PR-8 à jour, ratchet d'écriture de contenu servi inchangé, règle R2 : 0 finding.

## Non fait

- **Migration non appliquée** : elle le sera par `apply-supabase-migrations.yml` après fusion.
- Aucun changement de code applicatif ni d'intervalle d'entretien.

body:
## Schritt A-7 – Vergleich über mehrere Provider (Redundanz-Konsens)

Aus der Sammlung (`docs/neuordnung/SAMMLUNG.md`, A-7), Spur A, frei seit B-1 (#207). `consensus.ts` war gebaut, aber nicht angebunden. Umgesetzt wie in der Sammlung vorgeschlagen: Schalter je Frage, Standard aus, Kosten vorher sichtbar. Kein neues Event-Format.

### Was geändert wurde
- `packages/app/src/konsens.ts` (neu, ohne DOM):
  - `KONSENS_PROVIDER` = 3 (aus `recommendedRedundancy("important")`), `KONSENS_MIN` = 2, `KONSENS_WARTEN_MS` = 3 Minuten.
  - `konsensZiele()` wählt die ersten Provider der Rangfolge, jeden nur einmal.
  - `KonsensSammlung` nimmt je Anfrage genau eine Antwort an, nur vom gefragten Provider. Eine Rückmeldung mit Status `error` beendet die Anfrage; Zwischenstände tun das nicht.
  - `konsensText()` baut den Satz aus den Feldern, samt Hinweis „stimmig, nicht richtig“. Die deutsche `explanation` des Protokolls wird nicht angezeigt.
- `packages/app/src/shell/tabs/agent.ts`:
  - Haken „vergleichen“ neben dem Tier. Er gilt nur für eine Frage und ist danach wieder aus (`konsensGewaehlt()`). Bei Max und Swarm ist er ausgeblendet (`setupKonsens()`).
  - `konsensVorbereiten()`:
    - wählt 2–3 private-fähige Provider;
    - nennt im Dialog die Gesamtkosten (`consensusCostPreview(hoechstMsat(…))`, in beiden Einheiten);
    - bei Ablehnung oder zu wenigen Providern geht nichts hinaus, auch kein Einzelauftrag.
  - `askKonsens()`:
    - Sendet je Provider über `buildJobEvent()`: eigener Sitzungsschlüssel, kein Zusatz-Tag, erst gemerkt, dann gesendet.
    - Jede Antwort läuft nacheinander über `handleAnswer()`: gezeigt, abgerechnet und bezahlt wie sonst, höchstens das Gebot je Provider, Reklamation möglich.
    - Danach kommt das Ergebnis als eigene Blase, nur `textContent`. Es kommt nicht in den Verlauf, weil der als Kontext mit der nächsten Frage reist.
    - Stopp beendet das Warten und vergleicht, was schon da ist.
  - `handleAnswer()` meldet optional, wann die Antwort fertig angezeigt ist (`nachAnzeige`).
- `packages/app/src/shell/index.html`: Haken `#ai-konsens` im Label (mobil 40 px über die bestehende Regel).
- `packages/app/src/texte/agent.ts`: Texte `agent.konsens*` in beiden Sprachen.
- `packages/app/src/shell/app.ts`: `setupKonsens()`.
- `scripts/wiring-ausnahmen.txt`: alle fünf Ausnahmen für `consensus.ts` raus. `normalizeAnswer`/`similarity` zählen über `evaluateConsensus()` als verdrahtet.
- STATUS, Sammlung (A-7 → `fertig`), neuer Fallstrick und Stand-Zeile in `CLAUDE.md`.

### Verdrahtet
- `packages/app/src/shell/tabs/agent.ts:553`: `askAi()` → `konsensVorbereiten()`
- `packages/app/src/shell/tabs/agent.ts:582`: `askAi()` → `askKonsens()`
- `packages/app/src/shell/app.ts:907`: `setupKonsens()`

### Prüfungen
| Prüfung | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| protocol | 1131 grün, 6 übersprungen, 0 rot (nicht berührt) |
| node | 272 grün (nicht berührt) |
| app | 697 grün, 0 rot (vorher 693, +4 `konsens.test.ts`) |
| Leak-Tests | 68 grün + 1 todo |
| mls | 13 grün (nicht berührt) |
| check-wiring `--streng` / check-website | Exit 0 (151 Ausnahmen, fünf weniger) / 5 Seiten ok |
| check_innerhtml `--streng` | Exit 0 (keine neue Ausnahme) |
| Smoke-Test | bestanden |

### Offen / MENSCH
- [ ] Probe mit echten Providern (mindestens zwei private-fähige im Netz). Gezahlt wird über den bestehenden Pfad, der Vergleich selbst ist lokal.
- Knoten-Stand: unverändert, kein Update nötig.

### Annahmen und Risiken
- Die Frage sehen mehrere Provider; der Dialog sagt das vor dem Senden. Jeder sieht nur seinen eigenen Sitzungsschlüssel. Sprechen sich Provider ab, können sie gleiche Fragen verbinden – das ist im Verfahren angelegt.
- Einig heißt stimmig, nicht richtig. Die App nennt keine Antwort „verifiziert“; das Whitepaper sagt dasselbe.
- Auf die übrigen Antworten wartet die App höchstens 3 Minuten. Die Antworten erscheinen nacheinander, der Vergleich am Ende.

author: primerosresultados
body:
> **Va encima de #447** (carta de colores): usa sus tablas y su pantalla. Mergear #447 primero; este PR pasa solo a apuntar a `main`.

## Qué resuelve

Segunda etapa de tintometría (reunión del 30-sep): enviar a laboratorio **solicitudes de fórmula o de precio** y que **toda la comunicación pase por el panel**.

Hoy se hace con la planilla "Solicitud de fórmula tintométrica" por correo: el ejemplo FT-007 era Textu EIFS G-25, color SW 7019, para Electrocom. Ahora se pide en el panel con los mismos datos y laboratorio responde ahí mismo.

## Qué hay

**Nueva solicitud** (Tintometría → Solicitudes a laboratorio)
- Se elige qué se necesita: fórmula, precio o las dos.
- **Cliente**: se busca por nombre o RUT, o se escribe si no está.
- **Ciudad y obra.**
- **Color**: se elige de la carta o se escribe (código, nombre y cartilla: RAL, NCS, lo que sea).
- **Línea a desarrollar, base y formato.** Cantidad estimada, si se pide precio.
- **Continuación de obra**: patrón y lote.
- **Observaciones y foto de la muestra.**
- Desde la ficha de un color en la carta, el botón **"Pedir fórmula o precio a laboratorio"** abre la solicitud con el color cargado.

**Bandeja de laboratorio** (la misma pantalla, con el permiso "Bandeja de laboratorio")
- Ve todas las solicitudes.
- Puede **tomarla** (queda "en desarrollo") o **rechazarla** con motivo.
- Puede **responder** con:
  - la fórmula: colorantes y dosis como en el libro (`0Y57`, `1Y30-1`), para los galones del formato, que vienen prellenados;
  - el precio y su unidad;
  - observaciones.
- La fórmula respondida **queda en la carta de colores**, en la ficha del color, ligada al cliente, la obra y la solicitud. Si el color no estaba en la carta, se crea en su cartilla.

**Hilo y avisos**
- Cada solicitud tiene su conversación con adjuntos. Los cambios de estado quedan en el mismo hilo.
- **Contador en el menú**: para laboratorio, lo que llegó o le escribieron sin mirar; para quien pidió, lo que respondió laboratorio.
- **Correos**:
  - la solicitud nueva y los mensajes del vendedor van a laboratorio (usuarios con ese rol y los de Configuración → Correos → "Solicitud a laboratorio"), con copia a quien pide y a su supervisor;
  - la respuesta, el rechazo y los mensajes de laboratorio van a quien pidió, con copia a su supervisor.
  - Cada correo trae un botón que abre la solicitud.

## Decisiones

- **Quién ve la fórmula respondida.** La ve quien tiene "Ver fórmulas" (el operador), igual que las del libro. El vendedor ve que está lista y el precio, no las dosis (decisión de Panorámica: por ahora las fórmulas las ve solo el operador).
- **La dosis queda tal como la escribe laboratorio**, con la Y en mayúscula. Se valida que se entienda (`0Y5x7` se rechaza con un mensaje claro). No se reescribe `0Y57` como `1Y9`: el operador lee lo que escribió laboratorio.
- **Permisos por defecto** (se cambian en Roles y Permisos):

  | Permiso | Roles |
  |---|---|
  | Solicitudes a laboratorio | vendedor, supervisor, encargado de área, recepción y técnico |
  | Bandeja de laboratorio | laboratorio y jefe de planta |

  El supervisor ve las solicitudes de su equipo.

## Cómo se probó

En local, con cuentas de vendedor y laboratorio:
- **Crear**: se crea con los datos de la planilla; sin línea responde "Indica la línea a desarrollar".
- **Contadores**:
  - laboratorio ve 1 al llegar la solicitud;
  - el vendedor ve 1 cuando laboratorio escribe o responde, y 0 al abrirla.
- **Permisos**: un vendedor que intenta cambiar el estado recibe 403.
- **Respuesta**:
  - Una dosis mal escrita se rechaza.
  - La respuesta a "SW 7019" (Textu EIFS G-25, 4 galones: KX 0Y57, C 0y11, B 1Y30, F 0Y3, $45.990 por galón) queda como fórmula de laboratorio en la ficha de SW7019, junto a la del libro.
  - El vendedor ve el precio y "la fórmula está lista", sin las dosis; laboratorio ve las dosis.
- **Enlace del correo**: `?id=` abre la solicitud directo.
- **Correos**: no se probaron, porque en local no hay correo configurado. Salen con el mismo servicio que la solicitud de crédito.

## Configuración después de mergear

Opcional: en Configuración → Correos → "Solicitud a laboratorio", sumar otros destinatarios fijos. Sin eso, el aviso les llega a los usuarios con el rol Laboratorio.
