author: zhangfand
body:
## What this PR does

After #562, WeChat got a display of its own only when an operator set `WECHAT_USER_DISPLAY` and the entrypoint started it at container boot. Otherwise the client ran on the shared `:99`, beside Rome's Chrome, and its keystrokes went to the display Chrome uses.

This PR makes WeChat always run on its own desktop, started by the runtime:

- **Table:** the `wechat` row now exists whenever WeChat is enabled, at `:100` / 5901 / 6081. The legacy variables still override it.
- **Runtime:** before the client starts, or keys are captured, it runs `rome-start-desktop.sh` with arguments taken from the table.
- **Survival:** the desktop outlives Rome, so a Rome restart finds the client still running and signed in.

It also meets every T2 requirement deferred from #562's reviews. Each has a test that fails without it:

- **Owner check:** the start script reuses only the calling user's processes.
- **One run at a time:** runs for the same desktop take turns under `flock`.
- **Lock and logs:** they go to `ROME_DESKTOP_LOG_DIR`, by default a private `~/.cache/rome-desktop` (0700), so no other account can pre-create the lock and the tests leave nothing in `/tmp`.
- **Ports fail closed:** a malformed `ROME_WECHAT_*_PORT` removes the row, so the proxy answers 404 instead of 500.
- **Whole-path encoding:** `DesktopPage` encodes the whole socket path.
- **One source for the arguments:** the runtime takes its arguments from `desktopSlot("wechat")` and never restates them.

This is task T2 of the plan in the work repo, `zhangfand/rome-work` `named-desktops/technical-spec.md`.

## Design & Invariants

The durable home is [`docs/architecture/named-desktops.md`](docs/architecture/named-desktops.md). The WeChat side is in [`docs/wechat-personal.md`](docs/wechat-personal.md#wechats-own-display).

- **One source.** `desktopSlot("wechat")` is the only place the display, ports and Openbox config live. The proxy routes by it, and `startDesktopArgs` turns it into the script's arguments. `wechatUserDisplay` moved into `desktops.ts`, which owns the legacy input now. That also keeps `desktops.ts` and `wechat-user.ts` free of an import cycle.
- **Starting the desktop.**
  - `WechatUserRuntime.ensureDesktop()` runs the script under `env -i`, so the long-lived display programs get none of Rome's configuration or credentials.
  - `start()` calls it only when no client is running. The setup's capture step calls it after its last status read and before key recovery launches the client, and passes the display `ensureDesktop()` returns to key recovery, so a legacy client on `:99` cannot pull recovery back there, even through a concurrent probe.
  - A script file that does not exist, as on a host `pnpm start`, keeps the client on the shared desktop (E5r). Any non-zero exit from an installed script throws `WechatUserRuntimeError` and does not start the client.
  - With WeChat enabled, boot fails when the `wechat` row is invalid, such as a bad port or a display clash. So the runtime never mistakes misconfiguration for "no own desktop".
- **A running client keeps its display (E8).** `status()` reads the running client's `DISPLAY` from `/proc/<pid>/environ` and returns it, with its `desktopPath`. No query changes runtime state. `runtime.display` is the fixed display a new client starts on. Moving a live client would mean restarting it, which can make the phone confirm again. So a client already on `:99` moves to `:100` only when it next exits. `desktopPath` now derives from the display the client actually uses (`/desktop/wechat` or `/desktop`), rather than from configuration.
- **Script.**
  - `pgrep -u "$(id -u)"` means another account's matching process is never reused.
  - `flock` on `<log dir>/.rome-desktop-<name>.lock` serialises runs. The spawned programs close the lock's fd, or they would hold it for their whole life. The first version of this change hung for exactly that reason, and the tests caught it.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`: passes.
- [x] `pnpm lint:deadcode`: passes. Its hits are pre-existing unused-export warnings, none in this diff.
- [x] Biome over `packages/core/src`, `packages/web/src` and `scripts`: passes, with 6 pre-existing warnings in files this PR does not touch.
- [x] `scripts/lint-shell.sh` (shfmt and shellcheck): passes, run in `nix develop` on devbox.
- [x] Checks on `64de8a3`, after the extra review round:
  - `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint:deadcode`, Biome, `scripts/lint-shell.sh` and `pnpm build` pass.
  - `pnpm test:unit:core`: 425 files, 4955 tests pass.
  - `pnpm test:unit:web`: 1776 tests pass, and the UI package's 710 tests pass.
  - The devbox check below ran at `9494df5`.

author: retran
body:
The runner now ends a run `budget` before a call that could pass the budget, and `unmetered` after a call whose cost it can't read. This implements TSK-3370 under EPC-1910, tracked by #727, and closes REQ-0870, REQ-0876 and REQ-0878.

`run` in `crates/meow/src/runloop.rs` keeps the spend so far and the largest single call's cost. Before each call it ends the run `budget` where their sum is above the budget. After each call it writes the log's line with `sum_usd`, ends the run `unmetered` where the result holds no cost, adds the cost, and ends the run `budget` where the result's subtype is `error_max_budget_usd`, all before it evaluates the condition. `call` passes `--max-budget-usd` as the budget less the spend so far, where it passed the whole budget.

I made three choices the task leaves open. The log's field is `sum_usd`, and it is `null` on the line of a call that reported no cost. A cost that is negative or not finite counts as no cost, because adding it would lower the spend or make it unreadable. The run prints one line saying why it ended before its last line.

The first commit holds the five `Budget` checks and the changed `Files.test_run_directory`, which asserted the log held no sum. The `test` verb exited 1 on it with those six failing. Each verb passed on the change's tree through `meow-checks run format lint check test build`, exit status 0:

```text
format: passed, record e7e3a8760bb0, current at tree 8306360cb26b
lint: passed, record 7ba6d275794b, current at tree 8306360cb26b
check: passed, record 1db1c93e2aca, current at tree 8306360cb26b
test: passed, record fe4ed2c6a03c, current at tree 8306360cb26b
build: passed, record 0d9f0153b38e, current at tree 8306360cb26b
```

No real call ran, so the subtype and the cost field are as RES-0300 recorded them and the stand-in prints them. `meow-loop` goes to 0.3.0.

Read the top of the loop in `run` first: the check before the call and the two endings after it are the change.

author: saymon0123
body:
Primeiro item do bloco de funcionalidades. Também registra no backlog as decisões de 30/09 (o que entra, o 15 fora, o 17 em espera) e o descarte do `npm audit fix` com o motivo escrito.

## A porta já estava construída

O status `bloqueio` existe no CHECK de `appointments` desde sempre, o tipo do CRM o conhece, o modal de detalhe já o desenha em cinza e a contagem de reservas vivas já o ignora. **Faltava criar um** — o `NewAppointmentModal` gravava `agendado` ou `concluido`, e por isso havia **zero** linhas com esse status no banco. O barbeiro marcava o almoço como reserva no nome de um cliente inventado.

E abrir a porta **não precisaria de migration nenhuma**:

```
appointments_sem_sobreposicao: EXCLUDE (professional_id =, tstzrange(inicio,fim) &&)
                               WHERE status NOT IN ('cancelado','faltou')
```

`bloqueio` nunca esteve nessa isenção. No instante em que a linha existe, o banco recusa agendamento em cima dela **nas três portas** — CRM, link público e agente do WhatsApp. `client_id` e `service_id` já aceitavam nulo, e a RLS já limitava o barbeiro à própria cadeira.

## O que exigiu migration foi a folga

`folga_entre_atendimentos_minutos` existe para o barbeiro respirar entre dois clientes. **O bloqueio *é* a respiração** — cobrar folga em volta dele é cobrar descanso de quem não estava aqui.

Sem correção, a primeira coisa que ele tentasse já falhava: o salão de teste exige 10 minutos, então bloquear o almoço das 12h com um corte terminando às 12h era recusado com *"fica a menos de 10 minutos de outro atendimento"* — frase que ele leria como defeito do sistema.

A régua vale nos dois lados, e por isso **duas funções mudaram juntas**: o gatilho (decide se a linha entra) e `horarios_livres` (decide o que o cliente enxerga). Mexer só no gatilho deixaria o CRM aceitando 13:00 enquanto o link público escondia até 13:10 — as duas portas discordando sobre a mesma régua.

Em `horarios_livres` a folga **mudou de lado**: antes alargava o candidato e media contra o vizinho; como agora depende de *quem* é o vizinho, passou para o lado dele. É equivalente — alargar A em f e medir contra B é a mesma pergunta que alargar B em f e medir contra A.

## Dois defeitos que só apareceram andando pelos lados

- A Agenda desenhava `{client_nome ?? 'Cliente'}`: um bloqueio apareceria como **"12:00 · Cliente"**, e o leitor de tela diria *"12:00, cliente"* para uma hora em que não há ninguém.
- O detalhe abriria um almoço com **"Confirmar", "Cliente chegou", "Concluir" e "Cobrar"** — o mesmo defeito que a lista de Vendas acabou de perder no item 10, repetido noutra tela. Ganhou saída própria, com uma ação só.

A linha de excluir foi **extraída** em vez de duplicada: a catraca de botões tem teto 3 neste arquivo e o teto só desce. Foi a mesma saída da última vez que ela reclamou.

## De quebra: o "dia inteiro"

Um checkbox que cobre a maior parte do **item 18 (pedido de folga)** para uma equipe de três. O que sobraria do 18 é o fluxo de *pedir e o dono aprovar* — gestão de gente, não agenda. Vale reavaliar se ainda se justifica.

## As cinco peças

| Peça | O que mudou |
|---|---|
| **CRM** | modal (abas Reserva \| Bloquear), cartão da agenda, detalhe do bloqueio |
| **Supabase** | migration 0182, **já aplicada em produção** |
| **Vercel** | nada |
| **GitHub** | este PR |
| **n8n** | **nada** — a trava do banco e a `horarios_livres` já atendem as duas portas do cliente |

## Prova

- **Ensaio da migration** contra o schema real dentro de transação: 10 de 10, com o rollback conferido em três sinais (coluna, salão de ensaio e corpo do gatilho) antes de aplicar.
- **11 asserções pgTAP.** Sem Docker aqui, então as mesmas onze rodaram contra produção com rollback: 11 de 11, com os códigos de erro exatos (23P01, 23514).
- **10 asserções de unidade** no módulo puro da janela — separado justamente para o teste não arrastar `supabase.ts`.
- typecheck (sem cache) ✓, lint ✓, **513/513** em 60 arquivos (eram 503 em 59), build de produção ✓.
- Grants de `horarios_livres` conferidos **antes** de escrever o `revoke`: são `postgres` e `service_role`, e eu ia alargar para `authenticated` por descuido.

**Não verificado em tela logada:** entrar como barbeiro exigiria criar conta ou digitar senha, que eu não faço. A conferência visual do modal é tua.

author: patrick-hermann-sva
body:
An evening at the table with the piezos attached. The measurements are in
[#35](../../issues/35) and [#33](../../pull/33); this is what came out of it in
code — and it ends with a revert of most of what it started with.

## The short version

Counting was about half right. Five changes were made on top of the ported
sketch, each justified by a measurement, and the result was **worse**: a game
where almost every point had to be corrected by hand. Putting all five back the
way the sketch had them produced the first game that counted itself correctly —
**18 rallies, 19 points, one wrong**, kept as
[`docs/baselines/2026-09-30-first-clean-game.json`](docs/baselines/2026-09-30-first-clean-game.json).

The measurements were not wrong. They were taken on finger taps and on
deliberate bounces with nobody playing, and a rally is not that. Deriving
thresholds from them was the mistake.

## What the measurements did establish

**The circuit is good.** Both channels rest at exactly 0 with no jitter — nothing
like the 303..448 the floating pins read in #32. Thirty ball bounces, including
deliberately weak ones, all reached the 12-bit ceiling of 4095, while ringing
peaked at 685 and crosstalk at 309. The stage 1 gate — weakest real bounce at
least twice the strongest disturbance — **passes at 2.76×**.

**Detection is not the problem.** 30 of 30 bounces counted, on both the slow and
the continuous build.

**The ADC settles at 1 MΩ without the delay**, which is what #33 was blocked on:
sampling continuously gave 5794 readings/s against 769, and peaks roughly
doubled rather than collapsing. It is still not switched on by default, because
the sketch's numbers are the baseline and this is a change to make on its own,
with a game to show for it.

## What stays

None of it touches how a point is decided:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `/diag` | last reading per channel, both baselines, a min/max window that resets per read, tick count — issue #35 assumed these existed |
| Settings card | sliders for both log thresholds and the clear ratio |
| Settings | written to NVS. `/cfg` only moved the variable and logged it; the second argument was a label, not a key |
| Note field | a real button. It was a text link inside a grey hint, so a comment reached the log only by riding along with a correction |
| | the score it belongs to, next to it |
| Undo | says what it did. Taking back a double award needs two presses and the first one looked like nothing |
| Serve | marks the serving player in the name row. It rotated correctly all along and nobody could see it in an 11px caption under a 74px score |
| Page | `Cache-Control: no-store`. Without it a phone keeps serving the copy it cached, and an uploaded UI never arrives |
| Page | a bar when it has lost the board. Every failed poll was swallowed silently, so a whole game was played against a frozen scoreboard |

## One deliberate deviation from the sketch

A double bounce awards against the side that bounced twice. The sketch wrote
`andere(i)` with the loop index instead of the side, so `andere(1)` returned `'A'`
every time and **every** double bounce went to A regardless of which half the ball
hit. That is a bug, not a rule.

## Checks

- `task verify` — lint clean, both builds, 17/17 rule tests, sink tests

author: ojungo69
body: Milestone 4, Task 1 (`docs/milestone-4-plan.md`): the delivered set (spec 3.4, owner decision 31) and SessionStart's content (spec 4.4, D4). ## What the plan's names became - **`DELIVERED`** is `claims::delivered(which, links_end)`, an SQL builder beside `TIPS`: the chain tips, and each decided decision or preference whose every inbound edge is a curator link from a later claim (strictly later `valid_from`) that is active, decided or done, and backed by the owner as `anchored_through` defines it. That predicate is now one function both use (`owner_backed`). Each such claim carries `later`, the newest of those linkers. `TIPS` is unchanged apart from a NULL `later` column. - **`LINKS_END_DECISIONS`** (false) switches to the tips once curator links pass M3's control line; `with_links_ending_decisions_only_the_later_claim_is_delivered` runs the builder with it true. - **`deliver(k, repo, kinds, limit)`** had no ranking input (cubic and Codex on #300, #302 item 1). As built, ranking is each surface's and the pair rule is shared: `claims::units` takes the list a surface ranked and gives each claim with the chain of later claims that ended it as one unit (a later claim of another kind, a fix say, is fetched by uid), `place` fits whole units into a number of places, and `newest_first` lists units by their newest claim. SessionStart ranks `claims::decisions` (the newest 200 delivered decisions, preferences, open items and lessons) by the words each shares with the manifest's files and last prompt, then by recency. ## As built, against the plan - **Unapplied owner state (D3, #302 item 2).** A claim that an owner correction past the claims consumer names, whatever it corrects, is left out until the worker applies it, rather than having its status overlaid, so an old body is never injected either. A claim that quotes a record whose tombstone the anchors consumer has not reached is left out too (D4 shows delivered claims while a tombstone waits, and the manifest hides itself then for the same reason). A unit with such a claim is left out whole, and so is the digest when it cites one. `claims::Pending`, read-only. - **An earlier claim never stands alone.** A unit whose chain meets a later claim that is not delivered itself is left out. - **No `restates` edges (#302 item 3).** A restatement quotes the same words of the same event, so its link is not strictly later and still ends the claim. `a_restatement_ends_a_claim_as_before` shows it. ## What changes at SessionStart - Global preferences come first (they were not shown). - "## Current decisions and open items" becomes "## Decisions and open items": about 10 claims with bodies, a pair's earlier claim marked `superseded by the above`. Only spec 4.4's kinds: decided fixes, changes and repo facts no longer appear (they are for search). - The digest follows them while fresh, as before. - Last, "## More from memory": a line naming `search`, `get` and `timeline`, then up to 20 more claims one line each (a 12-character id, date, kind, first words). Being last, the hook's cut drops it first under an agent's size cap (`the_index_goes_first_under_the_size_cap`). `get` by that id is Task 4's (#302 item 4). - A checkout with no manifest to show (new branch, dirty manifest, tombstone not yet applied) still gets all of this. - `one_line` also cuts after a Japanese or Chinese clause mark: an index line of a body in Japanese showed only the ellipsis. Spec 8.4's milestone 4 fixture now says what #295 row 1 asks: both claims until curator links pass the control line, then only the later one. ## Measured A copy of milestone 3's dev home `ov-B1` (93 claims in the repository used), `oboete inject` from a checkout of that repository with no manifest row, release builds, 30 runs after 5 warm-ups, WSL: main 4.8 ms p50 (shows nothing), this PR 8.6 ms p50 / 9.9 ms p95 (4,152 characters: 10 claims with bodies, 20 one-liners). Of the added time, the delivered read is about 1.5 ms (the 200-claim pool query 0.8 ms, pairs 0.3, pending state, preferences and digest 0.4) and the redaction gate over the longer text about 1.8 ms. The read-hook line is Task 12's. ## Tests Plan Task 1 step 1's list, in `consumer::manifest`: `an_earlier_decision_ended_by_a_later_owner_decision_is_delivered_after_it_with_both_dates` (owner decision 31's fixture), `a_link_from_a_proposal_a_retracted_claim_or_an_earlier_claim_delivers_nothing_new`, `a_restatement_ends_a_claim_as_before`, `a_picked_earlier_claim_brings_its_later_claim_and_the_pair_takes_two_places` (Review Focus 1), `with_links_ending_decisions_only_the_later_claim_is_delivered`, `a_retraction_in_another_chunk_never_brings_the_decision_back` (row 54-6), `global_preferences_come_first_and_about_ten_claims_have_bodies`, `the_chosen_claims_are_listed_newest_first_whatever_chose_them`, `a_claim_dated_between_a_pair_never_separates_it`, `a_checkout_with_claims_and_no_manifest_row_still_gets_them`, `an_owner_retraction_the_worker_has_not_applied_is_not_shown` (a retraction, a body correction, a tombstone and a digest, before and after the worker), and `the_index_goes_first_under_the_size_cap`. The query plan check (no scan) now runs on the delivered query. Disabling `Pending::touches`, or its tombstone half alone, fails the unapplied-state test. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01WsENTuUpqqwyXLWfaueGG8 ## Summary by Sourcery Implement delivered-claim semantics and enrich SessionStart with safely filtered, relevance-ranked memory content. New Features: - Define delivered claims and expose them consistently across memory delivery surfaces. - Expand SessionStart with global preferences, relevant delivered claims, fresh digest content, and a compact searchable memory index. - Support delivery of superseded claim chains while preserving claim ordering and whole-chain placement. Bug Fixes: - Hide claims and digests affected by owner corrections or tombstones that the worker has not yet applied. - Prevent stale or retracted claims from reappearing through delivered chains. - Preserve readable truncation boundaries for Japanese and Chinese text. Enhancements: - Centralize owner-backed claim evaluation and add delivered-claim ranking, grouping, placement, and recency ordering. - Limit SessionStart decisions to the specified claim kinds and rank them using manifest files and the last prompt. - Update delivery semantics and milestone fixtures for curator links crossing the control line. Documentation: - Update the delivery specification and milestone acceptance criteria for delivered claim ordering and owner-backed links. Tests: - Add coverage for delivered claim chains, curator-link behavior, pending owner state, SessionStart ranking and layout, size-cap ordering, and multilingual truncation.

author: lior-nis
body:
Todoist, both from Nikol:
- «תיקון גלילה תקועה לאחר חסימת פורטל הורה» (6hfv9GRG6RvMw65q)
- «תיקון תקיעות עמוד בפורטל המורה» (6hfv9ppwWp8G3w8q)

They have the same root cause.

## Root cause

The home page's header sidebar locked page scrolling with this effect, which has no cleanup:

```svelte
$effect(() => { document.body.style.overflow = sidebarOpen ? 'hidden' : ''; });
```

The sidebar's links («לוח בקרה מורה», «פורטל הורה ותלמיד/ה», «הדף שלי») are client-side navigations, followed while the sidebar is open. The header is destroyed with the lock still on `<body>`, and every page after it inherits it until a reload:
- the tutor dashboard
- the parent/student portal
- a student's card

**Reproduced on a built server:** after home → menu → «לוח בקרה מורה», `body.style.overflow` was `'hidden'` on `/app/dashboard`, and PageDown left the 2622px page at `scrollY` 0.

**A second leak of the same kind:** an open tutor popup (mobile) is moved onto `<body>`, so it paints above the reveal transform, and it was never moved back. After Back or Forward it stayed on the next page as a visible 320×190 box, blocking clicks under it. Reproduced on `/booking`.

The dashboard's own modals (add student, confirm) are state-driven, live inside the page, and never touch `<body>`, so they aren't involved.

## Fix, at the shared level

- **New `src/lib/scroll-lock.ts`:** the one way to lock scrolling.
  - `lockScroll()` returns its own release, so `$effect(() => { if (open) return lockScroll(); })` releases on close and on destroy alike.
  - Locks are counted per page, so one overlay closing can't unlock another that's still open.
  - A release called twice counts once.
  - It never restores a leaked `'hidden'`.
- **Header sidebar and booking sheet** use it. The sheet's old save-and-restore would have saved and restored a leaked `'hidden'`.
- **The home page** calls `closeAllPopups()` in its unmount cleanup, which moves the popups back into its own DOM.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/scroll-lock.test.mjs` (4): lock and restore; two overlays; a double release; a lock taken on a page that already leaked `'hidden'`.
- `tests/unit/no-leaked-page-state.test.mjs` (3):
  - only the helper writes `body.style.overflow` anywhere in `src`
  - the sidebar and the sheet hold the lock through their effect
  - the home page's cleanup closes popups
- Full suite 1214/1214; `check:ci` 22 warnings (baseline).

## Browser QA (built server, the same flows as the reproduction)

- 390px, home → menu → dashboard: the body is locked while the menu is open, released on arrival, and PageDown scrolls to 738.
- 5 cycles in a row (Back, menu, then alternately the dashboard and the portal): locked while the menu is open and `''` after, every time.
- Dashboard → open Noga's student card → PageDown scrolls.
- Popup, Back and Forward: no leftover popups (`0`).
- The booking sheet locks while open, and releases on close.
- 1280px: closing the menu by its overlay releases the lock, and menu → dashboard releases it too.
- No console errors.

author: clickmatos
body:
## Summary

Migration `023_repo_metric_summaries_payload_and_prev.sql` (from #264) fails when applied against the live project:

```
ERROR: 42P16: cannot change name of view column "prev_stabilization_ratio" to "payload"
HINT: Use ALTER VIEW ... RENAME COLUMN ... to change name of view column instead.
```

`CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` requires every pre-existing column to keep its name **and ordinal position** — only appending new columns at the end is allowed. The migration inserted `payload` between `commit_metrics_reliable` and `prev_stabilization_ratio`, shifting every column after it by one position, which Postgres reads as a rename.

## Fix

Reorders the SELECT list: the 18 columns from `022_repo_metric_summaries.sql` keep their original positions, the 5 new ones (`payload`, `prev_created_at`, `prev_revert_rate`, `prev_churn_events`, `prev_ai_detection_coverage_pct`) are appended at the end. No application code changes — every caller (`getOrgLatestPayloads`, `getOrgReposSummary`, `getOrgChangeDetections`) selects by column name, never by position.

## Test plan

- [x] Confirmed the corrected column ordering matches `information_schema.columns` for the currently-deployed 022 view (verified against production before writing the fix)
- [ ] Apply the corrected 023 to the project (`supabase db push`, or paste the view body into the SQL editor) — still a manual step, not run from this environment

author: takecchi
body:
## 何を直したか

`packages/core/src/tools.test.ts` の、目印で出力を切り出してから assert する歯のうち、目印が消えても緑のまま残るものに、切り出す前の `expect(reply).toContain('mgr-2')` を足した（#2434 / #2441 と同じ直し方）。既存の assert は変えていない。直したのは 2 か所（`manager_list` の「lost は done と混ざらない」の `doneEntry` と、システムプロンプトの道具一覧の `# 委譲` 終点）。

`tools.test.ts` を触る open の PR は、着手時（`gh pr list --state open --json number,files`）に 0 本だった。行番号は main 7903bd94 のもの。

Issue: #2431

Alteroid-Issue-Done: 2431

## 探し方

`slice(` / `substring(` / `substr(` / `split(` と `indexOf(` の組み合わせを、このファイルで洗い直した（候補の一覧に頼っていない）。

- `grep -nE "\.(slice|substring|substr)\(" packages/core/src/tools.test.ts`（定数の `slice(0, N)` は除く）と、`split(` を全件、`indexOf(` を全件見た。
- 変数に取ってから切る形は `extractSection`（:16437）、`splitListingEntries`（:16960）、`extractMemorySizeEntries`（:17121）、`withoutRunnerDetail`（:5978）を読んだ。
- `indexOf` 同士の順序比較（`expect(a.indexOf(x)).toBeLessThan(b.indexOf(y))`、約 15 か所）は切り出しではないので、この PR の対象の形ではない。そのうち読んだもの（:1351、:3746、:8104、:11302、:13483）は、直前に `toContain` / `>= 0` か、`-1` が来ると赤になる向きで守られていた。残りは全部は読んでいない。

## 仕分けの表（判定であって実測ではない）

基準: 目印が消えて `slice(-1)` / `slice(0, -1)` / `split` の後半が `''` になったとき、後ろの assert が緑のまま残りうるか。「判定」列は私がコードを読んで下したもの。実測は次の節にあり、この表には含まれない。行番号は main 7903bd94。

| 箇所 | 形 | 切り出し後の assert | 判定 | 対応 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| :3599 `header` | `odd.slice(0, odd.indexOf('# A'))` | `toBe(header)` | 対象外（`odd` はテスト内の定数の入力で、製品の出力ではない。`# A` が消えることがない。直後の `outlineId(h, 'odd', '# A')` も見つからなければ落ちる） | 直さない |
| :13417 `lostEntry` | `slice(indexOf('mgr-1'), indexOf('mgr-2'))` | positive `toContain` x2 | 穴ではない（`mgr-1` が消えれば `''` で赤。`mgr-2` が消えると `slice(i, -1)` で全文近くに広がるが、`doneEntry` 側で見分けられる） | 直さない（`mgr-2` の guard で守られる） |
| :13418 `doneEntry` | `slice(indexOf('mgr-2'))` | `not.toContain('⚠')` | **穴**（`mgr-2` が消えると末尾の 1 文字になり、`not.toContain` は緑） | 直した |
| :14591 `body` | `continuation.split('⚠ 順位が上がった')` の前半 | `not.toContain('mgr-14')` | 穴ではない（`[body]` は前半。目印が消えると全文になり、`not.toContain` は厳しくなる側にしか動かない） | 直さない |
| :15573-15574 `headLine` / `body` | `separatorIndex = reply.indexOf('\n\n')` | `headLine` の `toContain`、`body` の `toContain('文字')` と `not.toContain('bytes=')` | 穴ではない（`-1` だと `body` が `slice(1)` で全文近くになり、head の `bytes=` を含むので `not.toContain('bytes=')` が赤） | 直さない |
| :15759 `section` | `prompt.split('# 道具')[1]?.split('# 委譲')[0]` | 直前に `toBeDefined`、`missing` が空 | 弱い歯（始点は `# 道具` が消えると `undefined` で赤。終点 `# 委譲` が消えると節が `# 道具` 以降の全文に広がり、他の節に出る道具名で照合が通って、一覧からの抜けを見逃しうる。#2441 の `slice(0, indexOf('### 委譲'))` と同じ形） | 直した（切る前に `\n# 道具\n` と `\n# 委譲\n` を確認。`# 委譲` は改行付きで一意にした） |
| :17121-17126 `extractMemorySizeEntries` | `reply.indexOf('## 記憶の大きさ')`、`-1` なら `[]` | 呼び側で `entries.length` が `toBeGreaterThan(0)`（:17203）。合成入力の他の 2 本は `toEqual` で中身を見る | 守られている（`-1` は `[]` を返して呼び側の正の assert が赤） | 直さない |
| :18483-18487 `commitmentsSection` / `jobsSection` | `slice(indexOf('引き受けた仕事'), indexOf('委譲（JOB_APPRAISAL_DECISION_PREFIX）'))` / `slice(indexOf('委譲（…）'))` | positive `toContain` x3 | 穴ではない（始点が消えると `''` か 1 文字で positive が赤。終点が消えると `commitmentsSection` は広がるが `jobsSection` が 1 文字になって赤） | 直さない |
| :16437 `extractSection` | `findIndex`、`-1` なら throw | - | 守られている | 直さない |
| :16960 `splitListingEntries` | 正規表現で行を拾う | - | 対象外（目印による切り出しではない） | 直さない |
| :5978 `withoutRunnerDetail` | `reply.split(transcribed).join('')` | 直前に `toContain(transcribed)` | 守られている | 直さない |
| :11019 | `expect(reply.split('器の合計であって内訳ではない')).toHaveLength(2)` | - | 切り出しではなく、それ自体が guard | 直さない |
| :15695、:2612、:6805 ほか `split('\n')` / `split('。')` | 行・句の分割 | - | 対象外（目印による切り出しではない） | 直さない |

## 陰性対照の結果（ここは実測）

製品コード `packages/core/src/tools.ts` の `manager_list` の行の id（`id: manager.managerId,`、:11092）を Edit で一時的に変え、`src/tools.test.ts -t 'lost は done と混ざらない'` を回した。回し終えたら戻した（`git status` は `tools.test.ts` 1 本のみ）。

- MA: `id: manager.managerId.replace('mgr-2', 'mgr_2'),`（`mgr-2` だけが出力から消える）
- MB: `id: manager.managerId.replace('mgr-1', 'mgr_1'),`（`mgr-1` だけが消える）

| 何を回したか | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 直す前のテスト + MA | 1 passed（緑のまま。`doneEntry` の穴が実際に残る） |
| 直す前のテスト + MB | 1 failed（`expected '' to contain '⚠'` at :13420。`lostEntry` が `''` になる。穴ではない、という判定と合う） |
| 直した後のテスト + MA | 1 failed（`expected '件数: 全 2 本 / …' to contain 'mgr-2'`。足した guard が赤） |

:15759 の弱い歯（製品側 `packages/core/src/prompt.ts:155` の見出し `# 委譲` を `# 任せ方` に一時的に変えて、`-t 'CLONE_TOOL_NAMES の全部が載っている'` を回した。戻してある）:

| 何を回したか | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 直す前のテスト + 見出し変更 | 1 passed（緑のまま） |
| 直した後のテスト + 見出し変更 | 1 failed（`expected 'あなたは、ある人間の価値観をコピーしたクローンである。…' to contain '\n# 委譲\n'`） |

限界: 穴は 1 か所なので、変異も 1 か所ずつである。直した後のテストに MB は当てていない（穴ではないので、guard を足していない）。他の「穴ではない」の判定（表の :14591、:15573、:18483 など）は、読んだ結果であって、変異では確かめていない。

## 確認

- `packages/core` の `vitest run src/tools.test.ts` を 1 回（930 tests 通過）。
- `tsc --noEmit`（`packages/core`）は、`node packages/core/scripts/write-canon.mjs` で canon の生成物を作った上で、エラーなし。生成物はコミットしていない。
- `eslint packages/core/src/tools.test.ts` と `prettier --check` は通過。
- 確認していない: 全リポジトリの `pnpm test` 一括と CI。

## #2431 の対象を全部扱ったこと

| PR | 扱ったファイル |
|---|---|
| #2434 | `appraisal.test.ts`、`memory.test.ts`、`prompt.test.ts`、`apps/cli/src/permission.test.ts`、`archive-remove-many.test.ts`、`inbox-remove-many.test.ts`、`commitment-close-many.test.ts`、および穴ではないと仕分けた残り（`digest`、`excerpt`、`clone-memory-injection`、`daemon index`、`swr` ほか）。`practice-candidates.test.ts` と `tools.test.ts` は open の PR と重なるので除いた |
| #2441 | `practice-candidates.test.ts` |
| この PR | `tools.test.ts` |

この 3 本で、#2431 が挙げた対象（Issue の 29 か所と、広げた形）のうち、重なりで除いていた 2 ファイルまで扱い終えた。残りは無いので、この PR の本文に `Alteroid-Issue-Done: 2431` を書いた。

author: voluntas
body:
## 概要

moqt-devtools で音声の再生を有効にすると映像の表示が遅れる (利用者の確認)。同じ経路・同じ時間帯で購読を 2 つ繋いで片方だけ音声を再生して比べると、映像の表示の遅延が 49.8 ms 増えていた。あわせて、目標の時刻を過ぎて届いた音と前の音と重なる音が捨てられ、実測で毎秒 8.5 個 (17%) の音が欠けていた。

原因は 2 つある。表示の遅れを音声と映像で 1 つ共有していたため、音声の jitter buffer の遅れ (下限 80 ms) が映像にも乗っていたこと。遅れて届いた音を捨てることで遅延を抑えており、遅延を抑えるか音を守るかのどちらかしか選べなかったことである。

音声の遅れは経路の揺らぎから決まる量であるため、到着の遅れの分布から求めるようにし、遅れて届いた音は捨てずに時間圧縮で目標へ戻すようにした。

## 変更内容

- `src/streamSynchronization.ts` (新規): 2 つのトラックの遅延を相対的に制御する。ずれ (映像の遅延 - 音声の遅延 + 経路の相対遅延) が 30 ms 未満の間は動かさず、超えたときだけ片側を 1 秒に 1 回 80 ms まで動かす。定数と計算は libwebrtc の `video/stream_synchronization.cc` の `ComputeDelays` と同じにする
- `src/audioDelayManager.ts` (新規): 音声の目標遅延を到着の遅れの分布から求める。直近 2 秒の窓で最も早く届いた観測を基準にした相対遅延を 500 ms ごとの最大値だけ 20 ms バケット (100 個) のヒストグラムへ入れ、0.95 分位から `(1 + バケット) * 20 ms` を目標にする。忘れ係数 0.983、観測が無い間は 80 ms
- `src/audioTimeStretch.ts` (新規): 波形の周期 (ピッチ) 1 つ分を削る時間圧縮と挿す時間伸長。第 1 チャンネルを 4 kHz へ間引いた自己相関で周期を求め、切れ目の前後の相関が 0.9 より大きいときだけ操作する
- `src/playbackTimeline.ts`: 表示の遅れをトラックごとに決める。同期は 1 秒ごとに両方のトラックへ新しい観測があるときだけ行う。`targetLatency` は 2 つの遅れの下限にする。基準の差が閾値を超えたときのフォールバックは従来のまま残す
- `src/audioPlayout.ts`: 目標を過ぎた音と重なる音を捨てず、今から鳴らせる最も早い時刻へずらして鳴らし、ずらした分を詰める量として返す。詰められなかった分は遅れとして持ち越し、目標から 500 ms 以上離れたら一度捨てる。目標の間隔と音の長さが同じときの浮動小数点の誤差 (10^-13 秒) を重なりとみなして音が 1 つおきに欠ける不具合も直す
- `devtools/src/hooks/useSubscriber.ts` / `src/createMediaSubscriber.ts`: 予約の前に波形の周期で詰め、実際に詰めた長さを返す
- `docs/HIGH_LEVEL_API.md` と `CHANGES.md` の `## develop` を更新する

## 完了条件

- [x] 経路が良いとき、音声を再生しても映像の表示の遅延が増えない (音声 OFF 101.1 ms / 音声 ON 101.3 ms)
- [x] 経路が悪いときも音が欠けない (90 秒に 770 個 → 0。映像の遅延は音声の jitter buffer に追随し、ずれは 30 ms 以内)
- [x] 音声の目標遅延が到着の遅れの分布から決まる (一定の遅れでは上がらない) ことをテストで固定
- [x] 遅れて届いた音が数フレームで目標へ戻り、遅れが積み上がらないことをテストで固定
- [x] `vp check` / `tsc --noEmit` / `vp test run` (3525 テスト) が通る
- [x] `CHANGES.md` の `## develop` に `[CHANGE]` と `[FIX]` が入る

## 関連 issue

- issues/closed/0782-bug-audio-playback-delays-video.md
- issues/closed/0783-bug-audio-playout-drops.md

## 後方互換

`MediaReceiverStats.avSync` の意味は変わらない (映像の表示の遅れを返す)。A/V のずれは最大 30 ms 程度になる (従来は 0 ms)。

author: patrickbradley-cog
body: ## Summary Linear: [COG-1153 — W1 · AppointmentResource.confirm → POST (server + Angular caller)](https://linear.app/cog-gtm/issue/COG-1153/w1-appointmentresourceconfirm-post-server-angular-caller) `AppointmentResource.confirm` was mapped with `@RequestMapping("/{id}/confirm")` (no method), so it answered **GET**. `CsrfFilter` only checks non-safe methods, so once W2 turns CSRF on this mutation would stay unprotected (`` confirms with the admin's session cookie). This converts it to POST now, while CSRF is still off, together with its single caller — behaviour-neutral on Boot 1.5.4, no Boot/Java bump. ```diff - @RequestMapping("/{id}/confirm") + @PostMapping("/{id}/confirm") public void confirmAppointment(@PathVariable("id") Long id) ``` ```diff // AdminPortal/src/app/appointment.service.ts - return this.http.get(url, { withCredentials: true }); + // X-XSRF-TOKEN added only if an XSRF-TOKEN cookie exists (none today, CSRF is off) + return this.http.post(url, null, { headers, withCredentials: true }); ``` - No shared AdminPortal CSRF helper exists on `master` yet, so a small private `readCookie` lives in `AppointmentService`; switch to the shared helper when the AdminPortal CSRF ticket lands. - Since the header is only sent when the cookie exists, today's request is still a CORS "simple" request (no preflight). Once CSRF is on, `RequestFilter`'s preflight `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` must include `x-xsrf-token` — that belongs to the CORS/CSRF tickets, not this one. - Added `AppointmentResourceTest` (standalone MockMvc + Mockito, no DB): POST → 200 and calls `confirmAppointment(42)`; GET → 405 and never calls the service. ### Merge order / smoke suite Merge **behind the W0 smoke suite**. The appointment smoke test lives in unmerged https://github.com/COG-GTM/Online-Banking-with-Java-Spring-Boot-Angular-2/pull/108 (`AppointmentSmokeTest.confirmsAppointmentOverGet`) and asserts `get(".../confirm")` → 200. **That test will fail once this PR lands.** It has to be flipped to `post(...)` (and renamed, e.g. `confirmsAppointmentOverPost`) in whichever PR merges second. I didn't edit it here because the file doesn't exist on `master`, and adding it would overlap with #108. ### Verification **Build/tests** — Temurin 8u504, MySQL 5.7 in docker (`SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=...?useSSL=false`; JDK 8u504 rejects the old connector's TLS): ``` $ mvn -B -f UserFront/pom.xml verify Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 - in com.userFront.resource.AppointmentResourceTest Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 - in com.userFront.UserFrontApplicationTests Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 BUILD SUCCESS ``` AdminPortal (Node 12): `ng build` succeeds. `ng lint` shows 6 errors that also exist on `master`, in other files (navbar, app.module, specs), and none in `appointment.service.ts`. **Running app** (`mvn spring-boot:run`: signed up `admin`, gave it ROLE_ADMIN, logged in through `POST /index`, created an appointment through `POST /appointment/create`): ``` --- GET /api/appointment/1/confirm {"status":405,"error":"Method Not Allowed","message":"Request method 'GET' not supported",...} HTTP 405 id confirmed 1 0 --- POST /api/appointment/1/confirm HTTP 200 id confirmed 1 1 --- unauthenticated POST HTTP 302 -> http://localhost:8080/index ``` Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7a967fb2d2c64eee91e222975dbc2ecb Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/7a967fb2d2c64eee91e222975dbc2ecb?variant=devin Requested by: @patrickbradley-cog --- #### Devin Review | Status | Commit | |---|---| | ⚪ Not started | — | > [Run Devin Review](https://staging.itsdev.in/review/cog-gtm/online-banking-with-java-spring-boot-angular-2/pull/336?analyze=true) ---

author: alice39s
body:
Branch `docs/fumadocs` → `feat/worker-proxy`. Top of the stack; merge last, after #1, #2 and #3.

## Why

The documentation was spread over `README.md`, `README.en.md`, `cli/README.md`, `cli/WORKFLOW.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `data/README.md` and package READMEs, partly in one language only, with no search, no cross-links and no place for the tokenizer, CORS and Worker features of #1, #2 and #3.

## What

- Add `docs/`, a React Router 8 SPA with Fumadocs 16 (Base UI) and Fumadocs MDX 15, pre-rendered in full at build time and published by `bun run build` into `web/dist/docs`.
- Add Chinese (`/docs`) and English (`/docs/en`) pages for every section, with fallback to Chinese for a missing translation and a language switch that keeps the page.
- Add `remarkContentLinks`: links to content files (`../cli/detect.mdx#options`, also in `<Card href>`) become page URLs of the reader's language at compile time, in pages, Markdown twins and `llms-full.txt`; a link to a missing file fails the build.
- Add `DOCS_BASE` (must end in `/docs`) and `SITE_ORIGIN` to `docs/site.config.ts` for sub-path deployments and absolute Open Graph URLs.
- Add static multilingual search, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, a Markdown twin per page (Copy Markdown, open in ChatGPT/Claude), last-modified dates from Git, and edit-on-GitHub links.
- Add Open Graph images per page with Takumi, registering Geist and Noto Sans SC so Chinese titles render.
- Add MDX support for Mermaid, KaTeX, step headings, file trees, tabs, accordions, type tables and zoomable images.
- Add proxy API reference pages generated by `fumadocs-openapi` from the new `worker/openapi.json`, with a request playground.
- Render the tokenizer class table and the first-party model mapping directly from `data/tokenizer_bank.json`.
- Include `web/design.md` in the development section instead of copying it.
- Move the shared color tokens and brand fonts into `web/src/tokens.css`; the docs import the same file and share the `fp-theme` preference with the detector.
- Add a Docs link to the detector header and point the CLI card at the matching docs page.
- Move the long-form content out of the READMEs, delete `cli/WORKFLOW.md` and `docs/deployment.md`, and turn `data/`, `shared/` and `web/` READMEs into pointers.
- Set `DOCS_BASE` and `SITE_ORIGIN` in the GitHub Pages workflow; add cache and content-type rules for the docs to `web/public/_headers`.
- Document the prompt replacement for abnormal samples from upstream `4323f40` in the web and CLI pages, and add the 2026-09-30 data change (GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude label normalization, `gpt-6-sol-20260922` retired) to the data change log.

## How verified

- `bun run build` (sync data, typecheck web/CLI/docs, build web, build and publish docs): pass in ~14 s, 48 pages pre-rendered, no network access during the build.
- A temporary page linking to `./no-such-page.mdx` fails the build with `points at no content file`; 0 `.mdx` hrefs remain in the pre-rendered HTML.
- `DOCS_BASE=/lm-detector/docs SITE_ORIGIN=https://ikaleio.github.io bun run --cwd docs build`: output under `build/client/lm-detector/docs`, `og:url` `https://ikaleio.github.io/lm-detector/docs/cli/detect`, links and Markdown twins under `/lm-detector/docs`. `DOCS_BASE=/manual` is rejected.
- An independent review of the diff against the code (CLI options, exit codes, proxy, tokenizer constants, data files) found 10 mismatches; all are fixed in this branch.
- `wrangler pages dev web/dist` on `127.0.0.1:8789`:

  | Path | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | `/`, `/docs/`, `/docs.data`, `/docs/en.data`, `/docs/cli/detect.data` | 200 |
  | `/docs/api/search` | 200, `application/json`, served with `br` |
  | `/docs/llms.txt`, `/docs/llms-full.txt`, `/docs/en/llms.mdx/cli/detect/content.md` | 200 |
  | `/docs/og/principles/tokenizer/image.png` | 200, `image/png` |
  | `/docs/no-such-page` | 404 with the docs not-found page |
  | `/api/proxy` (GET) | 200 health JSON |
  | `/docs/assets/*` | `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` |

- Chromium via Playwright on the pre-rendered site:
  - Docs link in the detector header opens `/docs/`; a dark theme chosen in the detector applies in the docs.
  - Client navigation fetches `/docs/cli.data`; search finds Chinese (`后验`) and English (`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) results in the current language.
  - Language switch from `/docs/principles/tokenizer` lands on `/docs/en/principles/tokenizer`.
  - Tokenizer page: 1 Mermaid SVG, 15 KaTeX nodes, a 62-row class table; OpenAPI page renders the playground and code samples.
  - `scrollWidth == clientWidth` at 390 px on `/docs/cli/detect/`.

author: thasmorato
body:
Stacked on #17 (the v0.5 base).

## Why
Technical debt is detected in four places (the architecture report, the component analyses, the reconciler, and the review's `pre-existing` verdict) and aggregated nowhere. A `pre-existing` finding is real, but it sits in code the diff did not change. Nobody owns it, so it disappears once the review is done.

## What
- **`retro` skill: new "Debt the reviews saw and nobody owned" section, plus workflow step 6.** It:
  - collects every `pre-existing` finding in the scope and groups them by component, or by directory when there is no component map;
  - marks an area as a hotspot when **two or more tickets** hit it, citing any `docs/analysis/components/<c>.md` debt for the same area as corroboration;
  - proposes **at most 3** structural tickets, ranked by benefit (severity × tickets that hit it) against cost (what the fix touches), each citing the findings it would close. The remaining hotspots are listed, not proposed.

  Nothing is created. If the owner picks a proposal, it becomes a `Type: structural` ticket with Source `retro — docs/retro/<scope>.md`.
- **`templates/retro.md`:** a new **Debt hotspots** section, and a pre-existing count under Measurements.

There is no new agent and no maintained roadmap: `/flow` refuses maintained documents, and the retro is append-only history. The cap of 3 matches the reconciler's.

## Gears
The owner invokes `/retro` over a finished epic or cycle. It has no gate.

## Test
`node --test scripts/*.test.mjs`: 38/38. Frontmatter parses as strict YAML. This PR only changes prompt text; no executable behavior changes.

body:
Part of [ISS 1469](https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1469), answering OpenSSF Baseline `OSPS-VM-04.02`. `generate_sbom.py` reads the tree's `.github/vex.toml`, from the tree the archive was built from. It then writes each finding into the CycloneDX 1.6 document as a `vulnerabilities` entry with `analysis.state` `not_affected`. The field mapping and the component resolution are the ones section 12 of btclib-org/.github's `README.md` states:
- a distribution is found by its PEP 503 name;
- a vendored submodule is found by its upstream repository name;
- a name that is ambiguous, or that the document does not carry, is refused.

A tree with no file gets no `vulnerabilities` key. An empty or malformed file stops the run, with a message that names the file.

Cleared locally over five review rounds. The reviewer validated one real document per variant against the CycloneDX 1.6 schema. The gates were green on the parent this lands on.

A rejected `validate_code` echoed the caller's literal path in its `structuredContent` (`explanation` and `metadata.accessed_types`/`accessed_fields`), even though the refusal message was value-free. author: amandaseibel-dev
body:
Última entrega do escopo. Ideias da equipe e a reorganização da Home.

⚠️ **A migration NÃO foi aplicada em produção.** Fica em `supabase/aguardando_aprovacao/20260930190000_portal_ideias_equipe.sql`. Enquanto não for aplicada, o card não aparece na Home.

## Não cria tabela de ideias

A fonte é `public.sugestoes`, que já existe com 48 registros e com a coluna `visivel_equipe` — criada em `20260806130000` justamente para marcar o que a equipe pode ver. **17 já estão marcadas**, então o mural nasce com conteúdo real.

## O problema resolvido

`sugestoes_select` restringe a leitura a `usuario_e_gestao_fila()` — a equipe não lê sugestão nenhuma, **nem a própria**. Afrouxar exporia tratativa interna, anexo, prioridade e retorno ao operador.

Então **a policy fica intocada** e o mural sai por `portal_ideias_equipe()`, `SECURITY DEFINER`.

| o mural devolve | o que nunca sai |
|---|---|
| `id` (para curtir) | `autor_email` |
| `descricao` | `observacao_tratativa` |
| `autor` (a coluna `nome`) | `motivo_impacto`, `retorno_operador` |
| `criado_em` | `anexo_path`, `anexo_nome` |
| `status` | `prioridade`, `tela`, `area`, `tipo` |
| `curtidas`, `eu_curti` | `status_por`, `status_em`, `validado_em` |

Há teste que serializa a linha e verifica que nenhum desses valores aparece, e outro que assere a assinatura exata.

**A gestão segue mandando:** só entra o que tem `visivel_equipe = true`, e quem liga essa marca continua sendo a gestão pelo Painel de Sugestões. A migration **só lê**: não escreve em `sugestoes`, não muda status e não mexe em `visivel_equipe` — e há teste reaplicando a migration e conferindo que uma sugestão fica idêntica.

## Status: o domínio real, não o desejado

Conferido em produção: **`FEITA` (43), `DESCARTADA` (2), `REABERTO` (2), `NOVA` (1)**, sem CHECK — o domínio é definido pelo fluxo existente.

A migration não mexe nisso. A tela **traduz**:

| banco | tela |
|---|---|
| `NOVA` | Nova |
| `REABERTO` | Reaberta |
| `FEITA` | Implementada |
| `DESCARTADA` | Não seguirá |

**"Em análise" e "Aprovada" não existem no fluxo atual e por isso não aparecem** — criá-las seria vocabulário que a gestão não teria como preencher. Status desconhecido aparece capitalizado em vez de sumir, então um status novo no Painel não quebra o mural nem exige deploy.

## Ordenação

"Mais curtidas" e "Mais recentes" vêm do banco, porque a primeira depende da contagem. As duas terminam em desempate determinístico, para a lista não trocar de ordem sozinha entre dois carregamentos. Ideia sem curtida aparece com zero, não some.

## Home reorganizada

```
Faixa 1   🎵 Música mais curtida da semana        (largura cheia)
Faixa 2   ⭐ Elogios da equipe | 🎯 Desafio da semana
Faixa 3   🎧 Playlist ReATIVA  | 💡 Ideias da equipe
Depois    clima, eventos, aniversários, feriados, curiosidade
```

Tudo em `src/components/portal/`: `PortalOperacional.jsx` **não cresceu** e `VisaoGeralInterativa.jsx` passou a compor em vez de acumular.

### Dois defeitos visuais corrigidos

Renderizei a Visão Geral real num preview com dublê de Supabase (descartável, fora deste PR) e olhei em desktop e em 375px. Apareceram dois problemas que só a tela revela:

1. **Token inexistente:** eu usava `var(--rv-verde, #16a34a)` na barra cumprida. O token real é `--rv-verde-ok` — o fallback mascarava o erro. Trocado.
2. **Faixa da música quebrada no celular:** as três colunas fixas colidiam a 375px, o título virava `Vo…` e "Escolhida por" passava por cima da contagem. Virou flex com `flexWrap`, e o título passou a quebrar em vez de virar reticências — é o elemento principal da faixa. Sem media query, coerente com o resto do arquivo.

## Testes

- `supabase/tests/portal_ideias_equipe.test.js` — 19 testes, migration e rollback reais em PostgreSQL real (PGlite), com as policies reais de `sugestoes` reproduzidas, **inclusive `painel_negado` como RESTRICTIVE** (conferido em `pg_policies.permissive` de produção; como PERMISSIVE ela seria OR com `sugestoes_select` e liberaria leitura para todos — o oposto do que o nome diz)
- `IdeiasEquipe.test.jsx` — 12 testes de interface

## Verificações

- testes do bloco ✅ 89
- suíte completa com todos os blocos ✅ **159 arquivos, 3021 testes**
- `npm run build` ✅
- `npm run check:migrations` ✅ `migrations novas: 0`

## What is in the change

  Its build action covers `OpenJevCore` and `OpenJevCoreTests`, its test action runs
  `OpenJevCoreTests`. A package opens in Xcode with autogenerated schemes, which are per-user and
  are never written to disk, so the job needs a committed one. `.gitignore` now allows that single
  path and keeps ignoring the rest of `.swiftpm`, `xcuserdata` included.
- **The `iOS` job.** It pins Xcode 26.6 through `DEVELOPER_DIR` and checks the version the same
  way the `macOS` job does, restores the SwiftPM checkouts that `xcodebuild` keeps under
  `.build/ios/SourcePackages` with a key shaped like the `macOS` job's, resolves the packages,
  runs `xcodebuild test` on `platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro,OS=latest`, checks the
  saved log with `.github/scripts/check-test-log.sh`, and uploads the `.xcresult` bundle when a
  step failed.
- **A build-only step** compiles `OpenJevDiffusionGemma` for `generic/platform=iOS Simulator`, so
  the target keeps compiling for the iOS 17 it declares. mlx-swift compiles for the simulator,
  arm64 and x86_64 both, and the Metal Toolchain step of the `macOS` job is carried over for its
  shaders. Only the build runs: the tests need weights that no iOS device holds. It runs even
  when the tests failed, so one push reports both.
- **A preflight step** fails with a readable message when the image holds no `iPhone 17 Pro` on
  the newest runtime, or more than one. A device name that matches none or several makes
  `xcodebuild` print a wall of destinations instead, and that is exactly what a developer machine
  with two simulators of one name does.
- **`docs/development.md`** gains the job in the CI table, the local commands, the rule that
  everything the iOS scheme builds must compile without Hummingbird and without MLX-only APIs,
  and notes on the cache, the log check and the required checks.

## Fixtures need no change

The core tests find `Fixtures/` through a path derived from `#filePath`. That works unchanged in
the simulator, which runs on the host and reads the checkout in place. All 192 tests in 28 suites
pass on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator with no skips, and `check-test-log.sh` accepts the
`xcodebuild test` log as is, so no move to SwiftPM test resources and no decision entry.

## The breakage experiment

A temporary file in `OpenJevCore` that imported AppKit and read
`NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication` was built for the simulator locally. The build failed:

```
Sources/OpenJevCore/TemporaryIOSBreakageProbe.swift:2:8: error: Unable to resolve module dependency: 'AppKit'
** BUILD FAILED **
```

The file was deleted afterwards and is not part of this branch. The macOS-only API a `swift
build` on a Mac accepts is therefore caught by this job.

## Not in this change

The `Linux` and `macOS` jobs are untouched, and no source or test file changes.

author: nawid3333
body:
Review items N1, N2, N3, N5 and OPEN-FIXES H1-H6 (review of 2026-09-30).

## The problem
A web page that read FastStream's address from a player iframe's `src` could frame `player/index.html#<url>?faststream-headers={"Referer":"x’;…;’"}` itself. If you clicked the mpv button in that player, the Referer went to the native host unchecked. The host put mpv's command line into its PowerShell script as a single-quoted string and escaped only the ASCII `'`. PowerShell also ends such a string at the typographic quotes U+2018-U+201B, so the value closed the string and the rest ran as code.

## Fixes
**Native host**
- mpv's command line reaches PowerShell through an environment variable. The script text never contains data. This also removes the ~9 KB URL limit of `-EncodedCommand` (H2).
- Only Referer, Origin and User-Agent are passed on, and only with printable-ASCII values.
- A message's length prefix is capped at 1 MB.
- `fs-*` tags a page put in the URL's fragment are dropped (N5).
- Only an executable named `mpv*` is started, never a UNC or device path. A UNC path is not even `stat`ed.
- H1: on Windows there is no direct-spawn fallback any more. Firefox kills that mpv when the host exits, so it used to report success while nothing played.
- H3: "mpv quit right after it started" comes after ~2 s instead of a 30 s wait.
- H5: a lock around loading into the running mpv, so two sends a few milliseconds apart can't swap headers.

**Extension**
- `MpvBackend` checks header values the same way the host does.
- A player inside a page ignores a source in its own address. The extension only puts one in a tab of its own: the stream-URL redirect is `main_frame` only. The copy-URL links still work in a tab.
- N2: header rules get `initiatorDomains` = the extension's host. Before, the page's own requests in that tab got the player's Origin/Referer/Cookie for 5 s.
- N3: `player/options/index.html` is no longer web-accessible. Only the player frames it.

**Installer (H4):** `install.ps1` writes UTF-8 without BOM, and the `.bat` runs `chcp 65001`. A non-ASCII user folder no longer breaks every path. New `-InstallDir`/`-NoRegister` switches exist for tests.

**CI:** the Windows job also runs the unit suite, so the tests that need the real PowerShell run there too.

**Docs:** CLAUDE.md (the chain and each layer; H6's stale "no suite covers the host"), native-host/README.md.

## Tests, each shown to fail without its fix
- `mpvHostSecurity.test.mjs`: runs the real WMI launch script in the real PowerShell, with `Invoke-CimMethod` stubbed, for all five quote characters. When the old splicing is put back, the payload runs. Also header values, `fs-*` tags, the message cap.
- `mpvHostInstall.test.mjs` (Windows): installs under `José 中文`, then pings the host through the written `.bat` the way Firefox starts it. It fails with ASCII writes, with a UTF-8 BOM, and without `chcp`.
- `mpvHostPath.test.mjs`: the name check, and no `stat` of UNC/device paths. `MpvNativeHost.test.mjs`: the lock, including two concurrent `loadIntoExisting`. `MpvBackend`, `NetRequestRuleManager`.
- `ext-specs/framed-player.e2e.mjs` on Firefox 156: 4 tests. With the three browser-side fixes reverted, all 3 attack tests failed on both attempts. They showed the forged Referer being sent, the page's request going out with `Origin: https://victim.test`, and the options page loading inside the page. The control still passed: a player tab takes its address's source, and its own request still gets the header rule.
- Unit mutations: 16 of 16 caught.

## Local runs
`pnpm run lint`, `typecheck`, `pnpm test` (772 passed), and the extension specs framed-player, header-rules, options-mpv and keybinds-storage, all green. No full verify, per the batch rule.

After merging: run `native-host/install.ps1` again (issue #73). The installed host copy doesn't update itself.

Geometry, scale, transforms and ordered path data agree in the independent artifact check; full GUI/headless byte or style equivalence is not claimed. The GUI proof covers highlighted rows, not the preserved failing preselected-object route. The blocked B16 repair and its locked evidence remain unchanged.

No product behavior, B14/B15 reference, shared normalizer, fixture, schema or authority changes. Hook investigation remains closed; accepted PR #81/#99 controls remain unchanged. author: e54-bot
body:
## Summary

`wright check` accepted OPY settings keys that `wright compile` then rejected during Workshop emission (`error[workshop-emission]: ... is outside the emission table`). Two coordinated changes fix the reproducer and the check/compile divergence:

- **workshop-rs** (wrightkit/workshop-rs#334, merged-side contract): `gamemodes.<mode>` leaf lookups fall back to the `gamemodes.general` entry — the pinned 9.7.10 oracle merges `general.values` into every declared mode (`elimination` inherits only its reviewed 12-key subset). The fallback returns the general `TableEntry`, so `gamemodes.ffa.enableKillCam` shares the canonical `gamemodes.general.enableKillCam` identity and emits `Kill Cam: Off` in the `Deathmatch` block. Also adds the public `settings::check_emission(&Settings)` validator.
- **opy-rs** (this PR): the HIR→canonical-settings conversion (constant expansion + `#!extension` merge) is extracted into `compiler::settings::workshop_settings`, now shared by lowering and `tooling::check`. `check` runs `check_emission` on the converted tree and surfaces each offender as a `workshop-emission` diagnostic at its source span — the same code `compile` reports.

## Verification

- Reproducer from #411 compiles: emits `Deathmatch { enabled maps { Workshop Island } Kill Cam: Off }`, matching `overpy@9.7.10` byte-structure (native emitter whitespace aside).
- `gamemodes.ffa.notASetting` now fails `check` **and** `compile` with the identical `workshop-emission` diagnostic at `main.opy` span.
- `gamemodes.elimination.enableKillCam` compiles (it is in the oracle's restricted elimination copy list); `gamemodes.elimination.heroLimit` is rejected — the oracle emits it verbatim, a deliberate difference of our canonical table.
- `gamemodes.general.enableKillCam` still compiles; `#!extension` valid/invalid inputs stay consistent across check/compile.
- Gates (run with a local path patch to the workshop-rs worktree): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features` (447 lib + all integration suites), `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/overpy/tests` — all green.

## Contract note

`CompileReport.compile.failureClass` for emission-table failures changes `integration` → `frontend` — the failure genuinely moved into the check stage (`compile_with_overlay_outcome` wraps `check`). Diagnostic code, message, and span are unchanged.

## Merge order

**Blocked on a workshop-rs release ≥ 1.3.0** containing wrightkit/workshop-rs#334 (`check_emission` + the table inheritance). The pin `workshop-rs = "^1.3.0"` intentionally cannot resolve yet; after the release ships, `cargo update -p workshop-rs` on this branch makes CI green. Merge workshop-rs#334 → publish → refresh this branch.

## Residual boundaries (not in scope)

- Upstream emits unknown keys inside groups verbatim (`notASetting: 3`); our canonical table rejects them — now consistently in both `check` and `compile`.
- Upstream `gamemodeKw` modes our catalog does not cover (`*BalancedOverwatch`, `*Community`, OW1-only `lucioball`, `yetiHunter`, ...) do not inherit `general` keys here since they have no reviewed table entries; upstream would emit canonical lines for the OW2-available subset.

## Test plan

- [x] `gamemode_kill_cam_compiles_into_the_deathmatch_block` (compiler regression for the #411 reproducer)
- [x] `settings_emission_agreement_between_check_and_compile` (tooling: shared verdict + code + span)
- [x] Full workspace suite + pinned oracle differential suite green
- [ ] CI green after workshop-rs ≥ 1.3.0 lands

Fixes #411

author: mudler-agent
body:
## Summary

Adds a `tensorfold` Python gRPC backend that runs [TensorFold](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold) (pinned to v0.5.0, commit 9cd52ab) inside the backend process, plus gallery entries and docs. TensorFold has no embedding API, so `LoadModel` runs upstream's own `cmd_serve` and captures the app it builds (`ChatApp` on MLX, `cuda.server.App` on CUDA) at the point where it would start its HTTP server. Two thin adapters then drive that app in-process, with reasoning split, tool calls, streaming and cancellation.

- Options (`key:value`) map onto `tensorfold serve` flags; upstream's argparse validates values and supplies defaults. An unknown key fails the load.
- `LoadModel` refuses checkpoints TensorFold does not serve before any weights are downloaded, and refuses GPUs below compute capability 9.0.
- `test_embed_surface.py` pins every upstream symbol the backend touches; a CI job (`tests-tensorfold`) runs it, so a bad upstream bump turns red.
- Engine ranking: `tensorfold` is ranked on Apple silicon and CUDA 13 hosts only (below vllm/sglang/mlx, above llama.cpp).
- Gallery: `qwen3.8-27b`, `nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b`, `gemma-4-26b-a4b` and `qwen3.8-flash-next`, each as `<name>:tensorfold`. `dflash` is tagged only where the entry sets a drafter.
- Docs: `docs/content/features/tensorfold.md`, the backends list, and the tagging table.

## Scope and what is NOT in this PR

- **Apple Silicon (metal) only for now.** The CUDA 13 image, its index entries, the frozen CUDA requirements and the toolchain packaging need a hardware spike (kernels compile at first load and need nvcc in the image) and follow separately. `requirements-cublas13.txt` / `requirements-l4t13.txt` are placeholders until then; no Linux matrix entry builds them. The NVFP4 gallery entry is held back for the same reason.
- No GLM-5.3-Flash (needs two GPU ranks), no embeddings/TTS/ASR, no vision-by-URL.

## Verification

- Unit tests: 92 pass (fakes); the 8 upstream-symbol tests pass against real TensorFold v0.5.0 source.
- `go test ./pkg/system/... ./core/gallery/... ./core/http/endpoints/localai/...` pass; all touched YAML parses.
- A real `load_engine` call against a bogus repo, a non-existent directory and a non-TensorFold checkpoint returns a `LoadError` quickly, before any weight download; `backend.py` serves Health over real gRPC.
- **Not verified:** an MLX or CUDA run on real hardware, the Docker image build, `make lint`, and the coverage gate. CI should cover the image build and lint; the hardware run is still to do, which is why this is a draft.

## Notes for review

- The engine-ranking change updates two existing pinned expectations (NVIDIA order in `pkg/system` and `core/gallery`), and splits the NVIDIA rule by capability so CUDA 12 hosts never rank an engine with no image.
- Design spec and plan are not part of the PR.

can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #151622

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: remote-node `exec` approvals always fail with "approval id does not match request" when the node-side prepared plan carries no session key, so the command never runs and its outcome becomes unknown.

## User Impact

User impact: `exec host=node` on a paired remote node completes its normal approval flow and executes, instead of permanently failing with an unknown command outcome and requiring manual verification on the node.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stored approval binding is created by `resolveSystemRunApprovalRequestContext`, which resolves each identity field as `plan?.field ?? params.field`. The runtime check rebuilds the binding with `resolveSystemRunApprovalRuntimeContext`, which read those fields from the plan only. A node-side `system.run.prepare` does not know the gateway session key, so its plan has no `sessionKey`: the runtime context resolved `sessionKey` to `null`, the strict binding comparison failed (`null !== "agent:main:..."`), and every run was rejected before reaching the node. The change gives the runtime context the same params fallback the request context uses for `cwd`, `agentId`, and `sessionKey`. Precedence is unchanged (plan values still win), and the strict equality match is untouched, so a runtime value that differs from the stored binding still fails closed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the mismatch shape from #151622 at the unit level: a plan without identity fields plus explicit runtime params now resolves `sessionKey`/`agentId`/`cwd` from the fallback instead of `null` (`resolveSystemRunApprovalRuntimeContext > falls back to explicit runtime params when the plan omits identity fields`), and plan values still take precedence over params when both are present.
- New tests: 2 added to `src/infra/system-run-approval-context.test.ts`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on the affected suites: `system-run-approval-context.test.ts`, `node-invoke-system-run-approval.test.ts`, `node-invoke-system-run-approval-match.test.ts` — 59 passed.
- Adjacent suites `exec-approval-manager.test.ts`, `system-run-approval-binding.contract.test.ts`, `system-run-approval-binding.test.ts`, `server-methods/approval.test.ts`, `gateway.hosted-routing.test.ts` — 120 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors; `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.

author: fujitsupolycom
body:
`sparkring install` and `sparkring up PROFILE` accept optional per-deployment serving settings. Each replaces one value of the profile's vLLM configuration; without a flag, the profile's value applies.

| Flag | vLLM value it replaces |
|---|---|
| `--max-images N` | the image count in `--limit-mm-per-prompt` (0 accepts none) |
| `--max-videos N` | the video count in `--limit-mm-per-prompt` (0 accepts none) |
| `--context-length N` | `--max-model-len` |
| `--max-concurrency N` | `--max-num-seqs` |
| `--kv-cache-gib N` | `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`, at most a tenth above the profile's value |

- A profile's configuration file stays the checked-in file that its evidence describes. `installer.specifications` writes the settings into every rank's container command, so the created containers, the rendered Compose files and the ownership checks agree.
- The deployment lock records the settings (`serving`), so they are part of the deployment's identity. `install` with other settings installs another deployment and replaces the running model with one restart; the same settings select the same deployment again. `up PROFILE` refuses settings that differ from an existing deployment's.
- A setting for a value the profile does not set is refused before anything is created and before `install` surveys the Sparks: `deepseek-v41-flash-tp4` sets no video limit and no KV cache size. Managed GLM deployments take no settings.
- `--kv-cache-gib` accepts up to a tenth above the profile's value, and at least 1 GiB above it (11 for a profile of 10, 26 for 24, 44 for 40), with a warning in the plan; a larger value is refused. vLLM allocates the KV cache when the model starts, and a Spark's GPU and CPU share one memory: on two Sparks, `--kv-cache-gib 200` made the worker's kernel stop processes and the worker stopped answering SSH for over a minute, so the installation could not restore the previous model; `sparkring install --profile PROFILE` restored it. The margin follows recorded GLM starts at 11 GiB on two Sparks and at 44 and 46 GiB on four. The profiles pin their CUDA graph capture sizes, so more concurrency or a longer context share the same KV cache.
- `install --plan` lists each setting beside the profile's value, and `sparkring status` reports a deployment's settings.

**Compatibility:** without settings, deployment locks and `install` request hashes are unchanged, so existing deployments keep their identities.

**Validation:**
- Unit tests cover replacing only the named values, settings a profile does not set, value ranges, the KV cap, the settings in the lock identity and every rank's command and Compose file, the managed-backend refusal, refusal before a deployment directory is created, `up` recording and keeping a deployment's settings, and `install` selecting another deployment and listing the settings. In the CI replica, lint, docs links, release safety and repository layout pass, and 7,881 tests pass; two runtime-status tests fail locally for want of `prometheus_client` and `setuptools`, in code this PR does not touch.
- Four Sparks (GLM-5.3-Flash TP4): `install --max-images 8` replaced the running model; the containers ran with `--limit-mm-per-prompt {"image":8,"video":1}`, a request with 8 images returned 200 and the right count, and one with 9 returned 400 ("At most 8 image(s) may be provided in one prompt").

author: johanhjelsethstorstad
body:
## Problem
- The seeder never ran in prod. The `prod` image only runs `node server.js`, and the `migrate` one-shot only ran `migrate:deploy`.
- An existing standard image was never updated, so a changed file in `standard_store/` never reached an existing database.
- The seeder overwrote study programmes and article category descriptions, which users can edit on the site.

## Changes
**The seed follows one rule:** content users can edit is only created if it's missing. Content they can't edit is brought in line with the source code.
- **Standard images:** new `replaceImageFile` swaps an image's file in place and keeps its id, so relations survive. It only writes when the bytes differ, and it drops the old resized versions so the worker makes new ones. The seeder now calls `updateStandardImageFromConfig`, which also sets name, alt, credit and license from config.
- **Special image collections:** refreshing from config no longer creates, and orphans, two visibility rows on every run.
- **Study programmes and article categories:** existing rows are no longer overwritten (only the group order is still updated).

**Prod seeding:** the `migrate` one-shot now runs `migrate:deploy-and-seed`, so every deploy applies migrations and then upserts standard content before the app starts. It mounts the `store` volume, because the seeder writes image files. It also pins `MIGRATE_FROM_OW=false`, so a value left over from an import can't start DobbelOmega on a deploy.

## Testing
- `tsc` and `eslint` are clean.
- Not tested yet: tests against a DB, and a real deploy.

  * Existing category descriptions and study programme details are preserved during seeding; programme group ordering may still be updated.

author: mz2
body:
## Description

`GET /v1/test-executions` returns every matching result with its full `io_log`, and a client paging through a reviewer's executions 1000 at a time drove the API out of memory (canonical/medic#115). This PR adds tooling to measure that kind of cost, and uses it to remove waste in how the execution endpoints load results.

**Tooling**

- `scripts/seed_performance_data.py` bulk-inserts a deterministic synthetic data set: reviewers, several versions of each artefact, reruns, undecided environment reviews, many results per execution with io logs of realistic sizes, and issues attached to some failed results through rules with execution metadata. Profiles are `small`, `medium` (115,200 results, 375 MB of logs, seeded in about 16 s) and `large` (about a million results). Every artefact gets the same identity fields and a unique name, so there is no family-specific logic.
- `scripts/benchmark_endpoints.py` calls 12 read endpoints in process against the heaviest targets in the data and reports time, response size, SQL statements and time, and the peak Python memory of one request.

**Query changes**

- The execution search read every matching result three times: through `TestExecution.test_results` in `TEST_EXECUTION_OPTIONS`, through its own result query, and through each result's execution and that execution's results in `_TEST_RESULT_QUERY_OPTIONS`. It now reads them once. Each execution gets its filtered results with `set_committed_value`, so validating the response does not lazy-load them per execution.
- The search now loads the build, the artefact and the artefact's builds with their environment reviews up front, instead of one lazy load each. It also loads each issue attachment's issue, rule and the rule's execution metadata with the results. Artefact reviewers stay lazy on purpose, see below.
- `GET /v1/test-executions/{id}` and the reload after `PATCH` loaded every result and log of the execution, but `TestExecutionResponse` has no `test_results`. They now use `BASE_TEST_EXECUTION_OPTIONS`. The first load in `PATCH` still loads results, which the status update needs.

Measured with the benchmark on the `medium` profile, a reviewer's search with `limit=1000` (544 executions, 117 MB response):

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Time | 3.7 s | 1.7 s |
| SQL time | 1.7 s | 0.7 s |
| SQL statements | 285 | 99 |
| Peak Python memory | 471 MB | 393 MB |

With `limit=50` the time goes from 326 ms to 138 ms and the SQL statements from 109 to 25.

Peak memory stays at 3 to 4 times the logs in the page: the loaded rows, then the JSON text and its encoded bytes at once. As long as the search returns `io_log`, the remaining levers are a way to request results without it, or the planned server-side cap on `limit`.

One thing found along the way and left alone: the legacy `assignee` field is the first entry of `Artefact.reviewers`, and that relationship has no `order_by`, so which reviewer is reported depends on how the relationship happened to be loaded. Eager-loading reviewers in the search changed it, which is why they stay lazy here. It is probably worth giving the relationship an explicit order.

## Resolved issues

None filed here. Context: canonical/medic#115.

## Documentation

`backend/README.md` has a new "Performance testing" section for the two scripts.

## Web service API changes

- No new endpoints and no request or response changes. The responses of the search in five query modes (a reviewer at 1000 per page, latest only, `test_result=any`, `none` and specific IDs) and of `GET /v1/test-executions/{id}` for three executions are byte-for-byte identical to `main` on the seeded data.
- Changed queries: the loader options of the execution search, `GET /v1/test-executions/{id}` and the reload after `PATCH /v1/test-executions/{id}`.
- No configuration changes and no migrations.

## Tests

- `tests/scripts/test_seed_performance_data.py` and `tests/scripts/test_benchmark_endpoints.py` cover the new scripts on the `small` profile.
- The full backend suite passes locally, except `tests/controllers/auth/test_saml.py`, which needs the Docker Compose SAML identity provider I did not run.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` pass on the changed files.
- To reproduce the numbers:

```bash
DB_URL=postgresql+pg8000://user:pass@localhost:5432/perf uv run python scripts/seed_performance_data.py --profile medium --truncate
DB_URL=postgresql+pg8000://user:pass@localhost:5432/perf uv run python scripts/benchmark_endpoints.py --runs 3
```

Not done: the `large` profile has not been benchmarked, and there are no CI checks on the benchmark numbers yet. Statement counts and response sizes are deterministic on a fixed seed, so they could become budgets in a follow-up.

body:
Check in an inventory of every Prometheus metric name the Zone crates export, and fail CI when the source and the inventory disagree. Renaming or removing a metric then shows up as an explicit diff in review, so dependent alerts can be updated in the same release.

Alerts in `tempoxyz/helm-charts` (`charts/tempo-zone-alerts`) query metric names directly. When a metric disappears, the alert becomes a query with no data and never fires. [#1489](https://github.com/tempoxyz/zones/pull/1489) renamed `reth_tempo_zone_prover_validation_failure_total` to `reth_tempo_zone_prover_failure_total`, so `ProverValidationFailure` stayed silent while every mainnet shadow-prover validation failed after the 0.3.3 upgrade (fixed in [helm-charts#1335](https://github.com/tempoxyz/helm-charts/pull/1335)).

- `scripts/metric-names.py` scans `bin/` and `crates/`, skipping `tests/` and `benches/`. It collects `#[derive(Metrics)]` fields as `reth_<scope>_<field>` (honouring `rename`, `skip` and `separator`) and `counter!`/`gauge!`/`histogram!` calls with literal names, adding Reth's `reth_` exporter prefix. It fails on metric names it cannot resolve statically (non-literal macro names, dynamic scopes) and on a name registered as two kinds.
- `docs/metric-names.txt` holds the generated inventory (113 metrics). Regenerate it with `scripts/metric-names.py --write`.
- The `Metric Names` workflow runs `--check` on pull requests that touch Rust sources, the inventory, the script or the workflow, and prints added and removed names. It needs only `python3` and does not build the workspace.

Validation: `--check` passes on this branch. Renaming `ProverMetrics::failure_total` makes it fail and report the removed and added names. Every `reth_tempo_zone_*`/`reth_zone_*` series currently scraped from the mainnet zones is in the inventory, except `reth_tempo_zone_monitor_resync_from_portal_total`, which [#1543](https://github.com/tempoxyz/zones/pull/1543) removed after 0.3.3.

This does not check the alert rules themselves. Comparing the alert expressions in `helm-charts` against this inventory would be a natural follow-up there. That comparison already finds that `L1SubscriberStalled` references `reth_tempo_zone_l1_subscriber_backfill_in_progress`, which no Zone crate exports.

author: gmelikov
body:
### Motivation and Context
`zpool get fragmentation <pool> all-vdevs` always reports 0% for every vdev, while `zpool list -v` shows the real values.

Closes #16459

### Description
`vdev_prop_get()` read `vd->vdev_stat.vs_fragmentation`, which is never updated: fragmentation is only filled into the copy returned by `vdev_get_stats_ex()`.

Now `VDEV_PROP_FRAGMENTATION` reports the same values as `zpool list -v`:
- root vdev: pool (normal class) fragmentation;
- top-level concrete vdevs: metaslab group fragmentation;
- everything else (leaves, holes, etc.): `-`.

Second commit: `zpool get -p` printed vdev fragmentation with a trailing `%`; now it prints the bare number, like pool fragmentation and vdev capacity do.

### How Has This Been Tested?
Mirror pool with a log device, fragmented by writing/deleting small files:
```
NAME                FRAG
tp                   10%
  mirror-0           10%
    /home/z/vf/d1      -
    ...
logs                   -
  /home/z/vf/d4       0%

NAME    PROPERTY       VALUE  SOURCE
root-0  fragmentation  10%    -
mirror-0  fragmentation  10%    -
/home/z/vf/d1  fragmentation  -      -
...
/home/z/vf/d4  fragmentation  0%     -
```
Before the change all of these were `0%`. `zpool get -p` now prints `9` instead of `9%`.

ZTS `cli_root/zpool_get/vdev_get_001_pos` and `vdev_get_all` pass.

  - Phone(s) and email(s) are comma-separated. Phones are formatted to `757-555-0100`, and emails are checked for a valid format.
