body:
Refs #1277. Contains #1278's commit until GitHub drops it from the diff (it's merged).

## Problem

`gah status` backs the dashboard's `/api/status`. It made one `gh api …/issues/N/sub_issues` call per open issue, then walked dependency targets fetching `issues/N` one at a time. On the Mac worker (18 open issues) that took **8.4 s**.

## Change

- `provider::parallel_provider_map(items, width, f)`: an order-preserving map on scoped threads. In test builds it carries the thread-local `TEST_PATH_OVERRIDE` into each worker, so fake `gh`/`glab` still resolve.
- `evaluate_issue_dependencies`: sub-issue lookups run through it (width 16), and first-level dependency targets are prefetched concurrently into the resolver cache. Deeper body-declared chains still resolve serially (rare).

| Mac worker, `gah status --profile gah --json` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| wall time | 8.4 s | ~2.3 s |

Output compared field for field against the previous binary (`available_tickets`, `dependency_blockers`, `issue_intake_rejections`, `blocked_work_items`, `merge_requests`, `errors`): identical.

## Tests

- `parallel_provider_map_keeps_order_and_the_test_path_override`
- `cargo clippy -D warnings`; `cargo test --lib`: 1728 pass. `claude_monitor::…pty_captures_usage_from_fake_claude` failed once under full-suite load and passed 3/3 on its own; it's unrelated.

author: arc86
body:
## Summary

FluidAudio 0.17 (already on `main`) ships two retrainings of Parakeet v3 as drop-in `AsrModelVersion` cases. This adds them as Parakeet model choices, and fixes a bug found while testing them.

**Parakeet Ultra and Redux** (`644cc08`)
- **Ultra**: more accurate than v3 on every upstream benchmark (FLEURS 24-language WER 11.67% vs 14.81%; LibriSpeech test-clean 2.13% vs 2.27%), same speed, languages and int8 encoder.
- **Redux**: smallest download (~220 MB vs ~480 MB for v3). macOS 15+ only; slower (~34% on ANE upstream) and compiles for several minutes on first use.
- `ParakeetModelInfo` is the single source of truth: variants carry `isEnglishOnly` and `minimumMacOSMajor`, and `find()` resolves unknown or OS-unsupported ids to v3, so the picker, provenance label and helper always agree on which model runs.
- Replaces the hard-coded "v2 else v3" branches (picker ids, Settings, reprocessing, onboarding, model card, evidence links) with catalog lookups.
- Download state is now per variant (`isParakeetCached(variant:)` → FluidAudio `modelsExist(at:version:)`); previously any FluidAudio file made every Parakeet model show as downloaded. Purge now clears all four model caches.
- FluidAudio `AppLogger.minimumLevel = .warning` at helper startup, so its debug lines (which can contain transcript text) are no longer emitted.
- Default stays v3.

**Bug fix: ML stops working after cancelling processing** (`540ec93`, pre-existing on `main`)
- Cancelling processing / stopping reprocessing calls `forceReleaseGPU` → `.forceUnload`, which permanently closes the helper's admission. The app kept using that process, so every later ML request failed with "ML helper is shutting down" until an app restart.
- `LocalAIPluginService.forceUnload` now retires the drained helper; the next request launches a fresh one.
- `MLHostConnection` only handles the exit of the *current* process, so a retired helper exiting after its replacement launched can't fail the new helper's requests.

## Testing

- New tests: variant catalog + OS gating, picker id round-trip for every variant, variant → `AsrModelVersion` mapping, cache-check routing of the variant, reprocessing language rules, provenance label, and a stub-helper reproduction of the cancel bug (fails before the fix with the exact user-visible error).
- Full suite: 1492 tests passing.
- Manual (beta build, macOS 26): Ultra download state and transcription, Redux download and transcription, purge clears both, purge works after cancelling a transcription.

## Not in this PR

- Settings hides the whole model card until the Whisper model list arrives from Hugging Face, so choosing Parakeet/Apple waits on the network. Pre-existing; proposed separately.

author: mharris-sgymd
body:
## Problem

`db/test-schema.ts` group [63] (migration 069's durable `jobs` table) seeds a `fresh` terminal job at `ended_at = now()`, then asserts `prune_jobs(0)` deletes it. `prune_jobs` deletes `WHERE ended_at IS NOT NULL AND ended_at < now() - make_interval(...)` — a **strict** `<`. PGlite's WASM clock is millisecond-resolution, so when the seed insert and the `prune_jobs(0)` call land in the same millisecond, `ended_at < now()` is false, nothing is deleted, and `prune_jobs(0) deletes the remaining terminal row` fails with `0`. It reddens the "Schema" step at random (measured ~2 of 6 runs).

Not a defect in `prune_jobs` or migration 069 — a real terminal row ends *before* the scheduler's `now()`. The fault is the test's seed.

## Fix

Seed `fresh` at `now() - interval '1 second'` (one line, `db/test-schema.ts:10692`, with a comment on the why). `prune_jobs(60)` still keeps it (well within its window); `prune_jobs(0)` deletes it every time. No assertion added — the count stays 2317.

## Verify

- **20/20 consecutive `bun db/test-schema.ts` runs pass** with the fix (was flaking ~1/3).
- **Mutant** (seed back to `now()`) **fails within 4 runs** on exactly `✗ prune_jobs(0) deletes the remaining terminal row (0)` — so the check still has teeth and this seed is what holds it.
- tsc (db) clean; check-fork-consistency PASS; check-landing PASS (test file, no fragment).

author: deanrie
body:
Technical crash fix, opened in the repo as the Security Team suggested for this class.

## Problem

The app crashes on every VeChain token fee estimate / send when the node's `gasUsed` for the contract call is huge or negative.

## Root cause

`VeChainTransactionBuilder.buildInput` adds the fee parameters' `vmGas` (the node's `gasUsed`, an unbounded `Int`) with a plain `+=` and then assigns `input.gas = UInt64(gas)`; a huge value overflows the addition and a negative one traps in `UInt64(_:)`.

## Fix

Use `addingReportingOverflow` and `UInt64(exactly:)` and throw `BlockchainSdkError.failedToBuildTx` (the function already throws it for a bad `params`) instead of trapping.

## Affected files

- `Modules/BlockchainSdk/Blockchains/VeChain/VeChainTransactionBuilder.swift`

Verified locally with Xcode 26.6 (Swift 6.3.3, the version pinned in .xcode-version): Tangem scheme built for testing against the iOS 26.5 simulator (iPhone 17).

author: gnurizen
body:
Repin to latest ebpf-profiler fork pre-req 1/3

The fork is deleting `util.GetCurrentKernelVersion` and `util.ProbeBPFSyscall` to match upstream, where nothing calls them any more. parca-agent is their last caller. Rather than keep copies, this hands both jobs to the profiler. It's part of keeping parca-agent thin and pushing work into ebpf-profiler.

## What changes

`flags.CollectorConfig()` maps our flags onto the profiler's `collector/config.Config`. `flags.Validate` then calls that config's `Validate()` in place of our own copies of these checks:

- map scale factor
- verifier log level
- probabilistic interval and threshold
- minimum kernel version

Fields with no parca-agent flag, like the frame cache size, take the collector's defaults. Our own checks stay: machine ID, CUPTI scale, off-CPU threshold, offline mode, remote store. The `--bpf-map-scale-factor` help text now reads its maximum from `config.MaxArgMapScaleFactor`.

`main.go` loses the bpf(2) probe with no replacement. It only caught `ENOSYS`. A container that blocks bpf gets `EPERM` from seccomp, which the probe let through, and `NewTracer` fails with a real error right after either way.

The mapping is also the first step toward letting the fork's controller run the tracer lifecycle. `main.go`'s tracer startup is a drifting copy of `controller.Start`, and this is the config that controller would consume.

## User-visible changes

- **The minimum kernel is 5.10 on both architectures**, up from 4.19 on amd64 and 5.5 on arm64. The profiler already assumes it: upstream raised its minimum in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-profiler#1310 and deleted the fallbacks for older kernels, such as the path for kernels without generic batch map operations. Our lower minimums were letting through kernels the profiler no longer supports. `--ignore-unsafe-kernel-version` still skips the check.
- **A CPU sampling frequency below 1 and a negative `--bpf-map-scale-factor` are now rejected** instead of being passed to the tracer.
- **The error wording and exit code change.** Errors come from the profiler, prefixed `Invalid configuration:`, and all exit 2. A too-old kernel used to exit 1.

Once the fork bump lands, its newer `Validate` also rejects `--profiling-duration` ≤ 0, and that commit adds the test case for it.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`
- New `flags/collector_test.go`:
  - The parsed default flags pass the collector's `Validate`. This matters because it rejects zero values we have no flag for.
  - Each bad tracer setting is rejected.

author: vhr1975
body:
Starts ROADMAP item 6: rewrite the pre-gate "why it matters" notes, which hold public groundedness at 0.685. The tooling (`POST /regenerate-blurbs`, #275) has existed since 2026-09-27 but has never run: the gate record shows 0 rewrites attempted.

## Sizing (dry run, before building this)

Read from production D1 (read-only query) and run through the worker's own `pickCandidates`, so it's the same selection the endpoint makes. No AI calls.

| | |
|---|---|
| Blurbs live | 337 |
| Already approved by the judge | 58 |
| **Backlog** | **259** |
| no approved note (`unapproved`, first) | 78 |
| unsupported "It matters…" sentence (`significance`) | 116 |
| citation problems (`citations`) | 65 |

20 a day ≈ 13 days. The first ~4 days give notes to titles that have none; the groundedness eval judges only approved notes, so the score moves from about day 5.

## What the workflow does

`.github/workflows/regenerate-blurbs.yml`, daily at 10:00 UTC (after the 08:00 queue) and manual:

1. **Checks `count`**: whole number, at most 20 (~2k neurons) unless `override_reason` is given.
2. **Dry run**: no AI calls, and the worker doesn't claim budget for `dryRun`. The backlog and the next titles go to the job summary.
3. **Nothing due → stop.** A real call claims `blurb-regen` even with an empty batch, which would take the day's slot and block the final groundedness run. Skipping it keeps that day free.
4. **Otherwise** runs the existing `regenerate:blurbs` script (batches of 10, replaces only rewrites that pass the gate). A budget refusal (409) fails the run and shows the worker's reason.

Inputs reach the shell only through `env` (no expression interpolation in `run:`), and concurrency is one run at a time. Secrets and variables are the existing `INGEST_ADMIN_TOKEN` and `INGEST_URL` that the eval workflows use.

## Trade-off

While the backlog lasts, regeneration claims the day's one optional 70B slot at 10:00 UTC. The MCP tool-selection or classifier eval then has to run before 10:00 UTC or with an override. That's written into CLAUDE.md, WORKFLOWS.md and the workflow header.

## After merge

- Run it manually with `dry_run: true` to confirm the secrets and the sizing from CI (free), then either wait for 10:00 UTC or dispatch the first batch of 20.
- Watch day 1's replaced/held ratio in the job summary and on the Eval page's blurb-gate chart before letting it run unattended.

## Checks done

- The workflow YAML parses; `pnpm --filter … regenerate:blurbs 20 --override "…"` passes the arguments through to the script unchanged.
- No Worker code changes; nothing redeploys.

body:
Removes the three places where the distant picture used to change in a single moment.

## Changes
- **Backdrop photographs.** The day, dawn, dusk and night plates now hand over with an eased 14 s crossfade.
  - The old exponential fade did about a third of the change in its first second, which read as the mountain range being replaced.
  - A new plate choice also waits for any crossfade already in flight to finish, instead of restarting it from a half-shown photo.
- **Forest streaming edge.** Props are streamed in 40 m bands, and each band used to appear whole at 440 m, where a clear day's fog is only about 0.82.
  - The window now reaches 13 bands (520 m, where the fog is about 0.97).
  - Every streamed prop dissolves into the haze over the last 110 m before that edge. The edge moves with the rider continuously, so the fade itself never steps.
  - Covered: trees, saplings, rocks, deadwood, gates.
- **Wildlife.** Hares, deer and wolves used to switch on 40–320 m ahead. They now dissolve in over 1.2 s using a screen-door dither, so depth is still written and nothing needs sorting. The shadow pass reads the same value, so the shadow arrives with the animal.

Terrain LOD seams and texture-detail fades were already smooth ramps, so they are left alone.

## Cost
- Two more prop bands are resident (from 18 to 20). The prop pools size themselves from the band count.
- Props pay one extra smoothstep in their fog term.

## Verification
- `node tests/{riding,flow,terrain-shadow,models,graphics,hud}-check.mjs` all pass.
- New checks:
  - The crossfade is gentle after 1 s and still running at 7 s, and it cannot restart mid-fade. The first of these fails on the old code.
  - The stream-fade shader is assembled only for props, reads the view direction after it is declared, and has its own program key.
  - A hare placed this frame is still dissolving and is fully drawn after 1.2 s.
- In headless Chromium there were no shader or console errors, including the wildlife shadow pass. The stream edge sat 514 m ahead of the rider, and a dusk plate swap started gently.

author: jhputschke
body:
## Summary

The top-level `CMakeLists.txt` sets `USE_ROOT` ON (`set(USE_ROOT ON)` before the `option`), but finds ROOT optionally with `find_package(ROOT)`, not `REQUIRED`. Without ROOT, `-DUSE_ROOT` and the `src/root` include directory are left out as intended. Two places still needed ROOT anyway, so **a build on a machine without ROOT failed**:

1. **`src/CMakeLists.txt`** compiled `src/root/{RootBulkWriter,FastRootBulkWriter,JetScapeWriterRootHepMC}.cc`, which include ROOT headers, and linked `${ROOT_LIBRARIES}`, all under `if(USE_ROOT)`. Now under `if(USE_ROOT AND ROOT_FOUND)`, in its four places.
2. **`src/framework/JetScape.cc`** included `RootBulkWriter.h` and `FastRootBulkWriter.h`, and created both writers in `DetermineTaskList()`, unconditionally. Both are now under `#ifdef USE_ROOT`, which is set only when ROOT is found. Without ROOT, an XML asking for either writer gets a `JSWARN` instead of being silently ignored.

Effects:
- **With ROOT installed:** nothing changes (`ROOT_FOUND` true, `-DUSE_ROOT` set).
- **Without ROOT:** X-SCAPE builds without the ROOT writers, as the top level already intends.
- No other compiled X-SCAPE source, and none of MUSIC4GPU, iSS or 3dMCGlauber, includes ROOT headers. (`examples/custom_examples/PythiaBrickTestRoot.cc` does, but it isn't built.)
- PyJetscape (js-contrib) binds its ROOT writer only under `-DUSE_ROOT`, and reports that as `jetscape.HAS_ROOT`.

Motivation: the ROOT-free production container in js-contrib (`utils/Dockerfile.prod`, `utils/BuildContainerProd.md`). The two-stage hydro productions write their output with h5py and need no ROOT, and leaving it out keeps the image several GB smaller. Until this is merged, the Dockerfile builds from this branch.

## Test plan

- [x] The ROOT-free container build (conda env without ROOT, arm64, CUDA 13.2) configures X-SCAPE with the `src/CMakeLists.txt` change. It then stopped at `JetScape.cc: RootBulkWriter.h: No such file or directory`, which led to the second commit.
- [ ] The ROOT-free container build compiles `libJetScape` and `pyjetscape_core` with both commits, and the image runs the production. In progress.
- [ ] A build with ROOT (e.g. `build_gpu` on the GB10) is unchanged; expected, since `ROOT_FOUND`/`USE_ROOT` are set there.

author: vllystopad
body:
The core flow had no interpretation at all — the prediction shown to a user came from the tarot stub generator. This adds the step, with the model still out of the loop.

- `InterpreterPort` is the seam the Anthropic adapter will replace, and nothing else changes when it does.
- `StubInterpreter` is deterministic: the same question and cards read the same way twice, different questions never read the same. That is what makes an application-level assertion on a reading possible.
- `interpretReading` owns the frame: it refuses a reading with no cards or no question, and every reading closes with the same fictional notice regardless of interpreter.
- `ai.reading.interpret` is exposed over TCP with full payload validation; a cosmic motif is accepted as symbolic colour and never touches the cards.

Scenarios: `docs/orchestra/features/interpretation.feature`. 95 tests green, lint and build clean.

author: alanray-tech
body:
## Summary

This PR extends the graph-native rigid Newton framework merged in #5 into a
GPU-only QIPC coupling stack, using CGQ as the numerical and architectural
ground truth.

- add `FEM.QCloth` with elastic and quadratic-bending constitutions without
  changing the existing FEM/Cloth API;
- add standard IPC PT/EE/PH contact, friction, CCD, initial intersection
  diagnostics, dynamic LBVH broad phase, and grow-and-replay checkpoints;
- add minimal-coordinate reduced-KKT rigid/contact coupling while preserving
  Genesis RigidSolver as the authoritative rigid state;
- add device-scalar dynamic extents, dynamic OneSweep radix sort, exclusive
  scan, warp FSR, packed DOP14f BVH nodes, and load-balanced warp PT/EE
  traversal;
- add fused rigid-forest PCG paths, QIPC-only collision ownership, and
  checkpoint-owned parallel contact branches;
- retain explicit legacy/fallback paths for performance and numerical A/B
  comparisons;
- add cloth/contact parity tests, parallel-primitive tests, Franka teleop,
  crossed-cloth, cloth-on-cube, and multi-case performance examples;
- add the complete optimization report, plot, machine-readable data, and
  reproducible report generator.

## Architecture constraints

- CUDA/ndarray execution only; CPU execution is rejected.
- Runtime sizes remain zero-dimensional device scalars.
- No host masks or frozen-capacity scene specialization.
- The pre-existing RigidSolver execution route remains available for
  comparison.
- Contact and solver parameter names follow CGQ unless an exception is
  documented.

CGQ ground truth:
`42e7d4cbbad08739107ad830a17918f5f0f209ff`.

Required Quadrants performance work is published on
`alanray-tech/quadrants:dev/compile-time-opt` through `bf3a00645`.

## Validation

- algebraic and virtual-work parity for rigid forest `P`, `P^T`, and
  preconditioner paths;
- FEM elasticity/bending, contact-gradient/Hessian, CCD, ET, reduced-KKT, and
  checkpoint overflow/replay regression coverage;
- dynamic radix sort, scan, and FSR coverage through simulation-scale inputs,
  including dynamic buffer growth without recompilation;
- 20 warmup + 250 measured frames on four matched pure-cloth workloads in both
  Genesis and CGQ;
- report generator formatting, syntax, JSON integrity, archive integrity, and
  Canvas checks.

The interpretable 250-frame Genesis/CGQ wall-per-PCG ratios are `0.965x`,
`0.979x`, and `1.005x`. The crossed-sheet stress case gives a coarse `1.037x`
but is explicitly classified as trajectory-divergent rather than strict
equal-work evidence.

## Performance evidence

The report separates strict same-window A/B results, pinned CGQ migration
evidence, numerical-work corrections, and trajectory-sensitive aggregates.
Representative results include:

- fused forest `P/P^T`: `3.83x` lower per-iteration cost;
- dynamic Morton OneSweep: `2.338x` stage speedup;
- OneSweep/scan/FSR: `1.985x` stage speedup;
- resident occupancy grid: `1.230x` wall and `1.301x` GPU speedup;
- dynamic-range inlining: five helper launches removed per PCG iteration;
- observed cold backend compilation: `175.64 s -> 28.44 s` across the
  documented compiler revisions.

Full report and downloadable assets:
https://github.com/alanray-tech/Genesis/releases/tag/qipc-coupling-performance-2026-09-30

## Known boundaries

- Impact cases still require frozen-state CCD trajectory parity before they
  can be treated as strict equal-work benchmarks.
- Some original Nsight SQLite captures are not retained; the report preserves
  the JSON/CSV summaries and exact profile windows needed to regenerate them.
- Remaining contact-performance debt is tracked explicitly in
  `dev-docs/contact-performance-debt.md`; scene-specific workarounds are not
  accepted as optimizations.

author: back-alexandre
body:
## What changes

### Sling sync no longer erases agendo's calendar events
- **The bug:** both sync paths save the Google events they create in the same tracking list, with nothing saying which path made which. The Sling day sync deleted the whole day's list, then re-added only what Sling had. On Sept 29 a day built and published in agendo was then synced from the Sling screen. Those agents had nothing in Sling, so every agendo event of the day was deleted and nothing came back. Their shifts still showed as synced.
- **The fix:** an event counts as agendo's when an agendo shift points to it (`syncedEvent`). The Sling sync now skips those and only deletes what's left. This also covers everything published before this PR, so there's no migration.
- Both Sling buttons go through the same check: **Sync to team calendars** and the per-person sync.
- If the ownership lookup fails, the sync stops before deleting anything.
- **The other direction needed no change:** every delete agendo makes (edit, unpublish, delete, duplicate-day replace) removes only its own shift's event.
- New sparse index on `shifts.syncedEvent.id` for the lookup.

### Publishing a published shift puts its deleted event back
- If an agent deletes an agendo event from their calendar, publishing the shift again restores it. There's no separate button: it's part of publish.
- An already-published shift gets its event checked with Google. If it's still there, it's left alone, even if the agent moved it. If it's gone (cancelled, 404 or 410), it's synced again. A shift that never got an event gets one, if the agent syncs its position.
- If the event is gone and the agent no longer syncs that position, the shift stops claiming an event.
- If Google can't be checked (for example a revoked token), the shift is reported as an error and nothing is created, so an event that's actually there is never duplicated.
- **No duplicates from racing publishes:** a new event is attached only if the shift still holds the event that was there when the check ran. Otherwise it's deleted. First publishes use the same guard, so a double-click is still harmless.
- **UI:** select mode's Publish (`p`) now sends the whole selection. Select one shift and press `p` to fix it, or `Ctrl+A` then `p` for a whole day. The drafts bar still sends drafts only.
- The toast says "N calendar events put back" or "Already published, no calendar events missing".

### Zoom centres on now, on today
- When the day shown is today and the now line is on screen, zooming in or out centres on the current time.
- If you've scrolled the now line out of view, zoom keeps your spot, as on any other day.

### Sling screen banner (admins only)
- Asks admins to schedule in agendo from October 1 2026, and says the Sling integration will be discontinued on November 1 2026.
- The "Agendo" link opens the same day in `/app/schedule`.

## Deploy notes
- **Until this is live, don't use the Sling sync buttons on a day that has agendo shifts.** Sept 28–30 each have 56–58 live agendo events that the old code would delete.
- The `syncedEvent.id_1` index already exists in the production database. Local dev shares it, and my test run built it. Deploying will find it in place.
- If the same shift exists in both Sling and agendo, the agent now gets both events. Before, the Sling sync happened to delete agendo's copy.

## Testing
Locally on 2027-01-05, on my own row, with test data cleaned up afterwards.

Sling sync:
- **Before the fix:** published an agendo shift, then ran the "Sync to my calendar" path. Google marked the agendo event as cancelled, while the shift still said synced.
- **After the fix:** same steps, and the event stayed live. The log shows "Leaving 1 agendo-published event(s) alone".
- **Read-only, on real days:** a Sling sync would leave 56–58 agendo events alone on each of Sept 28–30. Sling still picks up its own events (52 on Sept 25).
- **Index:** the lookup uses it (1 document read out of 6,708).

Republish, through the real publish handler:
- **First publish:** event created.
- **Publish again with the event present:** no change, no duplicate.
- **Agent deletes the event, then publish:** "1 calendar event put back", new event live.
- **Event deleted, then two publishes at once:** both created an event; the loser deleted its copy, leaving exactly one live event.

Zoom checked in the browser. Typecheck and lint pass.

Not yet tested:
- The Sling side adding shifts back. My local user row has no `slingId`, so no Sling shift can match it on localhost. To test in prod after deploy, on Jan 5 2027, where I now have a Sling shift: publish an agendo shift on my row, then click **Sync to my calendar**. Both events should be there, with one copy of the Sling shift.
- Republish and the banner, clicked through in the browser.

author: jeffscottward
body:
## Problem

In the mixed home layout, an agent that is idle and ready for input shows a hollow **grey** ring. Only an agent with an unread completion shows a green dot. There is no legend in the mixed layout, so a user sees one green agent and six grey agents, although all seven are ready for input.

Observed on an iPhone Home Screen app (relay v0.22.3 on Linux x86_64, Herdr 0.9.1, 7 oh-my-pi (`omp`) agents in one workspace). One agent showed a filled green dot. The other six showed a grey ring. The workspace card showed a green dot.

## Root cause

This is the relay frontend's status-to-color mapping. Herdr detection and the relay state are both correct.

- `herdr agent list` reports `agent_status=idle` for all 7 panes. `herdr agent explain` gives identical output for all 7 (`state: idle`, `fallback_reason: default_known_agent_idle_fallback`). Herdr does not distinguish the green agent from the others.
- The relay's `triage-state.json` explains the difference. The green pane had `last_active_at` and no `last_seen_at`, so `DisplayedStatus` returns `done` (an unread completion, §9.8). Its last turn came from `herdr agent prompt` and was never opened on the phone. The other six have `last_seen_at > last_active_at`, so they display `idle`.
- In `frontend/src/lib/agents.ts`, `agentStatusTone` maps the `ready` group (`idle`/`ready`) to `muted`. That is the same grey used for the `other` group (unknown or exited states). The row adds `hollow`, which draws a grey outline.

So the unread/read distinction works as designed. The problem is that "read and ready for input" uses the grey that otherwise means "state unknown".

## Change

- `agentStatusTone` returns a new `ready` tone for the `ready` group. `muted` is now only for states the relay cannot classify.
- `.status-dot.status-ready` draws a **green ring** (`var(--success)` border, transparent fill).
- Filled green (`success`) still means "finished, not yet opened". The unread signal stays distinct: filled means unread, a ring means ready.
- `workspaceStateTone` returns `ready` for a workspace whose most notable state is idle. The aria-label is now "All sessions idle and ready for input". `muted` stays for workspaces with no known state.
- The "Idle" section heading in the By State layout uses the same green ring.
- The agent rail and Global Jump use `agentStatusTone`, so they now show the ring too. Before this change, those views showed a filled grey dot for ready agents.

The relay-side status logic, acknowledgement, and notifications are unchanged. The committed `web/` bundle is not rebuilt, because the release process owns it.

## Repro

1. Run two agents in one workspace. Let both finish a turn.
2. Open one agent on the phone. That acknowledges its completion.
3. Return home. Before: the opened agent shows a grey ring, the same as an unknown state, and the other shows filled green. After: the opened agent shows a green ring, and the unopened one shows filled green.

## Tests

- `helpers.test.ts`: `idle`/`ready` map to `ready`, `done` maps to `success`, and an unknown status (`exited`) maps to `muted`.
- `adopted-features.test.ts`: workspace precedence is done > working > ready > muted.
- `mobile-journeys.spec.ts`: the idle-only workspace card has the new aria-label and `status-ready`. The done card keeps `status-success`.
- Local results: `lint`, `check` (0 errors), `test` (535 passed), `build`, and `size` passed. The full Playwright `chromium-mobile` project passed (107/107). I could not run `webkit-mobile` on this host because its WebKit browser is not installed.

No existing issue or PR covers this.

author: o2alexanderfedin
body:
"Try again" now rebuilds the app the window was asked to show. That is the window's description plus its tweak. It no longer rebuilds a plain app from the short slug or drops the tweak. The retry makes one model call, in place, through the same key and prompt the tweak used (`appIdentity` from #5).

**What the user saw**
- **A tweak of a described app failed** ("make the whole thing blue" on "a pomodoro timer with a gentle chime"). "Try again" closed the window and opened a new app from `pomodoro-timer-with-a-gentle-chime` only. The description was lost, the tweak was lost, and the call was paid anyway. (#4's bug, on one more path.)
- **A reload found a tweaked app no longer cached.** "Try again" rebuilt the app without the tweak.

**Mechanism.** Both buttons reopened the window through the plain open or describe path, and that path knows nothing about the window's tweak.

**Fix.** Both buttons now run the tweak again in place (`retryTweak` → `handleModify`). The window shows "Preparing…", keeps its position, and gets its tweak saved only after the tweak works, as before. Windows without a tweak retry as before (close, then open or describe).

**Choice made: retry the tweak, not "reset to base".** The failure is shown where the tweak was asked for, and the button says "Try again". Also, the restore path already asks the cache for (description, tweak), so a retry that resets to base would disagree with what a reload restores.

**Tests.** There are two new DesktopShell tests with fake timers. Each mutation below was applied, run, and restored (checked with `cmp`):
- Retry reopens by slug (the old code): test 1 fails, "Tweaked Result" is never shown.
- Retry re-describes without the tweak: test 1 fails the same way.
- The tweak ignores the description: both tests fail on `toContain(DESCRIPTION)`.
- Retry makes an extra model call: both tests fail on `toHaveLength(1)`.
- Restore retry drops the tweak (the old code): test 2 fails, "Tweaked Result" is never shown.
- Restore builds the app before the click: test 2 fails on `toHaveLength(0)`.

The test transport answers "Tweaked Result" only to a request that carries the tweak, so that check stands in for "the request contained the tweak".

DesktopShell.test.tsx passed 20 of 20 runs (4 in parallel). Typecheck, the unit suite (972), build, the hook tests and Playwright (6) pass locally on this branch merged with develop.

**Not changed**
- A failed tweak still shows the generic "couldn't load" text, even for a 401 or a throttle (`needsAuth`/`throttled` stay false on this path, as before).
- Widget tweaks inside an app are still not saved. That state lives in `wrapWidget`'s React state, in the app's component tree. Saving it needs a per-window map of widget tweaks carried into the app, which does not fit this PR.

## Summary

A batch of fixes and polish found while running the board locally at `http://tasks:5180` (an `/etc/hosts` alias).

**Bug fix**
- **Adding a task crashed on plain-http hostnames.** `crypto.randomUUID` only exists in secure contexts (HTTPS, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`), so on `http://tasks:5180` every new card threw `crypto.randomUUID is not a function`. **Reset view**

- Cards snapped unevenly (8px left, 4px right, 20px bottom, and 60px top, which overlapped the + button). Snapping now keeps a uniform 16px inset from every edge and from the + button, which moved to a 16px inset itself. author: lnds
body:
## The problem

GitHub scopes a cache to the ref that wrote it, so the caches a PR builds
can never be read again once it closes. They keep occupying the repo's
10 GB ceiling until LRU eviction reclaims them — and that eviction takes
live caches with them.

### Measured

| | |
|---|---|
| repo cache in use | **9.7 GB of 10 GB** |
| `cmodular-selfhost` copies (~1 GB each) | **9 of those GB**, one per PR |
| oldest surviving cache | **under 24 h old** |
| caches belonging to already-closed PRs | **8, totalling 4149 MB** |

The vendored libLLVM the release boots from was a casualty. The weekly
warmer saved it to `main` on 2026-09-28 (`Cache saved with key:
llvm-static-macOS-18.1.8-8b19c59…`) and the release a day later reported
`Cache not found` for the identical key, paying a cold build:
**25.3 min per platform, 2 platforms, every release** — roughly half of
the 82.6-minute release build.

`Cache not found` holds for all four of v0.125.0 → v0.128.0, both
platforms, with the key identical every time. The key is not the problem;
survival is.

## The change

One workflow: on a closed PR, delete every cache scoped to its merge ref.

- `pull_request_target` for the write-scoped token. It performs **no
  checkout** and runs none of the PR's code — it reads a PR number and
  calls the cache API, which is the safe shape for this trigger.
- `actions: write` is declared explicitly; the repo default is `read`, so
  without it the delete would fail while the job stayed green.
- A failed delete is a warning, not a job failure: a cache that is
  already gone must not turn a merge red.

## Verified

- The DELETE path works against a real cache (id 8289536838, PR #2327):
  gone from the listing afterwards.
- Backfill applied by hand for PRs already closed (2326, 2327, 2328,
  2330): **8 caches, 4149 MB freed**.
- Cache listing after the backfill: **17 caches, 5.62 GB** (was 25 /
  9.7 GB).

Note for whoever reads the usage number: `actions/cache/usage` lagged and
still reported 9.67 GB after the deletes landed. The
`actions/caches` listing is the figure that tracks reality.

## Not in this PR

Two further defects found while measuring, each worth its own change:

- `warm-llvm-cache.yml` has the matrix `[macos-14]` while `release.yml`
  builds `[macos-14, ubuntu-24.04]`, so the Linux release never had a
  warmer at all.
- Every workflow logs `Node.js 20 is deprecated` for `actions/cache@v4`,
  `checkout@v4` and `upload-artifact@v4`, currently force-run on Node 24.

author: okcompute
body:
## Change details

Adds an official release flow and prebuilt-binary installation.

- **Release workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): triggered by pushing a `v*` tag. Builds four targets (`x86_64-linux`, `aarch64-linux`, `aarch64-macos`, `x86_64-macos`), packages each as `git-session-<target>.tar.gz`, generates `SHA256SUMS`, and creates a GitHub Release whose assets are served via GitHub's CDN. The tag name is passed to `-Dversion`, so `git-session --version` matches the release.
- **Installer** (`install.sh`): downloads the matching release binary by default and verifies its SHA-256 against `SHA256SUMS`. Verification is mandatory — it refuses to install on a checksum mismatch, a missing `SHA256SUMS`, or a missing asset entry. It falls back to a source build only when no release is published yet or the platform is unsupported. New `--version` and `--from-source` options; `--from-source` clones the repository when run outside a checkout.
- **Docs**: `docs/installation.md` (new) covers supported platforms, quick install, manual install with checksum verification, and requirements. The `README.md` install/requirements/release sections are updated.
- **CHANGELOG.md**: 1.0.0 entries for the distribution changes.

Version alignment: changelog `1.0.0` ↔ `build.zig.zon` `1.0.0` ↔ tag `v1.0.0`.

## Type of change

- [x] CI / Build
- [x] Docs

## PR Checklist

- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Changes are tested locally (shellcheck, `bash -n`, and end-to-end tests of the installer's verification and fallback paths)
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated (required for all app changes)

author: saymon0123
body:
Dois pedidos do dono ao abrir o CRM: o cartão de ativação devia ser menor e flutuante, e a grade da agenda devia ocupar mais espaço.

## A agenda não era pequena — era desperdiçada

```
HOUR_START = 6     HOUR_END = 22     →  16 horas desenhadas
A barbearia trabalha 09:00 – 19:00   →  10 horas usadas
```

**Mais de um terço da altura eram horas que a barbearia nunca usa.**

Eu tinha oferecido ao dono uma escolha entre *"ver o dia inteiro sem rolar"* e *"blocos maiores com rolagem"*. **A escolha era falsa:** encolhendo a janela para o expediente do dia, os mesmos pixels servem menos horas — e dão as duas coisas.

A conta saiu do componente para `janelaDaGrade`, módulo puro com 9 asserções. Ela abraça a jornada com uma hora de folga de cada lado **e estica para caber horário fora do expediente** — encaixe fora da jornada é permitido de propósito neste projeto, e um horário das 20h numa barbearia que fecha às 19h ficaria desenhado fora da área visível: existindo no banco e invisível na tela, que é a pior combinação possível.

Sem jornada nem horário (barbearia nova, domingo sem ninguém), cai em 8h–20h — generoso, e já quatro horas menor que o antigo.

## O cartão de ativação virou pílula

Flutuante no canto superior direito, recolhido por padrão, **âmbar enquanto falta algo**. O estado vai para o `localStorage` com try/catch: aba anônima devolve recolhido, que é o padrão seguro porque não cobre nada.

Continua **sem botão de dispensar**, e isso é de propósito: recolher é diferente de sumir. Com o WhatsApp desconectado o produto não faz nada, e esconder isso não ajuda ninguém — o jeito de tirar da tela é resolver.

## Dois "está faltando" que eram da amostra, não do CRM

- **Arrastar na agenda** funciona e sempre funcionou: `handleDrop` muda cadeira **e** horário, com encaixe de 15 em 15 minutos. O dono não conseguiu porque a amostra tinha os 28 horários de hoje **todos finalizados**, e bloco finalizado não arrasta de propósito. Corrigido nos dados: hoje tem 6 arrastáveis, amanhã 29.
- **Promover/rebaixar** existe (`trocarPapel`, com RPC e trava de último dono). O seletor some quando o membro **não tem login**, e as quatro cadeiras fictícias não têm conta. Some em **silêncio** — mesmo defeito dos itens 8 e 10. Deveria aparecer desabilitado dizendo "só depois que ele aceitar o convite". **Fica em aberto no backlog.**

## Prova

typecheck ✓, lint ✓, **543/543** em 62 arquivos (eram 534 em 61), build de produção ✓.

**Não verificado em tela logada** — entrar exigiria criar conta ou digitar senha. A conferência visual da pílula e da grade é tua, e é justamente o que tu pediste, então vale olhar antes de mergear.

author: joelntemuse24
body: ## Root cause `section-master.ts` ran ffmpeg and ffprobe with `spawnSync`. That blocks the one Node event loop, so `setTimeout` and a main-thread `AbortSignal` do not fire until the child exits. On the live 12.8k-character Andrew job (after #145), section 0's QA finished in 1,568 ms and was kept. Its master then froze the loop. Sections 1–7 all logged `action=open` together at 12,327–12,737 ms with `wer=-` once the loop resumed. Claim-to-ready was **2m20s**, up from 1m50s. The same stall matches job `643391fe` (38 sections): OpenRouter QA calls stayed up 75–194s and ended `action=open`, plus fetch/handshake failures, one section-master failure, and `/health` and `/ready` timing out during a wave. The 5s cap was not wall-clock under load. The 7 ffmpeg `Invalid data found when processing input` lines (each paired with `Header missing`) are one pair per packet-copy join. The decoder resyncs at the boundary. The finished file is 917.97s, −16.7 LUFS, −1.8 dBTP, which matches the book and the delivery target. Those warnings are harmless. ## Fix - ffmpeg and ffprobe are async `spawn`. ffmpeg in flight is capped at the CPU count. - The transcript request runs on a worker thread with `AbortSignal.timeout`, so the socket dies at 5s even while this thread is inside a synchronous child. A backup timer terminates that worker if the message never arrives. - `GET /health` and `GET /` are answered in the HTTP callback, with no Turso query, so a processing wave does not hold them. `/ready` still checks Turso, and it can answer again once the loop is free. - `TTS_SECTION_QA_ENABLED=0` (also `false` or `off`) skips QA even when a key is set and logs `qa skipped: disabled` once. Unset leaves QA on. A missing key still logs `qa skipped: no provider`. ## Timing Before (live, after #145): **2m20s** claim-to-ready, 7 of 8 QA lines `wer=-`. After, on this host, replaying the earlier real Edge synth times for the same 12k-character / 8-section shape (`[40336, 35732, 38988, 56022, 34221, 75009, 38924, 67333]` ms), a local transcript that waits 2s and returns that section's source text, then the real async section master and the packet-copy join: - All 8 sections mastered: **80.1s** - Packet-copy join: **2.9s** (worst splice step 233) - Claim-to-ready: **83.0s** - Every QA line was `wer=0.000 action=keep`. The slowest was **2,077 ms**. - A 100ms interval fired 828 times across 83.0s (about 830 expected), so the event loop stayed free through the masters. This is not a fresh live Edge synthesis. The synth timestamps are the earlier unblocked Edge run of this book. Upload to R2 is not in the 83.0s.

author: copilot
body:
Redesign the Streamly front-end to look more polished and modern, and make API fetching less likely to fail because of CORS or blocked routes.

- **Visual redesign (`site/public/style.css`, `index.html`)**
  - Rewrote the stylesheet with a dark glassmorphism theme and animated gradient background glow.
  - Header is now a floating glass pill with a gradient logo and gradient search button.
  - Cards lift on hover with image zoom and a play overlay. Chips, buttons, category tiles and the age gate share the same gradient treatment.
  - Added page and card entrance animations and a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out.
  - Added a `theme-color` meta tag.
  - No markup or JS logic changed for the redesign, so routes and behavior are unchanged.

- **API fetching (`site/public/app.js`, `site/server.js`)**
  - `api()` now tries the API directly, then the local `/api/` proxy, then two public CORS proxies (`corsproxy.io`, `allorigins.win`).
  - Each attempt has a 10s `AbortSignal.timeout`, so a blocked or slow route falls through to the next instead of hanging.
  - The proxy in `server.js` now sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, sets `Accept: application/json`, and uses an 8s upstream timeout before trying the next host.

Fetching can't be guaranteed unrestricted. If the upstream blocks the network or the public proxies, requests can still fail. The third-party CORS proxies only help when the site is hosted statically without `server.js`.

author: kingchappers
body:
> **Stacked on #58 (PR-14)**, because it uses the new schedules (weekly to yearly). Merge that first; until then this diff also shows its commits. No infrastructure changes.

## Summary
- **EF2 (calendar)** An "Add bills to your calendar" button on the Recurring page downloads `budget-bills.ics`, with one line of help: "Adds each bill to your calendar with a reminder. Download again after changing bills." The file is built in the browser from the bills the page already has; nothing is sent anywhere and no API route is added, so sign-in (AUTH-01) is untouched. Re-downloading replaces events rather than duplicating them, because each event keeps the same id (`<recurringId>@budget`).
- One all-day event per bill, named like "Rent £850.00", with a recurrence rule for each schedule: `FREQ=WEEKLY`, `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=4`, `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=n`, `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=3;BYMONTHDAY=n`, `FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=m;BYMONTHDAY=n`.
- A single on-screen reminder at the bill's warning time, at 9am on that day rather than midnight (for example `-P2DT15H` for three days ahead, `PT9H` for none).
- Text is escaped (backslash, semicolon, comma, new line), lines end in CRLF, and lines are folded at 75 octets without splitting a multi-byte character such as £.
- **Month ends.** A bill on the 31st uses `BYMONTHDAY=-1` (the last day of the month), as the app does. On the 29th or 30th the months that are always long enough use the plain day and the short ones use the last day, as a second event with its own stable id (`…-end@budget`). Quarterly and yearly bills (including 29 February) follow the same rule.

## Results
- `yarn test`: 1402 passed (93 files). 62 of them are new calendar tests.
- `yarn typecheck`: clean
- `yarn build`: passes
- `yarn audit --level high`: passes with the new dev dependency

The tests parse the output with `ical.js` and expand every rule, then compare the dates with the app's own `nextOccurrences`, for 19 bills across two start dates (including a leap year, the 29th to 31st, quarterly runs through February, and 29 February). While writing them I found that the parser's iterator ignores `BYSETPOS`, which is why month ends use `BYMONTHDAY=-1`; that is also simpler and more widely supported.

## Decisions made without the user
- Income is left out: this is a calendar of money going out, so a salary day does not get a reminder. Say if you want it included.
- Each event starts on the bill's next due date, as an all-day event, and repeats from there.
- Only one reminder per event (at the warning time). A second one on the day itself would be easy to add.
- `ical.js` is a dev dependency only; it is not in the app bundle.

## Noticed, out of scope
- Calendar apps differ on whether they refresh an already-imported file or add a second copy; the stable ids should make modern ones update, but I have not tried Apple, Google and Outlook.
- Push notifications are the separate PR-16.

## Not done
- No browser check yet (the app cannot authenticate locally). Worth trying the downloaded file in a real calendar app, particularly on iOS.

author: toddhebebrand
body:
## What changes

Two follow-ups to #7560 in how the server ingests desktop start results:

1. **Unreadable start results fail the session instead of being dropped.** A `desk-start-*` result that does not match the result schema used to be dropped, which left its session `connecting` until the viewer gave up with a generic timeout. When the command id still names the start, the session is now marked `failed` with: *"The remote device's answer to this session start could not be read, so the session was not started. Make sure the agent and server are on matching releases, then try again."* Only a start that is still `connecting`, owned by the reporting device and dispatched under exactly that command id is touched (the same predicates as every other start result); a result from another device changes nothing.

2. **Consent prompt protocol 2 markers must be backed by their own outcome.** A version 2 agent reports what happened to the prompt (`consentOutcome`) alongside the reason. A consent-mode start now activates only when they agree: `user` needs `granted`, `timeout` needs `presented_expired`, `no_user_session` needs `unavailable`. An incoherent marker does not activate a consent-mode start and is not audited as a grant or bypass. Version 1 markers (no outcome) are unaffected.

No migration. No change for agents on consent prompt protocol 1.

## Tests
- `helpers.test.ts`: `consentMarkerIsCoherent` table (v2 combinations, v1 untouched, no reason).
- `agentWs-consent-ingest.integration.test.ts` (real Postgres as `breeze_app`): incoherent v2 `user` / `timeout` markers do not activate; an unreadable start result fails its session with the message; an unreadable result from another device changes nothing; the existing `helper_unreachable`-as-activation case now fails the start instead of leaving it `connecting`. The three new cases fail against the previous code (checked).
- Integration: `agentWs-consent-ingest` + `remote-session-consent` + `remoteDesktopTerminalIntent` 76/76 pass.

body:
## Why

GitHub shows the README from `main`, and it opened on `# Realm` and a line of dev notes. The product pictures added on `integration/v0.6` (b7d2f6b5) never reached `main`, and they were the old captures anyway.

## What

![README preview](https://github.com/31Carlton7/realm/blob/docs/readme-product-images/docs/images/banner.png?raw=true)

The README now opens with:

- **The share card as a banner**, linking to realm.computer.
- **The tagline, two badges and the links.** The badges are the latest release (live from GitHub) and macOS on Apple silicon; the links are Download for Mac, realm.computer and the changelog.
- **A short account of what Realm is**, from the landing page's hero and FAQ: any agent, no API key, in active development.
- **"What it looks like"**: the landing page's six claims in a 2×3 grid, each with its capture cropped to the region the page frames and a one-line caption.

The developer docs follow, unchanged, below a rule. The Website section gains a pointer to the script that builds the pictures.

## The pictures

`scripts/readme-images.mjs` builds all seven into `docs/images/`:

- **From the deployed site, not this checkout.** `main`'s `site/public/product` lags the branch the site ships from, so the script fetches `/product/*.png` and captures `/share` from realm.computer. `REALM_SITE_URL` points it at a local `pnpm start`.
- **The same crops as the page.** Each capture uses its claim's `focus` from `site/content/home.ts`, held inside the capture the way `Claim.tsx` holds it, in the page's 15/8 frame.
- **The site's frame**, drawn by Chrome: rounded corners and a hairline edge on a transparent ground, over Realm's page colour. The window is translucent, and GitHub would otherwise composite it onto white.
- **Chrome only.** The banner needs Chrome's WebGPU anyway (it renders the dimension field), so the ffmpeg version on `integration/v0.6` is replaced rather than extended.

## Checked

- Rendered through GitHub's own Markdown API (README mode) and viewed in GitHub's light and dark stylesheets. Nothing overflows, no image is broken, and the badges read `release: v1.5.0` and `macOS: Apple silicon`.
- The new prose has no em-dashes, and every claim in it is one the landing page already makes.

## Keeping integration/v0.6 in step

`integration/v0.6` carries the older header, a "Screens" section and four older images at the same paths. A companion PR gives it these exact files, so a later `integration/v0.6 → main` merge has nothing to reconcile here.

author: zmanian
body:
## What this changes

Session discovery now fails closed when a tool's folder exists but cannot be read.

**The consent problem on `main` today.** Claude Code, Cline, Gemini CLI and OpenCode returned `Ok(vec![])` from `discover()` whenever `read_dir(root)` failed, whatever the reason: permission denied, an unmounted volume, a transient I/O error. Claude Code also skipped an unreadable project folder with `else { continue; }` and returned a partial listing. Callers take an `Ok` listing as complete. Flow 1's grant recording (`record_sources_for_grant` -> `ProjectPolicy::record_source`) therefore recorded an unreadable source as holding nothing. Once the folder became readable again, every session and project that was on disk at the grant looked new. The project was armed by default and its pre-grant sessions became eligible for unattended upload, which breaks the promise that the grant "arms nothing already on disk".

The reviews of #1123 and #1134 found this, and a failing probe on #1134 confirmed it: queue a session as pending, arm, `chmod 000` the Claude root, settle, restore to 755, settle again. The pre-existing session came out `(Approved, true)` where `(Pending, false)` was expected.

**The fix**
- New `source::read_dir_for_discovery(dir, label)`. It returns `Ok(None)` only for `NotFound` (the tool isn't installed, or the folder is gone), and returns `Err` for anything else. The error is label-only (`<adapter>-discovery-...-unreadable: <ErrorKind>`) and never includes a path.
- It is used at the root of Claude Code, Cline, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, and also:
  - for Claude Code's per-project folders, which previously gave a silent partial listing;
  - for Gemini CLI's per-project `chats` folder, which had the same partial-listing shape;
  - for Codex's recursive walk. Codex was not in the original list, but it had the same bug at the root and at every nested date folder.
- Watcher `tick_over`: a source whose discovery fails was already left out of `discovered`, so it isn't recorded for the grant and keeps holding everything back. That exclusion is correct now that `Ok` means complete. This PR adds a label-only `warn` (source name only, not the error) instead of dropping the failure silently.
- Watcher `tick_over`: `finish_pass` gets `exhaustive = every_source_listed` instead of `true`. A full pass in which a source failed to list no longer retracts `LABEL_SESSION_TOO_LARGE` or the OpenCode export-version flag. It also reports no gate-held count, so the last complete count stays in place until every source lists again.

**Other callers of `discover()`, checked**
- `daemon::find_session` (upload drain): already `continue`s on `Err`. That source's entry just isn't found this pass.
- The default `TraceSource::session_at` propagates `Err`, but every adapter overrides `session_at` without calling `discover()`. The scoped pass maps any failure to "skip this path". Neither can abort a batch.
- `commands.rs` CLI session listing: this already used `discover().context(...)?`. An unreadable root now makes the command error with the label (`discovering local sessions: claude-code-discovery-root-unreadable: PermissionDenied`) where it used to list nothing from that source. That is a visible behaviour change, and I think it is the right one.
- The IPC and FFI surfaces don't call `discover()`. `source::discovery::count_sessions` (the onboarding source counts) is a display-only count, is not a consent input, and is unchanged.

**Coordination with #1123 and #1134.** Both PRs rely on this behaviour, and both branches are untouched here. #1123's cwd-cache prune guard (`discovered.len() == sources.len()`) is only sound once an `Ok` listing is complete, which this PR makes true. This PR also names that fact `every_source_listed` in `tick_over`. #1134's arm-from-now recording gets the same guarantee as the grant recording. Whichever of them lands after this one may need a small rebase adjustment around the `discovered` / `finish_pass` lines in `tick_over`.

**Out of scope / left undone**
- Per-entry failures inside a readable folder (`skipped += 1` when a `DirEntry` or `file_type()` fails) still give a partial listing. These are rarer mid-iteration errors. Making them fatal is a separate decision, because it would turn a single racy entry into a failed pass.
- `TrajectorySource` is deliberately unchanged. Its `WorkingDirectory` scope is the process's cwd, which could be a TCC-protected or otherwise unreadable folder, and failing there would wedge the staging scope as well.
- No user-facing "a source folder can't be read" health label was added. The failure is only logged, label-only. If shells should say so, the copy belongs in the core consent/copy module.
- A cwd-cache prune test can't be written against `main` because the prune only exists on #1123. `a_pass_with_an_unreadable_source_is_not_exhaustive` covers the `every_source_listed` fact that the prune should key off.

## Verification

Red first. Commit `8a2570f19` (pre-rebase) was committed, then the five adapter files were checked out from `origin/main` and `finish_pass(.., every_source_listed)` was reverted to `true`, keeping the new tests:

```
test source::tests::every_adapter_lists_a_missing_root_as_empty ... ok
test source::tests::every_adapter_fails_on_an_unreadable_root ... FAILED
test source::tests::codex_fails_on_an_unreadable_nested_folder ... FAILED
test source::tests::claude_code_fails_on_an_unreadable_project_folder ... FAILED
test source::tests::gemini_cli_fails_on_an_unreadable_chats_folder ... FAILED
test daemon::watcher::tests::a_pass_with_an_unreadable_source_is_not_exhaustive ... FAILED
test daemon::watcher::tests::a_source_unreadable_at_the_grant_arms_nothing_already_on_disk ... FAILED
test daemon::watcher::tests::a_source_unreadable_at_the_grant_arms_nothing_already_queued ... FAILED
```

The grant-case failures on `main`:

```
assertion `left == right` failed: a project on disk at the grant was armed
  left: (AutoUpload, true)
 right: (NotifyOnly, false)
```

(`every_adapter_lists_a_missing_root_as_empty` passes on both sides by design, since NotFound must stay empty.)

The permission tests are `#[cfg(unix)]` and skip themselves at runtime when `chmod 000` doesn't stop the running user from reading (root). A drop guard restores 0755 so a failing assertion can't leave behind a temp dir that won't delete.

Green, after rebasing onto `e11a70c2b`:

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo test -p trace-commons-contributor --lib`: `test result: ok. 2764 passed; 0 failed; 11 ignored`
- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo test -p trace-commons-contributor --tests`: 30 test executables, 30 `test result` lines, 0 with failures (pre-rebase)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p trace-commons-contributor --all-targets -- -D warnings <repo allow-list>`: exit 0, 0 warnings
- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check -p trace-commons-contributor --no-default-features`: Finished
- The server-crate checks in the template don't apply, because this touches only `trace-commons-contributor`. The FFI surface is unchanged.

## Licensing

- [x] I license this contribution under **MIT OR Apache-2.0**, per
      [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) — including for the AGPL-licensed
      server crates, which are distributed under AGPL-3.0-or-later regardless.
- [x] Any new `.rs` file in `trace-commons-server`, `trace-commons-gate-api`, or

body:
> Stacked on #1 (`voice-check`) — both touch README.md and install.sh. Merge #1 first; GitHub will retarget this PR to `main`.

## Summary

Adds `coherence-check`, the third writing skill: it checks whether a text holds together as one piece — especially after an AI draft has been edited by hand, which tends to tear the narrative.

- **Map first:** the promise (title, excerpt, intro, item by item), the one-sentence through-line, each section's job and its link to the previous one, threads set up to be picked up later, and whether the ending answers the promise.
- **Breaks it looks for:** broken promises, lost threads, detours, jumps without a bridge, wrong order, repeats, drift, a weak ending, proportion — and **editing seams**: a term that changes mid-text, back-references to removed passages, announced counts that no longer match ("two decisions" followed by four points).
- **Earlier draft:** `draft:`, the file's git history, or the PR's commits — used to check the edges of every edited region; for translations, the original's structure.
- **`scripts/skeleton.py`** (stdlib only): headings and first sentences with line numbers — they should tell the story on their own — plus back-references and announced counts to verify.
- **Guardrails:** report only; fixes are structural (move, cut, merge, a one-sentence bridge); never writes missing content — such fixes are marked ✍️ for the author.

README recommends the order fact-check → coherence-check → voice-check.

## Type of change

- [x] New skill / hook / enhancement
- [x] Documentation

## Scope

- [x] This change is generic and reusable (in scope per CONTRIBUTING.md — not project-specific logic).

## Testing

- [x] `bash -n install.sh` and `python3 -m py_compile scripts/skeleton.py` pass.
- [x] Installed with `./install.sh`; `/coherence-check` is picked up.
- [x] Ran it on a real Ukrainian article that had been AI-translated and then edited by hand. It found a topic promised in the intro and never covered, the literal answer to the title buried mid-section, a term that changed between the author's edits and the rest, and an announced "two decisions" that an earlier fact-check edit had turned into four points.

author: cett
body:
## Summary
A mass disable of scheduled tasks could swallow every due run with no trace. Catch-up then advanced its timestamp past the gap, so no `missed` rows appeared and no alert fired.

- New `src/web/schedule-skip-ledger.ts`:
  - **Review-gate holds:** every due occurrence of a DB-enabled task held by the review gate (draft / pending_review) gets a `task_runs` row (`skipped_not_live`, per target agent).
  - **Mass skip:** when most of the tasks that were runnable on the previous tick drop out at once (minimum 4 tasks), each dropped task gets `skipped_disabled` rows while it stays out (at most 24 h). One deduplicated alert fires (audit `mass_skip` plus Telegram when a token exists), and the detector re-arms when the event ends.
  - **Deliberate disables:** an operator's single-task disable, and tasks that were already disabled, get no rows and are not replayed by catch-up.
- `syncTaskConfigEnabledFromDb`: at startup and hourly, the mirror files' `task-config.json` `enabled` field follows the DB. Only that key is written, and a missing or corrupt file is left alone.

## Tests
- `schedule-skip-ledger.test.ts` (14 tests): fake clock with 15 s ticks, 24 tasks and a 10-hour window. They cover:
  - the expected rows per due occurrence;
  - one alert only;
  - no replay of disabled tasks after a restart;
  - recovery, a single toggle, a small fleet, re-arm and expiry.
- `schedule-task-config-enabled-sync.test.ts` (9 tests).
- 7 + 3 mutants all fail the tests. tsc passes, and 26 schedule test files (368 tests) pass.

## Restart baseline
Before the first scan, the tracker seeds its "previously runnable" set from the DB rows (enabled and live) instead of starting empty. A dashboard that restarts while already in the faulty state therefore still detects the mass skip from the first scan, with no warm-up tick. If the seed fails, the tracker falls back to tick evidence.
- Regression test: a fresh tracker with all 24 tasks effectively disabled at startup (enabled in the DB) writes `skipped_disabled` rows from the first scan and fires one alert. Tasks that are really disabled in the DB get no rows, and a fully DB-disabled fleet gives 0 rows and 0 alerts. The seed runs once.
- 4 more mutants fail: no seed, seed on every scan, seed with every task, runner not wired. 27 schedule test files (378 tests) pass.

author: shwetangsinha0509
body:
Closes #2741

---

A single LLM judge called once is noisy — at default temperature the same prompt doesn't always return the same score. This adds `SelfConsistency`, a wrapper that runs one judge N times with identical inputs and aggregates the results, giving a more stable signal without swapping providers.

`SelfConsistency` complements `Jury` (inter-judge diversity) rather than replacing it: use `Jury` to reduce inter-model bias; use `SelfConsistency` to reduce intra-run variance for a single model.

**Usage:**
```python
from trulens.core import Metric
from trulens.feedback.self_consistency import SelfConsistency
from trulens.providers.openai import OpenAI

sc = SelfConsistency(
    provider=OpenAI(model_engine="gpt-4o-mini"),
    method="relevance",
    n=5,
    aggregation="median",
)
m = Metric(implementation=sc, name="SC Relevance").on_input().on_output()
```

**Key design points:**
- Mirrors `Jury` in structure — plugs into `Metric(implementation=sc)` with no pipeline changes
- Supports `mean`, `median`, `trimmed_mean`, `majority_vote`, and any custom callable
- Returns `(score, {"reason": ...})` with per-trial scores, std dev, flip rate, and binary entropy in the metadata
- Trials returning `UNPARSABLE_SCORE` are dropped (not counted as a zero), matching `Jury`'s sentinel handling
- Parallel dispatch via `ThreadPoolExecutor`
- Exported from `trulens.feedback` alongside `Jury`
- 33 unit tests covering all aggregation strategies, error handling, sentinel filtering, and `Metric` integration

The batch.py change here is a second fix for #2849 (same method, same sentinel, same user-visible effect as #2866). Either PR can merge first; the changes are independent.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

- [x] This change follows the TruLens standards (https://www.trulens.org/contributing/standards/)

author: n-soder
body:
> **Not ready to merge.** Merging deploys the endpoint to production. It won't send anything until the Resend keys are set (it returns 503 until then), but bot protection should land first. See **What's next**.

## What this adds

An optional **"Email the links"** section on the Links tab. The organiser enters an address for each person who should get an email, plus their own name if they like, and presses **Email N links**. Each person gets their own private link. Anyone left blank is skipped, so their link can still be copied by hand.

## How it works

1. The browser builds each person's link the same way **Copy link** does and POSTs the list to `/api/send-links`.
2. `functions/api/send-links.ts` is a stateless Cloudflare Pages Function. It rejects the request unless:
   - it comes from this site (Origin check)
   - it has 1–50 emails
   - every address looks valid
   - every name is 80 characters or fewer
   - every link points to this site's `/pairing` page, so the endpoint can't be used to email arbitrary URLs
3. It renders an HTML and a plain-text email for each person, with names HTML-escaped, and sends them all in one Resend batch call.
4. Nothing is stored. Only Resend's status code is logged, never addresses. Addresses are remembered only in the organiser's browser (`localStorage`).

**Privacy change:** names, addresses and links now pass through Resend when someone uses this feature. The home page privacy line and a note next to the button say so. This deliberately relaxes the original "no backend" rule, at the owner's request.

## Verified

- `tsc --noEmit` is clean. Vitest: 78/78, including 23 new tests for the endpoint's checks, the template and the Resend error handling.
- `vite build` passes. `wrangler pages functions build` compiles, with `/api/send-links` as the only route.
- **Local run with `wrangler pages dev` (dummy env vars):**
  - A missing config returns 503, a foreign Origin returns 403, and a foreign link returns 400.
  - A valid request reaches Resend's real API. It was rejected with a 401 for the dummy key and shown in the UI as a clean error.
  - The `/pairing` single-page-app fallback still returns 200.
- **Browser check (Orca):** a three-person draw with two addresses filled in showed **Email 2 links**, and the error displays correctly.
- **Not yet tested:** a real send, because there's no Resend key yet.

## What's next

**Owner (Resend and Cloudflare setup):**
1. Create a Resend account and verify a sending domain, e.g. `soderholm.app` or a subdomain like `mail.soderholm.app`. Add the DNS records Resend gives you in Cloudflare DNS.
2. Create a Resend API key with **sending access** only.
3. In Cloudflare Pages → `secretsanta` → Settings → Variables and secrets, add these for **Preview** first:
   - `RESEND_API_KEY`: the key, as a **secret**
   - `EMAIL_FROM`: e.g. `Secret Santa <santa@soderholm.app>`, matching the verified domain
4. Retry this PR's preview deployment, run a draw on the preview URL and email the links to your own addresses. Check:
   - the email arrives and doesn't land in spam
   - the button opens the right reveal page
   - it looks right in Gmail and Outlook, on a phone and a desktop

**Build (before merge):**
5. **Add Cloudflare Turnstile to the send button.** The Origin check only stops other websites. A script can fake it, so a bot could use the endpoint to send spam from our domain and burn the Resend quota. Turnstile needs a widget created in Cloudflare, a small script on the page and server-side verification in the endpoint. It's a new third-party script, so it needs owner approval.
6. Consider a per-IP rate limit (Cloudflare WAF rule on `/api/send-links`) as a second layer.

**Before go-live:**
7. Add the same two variables for **Production**, then merge.
8. Note the Resend free plan's limits: **100 emails a day and 3,000 a month**. One big office draw could use a day's quota.

**Optional, later:**
- Store email addresses in the history CSV so they carry over to next year. This needs a format version bump, so it was left out.
- Offer a "Resend to this person" button per row.

## Local development

`vite dev` doesn't run Pages Functions. To test the endpoint locally:

```sh
yarn vite build
npx wrangler@4 pages dev dist --binding RESEND_API_KEY=re_xxx --binding 'EMAIL_FROM=Secret Santa <santa@your-domain>'
```

Or put the values in `.dev.vars`, which is gitignored.

body:
## What

The web side of PB-80, which does for learning paths what PB-68 did for courses (ADR-042; spec specs#147 and specs#151, core core#62 and core#63).

**Learner**
- **Find a path** (`/paths`), a new nav tab: published paths on the shared learning card, labeled "Path". It has the course catalog's filters (search, level, skill, concept, teacher, instrument, language; it starts in the learner's language), plus More from this teacher, Details and Enroll.
- **Path detail** (`/paths/:learningPathId`): header, summary, lesson count, and the outline grouped by section. Back returns to the catalog with the same filters, the same cards loaded, and the same scroll position (the browser's Back does too).
- **Enroll** always makes the path current, so both screens take the learner to `/path`. On a path they already hold, the button reads **Continue** and makes the same call, since the server reuses the active copy.
- **My courses → My learning** (the route is still `/courses/mine`). Standalone paths use the shared card with the new snapshots and show "N of M lessons". The current course or path gets an **Open** link. "Assigned by" is hidden when the learner enrolled themselves. The page links to Find a path, and so does its empty state.
- Detail pages now sit under their catalog's tab. `course-detail` used to fall under My path.

**Teacher / admin**
A teacher works only with their own paths, and a teacher's course uses only that teacher's paths, whoever saves it. The server enforces both (specs#151 / core#63). Only an admin works across authors.
- **Path list:** the catalog's filters and All/Draft/Published tabs. **Admins also get a creator picker**, fed by `GET /learning-paths/creators`. Each path shows on the shared card with a status badge and Edit. There are no publish controls in the list.
- **Course builder checkpoint picker:** the "Only my paths" toggle is gone, since a teacher's library is already theirs alone. Admins get the same creator picker instead.
- **Path editor:** Summary and Language fields, and a status badge once the path is saved.
  - An admin gets **Publish**, which saves first.
  - An admin gets **Unpublish**, which unpublishes first and then saves any pending edits onto the draft, so none are lost.
  - A refused publish, or a refused save of a published path, lists what's missing and names any unpublished lessons.
  - A refused unpublish (for example, the path is used by a published course) shows the server's reason.
- **Course builder:** a publish refused over draft paths names those paths.

**Refactors**
- `CourseCard` takes `kind: 'course' | 'path'`. `summary` and `level` are now optional, because older path copies lack those snapshots.
- The catalog return logic moves out of `CourseCatalogView` into `useCatalogReturn`, with one storage slot per catalog.
- `useCourseCreators` gains the `path-catalog` and `path-library` scopes.
- `useLearningPathLibrary` now sends `language` and `status`. `useListLearningPaths` is removed.
- `useReplaceLearningPath` throws `LearningPathNotPublishableError` (carrying `missing[]`) instead of a plain error.
- `groupPathSections` is generic over item type, so the catalog outline reuses it.

## Notes for review
- The regenerated types make `StudentPath.lesson_count` and `completed_count` required, so one My courses fixture needed them added (that's in the codegen commit).

## Testing
- TDD throughout. 2,404 tests pass, run offline (API URLs pointed at a closed port). Lint and `npm run build` (including typecheck) are clean.
- Manual smoke is still to do. See the Validation list in the PB-80 plan.

## Merge order
specs#151 → core#63 → the `@wip` removal (specs#150, extended to #151's scenarios) → this PR.
