author: ahmad986ferdaws
body:
## Problem and linked issue

Aggregate-only comparisons can hide a regressing subgroup such as age 80+.

## Change

New `src/ecg_trust/slice_gates.py`:
- `SliceObservation(group, count, value)`, validated.
- `evaluate_slice_gate(reference, candidate, max_overall_drop=0.02, max_slice_drop=0.05, min_count=30, higher_is_better=True, insufficient_policy=BLOCK)` returns a frozen `SliceGateResult`: `passed`, `overall_degradation` with both sides weighted by the **reference** group counts (fixed composition, `math.fsum`), so a change in group mix can neither fake nor hide a regression, per-group `SliceVerdict` (`pass` / `fail` / `insufficient`), `failing_groups`, `insufficient_groups`, and `to_dict()`.
- Boundary comparisons use `math.isclose`, so 0.80 → 0.75 against a 0.05 limit passes.

## Validation

- `tests/unit/test_slice_gates.py` (22 tests): an unchanged candidate passes; a one-group regression fails while the average moves 0.2 points; an overall drop fails without any group failing; a pure group-mix shift is not a regression, while a uniform 3-point drop under the same shift fails; lower-is-better direction; insufficient groups block by default but only report under `REPORT`; the exact-limit boundary; 10 malformed gate inputs; 5 malformed observations.
- Ruff and `mypy --platform win32` are clean.

## Risks and scientific boundary

A decision utility only; nothing calls it yet. Limits and `min_count` belong in each future release protocol. Small groups still have wide intervals above `min_count`, so pair this gate with interval reporting for high-stakes decisions.

Closes #128

author: jacaudi
body:
## What & Why

One bad value, or one slow SMTP peer, must not stop mail meant for other people. Before this change, three paths could do exactly that:

- **#90.** The self-service recovery notice is **one body** sent to every admin. A legacy non-ASCII stored address made the transport refuse it for every admin, on a pre-auth path (`POST /api/v1/auth/recovery/request`).
- **#184.** The feed-staleness admin digest is also one body for every admin. Any user could suppress it for all admins by naming a device `café`, and the owner's own notice failed on its Subject.
- **#83.** Self-service recovery ran every step on one 30s budget. A slow mail server on the user's send used it up, and no admin was notified.

This PR also accepts a display-name `email.from` (#94): `DIYDDNS <diyddns@example.com>`.

## Implementation notes

- **Fold at render time (#90, #184).**
  - User-controlled text is folded to 7-bit ASCII (`email.ASCIIFold`) in every `internal/email` renderer that interpolates it, and in `stale`'s mail channel. `notice.go` stays medium-neutral.
  - `checkSendable` keeps its #80 refuse-don't-rewrite policy, so a non-ASCII bug in one of our own templates still fails loudly.
  - The admin notice now also names the account by id.
  - A hostile-input test over every renderer enforces the rule. A go/ast check fails if a new renderer in the package is left out of that test.
- **Per-send budgets (#83).**
  - The 30s budget now bounds store work only, and the admin list is read before any send.
  - Every send runs through a new `sendBounded` helper: detached from the caller's cancellation and bounded by its own 12s delivery timeout. `sendAdvisory` and `AdminService.notifyOwner` use it too.
  - Failure audit rows are unchanged and still survive an expired budget (#81).
- **Display-name From (#94).**
  - `unraid/apprise-go` already sends the bare address as the envelope sender and writes the name into `From:`, but it writes an ASCII name **unquoted**.
  - So the name is limited to ASCII atext words separated by single spaces, written exactly `Name <address>`. Quotes, commas, dots and non-ASCII names are refused at startup.
  - `config` and `email` apply the same predicate. The lockstep test now checks config against `email.SplitFrom`, the function the send path actually uses.
  - The transport sends the name in `?name=` with `%20` spaces, because the library never decodes `+` as a space.
  - Every `email.from` accepted before is still accepted.
- **Trade-off, documented in `docs/email.md`.** While a mail server is slow, one self-service request can hold 1 + (enabled admins) of the mailer's 32 in-flight slots, instead of one.

**Deferred follow-ups:**
- two more inline detach-and-bound copies in `stale/dispatch.go`, a different package;
- a `UserRepo.ListEnabledAdmins` helper, if a fourth list-and-filter site appears;
- device labels have no length cap, so a very long label could push the owner's Subject past 998 characters. This predates the change.

## Test plan

- [x] `task lint` passes locally (`0 issues.`)
- [x] `task test` passes locally (exit 0, `-race`)
- [x] Added/updated unit tests:
  - a hostile-input renderer table plus the go/ast completeness guard;
  - `stale` mail-channel tests;
  - a #90 end-to-end service test;
  - the #83 tests, which assert that each send has its own deadline and that a context shared across the admin loop fails;
  - `SplitFrom` and lockstep tables;
  - a `targetURL` encoding test and a fake-SMTP wire test.
- [x] Added/updated integration tests: `TestAdminInviteIsEmailed` now boots the real binary with `DIYDDNS Alerts <diyddns@x.test>` and asserts the `From:` header on the wire.
- [x] Manual verification: `task test:e2e -- -skip-discovery`, all 4 smoke tests pass.

Mutation probes were run for each invariant: the fold, the #81 audit detach, one context per send, the lockstep atext class, and renderer completeness. Each one fails when mutated and passes once restored. The timing tests pass 20 times under `-race`. A differential fuzz of 15k `email.from` candidates found 0 disagreements between config and email.

## Linked issues

Closes #90
Closes #184
Closes #83
Closes #94

## Conventional Commit

`feat(email): display-name email.from; one bad value or slow peer no longer suppresses others' mail`

author: laruss
body:
- **Owner's console (ADR-023):** read-only HTML and `/api/status` served by the controller on its own listener, at `https://gateway.local` through the home server's Caddy (same `local_certs` CA as `mattermost.local`, second mDNS alias). HTTP Basic for one owner, only an Argon2id hash stored (`gateway console password set`, hidden entry), global failed-login limit with `429`, strict security headers on every response, bounded 15 s cache with stale/unavailable states. The listener binds only the controller's `gateway-console` alias on `agent-mm`: workers on `agent-control` cannot reach it; no host port. Off unless `CONSOLE_ENABLED=true`.
- **Context measurements, not a percentage:** input bytes vs the 2 MiB cap, recent-replies/root/summary/memory characters vs their own budgets (UTF-16 units, like the budgets), tokens of the last reported attempt, 7-day max of retained last-attempt reports.
- **Operator agent, installed with the examples:** Codex, answers mentions in hq from a system status snapshot (`permissions.observe_system`, turn input `schemaVersion: 2`, metadata only), can post and nothing else; `memory.write` denied, so no writable namespace and the prompt says memory is read-only.
- **Scheduling:** status collected only for observing agents, inside the scheduling transaction and within the 2 MiB cap; retries keep the snapshot, redrive and wait resumption build a fresh one; a failed status load skips that agent with an alert instead of breaking the transaction. A retried attempt's usage is now kept on the run.
- **Rollback:** 0.2.1 rejects `observe_system` and v2 run jobs; ROLLBACK.md separates database certification (unchanged, no migration) from config and queued-input compatibility, with the procedure; install-test rehearses it.
- Docs: `docs/operations/console.md`, home-server, observability, releases, INSTALL/UPGRADE/ROLLBACK, changelog, status.

Reviewed by Codex and Opus per step and over the whole branch (two rounds, no P1/P2 left).

author: mahmoudabdalrhmanmohamed
body:
## Summary
- warm route stylesheet links during pointer/focus route prefetch
- preload any still-missing route CSS before replacing visible page HTML
- overlap CSS preparation with plugins and middleware instead of serializing all navigation work
- keep old page DOM visible until route CSS is ready, preventing flashes of unstyled route content
- clean temporary preload links after the asset is cached

## Why
The Idea Store recording shows route content briefly rendered without its positioning/styles (for example the scroll cue appears as raw text at the top-left). The router currently swaps DOM before route stylesheet links have loaded.

## Validation
Adds a runtime regression test that holds the current page while a route stylesheet preload is pending, then verifies the new DOM is swapped only after that CSS preload completes.

## Stack
Based on #100 because both changes touch the navigation pipeline. Retarget to main after #100 merges.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Stylesheets are now preloaded during client-side navigation and route prefetching, helping pages display with their styles ready when route content appears.
  * Navigation waits for stylesheet preload attempts to settle before showing the next page. Existing stylesheets are reused, and failed or unsupported preloads won’t block navigation indefinitely.
